Regarding *cakṣāte*: [they] *cakṣate*. When the *thās* suffix is replaced by *se*, the *k* is elided by *skoḥ*; then, when the *ṣ* is changed to *k* by *ṣaḍhoḥ* and subsequently to *ṣ* again, we have *cakṣe* and *cakṣāthe*. In the case of *dhvam*: * *cakṣadhve* * *cakṣadhve* (with *ṣatva*) * *cakṣadhve* (with *ṣatva* and subsequent *ṣṭutva*) * *cakṣadhve* (with *ṣatva* and subsequent *ṣṭutva* and further *ṣatva*) * In *yuvanti*, since there is an absence of *vṛddhi* due to the suffix being marked with *p*, and since there is an absence of *guṇa* due to the suffix being marked with *ṅ*, the form is *uviṅ*. [The forms are: *yauṣi*, *yuthaḥ*, *yutha*;
*yaumi*, *yuvaḥ*, *yumaḥ*. [In the imperative: *yuyāva*. [In the perfect: *yuyuvatuḥ*, *yuyuvuḥ*.

*Yuyavitha*, *yuyuvathuḥ*, *yuyuva*; *yuyāva* (or *yuyava*), *yuyuviva*, *yuyuvima*. [In the derivation of] *yavitā*, the *guṇa* [substitution] applies by virtue of its higher priority, overriding the *uvaṅ* [substitution]. [The future form is] *yaviṣyati*. [The imperative forms are: *yautu*, *yutāt*, *yutām*, *yuvantu*. In the second person singular (*hi*), there is no *vṛddhi* because the suffix is not marked with *P*. [The form is] *yuhi* (or *yutāt*).

In *yuta*, even though it ends in a *pit* (a consonant), there is no *vṛddhi* because it does not begin with a *hal* (consonant). Because it is *pit*, it lacks the status of being *ṅit*, and thus there is no *guṇa*. [The forms are: *yavāni*, *yavāva*, *yavāma*; *ayaut*, *ayutām*, *ayuvan*;
*ayauḥ*, *ayutam*, *ayuta*; *ayavam*, *ayuva*, *ayuma*. Regarding the potential (*vidhiliṅ*), he says:

Regarding the word *yuyāt*: here, fearing that the substitution of *vṛddhi* for *u* might occur because the suffix *tip* (along with the augment *yāsuṭ*) is marked with *p*, he says: "In this case, there is no *vṛddhi* of *u*. To the question "Why?", he says: "In the Bhāṣya. [He adds:
"Because of the explanation," namely, at the occasion of explaining the rule *halaḥ śnaḥ śānajjhau*.

The meaning is "because of the statement. Now, one might object: since the suffix *tip* together with the augment *yāsuṭ* is marked as *pit*, and by the rule "that which is marked *pit* is not treated as *ṅ*" (*picca ṅnna*), there is an absence of *ṅtva* even for *yāsuṭ* in the case of the *parasmaipada* endings; consequently, because there is no prohibition of *guṇa* by the rule "before *kṅit* [suffixes]" (*kṅiti ca*), the *guṇa* substitution would occur.

To address this, he says: "by that which is specifically prescribed," and so on, ending with "due to sublation. Because of the rule *yāsuṭ parasmaipadeṣu*, the augment *yāsuṭ* is specifically prescribed for the *parasmaipada* endings; since it has the marker *ṅ*, the prohibition of the *ṅ*-marker—which would otherwise apply to *tiP* when accompanied by it due to the rule *ṅcci piṇṇe*—is [prevented].

The meaning is that because there is no sublation (*bādhā*), the prohibition regarding the quality-possessor (*guṇin*) is without obstruction. He states [the form] for the optative (*āśīr-liṅ*): *yūyāt*. Because it is an *ārddhadhātuka* suffix, there is no *vṛddhi*; rather, by the rule "ṭh-a-kṛt-sārvadhātukayoḥ," there is lengthening. [The forms] *yūyāstām* and so forth follow. He states [the form] for the aorist (*luṅ*): *ayāvīt*. There is *vṛddhi* before the *sic* suffix.
In *ṭhiṭa īṭ*, there is the elision of *sic*. [The forms] *ayāviṣṭām* and so forth; [the conditional form] *ayaviṣyat*. (274) *turustuśamyamaḥ sārvadhātuke* | Pāṇini 7.3.95.
*turustu*: [This is] the singular ablative case from a collective dvandva compound of *tu*, *ru*, *stu*, *śam*, and *am*.

From the rule *ṭhuto vṛddhir luki hali*, the word *hali* is understood; from *ṭhbhūsuvostiṅi*, the word *tiṅi*; from *ṭhbruva īṭ*, the word *īṭ*; and from *ṭhyaṅe ve’tyato veti*, the word *veti* is carried over. Thus he says: "from these," and so forth. Regarding *nābhyastasya*: [this refers to] *ṭhnābhyastasyā'ci piti sārvadhātuke*.

Therefore, since the recurrence (*anuvṛtti*) of the term *sārvadhātuke* is possible, the purpose of mentioning *sārvadhātuka* again is so that the recurrence of *pit* might not occur; this is the meaning. Regarding *ravīti*:
the point is that in the alternative where *īṭ* is applied, because the beginning is not a consonant (*hal*), the rule "vṛddhi for *u*" does not apply. Regarding *rauti*.
The meaning is that in the absence of *īṭ*, [the rule] "there is vṛddhi for *u* and *ū*" applies. Regarding *ruvītaḥ* and *rutaḥ*:
the meaning is that even though it is not marked with *pit*, there is an optionality regarding *īṭ*. Regarding *ruvanti*:

the meaning is that once the final substitution (*antādeśa*) has been made, because the beginning of the suffix is no longer a consonant (*hal*), *īṭ* does not apply, and thus *uvaṅ* occurs. Regarding *śāmyati*.

The intention is that because the *śyan* suffix lacks the property of being a *tiṅ*, there is no application of the rule *īṇniṭi*. Regarding "in the sense of benediction, *ruyāt*": since it is an *ārddhadhātuka* suffix, there is no *īṭ*; instead, there is lengthening by the rule *ṭhakkṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ*.
Regarding "but in the case of injunction (*vidhi*) and so forth": by "and so forth" (*ādi*), the inclusion of invitation (*nimantraṇa*) and other such functions is intended. [Thus one says] *ruyāt*.

Regarding the word *ruvīyāt*: the intention is that there is an optional *īṭ* augment because [the suffix] is a *sārvadhātuka* beginning with a consonant (*hal*). In the alternative case where *īṭ* is absent, it should be understood that when a *pittva* *sārvadhātuka* suffix beginning with a consonant follows, "vṛddhi" occurs in place of the *u* by the rule *uto vṛddhir luki hali*. Now, one might object: since the root *tud* is not seen in the *dhātupāṭha*, it lacks the status of being a verbal root (*dhātu*); how then [can this apply]?

Therefore, because the rule for the augment *īṭ* applies to the *sārvadhātuka* suffixes, he says: "The root *tu* is a Vedic (sautra) root. [It is used] in the senses of motion, increase, and injury. In this matter, the commentary itself is the authority. Now, one might ask: since it is separated from the *sārvadhātuka* by the *śap* affix, how can it be followed by a *sārvadhātuka*? To this he says: "And this..."

Regarding the statement "they remember [the rule] 'lug-vikaraṇa'": the reason for prescribing *īṭ* here is precisely the absence of an intervening *tiṅ*. However, it should be understood that in the Veda, when there is *luk* of the *śap* suffix—as in *śamīdhvam* and *abhyamīt* from the roots *śam* and *am*—this [root *mā*] is *aniṭ*. Before a *sārvadhātuka* affix beginning with a consonant (*hal*), it behaves like the root *rudh*.
However, there is no *iṭ* augment in the case of an *ārddhadhātuka* suffix. Thus it says: "tota" etc. Regarding the root *ṇu* in the sense of "praise":
this is a root taught with an initial *ṇ*, and it is *seṭ* (taking the *iṭ* augment). Its forms are like those of the root *yud*. The roots *kṣu*, *kṣṇu*, and *snu* are also *seṭ*;
their forms are like those of the root *yud*. Examples are: *cukṣāva*, *cukṣṇāva*, and *suṣṇāva*.

The sense is that this is an upadeśa (original instruction). The root *ūrṇuñ* is ubhayapadī (active and middle) and is seṭ (having an indicatory *i*). Since a vṛddhi substitute is invariably required by rule 6.4.13 (*uto vṛddhir laṅliṭoḥ*), [the following applies]: "Optionally for *ūrṇoti*, 7.3.90."

Regarding the rule *ūrṇoter vibhāṣā*: from the previous rule *uto vṛddhiḥ*, the word *vṛddhiḥ* is understood, as well as *halī*; from the rule *nābhyastasya*, the phrase *piti sārvadhātuke* is also understood. With this intention, he explains the sūtra by supplying the missing words, beginning with "vṛddhiḥ syāt" (there shall be vṛddhi).

Regarding the rules "liṭi ṭhijādeḥ" and "kāsyanekācaḥ," which would otherwise require the suffix *ām* [after the root *ūrṇu*], he says: "*ām* is not [applied] after *ūrṇoti*. The meaning is that because the substitution of *nuṭ* for *ūrṇu* will be stated later, it lacks both the property of beginning with *ij* (the vowel *i*) and the property of having more than one vowel (*anekāctva*). Thus, in the case of *ṇal*, we have *ūrṇu-a*.

When the rule "when [the substitute] ṭha and so forth are present, the second [element] is doubled" applies, and consequently, by doubling the *ṛ* together with the *r* in *ṛtnu*, and then by the application of *halādiśeṣa* (retaining only the first consonant), the *n* would be eliminated, resulting in the form *ūrunau*; however, this is prevented by the rule: (276) *na ndrāḥ saṃyogādayaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.3): "The letters *n*, *d*, and *r* are not doubled when they are the first members of a conjunct (*saṃyoga*)."
The term *na* (not) [is used]. From the rule *ṭhekāco dve prathamasya*, the word *dve* (twice) is understood to carry over (*anuvartate*).

From the rule *ajāderdvitīyasya*, the term *ajādeḥ* (beginning with a vowel) [is understood]. The compound *añc-ādiḥ* (the beginning which is *añc*) is a *karmadhāraya*, from which the ablative case is derived. *N*, *d*, and *r* form a *dvandva* compound. Thus he says: "following the vowel" (*acaḥ parāḥ*).
One might object: "If there were doubling of the element *ṭhṇu*, would not the letter *ṇ* be heard in both parts [of the reduplicated form]?

To this he says: "There is doubling of the word *nu*. Regarding the statement "of the *ṇ*-hood": in the Dhātupāṭha, the root is cited as *ūrṇu* with the *ṇ* already applied; the meaning is that when doubling is to be performed, that *ṇ*-hood is considered non-existent (*asiddha*).

Regarding the phrase "from the indicative mark" (liṅgāt): the meaning of the rule *ubhau sābhyāsasya* is this—both *n* sounds belonging to the two parts of the reduplicated root *an*, when following a cause situated in a prefix, undergo the change to *ṇ*. The example is *prāṇiṇat*. Here, the change to *ṇ* occurs by the rule *aniteḥ*.
Since the doubling of the syllable *ṇī*— based on the fact that the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* is not considered "asiddha" (non-existent) by the rule *pūrvatrāsiddham advirvacane*—
is sufficient to ensure the hearing of the letter *m* in both parts of the reduplication,
the statement *ubhau sābhyāsasya* indicates the non-universality (*anityatā*) of the rule *pūrvatrāsiddham advirvacane*.

The meaning is "he causes to go. Regarding the form *ūrṇunāva*: when the suffix *nu* is doubled, the first *n* undergoes the change to *ṇ* by the rule *raṣābhyām*. However, the second *n* does not become *ṇ* by the rule *aṭkupvāṅnumvyavāye*, precisely because of the indicative mark (*liṅga*) in the rule *ubhau sābhyāsasya*.
(277) *vibhāṣorṇoḥ* | 1.2.3.

Regarding *vibhāṣorṇoḥ*: the term *ṅit* is understood from the rule *gāṅkuṭādibhyo 'ṅidviṣayaḥ*, and the term *iṭ* is understood from the rule *vija iṭ*. With this in mind, he explains the sūtra by supplying the remaining words: [The augment *iṭ* is optionally applied after the root *ūrṇu* when followed by an affix marked with the indicatory letter *ṅ*.]

Regarding *iḍādi* and *ūrṇunuvitha*: in the alternative where *iṭ* is present, there is no *guṇa*, and thus *uvaṅ* substitution occurs, resulting in *ūrṇunuvitha*. In the alternative where *iṭ* is absent, *guṇa* occurs, resulting in *ūrṇunavitha*. [The forms] *ūrṇunuvathuḥ*, *ūrṇunuva*, and *ūrṇunāva* (or *ūrṇunava*) follow. Regarding the *luṭ* [suffix], having considered the optionality of *iṭ* after *tās*, he says:
*ūrṇavitā*, *ūrṇuvitā*; *ūrṇaviṣyati*, *ūrṇuviṣyati*;
*ūrṇaviṣyate*, *ūrṇuviṣyate*. When the suffix *luṅ* follows, the form *aurṇuid* is established; then, since both the optional *vṛddhi* (by the rule *ūrṇoter vibhāṣā*) and *guṇa* are applicable—
(278) *guṇo'pṛkte* | 7|3|91| The rule *guṇo'pṛkte* [is derived] from *ūrṇotervibhāṣā*, from *nābhyastasya*, and from *uto vṛddhiḥ*.

The word *hal* (consonant) also carries over [from the previous rule]. Thus he says: "of *ūrṇoti*, etc. [The phrase] "an exception to *vṛddhi*" means that it is an exception to the optional *vṛddhi* prescribed by the rule *ūrṇoter vibhāṣā*. Regarding the form *ūrṇuyāt*, having raised the doubt that there might be an optional *vṛddhi* by the rule *vibhāṣorṇoḥ*, he says: "here there is no *vṛddhi*."

"From the Bhāṣya": the sense is that, since *yāsuṭ* has the marker *ṅ*, it lacks the status of being *pit*; therefore, there is no optional *vṛddhi*. Nor should one suspect that, this being the case, the prohibition of *guṇa* would also not apply;
for by the specific rule that *yāsuṭ* has the marker *ṅ*, [the rule] "when *ṅ* follows, *pin* is [also treated as having the marker *ṅ*]" applies.

The intention is that the prohibition [of *guṇa*] by the suffix *niṣ* (in *niṣṭhā*) when applied to a root ending in *p* is set aside, because this has been stated specifically regarding the root *yū* "to mix" (*yu miśraṇe*). He states the form for the *āśīr-liṅ* (optative) in the *parasmaipada*:
*ūrṇūyāt*. The lengthening is by the rule *akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ*.

Regarding "ūrṇūyāstām" and so forth: in the *ātmanepada* [middle voice], the forms of the *liṅ* (optative) are *ūrṇaviṣīṣṭa* and *ūrṇuviṣīṣṭa*. The point is that there is an optional application of the *ṅit* designation by the rule "vibhāṣorṇoḥ. In the *luṅ* (aorist) in the *parasmaipada* (active voice), when the form *ā-ūrṇu-i* has been established, there is the alternative of the *ṅit* designation by the rule "vibhāṣorṇoḥ."
He states the form *ūrṇuvīt* when there is an absence of *guṇa*; for in the alternative where *ṅit*-ness is absent, *guṇa* is invariably applicable.
(279) *ūrṇoter vibhāṣā* || 7.2.6 || [The substitution of *uvaṅ* is optional for the root *ūrṇu*].

The rule *ūrṇoter vibhāṣā* (optionally for the root *ūrṇu*) follows from the previous rules *sici vṛddhiḥ parasmaipadeṣu* (vṛddhi is substituted before the suffix *sic* when followed by parasmaipada endings) and *neṭi* (this does not apply when *iṭ* follows). Therefore, he says: "when *iṭ* and so forth [beginning with the suffix] follow. However, in the ātmanepada, the forms are *āūrṇaviṣṭa* or *āūrṇuviṣṭa*; and *āūrṇaviṣyat* or *āūrṇuviṣyat*.

*āṬrṇaviṣyata*—*āṬrṇuviṣyata*. *Dyau* is a root that does not take the augment *iṭ*; it is conjugated as *dyauti*. By the rule "vṛddhi for *u*" (*uto vṛddhiḥ*), and because it is a root ending in *u*, it follows the pattern of the root *yudh* in the *sārvadhātuka* suffixes and the *liṭ* tense. Thus: *dyoteti*, *dyoṣyati*, *adyauṣīt*.
*Ṣu* (in the sense of) "impelling" (*prasava*)—this is a root beginning with *ṣ*. It is *aniṭ*. Its conjugation, starting from *saute*, is like that of *dyau*. The same applies to *ku*.
Regarding the root *stu*: *ṣṭuañ* in the sense of praise. It is conjugated in both voices (*ubhayapadī*) and is *aniṭ*.

Considering the optionality of *īṭ* by the rule "turustuśamyamaḥ" and, in the absence of *īṭ*, the *vṛddhi* of the *u* vowel, he says: *stauti* and *stavīti*. [They] praise: *stuvanti*. [Thou praisest: *stauṣi*—or *stavīṣi*; [you two praise: *stuthaḥ*—or *stavīthaḥ*.

[In the active voice (*parasmaipada*): *stuvīthaḥ*, *stutha-stuvītha*; *staumi-stavīmi*, *stuvaḥ-stuvīmaḥ*; *stumaḥ-stuvīmaḥ*. Regarding the middle voice (*ātmanepada*), considering the optionality of the *īṭ* augment, he says: *stute*, *stuvīte*. [The forms are: *stuvāte*, *stuvate*; *stuṣe*—*stuvīṣe*, *stuvāthe*.

Present tense: *studhve*, *stuvīdve*; *stuve*, *stuvahe*, *stuvīvahe*; *stumahe*, *stuvīmahe*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*): *tuṣṭāva*, *tuṣṭuvatuḥ*, *tuṣṭuvuḥ*. Because it belongs to the *krād-i* group, the augment *iṭ* does not occur even before the suffix *thal*. [Thus: *tuṣṭotha*, *tuṣṭuvathuḥ*, *tuṣṭuva*; *tuṣṭāva*—*tuṣṭava*; *tuṣṭuva*, *tuṣṭuma*.
*tuṣṭuve* and so forth. [The forms of] the agent (*stotṛ*) are: *stoṣyati*, *stoṣyate*. [The imperative forms are: *stautu*—*stuvītu*; *stutāt*—*stuvītāt*;
*stutām*—*stuvītām*; *stuvantu*. *Stuhi*—*stuvīhi*; *stutāt*—*stuvītāt*; *stutam*—*stuvītam*.
Let him praise—let him praise, let him praise; let us two praise, let us praise.
Let them two praise—let them praise, let them praise, let them praise. Praise thou—praise thou, praise ye two;
praise ye—praise ye. Let me praise, let us two praise, let us praise.

laṅ (imperfect): *aiṣṭaut*, *aiṣṭavīt*; *aiṣṭutām*, *aiṣṭuvītām*; *aiṣṭuvan*. *aiṣṭauḥ*, *aiṣṭavīḥ*; *aiṣṭutam*, *aiṣṭuvītam*; *aiṣṭuta*, *aiṣṭuvīta*. *aiṣṭavam*, *aiṣṭuva*/*aiṣṭuvīva*; *aiṣṭuma*/*aiṣṭuvīma*. *aiṣṭuta*, *aiṣṭuvīta*.

"astuvātām," and so forth; the optative (vidhiliṅ) is "stuyāt"—or "stuvīyāt," and so forth; in the middle voice (ātmanepada), it is "stoṣīṣṭa," and so forth. Regarding the aorist (luṅ), when the absence of the augment *iṭ* would otherwise apply due to the suffix *sic*, he says: "after the roots *stu*, *su*, and *dhū*" (*stusudhūñbhyaḥ*). Thus, by the rule "the *iṭ* [augment] is elided before an *īṭ*" (*iṭa īṭi*), there is the elision of *sic*, and then the *vṛddhi* [substitution] occurs in place of *sic*.

The form *astāvīt* is thus established; likewise *astāviṣṭām*, and so forth. Regarding the rule *stusudhūñbhyaḥ*, because the term *parasmaipadeṣu* (in the case of parasmaipada endings) is understood as a governing rule (*anuvṛtti*), the suffix *iṇ* does not apply in the ātmanepada. Thus, we have *astoṣṭa*, *astoṣātām*, and so on.

(280) *brūvaḥ pañcānāmādita āho bruvaḥ* | Pāṇini 3.4.84. [The root] *brūñ* becomes *bruvaḥ*. "Of the five" refers to the first five [personal endings]. This is a subsequent rule (*uttarasūtra*) to [Pāṇini 3.4.82] *parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatus...*. From [Pāṇini 3.4.83] *vido laṭo vā*, the word *laṭaḥ* or *vā* is understood (*anuvartate*).

He says that: "of the *laṭ* [suffix] following *brū*" and "of the first five. This means [the suffixes] *tip*, *tas*, *jhi*, *sip*, and *thas*. "The five beginning with *ṇal*" means these five: *ṇal*, *atus*, *us*, *thal*, and *athus*. "[The letter *ṛ* is] for the sake of pronunciation" means...
The purpose of that will become clear immediately hereafter. Regarding the form *āha*:

from the root *brū* (to speak), in the present tense (*laṭ*), third person singular (*tip*), with the substitution *ṇal*, the root undergoes the substitution *āh*. When the suffix *sip* takes the augment *thala*, and the root again undergoes the substitution *āh*, we have the form *āh-tha*. At this point, the substitution of *ḍha* for *ha* would apply.

(281) *āhasthaḥ* |8|2|35|. Regarding *āhasthaḥ*: the word *āhaḥ* is in the genitive case (*ṣaṣṭhyanta*). Intending that the term *jhali* is carried over from the rule *jhalo jhali*, he explains the sūtra by supplying the missing words: "when a *jhal* [consonant] follows. *Āh*.
Thus, by the rule *jhalīti*, the substitution of *th* for this [final *s*] is established. By the rule *ṭhalo’ntyasya*, it applies to the final [letter].

Then, by the rule *cartvam*, when *āth-th* is situated, the first *th* undergoes the substitution of *c* (cerebralization) by the rule *ṭhkhari ca*; the meaning is that the form *āttha* results. However, if the substitute *āh* were to end in *a*, then [the substitution would apply] to the *a* following the *h*.
It should be understood that when *th* is substituted [for *dh*], and *h* is changed to *ḍh*, and then by *ca*-rule [to *ṭh*], the form would be *āṭṭha*.
Regarding the case where there is an absence of *ṇal* and the other suffixes for the five [roots], he says:
(282) *bruva īṭ* | Pāṇini 7.3.93.

The word *īṭ* [is understood here]; from the rule *ṭhnābhyastasya*, the word *pitī* (before a *p*-suffixed ending) is carried over, and from the rule *uto vṛddhiḥ*, the word *halī* (before a consonant) is also carried over. Thus he says: "of that which follows *bruvaḥ*" and so forth. Now, one might object: in the form *āttha*, since the substitute *āha* is considered to have the same status as its original (*sthānivadbhāva*), it possesses the nature of *brū*; therefore, the augment *īṭ* would apply to the *th* following it. To this [he replies]:

He says: "In this case, 'āt-'" etc. The syntactical connection is: "This augment *iṭ*, which would have been applicable by virtue of the rule of *sthānivadbhāva* (the substitute being treated like the original), does not occur. Why? To this he says: "Because the substitution of *th* is prescribed [only] when a *jhal* [consonant] follows. By the rule "āhasthaḥ," the substitution of *tha* for *āha* is ordained when a *jhal* follows. However, if *iṭ* were present...

Because [the root *brū*] lacks the property of beginning with a *jhal* sound, that [rule] would be without scope; therefore, the meaning is that in the form *āttha*, it is understood as being governed by the rule *īṇniṭi*. Regarding "they say" (*bruvanti*): [the forms are] *bravīṣi*, *brūthaḥ*, *brūtha*; *bravīmi*, *brūvaḥ*, *brūmaḥ*. Regarding the *ātmanepada* of the present tense (*laṭ*), he says: *brūte*. In the rule *bruvaḥ pañcānām...* [the following applies].
Because of the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the rule "for the *parasmaipada* endings," there is no substitution for *ā*. Thus: *bruvāte*, *bruvate*;
*brūṣe*, *brūvāthe*, *brūdhve*; *bruve*, *brūvahe*, *brūmahe*.
(283) *bruvo vaciḥ* | Pāṇini 2.4.53. [The root *brū-* is replaced by *vac-* in the perfect tense.]

The word *bruvaḥ* [refers to] *vac*. The meaning is that *vac* shall be the substitute for *brū* in the *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes. The vowel *i* is for the sake of pronunciation. Regarding *uvāca*: the intention is that when reduplication has occurred before a suffix not having *k* (*akit*), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule "of the reduplicated syllable of the perfect" (*liṭo'bhyāsasya*). Regarding *ūcatuḥ*: [this occurs] before reduplication when a suffix having *k* (*kit*) follows.
The sense is as follows: after the *saṃprasāraṇa* by the rule "ṭhvacisvapiyajādīnām," and after reduplication has been performed, the *halādiśeṣa* applies;

then, because a homogeneous vowel follows, the *uvaṅ* substitution occurs for the reduplicated syllable by the rule "abhyāsasyāsavarṇe," and finally, a long vowel is substituted [for the two similar vowels] by the rule "savarṇadīrghaḥ.
The root *vac* is enumerated among those that are *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*); therefore, by the rule of Bhāradvāja, the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied before the suffix *thal*.

He says that: *uvacitha* and *uvaktha*. In the absence of *iṭ*, [the rule] *coḥ kuḥ* applies. In the rule *bruva īṭ*, because the term *sārvadhātuka* is also understood from the preceding rule *nābhyastasya*, there is no *īṭ*.
[The forms are] *ūcathuḥ*, *ūca*; *uvāca*—[from] *uvaca*; *ūcima*, *ūcima*. By the rule regarding roots beginning with *krī*, *iṭ* is added. Thus: *ūce*.

*ūcāte*, *ūcire*; *ūciṣe*, *ūcāthe*, *ūcidhve*; *ūce*, *ūcivahe*, *ūcimahe*. Regarding *vaktā*: there is a prohibition of *iṭ* when *vac* is replaced by *vaci*. [Thus: *vakṣyati*, *vakṣyate*. Regarding *bravītu* and *brūtāt*:
[one might object] that since the substitute *tātaṅ* for *tiP* is marked with *p* (pit), the augment *īṭ* would apply by the rule "after *bruva*, *īṭ* [is added]."

To address this, he says "ṅcci. [The forms are] *brūtām*, *bruvantu*; *brūhi*, *brūtāt*, *brūtam*, *brūta*; *bravāṇi*. The point is that because the augment *āṭ* is marked with *p* (indicating it is not *ṅ*), there is an absence of *ṅ*-status, and thus no prohibition of *guṇa* applies.
[The forms are] *bravāva*, *bravāma*; *brūtām*, *bruvātām*, *bruvatām*; *brūṣva*, *bruvāthām*.

Taking it as an established fact, he says "brūdhvam" (you all speak). Because the augment *āṭ* is marked with *p*, it lacks the *ṅ* designation; thus, there is *guṇa* substitution [in the first person plural]. [The forms are] *bravāvahe* and *bravāmahe*. In the *laṅ* [mood]: *abravīt*, *abrūtām*, *abruvan*; *abravīḥ*, *abrūtam*, *abrūta*; *abravam*, *abrūva*, *abrūma*.
He states the potential mood (vidhiliṅ): *brūyāt* ("he should say"), *brūyātām*, and so forth.

He states the benedictive mood (āśīrliṅ): *ucyāt* ("may he speak"). The intention is that when the substitute *vac* occurs, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule "vacisvapi... [Pāṇini 6.1.15]. [He gives] *ucyāstām*, and so forth, in the middle voice (*ātmanepada*).

In the *āśīrliṅ* (benedictive) mood: *vikṣīṣṭa*, *vakṣīyāstām*, and so forth. Because it does not end in *kit*, there is no *saṃprasāraṇa*. When the *luṅ* suffix *ic* is applied and the substitution of *vac* occurs, resulting in the form *avac s t*, he says: "by *asyati*" (*as* replaces *vac*). When the form is *avac a t*—

(284) *vaca um* |7|4|20|. He explains the sūtra by supplying the missing portion: *aṅ pi re iti*. The intention is that this follows from the recurrence (*anuvṛtti*) of [the word] *aṅ* from the rule *ṛdṛśo’ṅi* (6.1.127). Because it has the marker *m*, it is placed after the final vowel. [The result is] *vacom*, by the rule *ādguṇaḥ* (6.1.87).

He says that: "he said" (*avocat*). [In the conditional mood: "he would say" (*avakṣyat*, *avakṣyata*). Regarding "the root *iṅ*": the meaning is that the root *iṅ* "to study" is ātmanepada because it has the marker *ṅ*. Regarding "the root *iṇ* in the sense of motion": the letter *ṇ* is for the purpose of distinguishing it in rules such as "for *iṇ*, there is *yaṇ*" (*iṇo yaṇ*). Regarding "he goes" (*eti*): [this occurs] when the *śap* suffix is elided and the *tip* suffix remains.
Because it ends in a non-pit vowel, there is no *ṅ* designation, and thus no *guṇa*. Regarding "itaḥ": because it ends in a non-pit vowel, there is no *ṅ* designation, and thus no *guṇa*.
In the case of "iyanti," since there is no *guṇa* due to the absence of the *ṅ* designation, *iyuṅ* would be expected; however—(285) *iṇo yaṇ* 6.4.81.

Regarding the rule *iṇo yaṇ*: since the term *aci* (in an affix beginning with a vowel) is understood from the previous rule *ṣṇudhātu...* and, being obtained through the governing heading (*adhikāra*) on "stems" (*aṅga*), it serves as a qualifier for the specific suffixes implied by that heading—therefore, the rule applies to the beginning of such a suffix. With this intention, he explains the sūtra by supplying the missing words: "when a suffix beginning with a vowel follows. The phrase "this is an exception to *iyaṅ*" means that this rule is formulated precisely because *iyaṅ* would otherwise apply. However, *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* substitutions take precedence over this [rule] due to their higher status in the order of rules. For example: *ayanam*, *āyakaḥ*, and *yantīti*. [From the root *i*: *eṣi*, *ithaḥ*, *itha*; *emi*, *ivaḥ*, *imaḥ*; and *iyāya*.

When there is reduplication, upon the increase of the subsequent portion (*uttara-khaṇḍa*) and the substitution of *āy* for *ai*, the rule *ṭhabhyāsasyā'savarṇe* applies, resulting in *iyaṅ*. However, in the case of the suffix *atus*, after reduplication and the absence of *guṇa* due to the *kit* designation, we have the state *i i atus*. Then, by the rule *ṭhiṇo yaṇ*, the *yaṇ* substitute is applied to the subsequent portion, resulting in the state *iy-atus*. At this point—(286) *dīrgha iṇaḥ kiti* [Pāṇini 7.4.69]:
"There is lengthening of *iṇ*. From the rule *ṭhatra lopaḥ* [7.4.58], the word *abhyāsasya* ("of the reduplicated syllable") is understood, and from the rule *ṭhvyatho liṭī* [7.4.68]...

The term *liṭ* also carries over [from the previous rule]. Thus he says: "of the reduplicated stem of *iṇ*" (*iṇo'bhyāsasya*). Regarding *īyatuḥ*, since the rule of Bhāradvāja applies, considering that *viṭ* follows, he says: *iyayitha* and *iyetha*. [The forms are: *iyathuḥ*, *īya*;
*iyāya*, *iyaya*, *īyiva*, *īyima*. [In the future: *eṣyati*. [In the imperative: *etu*—*itāt*, *itām*.

*yantu*, *ihi*—from *ita* [the imperative suffix] *hi*. *ayāni*, *ayāva*, *ayāma*—from *ait* (the imperfect form), by the elision of the *ik* suffix (*it*), the *guṇa* substitution of the vowel *i*, and the *vṛddhi* substitution for *āṭ*. *āyan*—when *jhi* is replaced by *ant*, the *ik* suffix is elided, resulting in *i-an*; then, by applying the rule *ṭhiṇo yaṇ* (*thiṇ* becomes *yaṇ*), the *yaṇ* substitution is made.

The sense is that because it is an *abhīya* (an augment applied before the suffix), it is considered *asiddha* (non-existent) for the purpose of [applying] *āṭ*. [The forms of the present indicative are: *aitam*, *aita*; *āyam*, *aiva*, *aima*.
Regarding the optative (*vidhiliṅ*), he says: *iyāt*. [The forms are: *iyātām*, *iyuḥ*, and so forth.
Regarding the precative (*āśīrliṅ*), he says: *īyāt*. [This is formed] by the lengthening [of the vowel] according to the rule *akṛtsārvadhātukayordīrghaḥ*.
The state [of the suffix]. "īyāstām," and so forth. (287) *eter liṅ* |7|4|24|.
Regarding *eter liṅ*: from the rule *upasargād dhrasva ūhateḥ*, the portion *upasargād dhrasvaḥ* is [applied].

The term *aṇ* is carried over from the rule "ṭhke'ṇaḥ," and the term *kiti* is carried over from the rule "ayaṅ yi kṅtī. Therefore, he says: "of that which follows an upasarga," and so forth. Here, the mention of *ārddhadhātuke* (in an ārdhadhātuka suffix) is an error, because it was absent in the preceding rules and thus its recurrence is impossible; [this applies] when there is a *kit* suffix.

Since the rule is already established by [the condition] "in a *liṅ*," the term "*ṅtī*" does not carry over; this is because the *liṅ* of the *ārddhadhātuka* [suffixes] following the root *iṇ* lacks the property of having a *ṅ*. Furthermore, lest a short vowel occur even in the case of *ninvyamīyāt*, he says: "on both sides.
Here, if the single-substitute *īkāra* were treated as belonging to the preceding part (*pūrvāntatva*), [the desired result would follow].

The status of being the root *iṇ* cannot occur due to the incorporation of the prefix (*upasarga*), because if one relies on its being the root *iṇ* by virtue of the principle that "that which begins with [the prefix] is like the whole," then there is no status of being subsequent to a prefix; for since the vowel *i*, which is a portion of the prefix, exists as the vowel *ī* through the single-substitute (*ekādeśa*) operation, the element *abha* lacks the status of being a prefix. This is because of the single-substitute...

It is also not possible to maintain that the root *iṇ* possesses the status of being "initial" (ādivat) while simultaneously having the status of being "final" (antavat) such that it enters into a prefix;
for the contradiction between the terms "prior" (*pūrva*) and "subsequent" (*para*), as well as "beginning" (*ādi*) and "end" (*anta*), is immediately apparent.

The meaning is that two contradictory extended applications (*atideśa*) cannot occur simultaneously. This is clear in the *Bhāṣya* on the sūtra *antādivat*. Nor should it be argued that because the portion ending in *bha*—namely, *abha*—is treated as a prefix by the maxim of "modification of a single part" (*ekadeśavikṛtanyāya*), and because the vowel *ī* is treated as the initial element of the following word, the shortening [of the penultimate vowel] would be unavoidable.
"In some cases, the principle of 'modification of a single part' (*ekadeśavikṛtanyāya*) is not resorted to in accordance with the intended meaning;
this is explained in detail in the *Śabdenduśekhara*. Regarding the form *sameyāt*: [it is derived from] *ā-iyāt* or *eyāt*.

In the form *sameyāt*, because the vowel *e* is not an *aṇ* (i.e., it is not one of the vowels *a, i, u, ṛ, ḷ*), the substitution of a short vowel does not occur, according to the rule *grahaṇaka-sūtra* which applies elsewhere."
The intention is that the pratyāhāra (abbreviation) is based on the preceding letter *ṇ* itself. Then, raising the objection as to how the usage "samīyāt" occurs in some places, he says:
"But the usage 'samīyāt' belongs to the root belonging to the Bhūvādigaṇa," namely the one included by the elision [praśleṣa] in the rule "iṭa kiṭa kaṭī gatau."

The intention is that the long vowel [of the root] is to be understood here by the rule "idātorāśīrliṅṅ-ṭhikṛtsārvadhātukayordīrghaḥ" (Pāṇini 7.3.101). He states a specific rule regarding the *luṅ* [tense]:
(288) *iṇo gā luṅi* (Pāṇini 2.4.45).

The meaning of the rule *iṇo gā*—"the substitute *gā* shall take the place of the root *iṇ* in the *luṅ* [tense]"—is clear. When the form *agās t* has been established, he says: "by the rule *gātisthāghupābhūbhyaḥ sicaḥ parasmaipadeṣu*" (Pāṇini 2.4.77). The *lṛṅ* [conditional tense] is intended here. [Regarding the root] *iṅ* in the sense of "studying": the prefix *adhi* signifies "superiority" (*uparibhāva*). And "superiority [in this context] consists in being preceded by a rule regarding recitation."

This is clear in the Bhāṣya on the *bhūvādi* sūtra. Regarding the statement "it is always preceded by *adhi*," this is a specific entry in the Dhātupāṭha. In the Bhāṣya on the *bhūvādi* sūtra, it is stated that in the case of *adhīte*, the root does not deviate from its association with the prefix (*upasarga*). Thus, in *adhīte*, [the suffix] is *sārvadhātuka* by the rule *sārvadhātukam apit*.
Because of the *ṅ* marker, there is a prohibition of *guṇa*; [instead], there is *savarṇa-dīrgha*. But before vowels beginning with *a*, there is *iyaṅ*. Thus he says: *adhīyāte*, *adhīyate*.
[In the middle voice: *adhīṣe*, *adhīyāthe*, *adhīdhve*; *adhīye*, *adhīvahe*, *adhīmahe*. (289) *gāṅ liṭi* | Pāṇini 1.2.49.
The intention is that [the term] *iṅ* is understood from the rule "ṭhiṅśca" (Pāṇini 1.2.1), as it is carried over [into this context].

Since the status of having the marker *ṅ* (*ṅtva*) would already be established by the principle of "as if original" (*sthānivadbhāva*), the explicit mention of the marker *ṅ* (*ṅtkiraṇa*) is for the purpose of ensuring that the form "iṇo gā luṅi" (Pāṇini 2.4.49) is not included under the rule "gāṅkuṭādibhyaḥ" (Pāṇini 1.2.1). This is the view of the Bhāṣya. Now, if [the marker *ṅ*] were applied...

It will be stated that in the case of *gāṅ*, when there is doubling (*dvitva*), the substitution of the *jaś* sounds (*jaśtva*) and the elision of *āl* (*āllopa*) result in the form *adhijage*. That is incorrect; because the prohibition of the *gāṅ* substitution applies "when there is doubling before a vowel" (*dvirvacane'ci*), doubling occurs prior to the *gāṅ* substitution. Consequently, if the *gāṅ* substitution were applied to the latter portion [of the reduplicated root] first, the undesired form *adhīge* would result. Therefore...

He says: "In the state of *l* (the substitution of *l* for *r*), or when [the substitution] is intended. Regarding this, according to the view of the *Vārttika*, the rule *dvirvacane'ci* does not apply prior to the substitution of *gāṅ* for *gam*, because there is no vowel (*ac*) that serves as the cause for reduplication. However, according to the view of the *Bhāṣya*, it is "when [the substitution] is intended."

The rule "dvirvacane'ci" (Pāṇini 1.1.59) certainly does not apply here, because it is not occasioned by a specific condition (*anaimitikatvāt*); this is the intended meaning. Regarding *adhijagire*: *adhijagiṣe*, *adhijagāthe*, *adhijagidhve*;
*adhijage*, *adhijagivahe*, *adhijagimahe*. In the *loṭ* (imperative): *adhītām*, *adhīyātām*, *adhīyatām*.

Having treated "adhīṣva," "adhīyāthām," and "adhīdhvam" as already established, he says "adhyayai. Therein, he demonstrates the grammatical process: "of the guṇa and the ay-ādeśa. This is because of the established conclusion of the rule "suṭ kāt pūrvaḥ," which holds that "the root is first joined with its suffix, and subsequently with the prefix."
This is the state of affairs. Thus, when *iṭ* is applied, *āṭ* is added, and *vṛddhi* occurs, we arrive at the form *adhi-i-ai*.

When *guṇa* is applied and replaced by *ay*, the result is *yaṇ*. Now, one might object: "Is there not also the position that 'the root is first joined with the prefix (*upasarga*), and afterwards with the suffix (*sādhana*)'? This view is indeed mentioned in the Bhāṣya on the rule *suṭ kātpūrvaḥ*.

When [the rule] "sthitaḥ" is established, and likewise when "adhi i ai" is established, one might suspect that after the substitution of the long vowel homogeneous with the preceding (pūrvasavarṇadīrgha), and then the application of the *guṇa* and *ayādeśa* substitutions, the form would become "adhayai";
anticipating this, he refutes it by stating "pūrvaṃ dhātuḥ" (the root first). This refers to the phrase "sādhanena" (by the instrument).

The meaning is "by that which indicates the agent" (kāraka); that is to say, by the suffix (pratyaya). Regarding the word *darśane*, the meaning is "in the opinion [of those who hold this view]. According to the position that "the root is first joined with the prefix (*upasarga*), and afterwards with the factor of action (*sādhana*)," because it applies earlier and is thus *antaraṅga* (internal), the rule *sārvadhātukārddhadhātukayoḥ* [applies].

The logical connection (*anvaya*) is that the *savarṇadīrgha* (long vowel of homogeneous quality), which would otherwise have applied by overriding the *guṇa*, does not take place. To the question "Why?", he says:

"Because of the technical indication (*nirdeśa*) in the rule *ṇeradhyayane vṛtam*. Otherwise, if the *lyuṭ* suffix were applied, and the substitution of *na* for *ṇa* had occurred, leaving the form *adhi-i-ana*, the *savarṇadīrgha* would first apply, and subsequently both *guṇa* and the *ay*-substitution would follow.

The sense is that the mention of "the two having been performed" (kṛtayoḥ) is by way of incidental discussion (*prasaṅga*). In reality, however, the view supported by the Bhāṣya is precisely that "first the verbal root is joined with its instrument (*sādhana*)," for the Bhāṣya states: "First the root [is joined] with a prefix;
this is not the core point. This has been explained in detail elsewhere. [The forms] *adhyayāvahai* and *adhyayāmahai*.

Regarding *laḍ-laḍha-adhyaita*: when *adhi-ā-ita* is established, the intention is that by the rule *āṭaśca*, there is vṛddhi, and then by *yaṇ*. When *adhi-i-ātām* is established, after vṛddhi due to *āṭ*, *yaṇ* would result in *adhyaitām*;
to this, he says: "Because it is subsequent, *iyaṅ* [occurs]. That is to say, because it is subsequent, *iyaṅ* replaces the vowel *i* even before *āṭ*.
The meaning is that the form is *adhyaiyata* [etc. from the root *āṭ* (to increase) with the substitution of *yaṇ*. Regarding *adhyaiyata*:

the substitution of *at* is applied by the rule *ātmanepadeṣvanataḥ*. Having taken for granted the forms *adhyaiyathāḥ*, *adhyaiyāthām*, and *adhyaidhvam*, he says—presupposing them as established—*adhyaiyi*, *adhyaiṣvahi*, and *adhyaimahi*. He now states the forms for the potential mood (*vidhiliṅ*): *adhyaiyeta adhyaiyeyātām adhyaiyeran* *adhyaiyethāḥ adhyaiyeyāthām adhyaiyedhvam* *adhyaiyeya adhyaiyevahi adhyaiyemahi* He says this regarding the potential mood (*vidhiliṅ*).
Regarding *adhīyīta*: when *adhi i ta* is present, with the addition of *sīyuṭ*, *suṭ*, and the elision of *s*, we have *adhi i īta*.

At this stage, the intention is that the vowel *i*—which has become part of the verbal root—undergoes the substitution *iyaṅ* by the rule *iṅśtipāḥ śap* (Pāṇini 3.1.78), and the long vowel *ī* results from the rule for lengthening similar vowels (*sivarṇadīrgha*).
Regarding *adhīyīyātām*: when *adhi i ātām* is present, with the addition of *sīyuṭ*, *suṭ*, and the elision of *s*, [we have *adhi i īyātām*].

When *i īyātām* is established, the intention is that the vowel *i*, having become part of the verbal root, undergoes the substitution *iyaṅ* by the rule *sivarṇadīrgha*. When *jha* is replaced by *ran*, and after the addition of *sīyuṭ* and the elision of the letters *sa* and *ya*, we have *adhi i ī ran*. Here, the vowel *i*, having become part of the verbal root, undergoes the substitution *iyaṅ* and the lengthening of the *si*-vowel (*sivarṇadīrgha*), resulting in *adhīyīran*; likewise, *adhīyīthāḥ*.

He says "adhīyīdhvam" (you all should study), taking it as already established that "adhīyīyāthām" (you two should study). When *dhvam* follows, with the addition of *sīyuṭ*, the elision of *s*, and the elision of *y*, the form stands as *adhi i ī dhvam*. The intention is that *iṅ* becomes *iyaṅ* and there is vowel lengthening (*sivarṇadīrgha*).
As for "adhīyīya": the *ṭhiṭ* suffix is added, followed by *sīyuṭ* and the elision of *s*, resulting in *adhi i īya*.

The intention is that when [the suffix] *iṅ* remains, there is the substitution of *iyaṅ* and the long vowel by the rule *sivarṇadīrgha*. [In the first person dual and plural of the imperfect, we have: *adhīyīvahi*, *adhīyīmahi*. Regarding the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), he says:
*adhyeṣīṣṭa*. With the addition of *sīyuṭ*, there is *guṇa*; then *yaṇ* and the change to *ṣ*. [Thus: *adhyeṣīyāstām*, *adhyeṣīran*; *adhyeṣīṣṭhāḥ*, *adhyeṣīyāsthām*.

[The forms] *adhyeṣīṭ*, *adhyeṣīṣṭhāḥ*, *adhyeṣīṣṭa*; [the middle voice forms] *adhyeṣīya*, *adhyeṣīvahi*, *adhyeṣīmahi*. In the *luṅ* [tense], when *adhi-ā-i-ta* is situated [after the root], [the rule applies]:
(290) *vibhāṣā luṅ-lṛṅoḥ* 2.4.50.

Regarding the rule *vibhāṣā luṅ-lṛṅoḥ*: he completes the remainder [of the statement]—namely, that *iṅ* may optionally become *gāṅ*. This is because the words from *iṅśca* and *gāṅ liṭi* are understood by way of anuvṛtti (carrying over). When the form *adhi-agās-ta* is established in the *sic* [suffix],...

(291) *gāṅ-kuṭādibhyo 'ñ-ṇid-ṅit* | 1.2.1 | From *gāṅ* and the roots beginning with *kuṭ*: *ñ* and *ṇ* are *ñṇ*; that which has these as its *it* (indicatory letters) is *ñṇit*. That which does not possess such [an *it*] is *añṇit*. *Gāṅ* and the roots beginning with *kuṭ* form a copulative compound (*dvandva*), from which the ablative case is derived. Thus, *gāṅ*.

It has been stated that because of the connection with the marker *ṅ*, there is no inclusion of the root *ṣṭhā* (as in the rule *ṣṭhivuklamvācamācaṃ kaṃścaṇo gā luṅi*). Nor is there an inclusion here of the root *gāṅ* (meaning "to go"), because in that case the marker *ṅ* has already served its purpose by bringing about the middle voice (*ātmanepada*). As for the *gāṅ* that is a substitute for *iṅ* (the root "to study"), its marker *ṅ* does not serve to bring about the middle voice.

The purpose [of the rule] is already fulfilled, since that is established by the status of being *sthānivadbhāva* alone. Thus he says: "due to the substitution of *gāṅ*. And so, when there is the *ṅ* of *sic*, [we have] *āhi*:
(292) *ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali* 6.4.66.

*Ghumasāthā*: This is a reference to the root *ṣo* (meaning "to finish") after its vowel has been changed to *u*. [The term *ghu* consists of] *ghu*, *mā*, *sthā*, *gā*, *pā*, and *jahāti*; the genitive case here follows from their being a *dvandva* compound. The governing rule *ārddhadhātuke* ("before an *ārddhadhātuka* suffix") is in force.

From the rule *āto lopa iṭi ca* ("there is elision of *ā* before an *ārddhadhātuka* suffix beginning with *iṭ*"), the word *ātaḥ* is understood; and from the rule *īdyati* ("*ī* is substituted for the final vowel of roots ending in *ā* before the suffix *yat*"), the word *īt* is understood.
The words *anudāttopadeśa* from [Pāṇini 6.4.37] and *kṅiti* from [Pāṇini 1.1.5] are understood to carry over.

Thus he says, "of these," and so forth. Regarding *adhyagīṣṭa*: in the sequence *adhi-a-gā-s-ta*, the vowel *ā* becomes *ī*, followed by *yaṇ*-sandhi; then the *s* of *sic* becomes *ṣ*, and the *t* becomes *ṭ* by [Pāṇini 8.4.41], resulting in *adhyagīṣṭa*. This is according to [Pāṇini 2.4.77]: *gātisthāghupābhūbhyo 'ṅ*.
There is elision of the suffix *ti*, because there is no *parasmaipada* [ending]. [The forms are: *adhyagīṣātām*, *adhyagīṣata*;

*adhyagīṣṭhāḥ*, *adhyagīḍhvam*; *adhyagīṣi*, *adhyagīṣvahi*, *adhyagīṣmahi*. Regarding the alternative view where *gāṅ* is substituted, he says: *adhyaiṣṭa*. When the form *adhi-ā-i-s-ta* has been established, [the following applies] to the vowel *i*.
The intention is that [the form] *adhyaiṣata* arises through the substitution of *āṭ*, vṛddhi, *yaṇ*, and the changes to *ṣatva* and *ṣṭutva*.
[The forms] *adhyaiṣātām*, *adhyaiṣata*; *adhyaiṣṭhāḥ*, *adhyaiṣāthām*, *adhyaiḍhvam*—[in the latter], there is the elision of *s* by the rule *dhi ca*.
[The forms] *adhyaiṣi*, *adhyaiṣvahi*, *adhyaiṣmahi*. For the *lṛṅ* (conditional), it is *adhyagīṣyata*, etc., according to the rule *vibhāṣā*.

The intention is as follows: in the case of the *luṅ* and *lṛṅ* [suffixes], there is the substitution of *gāṅ* by the rule *gāṅ liṭi*; then, when *sya* follows, *iṅ* is substituted for it by the rule *gāṅ-kuṭādibhyaḥ*; then *ī* is substituted by the rule *ghu-mā-sthā-gā-pā-jahāti-sā-hā-līy-ati-dīy-ati-dṛś-yati-pibatīnām ī ca*; then *aṭ* is prefixed; then *yaṇ* [sandhi] occurs; and finally, the *ṣatva* (change to *ṣ*) takes place. Thus we have *adhyagīṣyetām*, and so forth.
Regarding the alternative where there is no substitution of *gāṅ*, he says: *adhyaiṣyata*, *adhyaiṣyetām*, and so forth. [The root] *iṅ* is used in the sense of "remembering."
"This too" means that this verbal root (*dhātu*) also always has *adhi* as its prefix, just like the root *iṅ*. Now,
while it is appropriate for *iṅ* to be invariably preceded by *adhi*— given the statement in the Dhātupāṭha,
"it is always preceded by *adhi*," and the commentary on the *bhūvādi* sūtra— it is not so for this [other] one.

To the question, "What is the proof for this being so?", he says: *adhīgartha* (Pāṇini 2.3.52). For in that rule, by the term *adhīgartha*, the giver who has the sense of remembering (*smaraṇa*) is intended. Even though the root *iṅ* lacks the prefix *adhi*, since it has the sense of remembering, the mere expression *ig-artha* is sufficient to include any root having the sense of remembering; thus, the word *adhi-* [is used] there.

It would be redundant. Therefore, the meaning is that it is understood that this root *i* is always preceded by the prefix *adhi* when it has the sense of "remembering. Regarding the phrase *iṇvadikaḥ*: the suffix *vati* is added to a word ending in the genitive case. The meaning is that whatever grammatical operation applies to the root *iṇ*—such as "the substitution of *yaṇ* for *iṇ*" (Pāṇini 6.1.77)—that same operation applies to *ik*. Thus, one says *adhyeti* and *adhīta*.

Treating it as already established, he says: "they study" (*adhiyanti*). This is an exception to *iyaṅ* when there is the substitution of the final vowel (*antādeśa*). The intention is that [the rule] "for *iṇ*, *yaṇ*" applies. [The forms are: *adhyeṣi*, *adhīthaḥ*, *adhītha*; *adhyemi*, *adhīvaḥ*, *adhīmaḥ*. [In the perfect tense: *adhīyāya*.
But in the case of *atus*, after reduplication has occurred, when we have the state *adhi i i atus*, [the rule] "for *iṇ*, *yaṇ*" applies.

When *yaṇ* substitution occurs for the second *i*, and *dīrgha iṇaḥ kiti* applies to the first *i*, followed by *savarṇadīrgha*, we have: *adhīyatuḥ*, *adhīyuḥ*; *adhīyayitha* (or *adhīyetha*), *adhīyathuḥ*, *adhīya*;
*adhīyāya*, *adhīyaya*, *adhīyiva*, *adhīyima*; *adhyetā*; *adhyeṣyati*; *adhyetu*.
Having studied [the past participle] *adhīta*, [one says] *adhītām* and *adhiyantu*; [one says] *adhīhi*—[the imperative forms] *adhītāt*, *adhītam*, and *adhīta*;

[the first person optative forms] *adhyayāni*, *adhyayāva*, and *adhyayāma*; [the imperfect forms] *adhyait*, *adhyaitām*, and *adhyāyan*; [the second person imperfect forms] *adhyaiḥ*, *adhyaitam*, and *adhyaita*;
[and the first person imperfect forms] *adhyāyam*, *adhyāva*, and *adhyaima*. Thus, taking these as established.
The *Lug-vṛtti* says: "He studied" (*adhyagāt*). Because [the root] belongs to the *iṇ*-class, by the rule "for *iṇ*, *gā* is substituted in the *luṅ* tense," there is the substitution of *gā*.

Since the *sic* suffix is elided by the rule "in the case of *gā*, *sthā*, etc.," the change to *ī* (as prescribed by the rule "for *ghu*, *mā*, *sthā*, etc. does not occur. [Thus we have] *adhyagātām*, *adhyagām*, *adhyagāva*. [In the conditional: *adhyaiṣyat*. "Some, however... refers to the following.

The meaning is that, within the governing rule (adhikāra) "ṭhārddhadhātuke," this vārttika reading is seen in the Bhāṣya on the sūtra "ṭhiṇo gā luṅi"; therefore, only those operations mentioned under that governing rule are present [in the current context]. Thus, according to that view, there is no *yaṇ* substitution, because the rule is "ṭhiṇo yaṇ."

The meaning is that there is no extended application (atideśa) because [the rule] does not reside within the governing heading (adhikāra) for *ārdhadhātuka* suffixes. Consequently, in forms such as *adhīyantī*, the substitution of *iyaṅ* for the final *jha* and the lengthening by the rule *sivarṇadīrgha* should be inferred accordingly. In the phrase *rāghavayoradhīyan*, the genitive case is used according to the rule *adhīgarthakarmaṇi*; the meaning is "remembering the two Rāghavas. This is derived from the root *iṅ* preceded by the prefix *adhi*, in the present tense (*laṭ*).

In the case of the *śatṛ* suffix, when there is the elision (*luk*) of *śap*, the *ikāra* undergoes *iyaṅ* substitution; then, through the rule of lengthening a vowel before a *si*-varṇa, the form *adhīyan* is derived from the *śatṛ*-stem when the nominative singular (*su*) is produced. Regarding the root *vī* (to go), according to the view of the Bhāṣya on the rule *ṭherjyaghañapoḥ*, it has no usage in the *ārdhadhātuka* domain; this is stated in the *Śabdenduśekhara*.

[The form] *sthitam* [is established]. Regarding *viyanti*: because it consists of a single vowel (*ekāctvāt*), there is no substitution of *yaṇ*; rather, *iyaṅ* occurs—this is the intended meaning. In the case of the imperative (*loṭ*), having taken for granted that *vetu*, *vītāt*, *vītām*, and *viyantu* are established, he says *vīhi*. Because the suffix *hi* is not marked with *p* (*apitvena*), it is marked with *ṅ*; therefore, by the rule "there is no guna" (*ṅtvānna guṇaḥ*), there is no guna-substitution—this is the intended meaning. [The forms are: *vītāt*, *vītam*, *vīta*, and *vayāni*.

*vayāva*, *vayāma*. Regarding *laḍaḷaha*—it is explained as *avediti* (he knew), *aviyanniti* (he was knowing), and *vī-anniti* (having known). The point is that when *vī-anniti* is established, since it is subsequent, the substitution *iyaṅ* is applied before the augment *aṭ*, after which the augment *iṭ* is applied. He states another opinion: "when the augment *aṭ* exists. According to the view that *aṭ* is added in the state of the suffix *lā*, there is *iyaṅ*.

The meaning is that some say that [the substitution of] *yaṇ* occurs by setting aside [the augment *aṭ*], because [the base] consists of more than one vowel (*anekāctvāt*). The phrase "some" indicates a lack of conviction (or dissatisfaction) on the part of the author. The reason for this is as follows: even if *aṭ* has been applied, since *aṭ* is considered "unestablished" (*asiddha*) when the substitution of *yaṇ* is to be performed—due to its being an *ābhīya* element—the base lacks the status of having more than one vowel; consequently, there would be no *yaṇ*, and thus the substitution of *iy* is appropriate.

Thus ends the detailed discussion in the *Śabdenduśekhara*. Regarding the word "atra" (here): the intention is that when the *savarṇadīrgha* (vowel-lengthening) rule applies to *vī-ī*, the form is cited as *vī* in the sense of "motion" (*gati*). As for *īyāt*: this form is identical whether it is the potential mood (*vidhiliṅ*) or the benedictive mood (*āśīrliṅ*). The elision of *s* occurs by the rule *skoḥ*. Among these, in the case of the potential mood (*vidhiliṅ*):

Regarding "īyātām" and so forth, the distinction is that in the benedictive (āśīrliṅ) it becomes "īyāstām" and so on. As for "aiṣīt," there is a vṛddhi [strengthening] due to the suffix *sic*. Regarding the root *yā* in the sense of "reaching" (*prāpaṇe*), one might ask: "How can *yāti* mean 'he goes'? To this he says: "In this context, reaching is going. The meaning of the causative suffix (*ṇic*) is not intended here; such is the intention.
*prāṇiyātīti*: the substitution of *ṇ* [for *n*] occurs by the rule *ṇer gade*. [Forms: *yayau*, *yātā*, *yāsyati*, *yātu*, *ayāt*, *ayātām*. (293) *laṅḥ śākaṭāyanasyaiva* 3.4.111.

According to Śākaṭāyana alone, [the substitution of] *jus* occurs for *jhi*. The words "for *jhi*" (*ṭhjherjusi*) and "from that which ends in long *ā*" (*ṭhāta*) are understood as being carried over [from previous rules].
Thus he says: "from that which ends in long *ā*" (*ādantāt*). Regarding "*jusve*" (in the case of *jus*), the intention is that the option is obtained because of the mention of Śākaṭāyana.

However, the restrictive particle *eva* is for the sake of subsequent rules, such as "also after the periphrastic perfect" (*liṭ ca*) and "after the optative in the sense of benediction" (*liṅaśiṣī*), according to the Bhāṣya.

This is clear. Furthermore, one should not suspect that the optional use of *jus* would apply even in the case of *yāntu* due to the extended application (*atideśa*) of the rule "the *loṭ* [ending] is like the *laṅ*";

for this is already established by the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the word "hi" from the rule "nityaṃ ṅtiḥ," since the mention of *laṅ* in the present rule is intended to prevent its application by taking it as an extended application of the status of being like *laṅ*.

This is also clear in the Bhāṣya. *Ayān*: this is the form when the *jus* substitute does not occur. *Ayāsīt*. The root *snā* is taught with an initial *ṣ*; the *ṇ* is indicated by the rule for *ṣṭuan* (the substitution of *ṇ* for *s*).
*Snāti*. *Snāyāt* or *sneyāt*. The root *pā* in the sense of "protecting" [is mentioned] in the sūtra *ṭher liṅi* and in the sūtra *gāti-sthā-*.
Because only the root *pibati* is included [in the rule], there is no substitution of *et* nor elision of *s*. Thus he says:

*pāyāstām* and *apāsīt*. Regarding the root *dāp* in the sense of "cutting," since it lacks the quality of being *ghu*, one considers the optionality of the substitution of *ṇ* by the rule *śeṣe vibhāṣā*, and thus he says: *praṇidāti* and *pranidāti*.

Because of the absence [of the suffix] after the root *ghu*, the *liṅ* (optative) is used for the benediction (*āśīḥ*), and the *luṅ* (aorist) is elided; thinking that *ci* does not apply here, he says "adāyāstām" and "adāsīt. Regarding the root *khyā* (to tell): the phrase "only within the domain of *sārvadhātuka*"—the word *mātra* is used for restriction—means that the usage of this root *khyā* occurs only with *sārvadhātuka* suffixes, and not otherwise.

The meaning is "before an *ardhadhātuka* suffix. To the question "Why?", he says: "because of the commonality of place (*saṣṭhānatva*). In the rule *cakṣiṅ khyāñ*, it should have been stated that *khyāñ* occurs in place of *khyā*.
Having stated that the letter *y* should be prescribed for this letter *ś* under the governing heading *pūrvatrāsiddham*, [the author] stated the purpose.

Having begun with the rule "vuñ is prescribed after words meaning 'well-known'," the *Vārttika* states: "The status of being a *saṣṭhāna* (a substitute for the genitive) does not apply to *namaḥ khyātre*.

Therein, the *Bhāṣya* explains that by supplying the negative particle *nañ*, the phrase "namaḥ khyātre" does not possess the status of a *saṣṭhāna*. This *Vārttika* and this *Bhāṣya* [refer] to this root *khyā*.
The meaning is that this serves as the *jñāpaka* (indicative evidence) for the rule that usage occurs only in the context of *sārvadhātuka* suffixes. In that regard, he explains the term *sa-sthāna*:
"the *jihvāmūlīya* is *sa-sthāna*. The intention is that this is according to the convention of the ancient teachers (*prācīnācārya*).
"That [is] not [used]" means that the *jihvāmūlīya* is not used in the expression *namaḥ khyātre*.

The meaning is that "it exists" (bhavati) serves as the purpose for the rule prescribing *khśyādi* for the substitute *khyāñ*, and also for the rule prescribing *yatva* for the letter *ś*. Regarding the phrase "in the case of *khśyādi*," this is also an elliptical expression (*upalakṣaṇa*) for the rule prescribing *yatva*. This is because the *yatva* [substitution] of the *ś* resulting from the sense of "able" (*śak*) is considered *asiddha*.
The intention of the Bhāṣya and the Vārttika is that the *visarjanīya* is desired [by the rule] "ṭh-śarpare visarjanīyaḥ," whereas the *jihvāmūlīya* is not desired. However,
if the root *khyā* is present even in the *ardhadhātuka* state, then in the word *khyātṛ*, ending in *-tṛ*:

Since the letter *y* is not the substitute for *ś*, it does not possess the status of being "asiddha" (non-existent for the purposes of rule application); consequently, the rule *ṭhśarpare visarjanīyaḥ* does not apply, and the substitution of the jihvāmūlīya for *k* or *p* would be unavoidable.
Therefore, the root *khyā* would never be employed anywhere within an *ardhadhātuka* suffix.

The meaning is that it is understood because an indicator (jñāpaka) depends upon a general rule. Regarding the phrase "of [the root] preceded by *sam*," the intention is that this applies even before a sārvadhātuka suffix. In this matter, the commentary itself is the only refuge. And thus, the result is that forms such as *saṅkhyati* do not exist. As for words such as *saṅkhyā* and so forth...

It should be understood that this refers to the substitute *khyāñ*. Regarding the root *mā* in the sense of "measuring" (*māne*), the intended meaning is that "measure" (*māna*) signifies limitation (*parimiti*).

Thus he says: "it is intransitive" (*akarmaka*). An example is: *māti ghṛtaṃ pātre'smin* ("the ghee measures [fits] in this vessel"). The meaning is that it becomes limited; that is to say, it becomes contained.

In this regard, he shows the agreement with the usage of the learned (*śiṣṭa*): "They did not fit within his body" (*tano mamustatra*). In the *Māghakāvya*, [it says]: "The joys arising from the arrival (*abhyāgama*)—that is, the coming (*āgamana*)—of the ascetic (*tapodhana*), Nārada, did not fit within the body of the enemy of Kaiṭabha. Thus, it refers to the joys produced by the arrival of the ascetic Nārada.

The satisfactions of the enemy of Kaiṭabha—that is, of Śrī Kṛṣṇa—did not fit within his body; they were not limited, meaning they could not be contained due to their excess. "In another sense" means "in the sense of measurement. "The belly" refers to that which measures [the contents].
In the *Naiṣadhacarita*, it says: "Does some curious person measure Damayantī’s belly with his fist?
This means: does some curious person measure (*parimāti*) the belly (*udara*) of Damayantī—that is, of Umāyanti—with his fist? Or does he grasp it? It is not that he grasps it.
The intention is that [the substitution of *ṇ*] occurs when the root begins with a consonant other than *k* or *kh*, according to the Bhāṣya.

Thus, considering that there is an option for the substitution of *ṇ* by the rule "optionally when the suffix begins with a letter other than *k* or *kh* in the remaining cases," he says: *praṇimāti* or *pranimāti*. [Perfect: *mamau*;
[First person singular perfect: *mamitha* or *mamātha*; [First person plural perfect: *mamima*; [Imperative: *māta*; [Future: *māsyati*; [Infinitive: *mātu*.
*amāt*, *amāsīt*, *amāsyat*. The root √*vac* means "to speak" and is *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment). Regarding the form *ayamanti*:

the meaning is that the third person plural (*prathamapuruṣabahuvacana*) does not exist in the present tense (*laṭ*). As for the phrase "when followed by a plural [suffix]": the ellipsis is "it is not employed. According to this view, the third person plural does not exist across all three persons.

Regarding the word *jhipara*: the phrase "it is not employed" (*na prayujyate*) is the ellipsis (*śeṣaḥ*). On this view, the meaning is that even in the case of the *liṭ* and other suffixes, the third person plural does not exist. In that context, for the *liṭ*, when it is not followed by a *kit* suffix, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to the rule *liṭaḷbhyāsasya*; thus, *uvāca*. But when it is followed by a *kit* suffix, [the rule] *vacisvapi-* applies.

There is *saṃprasāraṇa* (vowel substitution). Perfect: *ūcatuḥ*. Periphrastic perfect: *uvacitha*—or *uvaktha*. First person plural: *ūcima*. Future: *vaktā*, *vakṣyati*. Conjunctive participle: *vaktvā*. Aorist: *avak*. Optative (*vidhiliṅ*): *vacyāt*. Having considered that there is *saṃprasāraṇa* by the rule "vicisvapī" for the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), he says: *ucyāt*. Aorist (*luṅ*): *avocat*. This is by the rule "isyativaktī".
The meaning is that *u* is the augment for *cli* (the aorist suffix). Regarding the root *vid*, it means "to know.

Since it is not included among the roots marked as *aniṭ* (those lacking an *iṭ* augment) in the context of the *luṅ* (aorist) *vikaraṇa*, this [root] takes the *seṭ* (augmented with *iṭ*) suffix. (Pāṇini 3.4.83: *vido liṭo vā* ("After the root *vid*, there is optionally [the substitution of *kvasu*] for the *liṭ* [perfect]").

"Or [the substitutes occur] for *laṭ* after *vid*. The sūtra beginning with "ṭhparasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatu... is understood here. "*Vida*" is in the ablative case; thus he says: "for *vid* in *laṭ*. However, these substitutes do not apply to *vindati* and *vidyati* because they are separated by *śa* and *śyan*. Regarding "and so forth": *vidanti*, *vetsi*, *vitthaḥ*.

*vittha*, *vedmi*, *vidvaḥ*, *vidmaḥ*, *vividatuḥ*, *vividuḥ*, *viveditha*, *vividathuḥ*, *vivida*, *viveda*, *vividiva*, *vividima*. Regarding the alternative form with the suffix *ām*: the connection is that there is no *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*). To the question "Why?", he says: "Because of the irregular derivation (*nipātana*) ending in the vowel *a*."
In the sūtra *ṭhuṣavide*, the meaning is that the form *videt* with a final vowel *a* is an irregularly formed (nipātita) base in conjunction with the suffix *ām*.

[The rule] *ato lopaḥ* applies to this *ām*; because of its status as a *sthānivadbhāva*, there is no guna substitution for the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*). Thus, the sense is [that the form is established].
One should also understand that *veditā* and *vediṣyati* are likewise derived.

(295) *vidāṅkurvantv-ity-anyatarasyām* |3|1|41|. The form *vidāṅkurvantu* may optionally [be used]. This sūtra follows the rule *kṛñ cānuprayujyate liṭi* ("and the root *kṛ* is employed subsequently when the periphrastic perfect suffix *liṭ* occurs"). The word *iti* indicates a manner; that is to say, it refers to forms of this kind.
The meaning is that [the action] is to be understood through its various forms (*vaikalpyena*). Regarding *veter*:

the meaning is that the suffix *ām* is prescribed by way of a grammatical irregularity (*nipātana*) after the root *vid* (from which the *vikaraṇa* suffix is elided) when followed by the imperative (*loṭ*). Regarding "ending in the imperative": after the root *vid* ending in *ām*, there is the employment (*anuprayoga*) of the roots *na*, *kṛ*, and *dhā* in the imperative.

The meaning is "it is caused to fall. Now, one might object: since the sūtra specifies only the third person plural of the imperative (*loṭ*) in the form *vidāṅkurvantu*, how can there be a general application of the imperative ending? To this, he says: "person," etc.—namely, *kurvantu*.
The meaning is that neither the third person nor the plural number is intended to be significant;

rather, the intention is that their utterance is merely incidental. Regarding the phrase "from the word *iti*," the meaning is that this particle, which expresses a manner or form, follows the usage found in common worldly speech.

(296) *tanādikṛñbhya uḥ* | Pāṇini 3.1.79. "After the roots beginning with *tan* and after *kṛ*, the suffix *u* [is applied]. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to *śap*. By this, it is indicated that its application occurs only in the domain of *śap*. [This is understood] from the rule *sārvadhātuke yaK* [Pāṇini 3.1.67].

The intention is that [the suffix] *śa* is applied because of the inclusion of the term "possessing a meaningful root" (*sāravadhātuka*) and the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the word "in the sense of the agent" (*kartari*) from the rule *ṭhkartari śa*. Regarding the phrase "by that": since the operations of a class (*gaṇakārya*) are not invariably obligatory (*anityatā*), the operation belonging to the *ad*-class (*adādigaṇakārya*), namely the elision of *śap*, does not occur in the case of *śvas*. However, in reality...

They say that because the mention of the root *kṛ* has been rejected in this Bhāṣya, there is no such implied teaching (jñāpana), and thus the form *viśvaset* is indeed incoherent [as an example of that teaching]. However, regarding *viśvasta*, they say that the augment *iṭ* does not occur because the rule for augments (*āgamaśāstra*) is not invariably obligatory (*anitya*).

"Let him know" (*vidāṃ karotu*). Here, from the root *vid* in the imperative (*loṭ*), after the imperative suffix has been elided, there is the subsequent application (*anuprayoga*) of the root *kṛ* ending in the imperative. In that context, when the imperative suffix *tiP* is present, by the rule "the substitution of *u* for *ṭhi*" (*ṭheruḥ*), the affix *śap* is superseded;
then, with the addition of the affix *u*, the *ṛ*-vowel undergoes *guṇa*, followed by the replacement of *ra* (*raparatva*), and the *u*-vowel is caused by the suffix *tiP*.

[The substitute] *tātaṅ* [is introduced]. However, when there is *guṇa* for the *ṛ*-vowel, because *tātaṅ* has the marker *ṅ*, there is no *guṇa* for the *u*-vowel; thus, the form *vidāṅkarotu* is established. (297) *ata utsārvadhātuke* 6.4.110.

The phrase "ending in the suffix *ut*" [is used] because of the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the rule "and after [a vowel] ending in *u*, when a suffix follows" (*utaśca pratyayāt*). Having raised the objection that once the substitution of *u* for the vowel *a* has been made, the *guṇa* substitution of the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*) might apply, he says: "when followed by *t*. This is clear in the *Bhāṣya* on the *sthānivat* sūtra.
"Let them know" (*vidāṅkurutām*); it should also be understood that "let them know" (*vidāṅkurvantu*) is likewise [formed].

Due to the prohibition "not before *bhakurchurām*," there is no lengthening by the rule "before a consonant" (*hali ca*). Regarding the statement "there is elision of *hi*" (*her luk*), one might ask:
"In that case, since there is an absence of a *sārvadhātuka* suffix, how can the substitution of *u* (*utvam*) occur? To this, he says: "Because it is *ābhīya*."
"vidāṃkurviti" (let him know). [The forms] "vidāṃkurutāt," "vidāṃkurutam," and "vidāṃkuruta" [are derived similarly].
Regarding "vidāṃkaravāṇi": because the augment *āṭ* is *pit*, it lacks the marker *ṅ*; thus, by the rule "there is guna for *u* followed by *kari*," there is guna.
[The forms] "vidāṃkaravāva" and "vidāṃkaravāma" [follow the same pattern]. For the *laṅ* [mood], [the form is] "avedīt."
Having stated that *sip* is elided by the rule *halṅyādi*, he states a specific exception:

(298) *daśca* |7|2|75|. [The word] *daḥ* [is used]. The phrase "after a root, *ru* is optionally [substituted] for *sip*" (*sipi dhāto rurvā*) is understood [as a governing rule]. The term *daḥ* is in the genitive case.

The *dhātu* (verbal root) is qualified [by the preceding rule]. This is a case of *tadantavidhi* (application of a rule to that which ends with the specified element). The term *padasya* (of a word) is understood as the governing heading (*adhikṛta*). Thus it says: "of a word ending in *d* which is a verbal root. By the rule *alo'ntyasya*, it should be understood that the final [letter] is affected. Regarding *avedi*: after the elision of *sip* by the rule *halṅyābbhyo dīrghāt...* etc., there is an optional substitution of *ru* for the letter *d*. [Thus we have] *avitaṃ*.
*ava* (protect); *avedam*, *avidva*, *avidma* (I, we two, we knew/protected). [Optative: *vidyāt*, *vidyātām*, *vidyāḥ*;
*vidyāt*, *vidyāstām*, *vidyāsuḥ*. [Aorist: *avedīt*, *avediṣṭām*, *avediṣyat*.
Regarding *as* in the sense of "being" (*bhū*): becoming is *bhūḥ*; the meaning is "existence. [Present indicative: *asti*. Even though there is *c*-substitution for *s*.
It becomes *sakāra* alone, and not *takāra*, due to the difference in effort (*prayatna*) caused by its being a weak breath (*alpaprāṇa*).
(299) *śnasorallopaḥ* | Pāṇini 6.4.111.
[The rule] *śnasorallopaḥ*: the word *aditi* is a term with its genitive case ending elided. *śna-as*.

This is the genitive dual from the compound of these two [words]. The single-substitute form (*pararūpa*) occurs because they belong to the *śakandhu*-class. In the term *śna*, there is a reference to a portion of the *śnam* suffix. From the rule "ata utsārvadhātuke," the word *sārvadhātuke* is understood to follow; and from the rule "gāmādane," the word *kṅti* is understood. Thus he says: "of *śna*, etc."
(300) *asterbhūḥ* |2|4|52|. The meaning is that the substitution of *bhū* occurs for the root *as* when an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix follows. When *as* and *hi* remain [in the form *as hi*]—

(301) *dhvasoreddhāvabhyāsalopaśca* | Pāṇini 6.4.19. The rule *dhvasoreddhau* [is explained as follows]: *ghus* and *as* form a *dvandva* compound. The word division is *et-hau*. Now, when *as* + *hi* is situated, would not the substitution of *dhi* for *hi*—by the rule *hujhalbhyo herdhiḥ*—apply because it is subsequent? [No, for] it is superseded.

[Objection: Since the rule *dhvasoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.4.119) applies later, it subverts [the application of] *etva* (the substitution of *e* for *s*) by the rule *sasajuṣo ruḥ*; and since there is no longer a *hal* following the *hu*, how can the substitution of *dhi* occur? To this, he says: "By virtue of being *ābhīya*. Thus, when *a e dhī* is established, he says: "By the rule *śnasoḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.108). [Objection: But in the benedictive (*āśis*), when *as hi* is established, [the substitute] *tātaṅ* [should apply].

Since the substitution of *e* (etva) would apply by virtue of its being subsequent (*paratva*), having set aside [the substitution of *tāt*], he says: "In the case of *tāt*, there is no *e*-substitution.

Why? To this he says: "By the subsequent [rule]. But surely, once *tāt* has been applied, because of its status as a *sthānivadbhāva*, why does the *e*-substitution prescribed by the rule *dhvasor eḥ* not occur when that [suffix] follows? To this he says:

Regarding the phrase *sakṛdgatau*: "once" (*sakṛt*) means "one time"; "in application" (*gatau*) means "when [two rules] have come into operation"; and "in case of conflict" (*vipratiṣedhe*) means "when there is a contradiction. Its meaning is that whatever is once sublated remains sublated and does not apply again. He states a specific rule for the *laṅ* tense with the suffix *tip*: *astisicaḥ*. When the *ik* vowel is elided and *āṭ* is applied...

The meaning is that the augment *īṭ* is applied by the rule "vṛddhau ṭhastisicaḥ. Now, one might object: since the suffixes beginning with *ta* are *ṅit*, the elision of the *a* of *śna* (by the rule "śnasor al") would occur first because it is subsequent [to the augment *āṭ*]; consequently, the root would no longer begin with a vowel (*ajādi*), so how could the augment *āṭ* apply? To this, he replies: "Because the elision of the *a* of *śna* and *as* is *abhīya* (non-stable)."

"Let it be so. In this case, once the augment *āṭ* has been applied, the letter *t* is used as a *tapara* (specifying the duration) in the rule "the elision of the *a* of *śn* and *as*" (*śnasorallopaḥ*) for the purpose of preventing its subsequent elision.

However, in reality, since *āṭ* is considered *asiddha* (non-existent) by virtue of being an *ābhīya* (belonging to the *ārdhadhātuka* category), the elision does not occur; thus, [the *tapara* marker is unnecessary] in the rule "the elision of the *a* of *śn* and *as*."
It is clear in the Bhāṣya that the inclusion of the long vowel *ā* (taparakaraṇa) is purposeless. Regarding the forms *āsann* [imperfect]:
*āsīḥ*, *āstam*, *āsta*, *āsam*, *āsva*, *āsma*. Regarding the optative (*vidhiliṅ*), he says: *syāt*; *syātām*, *syuḥ*, and so forth.
Regarding the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), considering that there is a substitution of *bhū* because it is an *ārddhadhātuka* suffix, he says:

[He says] "bhūyāt. Regarding [the form] "abhūt," however, he states it while considering that the *sic* suffix is elided by the rule *gāti-sthā-*, after the root has undergone the change to *bhū* in the *luṅ* tense with the *isic* affix. In that context, having raised the doubt regarding the augment *īṭ* by the rule *astisico 'pṛkte*, he says: "of *sic* and *as*" (*sico 'steśca*). Here, since the root *as* is not heard because of its change to *bhū*, there is no *īṭ*.
The suffix *bhāva* [is applied].
(302) *upasargaprādurbhyāmastiryacparaḥ* | Pāṇini 8.3.87. [The rule] *upasargaprādurbhyām*: *upasarga* and *prāduḥ*—this is a *dvandva* compound of these two.

The phrase *iṇkoḥ* is the governing rule (*adhikṛta*). Therein, *iṇ* is connected with the prefix (*upasarga*), and not with *pra* or *ud*, because it is impossible for the *s* of the root *as* following those [prefixes] to be preceded by *iṇ*. Furthermore, it is not connected with *ku* either, due to impossibility. In the term *asteḥ*, the nominative case is used in the sense of the genitive. [This is illustrated by the rule: *saheḥ sāḍaḥ saḥ*.

Therefore, the word *saḥ* (that) in the genitive case (*ṣaṣṭhyanta*) is understood from the previous rule, and *mūrdhanyaḥ* (cerebral) is the governing topic (*adhikṛta*). *Ya-cau* is a *dvandva* compound of *ya* and *ac*. The analysis (*vigraha*) is "that after which *ya* and *ac* follow. Thus, it is understood as "when *ya* and *ac* follow. He states this with the words: "by the prefix" (*upasargeṇa*). That is, [the *iṇ*] situated in a prefix (*upasarga*).

This is the meaning. Regarding the word *parasya* (of the following): this is an adjective qualifying the *s* of the root *as*, not the root *as* itself; therefore, in the case of *prādurāsīt*, there is no substitution of *ṣ*. He gives examples when followed by the letter *y*: *niṣyāt* and *prāduṣṣyāt*. *Prāduḥ* is an indeclinable ending in *s*. When there is the substitution of *ṣ* for that *s*, [the rule applies] to the preceding [element].

The *s* becomes *ṣ* by virtue of the rule for *ṣṭu*. However, if it were to end in *ṣ*, the mention of *ṛt* in the rule *ṭhprādurbhyām* would be untenable. He provides examples where it is followed by a vowel: *niṣanti* and *prāduṣṣanti*. Regarding the root *mṛjūṣ* in the sense of "cleansing," its designation as *ūdita* is for the purpose of optional *iṭ*.

The *ṣit* designation [of the suffix] after roots such as *ṣidh* and *bhid* is for the sake of [the application of] *ṅīp*. In reality, however, since the formation is already established by the inclusion of the word *mṛj* in the *bhidādi* group, they say that the assignment of the *ṣit* designation here is not of Vedic origin (*anārṣa*).
(303) *mṛjer vṛddhiḥ* | Pāṇini 7.2.114.

Regarding the rule *mṛjervṛddhiḥ*: by the technical rule (*paribhāṣā*) *ṭhiko guṇavṛddhī*, the term *ika* is supplied. In the expression *mṛjeḥ*, the genitive case denotes a part-whole relationship (*avayava-ṣaṣṭhī*). Thus he says: "In place of the *ik* [vowel] of the root *mṛj*, there shall be *vṛddhi*. With the technical rule *dhātoḥ svarūpagrahaṇe tatpratyaye kāryavijñānam* in mind, he says: [the operation applies to the suffix following that root].

"When a suffix following a root [is applied]" means when a suffix prescribed after a root is present. By this, there is no *vṛddhi* in the case of *parimṛḍbhyām*; such is the intention. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to *guṇa*.

It is desired [that the rule applies] before suffixes marked with *k* or *ṅ*, and before those beginning with a vowel other than *i*. The remainder [of the rule] is "there is *vṛddhi* for the root *mṛj*" (Pāṇini 7.2.114). [And the general rule is] "the *guṇa* and *vṛddhi* substitutions apply to *ik*" (Pāṇini 1.1.3).

This is stated in the Sūtra-bhāṣya: "vraśca-ṣa. When *mṛj* followed by *ti* is established, the vowel *ṛ* undergoes vṛddhi, which is then replaced by *ra*; the *ja* undergoes the substitution of *ṣ* according to the rule *vraśca-ṣa*; and the *ta* becomes *ṭa* by the rule *ṣṭunā ṣṭu*.
Thus, the form is *mārṣṭi*. As for *mṛṣṭa*, because of the marker *ṅ*, there is neither vṛddhi nor [the substitution of *ṣ*].

The sense is that it is a *guṇa* [substitution]. Regarding "they cleanse" (*mṛjanti*), they polish (*mārjanti*); the sense is that there is an option for *vṛddhi* by the rule "ṭkṅtyijādau. [The forms are: *mārṣi*, *mṛṣṭhaḥ*, *mṛṣṭha*; *mārjmi*, *mṛjvaḥ*, *mṛjmaḥ*. Regarding *mamārja*: in the case of the *ṇal* suffix, by the rule "vṛddhi for *mṛj*" (*mṛjervṛddhiḥ*), [the substitution occurs] before *atus* and other suffixes beginning with a consonant (*ajādau*) that are *kit*.
Considering the optional substitution of *vṛddhi*, he says: *mamārjatuḥ* and *mamṛjatuḥ*.
It should also be understood that *mamārjuḥ* and *mamṛjuḥ* are likewise formed. Considering the optional *iṭ* augment due to the root being marked with *ū* and the *vṛddhi* of *mṛj*, he says:
*mamārjitha* and *mamārṣṭha*. In the absence of *iṭ*, the *j* is changed to *ṣ* by the rule *vraśca-ādināṃ ṣaḥ*; [the same applies] to the *th*.
The sense is that *ṭha* [is substituted] because of the status of being *ṣṭua*. *Mamārjathuḥ*—[alternatively] *mamṛjathuḥ*; *mamārja*—[alternatively] *mamṛja*.
*Mamārja*, *mamārjiva*—[alternatively] *mamṛjiva*, *mamañjiva*; *mamārjima*—[alternatively] *mamṛjima*, *mamṛjma*.
In the *luṭ* [future tense], [the forms are] *mārjitā* and *mārṣṭā*, depending on whether *iṭ* [augment] is present due to the quality of being *ūdit* or not.

The meaning is that there is *vṛddhi* [substitution] by the rule "ṭhmṛjervṛddhiḥ. [Thus: *mārjiṣyati*—*mārkṣyati*; *mārṣṭu*—*mṛṣṭāt*, *mṛṣṭām*, *mārjantu*—*mṛjñatu*. [In *mṛḍḍhi*: because the *hi* [augment] is not *apit*, it is *ṅit*, and thus there is *vṛddhi*. By the rule beginning with "vraśca," the *j* becomes *ṣ*. [Then] *hi* becomes *dhi*, and the *ṣ* becomes *ḍ* by the rule for *jaś*-sounds.

When *ṣṭu* is substituted for *dh*, it becomes *ḍha*. [The forms are] *mṛṣṭāt*, *mṛṣṭam*, *mṛṣṭa*; [and in the first person singular of the imperative] *mārjāni*, *mārjāva*, *mārjāma*. Regarding the *laṅ* [tense], he says: *amārṭ*. When the *ik* of *tip* is elided, there is *vṛddhi* [substitution], followed by the substitution of *ra* for the *apṛkta* vowel; then, by the rule *halṅyādi*, the *takāra* is elided, and by the rule *vraśca-ādi*, the *jakāra* is changed to *ṣakāra*, and of that...

The sense is that [the rules for] *jaś*-ness and *car*-ness apply. [The forms are: *amṛṣṭām*, *amārjan* (or *amṛjan*), *amārṭ*, *amṛṣṭam*, *amṛṣṭaṃ*, *amārjam* (or *amṛjva*), *amṛjma*. [In the optative: *mṛjyāt*, *mṛjyātām*, *mṛjyāt*, *mṛjyāstām*. [In the aorist: *amārjīt*, *amārkṣīt*.

The intention is that there is an optional *iṭ* augment because the root begins with a vowel (*ūdit*). In the case where *iṭ* is present, forms such as *amārjiṣṭām* and *amārjiṣuḥ* are easily understood. In the absence of *iṭ*, the forms are *āmārṣṭām*, *amārkṣuḥ*;
*amārkṣīḥ*; *amārṣṭam*, *amārṣṭa*; and *amārkṣam*, *amārkṣva*, *amārkṣma*.
*amārjiṣyata*—*amārkṣyat*. Regarding the root *rudh*: it is *seṭ* (taking the augment *iṭ*).
