The meaning is that the roots *juhoty-ādi* do not take the *ślu*-vowel modification (*vikaraṇa*). Thus, the forms derived from the root *sṛ*, which functions in the sense of general motion, have been stated. If the root *sṛ* refers to swift motion, he states its specific form: "But in the case of swift motion... [and] "the substitute *dhau*... is used.
The word *dhau* in the rule is in the nominative case, meaning that *dhau* is the substitute ending in the vowel *au*. In the rule *pāghrā*, the mention of *sarti* is by means of the *śtip* affix;
the intention is that the mention [of the root] without the *vikaraṇa* suffix is not intended [to be significant]. [This refers to] *sarti* in the sense of rapid motion.

This is stated with reference to the Vārttika *dhāvādeśaḥ*. Regarding *dhāvati*: when the suffix *śap* is applied, the root *sṛ* undergoes the substitution of *dhau*, and then the substitution of *āv*. [The forms are: *dhāvatu*, *adhāvat*, *dhāvet*. The root *ṛ* (meaning "to go" and "to reach") is *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*). In the domain of *śit* suffixes, by the rule *pāghrādhmeṭ*, it undergoes the substitution of *ṛccha*.
Regarding this, he says: "He goes" (*ṛcchati*).

[Pāṇini 7.4.11 states: *ṛcchatyṛtām* | Now, when the form *ṛ-atus* is established, after doubling, the substitution of *urat*, the substitution of *rapara*, and the application of *halādiśeṣa*, [we have] *ata-*...

When "ā" is substituted for "ādeḥ" (Pāṇini 6.4.72), the form becomes "ā-ṛ-atuḥ". At this stage, since the suffix *atus* is treated as *kit* by Pāṇini 1.1.5 (*ṭh-saṃyogādi*), the substitution of *yaṇ* (Pāṇini 6.1.77) would be blocked; however, because the rule for *guṇa* (Pāṇini 7.3.84) is subsequent, it would supersede *yaṇ*, resulting in the undesired form *aratur*. To prevent this, he states the rule for *guṇa* in that context: *ṛcchatyṛtām* (Pāṇini 7.4.11).

From the rule "ṭhdayaterdigi liṭi," the word *liṭi* (in the periphrastic perfect) is understood; from the rule "ṛtaśca saṃyogāderguṇaḥ," the word *guṇaḥ* (guṇa substitution) is also understood. The term *ṛcchati-ṛ-ṛt* is a copulative compound (*dvandva*) in the plural. From this very plural form, the inclusion (*praśleṣa*) of the letter *ṛ* is understood. And by means of this included *ṛ*—

Only the root *ṛ* is understood here; for if there were a reference to roots ending in the vowel *ṛ*, the rule "ṭhṛtaśca saṃyogāderguṇaḥ" (Pāṇini 7.2.43) would be rendered purposeless. As for the root *ṛcch* belonging to the Taudādika class, meaning "to go, to lose the senses, to dissolve, or to become solid," its mention as "ṛcchati" is by way of the *śit* suffix. However, regarding the root of the Bhauvādika class...

Since this is already established by the very mention of *ṛ*, he says "of the root belonging to the *tud*-class," and so forth. This rule is for the sake of the *kit* suffixes as well; because it is subsequent [to other rules], it applies even when there is no *kit* suffix. Regarding "in *ṇal*, as before": although this *guṇa* substitution finds its scope of application among the *kit* suffixes according to the method stated under the rule "√*hvṛ* in the sense of crookedness" (*hva kauṭilye*), it nevertheless applies by the rule "after a vowel, before a suffix marked with *ñ* or *ṇ*" (*aco ñṇiti*).

Because it is subsequent (para) with respect to the augment *vṛddhi*, the substitution of *ṇal* occurs; thereafter, when *ra* is substituted for the final element, there is *vṛddhi* of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā*)—this is the meaning. Regarding *āra*: from the root *ṛ*, in the perfect tense (*liṭ*), after *tip* has been replaced by *ṇal*, doubling occurs, followed by the substitution of *u* for *ṛ*, the elision of all but the first consonant (*halādiśeṣa*), the lengthening of the initial *a* according to "the substitute for *at* is long" (*ata ādeḥ*), and finally the *vṛddhi* of the latter portion.
The intention is that when *ra* replaces *ṛ*, the long vowel rule (*savarṇadīrgha*) applies. Regarding *āratur*: as before, after doubling and so forth, we have *ā ṛ atus*.

Since the suffix is *kit*, the prohibition of *guṇa* would apply; however, by the rule *ṛcchatyṛtām*, *guṇa* is applied, followed by the replacement of *ṛ* with *ra*, and finally the long vowel rule (*savarṇadīrgha*). The same process applies to *āruḥ*.

(220) *iḍatyartivyayatīnām* | Pāṇini 7.2.66. Regarding the rule *thali ca seṭi*, which prohibits the augment *iṭ* that would otherwise be required by the restriction for roots beginning with *krī-* etc., there arises a further prohibition according to the opinion of Bhāradvāja because the root ends in *ṛ* (by the rule *ṛto bhāradvājasya*). To this, [the present sūtra] applies: *iḍatyarti*. This is used in the sense of the ablative case.
The genitive [case ending] is used. From the rule "ṭhacaḥ tāsvat," the word *sthali* is understood as a subsequent reference (*anuvartate*).
The mention of *vibhāṣā* from the two preceding rules—"ṭhvibhāṣā sṛjidṛśoḥ" and "ari"—does not carry over because it is not marked with the *svarita* accent.
This is what he says with the words beginning "ad ṛ. While the phrase "ārddhadhātukasyeṭ" is understood as a subsequent reference (*anuvṛtti*), [the following applies].

They say that the repetition of the word *it* (the augment) is for the purpose of removing the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the prohibition "not after *vṛ*, *vṛdh*, and the four [roots beginning with *śī*]. Thus: *ārīt*, *ārathuḥ*, *āraḥ*, *āra*, *āriṣva*, *ārima*. The augment *iṭ* is applied by the rule governing roots beginning with *kṛ* (Pāṇini 7.2.13). Regarding *ariṣyati*: the augment *iṭ* is applied by the rule "after a root ending in long *ṝ* or the root *han*" (Pāṇini 7.2.36).
*ṛcchatu*, *ārcchat*, and *aryāt*: the intention here is that there is *guṇa* substitution by the rule "guṇo 'rteḥ," followed by the replacement of *ṛ* with *ra*.

In *ārṣīt*, there is *vṛddhi* substitution due to the *sic* suffix. However, the *aṅ* augment does not apply by the rule "sarti-śāsti-artibhyaśca," because it was stated immediately following [this point] that the root *ṛ* belonging to the *bhūvādigaṇa* (the root *ṛdh*) is not included [in this rule].

The verbal root *bhū* [is used]. [In the future tense] *āriṣyat*, the augment *iṭ* is applied by the rule "ṛddhanoḥ sye. The roots *gṛ* and *ghṛ* are both *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*). From *gṛ*: *garati*; [in the perfect tense] *jagāra*. Because it does not begin with a conjunct consonant (*asaṃyogādi*), there is no *guṇa* substitution by the rule "ṛtaśca. [Thus,] *jagratuḥ*, *jagruḥ*.
Although the augment *iṭ* would have been required by the rule "krādiniyamena," it is prohibited by the rule "acastāsvat."

Because it ends in *ṛ*, even according to the opinion of Bhāradvāja, the augment *iṭ* does not apply. He states this with the example "jagartha. [The forms are: *jagrathuḥ*, *jagra*; *jagāra*—*jagara*; *jagriva*. [In these cases] *iṭ* is applied by the rule governing roots beginning with *kṛ*. [The form is] *jagrama*. [The noun] *gartā*. [The future form] *gariṣyati*. [Here] *iṭ* is applied by the rule "ṛddhanoḥ". [The imperative form] *garatu*. [The imperfect form] *agarat*. [The optative form] *garet*. [In the case of the root *gṝ*, the substitute] *riṅ* applies.

In the case of the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), because the root begins with a conjunct consonant (*saṃyogādi*), there is no *guṇa* substitution by the rule "artī" [Pāṇini 1.1.57]; consequently, by the rule "riṅ śayagliṅkṣu" [Pāṇini 7.4.28], *riṅ* is substituted for *ī*. Thus, from the base *gri*, we have *griyāt*. As for *griyāt*: since *rīṅ* was prescribed for the original form, the long vowel does not apply here due to the prescription of *riṅ*. As for *agārṣīt*: after the *vṛddhi* substitution in the *sic* suffix, *ra* is substituted for the semivowel (*raparatva*).

*agārṣṭām*; *agariṣyat*. [The suffix] *iṭ* is applied by the rule "ṛd-dhanoḥ". However, regarding the root *ghṛ* belonging to the Bhvādigaṇa, its usage occurs only in such forms as *ghṛtam*, *gharmaḥ*, and *ghṛṇā*, and not elsewhere;
this is clear from the Bhāṣya on the sūtra "*tṛjvat kroṣṭuḥ*". As for *dhvṛ*, it means "to be distressed" (*hūrcchanam*).

The root *dhvṛ* (to bend): *kuṭilībhavanam*. Present: *dhvarati*. Perfect: *dadhvāra*. By the rule "ṛtaśca," there is *guṇa* substitution. Periphrastic perfect: *dadhvaratuḥ*, *dadhvaruḥ*. In the case of the suffix *thali*, the augment *iṭ* does not apply; this is because it is prohibited by the rule "krādiniyama" (*krādi-niyama*). Furthermore, according to the opinion of Bhāradvāja, the augment *iṭ* is also absent because the root ends in *ṛ*. Second person singular: *dadhvartha*. Second person dual: *dadhvarathuḥ*. Second person plural: *dadhvara*. First person singular: *dadhvāra* or *dadhvara*.
*dadhvar*—we have caused to fall or destroyed. The augment *iṭ* is applied due to the rule *krādiniyamāt*. [Future: *dhvartā*. The augment *iṭ* is applied by the rule *ṛddhanoḥ*—[future:

*dhvariṣyati*. Imperative: *dhvaratu*. Imperfect: *adhvarat*. Optative: *dhvaret*. In the precative (*āśīrliṅ*), there is *guṇa* substitution by the rule *guṇo'tiṅ*. [Precative: *dhvaryāt*. Aorist: *adhvārṣīt*. Conditional: *adhvariṣyat*. The root *sru*, meaning "to flow," is *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*). [Present: *sravati*.
*susrāva*, *susrava*, *susruve*—because it belongs to the *krādiniya* group, there is no *iṭ* augment. *susruma* should also be understood in the same way.
*srotā*, *sroṣyati*, *sravatu*, *asravat*, *sravet*, *srūyāt*—the intention here is that the vowel lengthening occurs by the rule *ṭhakkṛtsārvadhātukayordīrghaḥ*.
[In the case of] *luṅ*: The intended meaning is that the vowel lengthening occurs by the rule *ṭhakkṛtsārvadhātukayordīrghaḥ* (Pāṇini 7.4.25). [In the case of] *luṅ*:
He states the distinction: "ṇiśrīti caṅi. It should also be understood that by the rule "caṅi," reduplication occurs.

Now, an objection is raised: when *asusra a t* is established, would not the *guṇa* substitution—governed by the rule "sārvadhātukārddhadhātukayoḥ" and caused by the *caṅ* suffix—apply to the *u* following the *repha*?

Even though there is a prohibition of *ṅtva*, since the substitution of *uvaṅ* is subsequent to [the application of] *iṭ*, the *guṇa* of the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*) would apply to the *u* following the *repha* by taking that as its cause; therefore, he says:
"The *uvaṅ* [substitution] takes precedence because it is *antaraṅga* (internal) compared to the *guṇa* of the light penultimate vowel."

The *guṇa* substitution for the penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*) is *bahiraṅga* because it depends on the external element *tiP*; the *uvaṅ* substitution is *antaraṅga* because it depends on the internal element *caṅ*. Therefore, only *asusruvat* occurs. The sense is that the *antaraṅga* rule is stronger than the *parā* (subsequent) rule. [The example] *asusruvat* is from the root *sru*, meaning "he would have flowed. *Asroṣyat*. *ṣu*...

He says "prasaveti. Here, he dispels the misconception that the word *prasava* refers to the release of the fetus, stating: "prasava means permission (*abhyanujñāna*). The intention is that this is seen in such passages as "Brahmā gives the *prasava* [command] with 'ṭhai praṇaya'. This is a root taught with the augment *ṣ*. In the presence of the suffix *śap*, it supersedes the substitution of *uvaṅ*.

By the rule *paratvāt sārvadhātukayor guṇaḥ*, there is guṇa [substitution]. Thus: *savati*. In the forms *suṣāva* and so on, because the suffixes beginning with *atus* are *kit*, there is an absence of guṇa, and *uvaṅ* substitution occurs: *suṣuvatuḥ*, *suṣuvuḥ*.
According to the rule of Bhāradvāja, there is optionally *iṭ* in the case of the suffix *thal*; thus he says: *suṣavitha*, *suṣotha*.

The sense is that there is no *guṇa* substitution because [the suffix] is marked with *k*. [Examples are: *suṣuvathuḥ*, *suṣuva*; *suṣāva*, *suṣava*. However, for the two forms ending in *-vam*, the augment *iṭ* is obligatory by the rule of *krādiniyama*.
Thus he says: *suṣuviva*. Because it is marked with *k*, there is an absence of *guṇa*, and consequently *uvaṅ* is substituted [resulting in]: *sotā*.
He will press; he pressed; he pressed; may he press; may he be pressed; *sūyāt*.

(221) Regarding *stusudhūñbhyaḥ parasmaipadeṣu* [Pāṇini 7.2.72]: when *iṭ* would have been obtained by the rule *luṅi ca* [7.2.70], [the prohibition applies] after the roots *stu*, *su*, and *dhūñ*. This follows from the rule *iḍatyartī* [7.2.66].

The term *iṭ* is understood [from the previous rule]. From the rule *ṭhañjeḥ sicī*, the word *sici* is carried over and is transformed into the genitive case. Thus he says: "after these, [the augment] *sic*. Regarding the form *asāvīt*:

after the *vṛddhi* [substitution] caused by *sic*, the *sic* is elided by the rule *iṭa īṭi*. Regarding the phrase "from the preceding and the following": [this refers to the two rules mentioned above].

The meaning [of the roots] *stuñ* and *dhūñ* is "to press. Regarding *sunoti*: this refers to the root *ṣuñ* "to press," which takes the *śnu* suffix. Regarding *asauṣīt*: the point is that when there is no augment *iṭ*, the rule "vṛddhi before *sic*" applies. *Asoṣyat*. Regarding *śru* "to hear": this root ends in *u* and is *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment).

(222) *śruvaḥ śṛ ca* | 3|1|74|. Regarding *śruvaḥ śṛ ca*: the term *śṛ* is in the nominative case, though its case-ending has been elided. By the particle *ca*, the suffix *śnu* from the rule *svādibhyaḥ śnuḥ* is also included. Thus he says: there is the substitution of *śṛ* for the root *śru*.

It may be that there is the suffix *śnu*; it is an exception (*apavāda*) to *śap*. By this, it is indicated that its application occurs only in the domain of *śap*, specifically in the case of a *sārvadhātuka* affix denoting the agent. "Because of the doubling of *śnu*"—the intention is that this is by means of the rule "a *sārvadhātuka* [affix] also [causes reduplication]. "He hears" (*śṛṇoti*)—this is with reference to the suffix *tip*.
There is *guṇa* for *śnu*. Because the suffixes beginning with *ta* have the marker *ṅ*, there is no *guṇa* for *śnu*. Thus it says: "śṛṇuta" (you all hear).

(223) *huśnuvoḥ sārvadhātuke* 6.4.87. When *śṛṇvanti* is established, because the suffix *anti* has the marker *ṅ*, the prohibition of *guṇa* for *śnu* applies, and [the substitution of] *uv* takes place in place of *eṅ*.

Regarding the rule *prāpte—huśnuvoḥ*: because *śnu* is an affix (*pratyaya*), there is an inclusion of that which ends in it. From the rule *iṇo yaṇ*, the term *yaṇ* is understood by anuvṛtti; from the rule *aci śnu*, the term *aci* is understood. Since that [term *aci*] qualifies the *sārvadhātuka*, there is an application of the rule to what begins with it. [The rule is] *eranekācaḥ*.

The phrase *iti sūtreṇa* (by this rule) continues [from the previous context], with the exception of the word *varjam*. From the rule *ṭhoḥ supi*, the term *oḥ* is in the genitive case. This is what he states by saying "of *juhoti*" and so forth. However, the term *asaṃyogapūrvasya* is a qualifier of the vowel *u*, not a qualifier of the suffix *śnu*; therefore, in the form *āpnuvanti*, the *yaṇ* substitution [occurs].

Why [is it said] "not for *hu* and *anuśva*"? Consider *yoyuvati*. Here, after the elision (*luk*) of *yaṅ* from the root *yu*, when *jhi* is replaced by *at* according to the rule *tadabhyastāt*, the form *yoyu-ati* results.
In this state, the *yaṇ* substitution does not occur for the *u* that is part of a multi-syllabic (*anekāj*) stem and is not preceded by a consonant cluster (*asaṃyogapūrva*). In this case...

In the Bhāṣya, under the continued application of the rule "bahulaṃ chandasi," since the elision of *yaṅ* (*yaṅluk*) prescribed by "yaṅo 'ci ca" is Vedic, the absence of *yaṇ* in the form *yoyuvatī* is established simply by resorting to its status as an *ārddhadhātuka* suffix via the rule "chandasyubhayathā. Therefore, the inclusion of *huḍ* and *śnu* [in the rule] is for the sake of [extending this behavior] even to the secular (Bhāṣā) language.

It has been stated that [the mention of *hu*] indicates the elision of *yaṅ* in certain cases. And thus, since the elision of *yaṅ* is established even in the common language (*bhāṣā*)—as in *yuvati* and so forth, which end in *u* and are preceded by non-conjunct consonants and consist of more than two syllables—it follows as a result that the inclusion of *hu* and *śnu* is for the purpose of excluding *yaṅ* in those instances. This is the indicator (*jñāpaka*).

Because it depends on a general rule (*sāmānya*), the elision of *yaṅ* (*yaṅluk*) established by the cited example is valid even in cases other than those ending in a vowel. Intending this very point, the Bhāṣya states: "The mention of *hu* and *śan* indicates that *yaṅluk* occurs even in the colloquial language (*bhāṣā*). [Question: "What is the purpose of this indication? [Answer: "As in *bebhidīti*."

It has been stated that "cecchiditi" is thus established. Here, because only *bhid* and *chid* are mentioned, they say that the *yaṅluk* occurring elsewhere than after the aforementioned forms ending in /ū/ occurs only after these two, and not after others. Others, however, maintain that the mention of *bhid* and *chid* is merely illustrative.
One should understand that *śṛṇvanti*, *śṛṇuthaḥ*, and *śṛṇuta* are also [forms].
Intending to apply the rule "the elision of this [nasal] optionally before *m* and *v*" (*lopaścāsyānyatarasyāṃ mvoḥ*), he says: *śṛṇvaḥ*, etc.
[The forms] *śuśrāva*, *śuśruvatuḥ*, and *śuśruvuḥ* [are derived]; and likewise in the case of *thali* and the suffixes *vas* and *mas*.
Because it belongs to the *krādi* group, there is a permanent prohibition of the *iṇ* augment. Thus he says: *śuśrotha*, *śuśruva*, and *śuśruvuḥ*.

It should also be understood that *śuśruma* occurs as well. [The forms] *śrotā*, *śroṣyati*, and for the imperative: *śṛṇotu*, *śṛṇutāt*, *śṛṇutām*, and *śṛṇvantu*. By the rule "utaśca pratyayād asaṃyogapūrvāt," there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix *hi*.
Having considered this, he says: "Listen" (*śṛṇu*). [The forms] *śṛṇutāt*, *śṛṇutam*, *śṛṇuta*, and *śṛṇavāni* [are derived from the root *śru*].

The intention is that because the augment *āṭ* is marked with *p* (indicating it is not *ṅ*), there is no absence of the *ṅ*-marking, and thus [the rule for] *guṇa* applies. Regarding the root *dhru* in the sense of "steadiness": it is *aniṭ*. It takes the form *dhravati*.
The forms *dudhrāva*, *dudhruvatuḥ*, *dudhruvuḥ* [follow]. According to the rule of Bhāradvāja, the suffix *thala* optionally takes the augment *iṭ*.

*dudhravitha*—*dudhrotha*, *dudhruvathuḥ*, *dudhruva*; *dudhrāva*, *dudhrava*, *dudhruviva*, *dudhruvima*. By the rule of the *krādiniyama*, the augment *iṭ* is added. *dhrotā*. *dhroṣyati*. *dhravatu*. *adhravat*. *dhravet*. *dhrūyāt*. *adhrauṣīt*. *adhroṣyat*. [The roots] *du* and *dru* mean "to move."
[The roots] *du* and *drū* are both *aniṭ*. [Present tense: *davati*, *dravati*. [Perfect tense: *dudāva*, *duduvatuḥ*, *duduvuḥ*;

*dudrāva*, *dudruvatuḥ*, *dudruvuḥ*. Regarding this root, he says that according to the rule of Bhāradvāja, there is an option for the *iṭ* augment in the *thal* suffix: *dudodha*, *dudavitha*. [The forms] *duduvathuḥ*, *duduva*; *dudāva*—*dudava*—in the *vas* and *mas* suffixes.

He says that *iṭ* is optional for roots beginning with *krād*—hence *duduviva*. Because the second [form] belongs to the *krād*-class, there is no *iṭ* necessarily after *thal*; thus he says *dudrotha*. *Dudruvathuḥ*, *dudruva*. *Dudrāva*, *dudrava*. Because of the *krād*-class status, there is no *iṭ* in the first person dual (*vam*) and plural (*mas*); thus he says *dudruma*. [The futures are] *drotā*, *drotā*.

*doṣyati*, *droṣyati*; *davatu*, *dravatu*; *adavat*, *adravat*; *davet*, *dravet*; *dūyāt*, *drūyāt*; *adauṣīt*. Regarding the mention of *caṅ*: the intention is [to refer to] the root *du*. "Diminution" (*nyūnīkaraṇa*) means making something low (*nīcīkaraṇa*). "Becoming diminished" (*nyūnībhavana*)...

The meaning is "becoming one whose strength is exhausted. "He conquers his enemies" means "he humbles them. Now, since the root *ji* (to conquer) is *parasmaipada*, one might ask how there can be the *ātmanepada* form *parājayate*; to this he says: "from *vi* and *parā*" [according to Pāṇini 1.3.19]. But [one might object] that defeat is [contrary to] study...

Since there is an absence of both conjunction (*saṃśleṣa*) and disjunction (*viśleṣa*), how can the study (*adhyayana*) function as the *apādāna* (ablative) in relation to defeat? To this, he says: "In the case of *parāji*" [Pāṇini 1.4.26]. [The root] *jayati*. In the perfect tense (*liṭ*), by the rule "saṬ-liṭor jeḥ" [Pāṇini 7.3.57], there is the substitution of *k* for *j*, resulting in *jigāya*, *jigyatuḥ*, *jigyuḥ*.
According to the rule of Bhāradvāja, the augment *iṭ* is optional before *thal*. Thus: *jigayitha*, *jigetha*; *jigyathuḥ*; *jigya*.
Before *vas* and *mas*, the augment *iṭ* is mandatory by the rule of Kṛtādi; thus: *jigyiva*, *jigyima*. [The forms for the other tenses are: *jetā*; *jeṣyati*;
*jayatu*; *ajayat*; *jayet*; *jīyāt*; *ajaiṣīt*; *ajaiṣṭām*.
*ajaiṣuḥ*, *ajaiṣīḥ*, *ajaiṣṭam*, *ajaiṣṭa*; *ajaiṣam*, *ajaiṣva*, *ajaiṣma*; [and] *ajeṣyat*.

Thus end the roots beginning with *dheṭ* that terminate in a vowel (*ajanta*) and take the *parasmaipada* endings. Now, those ending in *ḍīṅ* are marked with *ṅ* (*ṅti*). The meaning is that all roots up to "*ḍīṅ vihāyasā gatau*" (to fly through the air) take the *ātmanepada* endings because they are marked with *ṅ*.

The root *smiṅ* is used in the sense of "slight laughter. This is a root taught with an initial *ṣ*. Thus, *smayate*. (232) *veḥ skander aniṣṭhāyām* | Pāṇini 8.3.73. Regarding the rule *veḥ skande*, he explains the sūtra by supplying the missing portion: "there may optionally be the substitution of *ṣ*."

The meaning is that this is because of the governing rule "ṭhapadāntasya mūrdhanyaḥ" (a dental becomes a retroflex when following a word-final ṭ or ṭh) and because of the continuation of the word "vā" from the rule "sivādīnāṃ vā. The resulting sense is that the *s* of the root *skand*, when preceded by the prefix *vi*, may optionally become *ṣ* when followed by any suffix other than the *niṣṭhā* (past passive participle). But [one might ask]: why does this not apply in cases such as *viskandati*?

Because there is a doubt regarding the status of the *ṣatva* (the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*), he says: "This is indeed a *kṛtya*. The intention is that a *paryudāsa* (an exclusion) depends on something of the same class, as in examples such as "bring one who is not a Brāhmaṇa" (*abrahmaṇam ānaya*). Regarding the forms *viṣkantā* and *viskantā*, these are forms derived from the suffix *tṛc*. Since [the root] is not taught with an initial *ṣ* (*aṣopadeśa*), this option (*vibhāṣā*) does not otherwise apply.

(233) *pareśca* | 8|3|74|. Regarding the rule *pareśca*: one might object that since the form would already be established by the rule *viparibhyāṃ skanderaniṣṭhāyām*, the division of this into a separate sūtra is redundant; to this, he replies: "In the case of the [separate] yoga," etc. "In the alternative where *ṣatva* applies": *pariṣkand-ta*.

This being the case, by the rules "aniditām" and "radābhyām," the *t* of the *niṣṭhā* suffix [is replaced], and then, through the substitution of *ṇ* for the *d* preceding it by virtue of the rule for *ṣṭu*-substitution, the form "pariṣkaṇṇa" is obtained; this is the meaning. Now, one might object that the substitution of *ṇ* for the *n* in place of the *d*, caused by the *ṣ*, is an *antaranga* (internal) operation.

Because the cause (*nimitta*) and that which possesses the cause (*nimitin*) reside in a single word, whereas the substitution of *ṣ*— occurring by depending on the *iṇ* sound situated at the end of a different word consisting of the prefix *pari* according to the rule *ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ*—
is extrinsic (*bahiraṅga*). Consequently, when the substitution of *ṇ* is to be applied, [the extrinsic factor is considered as not having taken effect].

Having raised the objection—"Since the substitution of *ṣ* is not established (*asiddha*), there is no occurrence of a letter subsequent to *ṣ*; how then can there be the substitution of *ṇ*?"—the author refutes it with the words "na ca" (and not). The connection is as follows: that which was suggested—the non-establishment of the external (*bahiraṅga*) substitution of *ṣ* because it depends upon two words—that should not be suspected. Why? From this [it follows].

He says: "Of the root and the prefix"—first the root; [first the root is joined with the prefix, and it receives the grammatical operations such as *saṃdhi* and so forth. Afterwards—that is, after the operation of the root and prefix has taken place—it is joined with the *sādhana*. The word *sādhana*...]

[The word *kāraka*] denotes the factor of action (*kāraka*). Here, however, the suffix expressing that [factor] is indicated; that is to say, "by means of the suffix. This is clear from the Bhāṣya on the sūtra beginning with *saṃprasāraṇācca*. Thus he says: "the Bhāṣya. Regarding the view of another school (*matāntara*), however: "First, the verbal root (*dhātu*) is joined with the factor of action (*sādhana*)."

In the alternative view that [the rule] applies "after a prefix," however, because the substitution of *ṣ* is considered *asiddha* (non-existent) due to its being *bahiraṅga*, the substitution of *ṇ* does not occur; this is the meaning. The root *yabh* is devoid of *iṭ*. It forms *yabhati*, *yayābha*, *yebhatuḥ*. But in the case of the suffix *thali*, according to the rule of Bhāradvāja, when there is the optional presence of *iṭ*, although it is not *akit* because it is *pit*, the rule "ṭhthali ca seṭi" [applies].

Having considered that the substitution of *et* (for *ay*) and the elision of the reduplication (*abhyāsalopa*) do not apply here, he says: "yebhiḥ" and "yayabdha. The intended meaning is as follows: in the case of the suffix *thal*, when there is no *iṭ* augment, because the suffix is marked with *p* and thus lacks the *k* designation, the substitution of *et* and the elision of the reduplication do not occur. Thus, we have the form *yayam-tha*.
Then, by the rule *jhaṣas tathoḥ*, the *th* is changed to *dh*; subsequently, by the rule of *jaśtva*, the *bh* (of *yayambha*) is changed to *b*, resulting in *yayambha*.

*yebhathuḥ*, *yebha*, *yayābha*—*yayabha*. [In the case of] *krādiniyamāt iṭ* (the rule regarding the augment *iṭ* after roots beginning with *kru*), [we have] *yebhiva*, *yebhima*, and *yabdha*. In the *luṭ* [suffix], for the *takāra* of *tāsi*, there is the substitution of *dha* by the rule *ṭhjhaṣas tathoḥ*; the intention is that the *bhakāra* becomes *bakāra* by the rule of *jaśtva*. [Thus we have] *yapsyati*; in the presence of *sya*, the *bha* becomes *pa* by the rule of *cartva*.

*yabhatu*, *ayabhat*, *yabhet*, *yabhyāt*, *ayāpsīt*—the intention here is that there is vṛddhi by virtue of the rule concerning roots ending in a consonant (*halanta*). *Ayapsyat*. Regarding the root *ṇam* in the sense of "striking": this root is without the augment *iṭ* and has *ṇ* as its initial letter. However, some read this root as having the marker *u* (i.e., as *ṇam-u*). But that...

[This would be] due to carelessness; for if that were the case, it would result in the optional addition of *iṭ* in the *ktvā* affix by the rule "udito vā," and the optional addition of *iṭ* in the *niṣṭhā* (past participle) affix by the rule "yasya vibhāṣā.
[The forms are: *namati*, *nanāma*, *nematuḥ*, *nemuḥ*. However, in the case of the *thali* affix, when *iṭ* is optionally present according to the restriction of Bhāradvāja—
Even though [the root] is *pit* (having a penultimate *i*), considering that there is elision of the reduplication and *it*-guṇa substitution by the rule "ṭhthali ca seṭi," he says:

*nemitha*, *nanantha*. In the alternative where *iṭ* is absent, because it is *pit* and thus not *akit*, there is no *it*-guṇa substitution or elision of the reduplication; the forms are *nemathuḥ*, *nema*, *nanāma*—*nanama*.
*nenema*—the augment *iṭ* is applied due to the rule *krādiniyamāt*.

*namanta*—the *m* undergoes *anusvāra*, which is then changed to the *parasavarṇa*. *naṃsyati*. *namatu*. *anamat*. *namet*. *namyāt*. Regarding *anaṃsīt*: the sense is that the suffix *sic* is applied by the rule *hy-antardha-bhava-yama-ram-eti*. *anaṃsyat*. [Now for] the roots *gamlṛ* and *sṛplṛ*.
Regarding the roots *gatau* (in the sense of "gone"): they are both *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment). *Sṛp* is taught with an initial *ṣ*. (Pāṇini 7.3.77) states: *iṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ*.
[The mention of] *iṣu-gami* [is made] because of the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the word *śit* from the rule *ṣṭhivuklamvacamām* (6.1.67); this is the intended meaning.

Because of the mention of the vowel *u* (in the form *udit*), there is the inclusion of the root *iṣ* belonging to the *tud-ādi* class. Here, without revoking the condition "before a vowel" (*aci*), the *Bhāṣya* establishes that the substitution of *ch* does not occur in forms such as *iṣyati* and *iṣṇāti*, by relying on the rule "before a *śit* suffix beginning with a vowel. Thus, in this sūtra and in the *tud-ādi* class, the reading of the root as *udit* is considered non-Vedic (*anārṣa*) according to the *Śabdenduśekhara*.

[The root] *sthā* [becomes *tiṣṭhati*]. [In the case of *gacchati*,] after the suffix *śap*, the letter *m* becomes *cch*. [In the case of] *jagmatuḥ*, there is elision of the penultimate vowel by the rule *gamahana-*. Likewise, *jagmuḥ*. According to the restriction of Bhāradvāja, there is optionally *iṭ* in the *thal* [suffix]; thus he says: *jagamitha*, *jagantha*. [The forms] *jagmathuḥ*, *jagma*; *jagāma*—*jagama*; *jagmiva*.
We went (*jagmima*). The augment *iṭ* is applied by the rule *krādiniyamāt*.

(235) *gamer iṭ parasmaipadeṣu* (Pāṇini 7.2.58): "The augment *iṭ* [is added] after the root *gam* in the Parasmaipada endings. Here, *gameḥ* is in the ablative case (*pañcamī*). From the previous rule *se'sici*, the word *se* is understood as an anuvṛtti.

The term *ārddhadhātukasya* (of an ārdhadhātuka suffix), which is understood from the previous rule, is here specified. This is a rule governing the initial element [of the following suffix]. Thus he says: "of that which follows *gam*" and so forth. The phrase *parasmaipadeṣu* means "in the absence of an ātmanepada [suffix].
In this way, the augment *iṭ* is established for the suffix *tṛc* in the form *saṃjigamiṣitṛ*. [Examples include] *gamiṣyati* and *gacchatu*.
He went (*agacchat*), he might go (*gacchet*), or he may go (*gamyāt*). Regarding the specific form of the *luṅ* [aorist], it says: "Because it is marked with *ḷ*, there is *aṅ*" (*lṛditvādaṅ*).
He states that there is no elision of the penultimate vowel according to the rule "gamahana—" (*gamahana...*), because of the exclusion (*paryudāsa*) by the term "not when *aṅ* follows" (*anaṅīti*).
Thus: *agamat*. For the *lṛṅ* [conditional]: *agamiṣyat*. Regarding "he creeps" (*sarpati*): when the suffix *śap* is applied, there is the substitution of the vowel *ṛ*.

The *guṇa* substitution for the short penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇaḥ*) applies. Then there is the substitution of *ra* for the final consonant (*raparatvam*). Thus: *sasarpa*, *sasṛpatuḥ*, *sasṛpuḥ*. In the case of the suffix *thali*, by the rule *krādiniyamaḥ*, *iṭ* is necessarily added. Because the root does not end in a vowel (*ajantatva*) and because it does not possess the letter *a* (*akāravattva*), the optional addition of *iṭ* (*iḍvikalpaḥ*) does not apply. [Thus]: *sasarpitha*, *sasṛpathuḥ*, *sasṛpa*; *sasarpa*, *sasṛpiva*, *sasṛpima*.
When *luṭ* [is applied], the substitution of *guṇa* for the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*) would apply, followed by *ra* (as in *rapara*). To this, [the rule] *anudātasya ca* applies.
From the rule *sṛjidṛśor am kitī*, the phrase *jhali am akiti* is understood to carry over; and from the rule *ādeca upadeśe*, the phrase *upadeśe* is understood to carry over. Thus he says:
"in the original enunciation (*upadeśe*), being unaccented (*anudāta*)," and so forth. Because of its status as a *mit* [augment], it is placed after the final vowel.

[The rule applies] when [the suffix] is *paraḥ* (subsequent). What is the purpose of specifying "in the case of instruction" (*upadeśe*)? [Consider] the suffix *kta*: *sṛptaḥ*. [In the form] *sraptā*, the meaning is that after the verbal root *sṛp*, in the *luṭ* [suffix], with the addition of *tās* and the augment *am*, there is the *yaṇ* substitution for the vowel *ṛ*.

[In the form] *sarptā*, the meaning is that in the absence of *am*, there is the *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadha*), followed by the substitution of *ra* for *ṛ*. Likewise [for] *srapsyati*.

It will creep (*sarpṣyati*). Let it creep (*sarpatu*). It crept (*asarpat*). May it creep (*sarpet*). It may be crept upon (*sṛpyāt*). It crept (*asṛpat*). Because it belongs to the *lṛdita* class, *aṅ* is substituted for *cli*; since [the suffix] has the indicatory letter *ṅ*, there is no *guṇa*. It would have crept (*asrapsyat*) or it would have crept (*asarpsyat*). Regarding *yama* in the sense of "ceasing" (*uparama*), "ceasing" means desisting (*viramaṇa*); this root is *aniṭ* (without the *iṭ* augment).
Regarding *yacchati*: by the rule *ṭhiṣugamiyamāṃ chaḥ*, the substitution *cha* occurs before the suffix *śap*. [The forms] *yayāma*, *yematuḥ*, *yemuḥ* are derived accordingly.

In the case of the suffix *thal*, when the augment *iṭ* is optionally present according to the restriction of Bhāradvāja, the rules *thali ca seṭi* apply, resulting in the substitution of *et* (the final vowel) and the elision of the reduplication. Thus he says: *yemitha*. *Yayantha* is the form when *iṭ* is absent. [The forms] *yemathuḥ*, *yema*, *yayāma*, *yayama* are likewise derived.

*yemiva*, *yemima*. [The suffix] *iṭ* is added by the rule *krādiniyama*. *yantā* (the root form). *yaṃsyati*. *yacchatu*. *ayacchat*. *yacchet*. *yamyāt*. Regarding *ayaṃsīt*: by the rule *hyarameṭ*, the suffixes *iṭ* and *sak* are added; by the rule *iṭa īṭi*, there is the elision (*lopa*) of the *sic*; and because of the prohibition in the rule *neṭ*, the *vṛddhi* substitution conditioned by a stem ending in a consonant does not take place.
The verbal root *tap* (meaning "to heat" or "to torment") is without the augment *iṭ*. It is conjugated as follows: Present: *tapati* Periphrastic Perfect: *tatāpa*, *tepatuḥ*, *tepuḥ*;
*tepitha*, *tataptha*, *tepathuḥ*, *tepa*; *tatāpa*, *tatapa*, *tepiva*, *tepima* Future: *tapsyati* Imperative: *tapatu* Aorist: *atapat* Optative: *tapet* Precative: *tapyāt*

"He heated" (*atāpsīt*). The intention is that the vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*) is conditioned by [the root ending in] a consonant (*halanta*). "He will heat" (*atapsyat*). Regarding the rule *nisastapatau*:

he explains the sūtra by completing the remainder of the text—namely, "there shall be *ṣ*. The intention is that this follows from the governing rule (*adhikāra*) "for a non-final [consonant], there is a retroflex [substitute] (*mūrdhanyaḥ*). Thus, the *s* of the prefix *nis-* becomes *ṣ* when followed by the root *tap*.

In order to explain the phrase "in the case of non-repetition" (*anāsevanam*), he explains the word *āsevana* [itself] as "repetition" (*paunaḥpunyam*). Intending that it forms a negative compound (*nañ-samāsa*) with the word *āsevana*, he says: "in a domain other than that."

This is a statement [of a rule] because [the substitution] would not otherwise apply due to the absence of being a substitute (ādeśatva) and because it occurs at the end of a word (padāntatva). "Niṣṭapati" means "he heats after having drawn out. Since the *s* of *nis* undergoes the change to *ṣ*, the *t* of *tap* becomes *ṭ* by the rule of *ṣṭutva*. However, when there is continuous practice (*āsevana*), the change to *ṣ* does not occur. Regarding "tyaja" in the sense of "abandoning" (*hāni*), abandonment means relinquishment (*utsarga*). This root is without the augment *iṭ* (*aniṭ*).

He abandons: *tyajati*. He abandoned: *tatyāja*, *tatyajatuḥ*, *tatyajuḥ*. Because the root vowel is long (*tavy-*) and situated between two consonants (*saṃyukta-hal*), the substitution of *e* for the root vowel and the elision of the reduplication do not occur. However, in the case of the suffix *thali*, by the rule of Bhāradvāja, the augment *iṭ* is optionally applied. Thus he says: *tatyajitha* or *tatyaktha*. In the absence of *iṭ*, [the following applies] to the *c*-sounds...

The meaning is "he has abandoned. Regarding *tyakta*: [the forms] *tyakṣyati*, *tyajatu*, *atyajat*, *tyajet*, *tyajyāt*, and *atyākṣīt*. The intention is that there is a vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*) conditioned by the suffix beginning with a consonant (*halanta*). [The conditional form is] *atyakṣyat*.
Regarding the root *ṣañj* (to cling): this is a root taught with an initial *ṣ* (*ṣopadeśa*), it is *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment), and its penultimate letter is *n*.

The mention [of the root] includes the *anusvāra* and the resulting *parasavarṇa*. Since the suffix *śap* is marked with *p*, it lacks the *kit* designation; consequently, when this suffix follows, the rule "an idit [root] loses its nasal" (*aniditām*) does not apply. Therefore, he says: "the nasal is dropped by the rule *daṃśasañja-svañjām*."
The sense is that [the substitution] is not applied because the *anusvāra* and *parasavarṇa* are considered *asiddha*. Regarding *sasañja*: in the *liṭ* [perfect], however, it is *sasañja*.
But in forms such as *atus* and so on, there is no elision of *n* because they are not *akit*. Thus, *sasañjatuḥ*, *sasañjuḥ*.
In the *thal* [suffix], by the rule of Bhāradvāja, the augment *iṭ* is optional: *sasañjitha*—*sasaṅktha*. In the absence of *iṭ*, by the rule of *kutva*, [the *j* becomes *g*].

When the letter *ga* undergoes the change to the *ca*-class (*cartva*), there is the disappearance of the fifth letter of the *ca*-class—which has been produced by the *anusvāra* through *parasavarṇa*—when followed by the letter *ka*. Thus, the *anusvāra* becomes the *ṅ*-sound through *parasavarṇa*. [The forms are: *sasañjathuḥ*, *sasañja*, *sasañja*, *sasañjiva*, *sasañjima*; the augment *iṭ* is applied here according to the rule beginning with "roots beginning with *kṛ*" (*krādiniyama*).

Regarding *saṅkte*: when the *j* of *tās* is changed to *g* by the rule of *kutva*, and that [g] undergoes *cartva* (the change to *c*), there is the removal of *ñ*, and the *n* becomes *ṅ*; this is the intended meaning. [The forms are: *saṅkṣyati*, *sajat*, *asajat*, *sajet*, *sajyāt*, *asāṅkṣīt*. Because it ends in a consonant (*halanta*), there is *vṛddhi* [in the aorist]. [The conditional is: *asaṅkṣyat*. [Now for] *dṛśir* in the sense of "seeing."

Thus [it is said]: it is marked with *ṛt* (indicating the substitution of *ir*), and it is *aniṭ*. The form *paśyati* is derived because, when a *śit* affix follows, there is the substitution of *paśya* according to the rule *prāghrādhme*. The forms are *dadarśa*, *dadṛśatuḥ*, *dadṛśuḥ*. However, regarding the suffix *thali*, the augment *iṭ* is invariably required by the rule *krādiniyamāt*. Since the root lacks both an *ajanta* (ending in a vowel) and the presence of the letter *a*, the rules *acaḥ tāsvat* and *upadeśe 'tvataḥ* do not apply.
Thus, because the prohibition does not apply, and because the absence of the suffix *ṛt* renders the restriction of Bhāradvāja irrelevant,
[the rule] "vibhāṣā sṛjidṛśoḥ" (Pāṇini 7.2.65) applies.

Regarding this, he says: *vibhāṣā sṛji*. The genitive case is used in the sense of the ablative. From the rules *gamer iṭ* and *astisico 'pṛkte*, the word *iṭ* and the word *thali* respectively are understood as being carried over (*anuvartate*). Therefore, he says: "from these two. (237) *sṛjidṛśor jhaly am akiti* (Pāṇini 6.1.58).
In the alternative where *iṭ* is absent, when the optional insertion of *am* (by the rule *anudātasya*) would apply, [the sūtra] *sṛjidṛśoḥ* [is stated].

The analysis is *am akiti*. This is for the sake of making it compulsory. Regarding *dadraṣṭha*: when *dadr̥ś tha* is the state [of the stem], if *iṭ* is absent, *am* is inserted; then, after the *r̥*-vowel undergoes *yaṇ*-substitution, the *ś* is changed to *ṣ* by the rule *vraśca* etc.

The intention is that *ṭha* arises from [the substitution] of *ṣṭu* for *ṣṭh*. Regarding the case where *iṭ* is present, he says: *dadarśitha*. The intention is that *am* does not apply because it is neither a vowel (*aj*) nor the beginning of a consonant (*jhal*). Regarding *draṣṭā*: when *tāsi* is added, there is *ṣatva* of *ś*, and by the rule of *ṣṭu* for *ṣṭh*, there is *ṭ* for *t*; this is the intention. Regarding *drakṣyati*: when *am* is added, there is *ṣatva* of *ś*.

In the case of *ṣaḍhoḥ kaḥ si*, the intention is that *s* becomes *ṣ*. [Examples: *paśyatu*, *apaśyat*, *paśyet*. Regarding the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), [the form] is *dṛśyāt*; the intention is that *am* does not apply because it is neither a vowel (*ac*) nor a consonant (*jhal*) beginning [affix]. He states the specific rule for the aorist (*luṅ*): "due to the *irit* designation, there is optionally *aṅ*. Here, in the alternative where *aṅ* applies, the prohibition of *guṇa* would otherwise have occurred.

(238) *ṛdṛśo’ṅ guṇī* | Pāṇini 7.4.16. Regarding *ṛdṛśo’ṅ*: since *ṛt* is a qualifier of the *liṅga* (the verbal base), there is an application of the rule *tadantavidhi* (extension of the rule to that which ends with it). Thus he says:

"of those ending in the vowel *ṛ*" (*ṛvarṇāntānām*). Regarding "in the absence of *aṅ*": this refers to the alternative view where *aṅ* is not applied, [resulting in the suffix] *ślu* by the rule *śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ ksaḥ*.
The meaning is: "when the substitution of *ksa* was about to occur.

(239) *na dṛśaḥ* | 3|1|47|. Regarding *na dṛśaḥ*: the word *cleḥ* is supplied from the rule *cleḥ si* [Pāṇini 3.1.44], and the word *ksa* is supplied from the rule *śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ ksaḥ* [Pāṇini 3.1.45].

And this [rule] continues [to apply]. Thus he says: "There is no *ksa* for the *cli* of the root *dṛś*. The intention is that if there were the substitute *ksa*, the form would be *adṛkṣat*. Regarding *adrākṣīt*: with the augment *am* in the *sic* suffix, the *ṛ*-vowel undergoes *yaṇ*-substitution; then, by the rule concerning the increase (*vṛddhi*) of a vowel at the end of a consonant, the *a* is increased; then the *ś* becomes *ṣ*; then that [ṣ] becomes *k*; and then the *s* [becomes *ṣ*].

The intended meaning is that there is the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*. [He] would have seen (*adrakṣyat*). Regarding the root *daṃś* (to bite): this is a root that lacks the augment *iṭ* (*aniṭ*) and has *n* as its penultimate letter (*nopadha*).

The mention of the anusvāra in the grammatical rule is for the sake of brevity (*kṛtānusvāranirdeśaḥ*). "The operation of the fangs" (*daṃṣṭrāvyāpāraḥ*): fangs (*daṃṣṭrāḥ*) are the large teeth located at the base of the jaw; their "operation" means the action consisting of wounding and so forth. Now, an objection:

The word *daśana* is derived from the verbal root *daṃś* with the suffix *lyuṭ*. In this case, the elision of the nasal *n* by the rule *ṭhaniditām* is not possible, because *lyuṭ* lacks the *kṅit* designation. Furthermore, the elision of the nasal *n* by the rule *diṃśasañja* is also not possible, as that rule applies only when the suffix *śap* follows. Thus, [the form] *daśana* [is established].

Regarding the explanation of the meaning, [the author] asks "How so? and replies: "Because it belongs to the *pṛṣodarādi* group. "For this very reason" means that others believe the elision of the letter *n* occurs precisely because of the mention of the word *daśana*.
"Even for them" refers to those who assert that "the elision of the letter *n* occurs by way of irregular derivation (*nipātana*) within the *pṛṣodarādi* group."

The meaning is that the intended purport lies solely in the *nipātana* (the specific grammatical rule of formation), and not in the indication of the meaning "to bite" (*daṃśa daśane*) found in the list of verbal roots (*dhātupāṭha*); this is the underlying thought. Anticipating the objection that there is no decisive criterion for choosing one over the other, he says: "because the indication of the meaning is a modern [addition]," referring to the fact that the indication of meanings applies to all verbal roots.

In *tveṣṭa*, the *t* of *tasi* becomes *ṣṭu* [by *ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ*]. *tvekṣyati*, *tvekṣyate*: here, by the rules for *syapratyaya*, there is *katva* (change of *s* to *ṣ*) and *ṣatva* (change of *t* to *ṣ*). *tveṣatu*, *tveṣatām*. *atveṣat*, *atveṣata*. *tveṣet*, *tveṣeta*. Regarding *tviṣyāt*: because the *yāsuṭ* augment in the *āśīr-liṅ* is *ikit* (marked with *k*), it does not [cause the elision of the final vowel].

There is the *guṇa* substitution for the light penultimate vowel. In *tvikṣīṣṭa*, there is no *guṇa* because the suffix is *kit* by the rule "liṅsicāvātmanepadeṣu. In the *luṅ* [aorist] parasmaipada, the *ksa* substitute is applied to the *cli* by the rule "śala igupadhād aniṭaḥ ksaḥ";
there is no *guṇa* because it is *kit*. Thus he says: *atvikṣat*, etc. In the *luṅ* ātmanepada, the *ksa* substitute is applied to the *cli*.

The intention is that, having considered [the rule] *matvā ṭhātmanepadaṣvanataḥ*, since the substitution of *ad* is impossible, there is either the substitution of *at* (the final letter) or, after the elision of the final letter of the suffix *ksa*, the form [is derived] by the application of the *pararūpa* (single-substitute) rule. The root *yaja* means "to worship the gods. This is without the augment *iṭ*. Thus: *yajati* and *yajate*. He worships the gods, causes them to assemble, or gives [them offerings].
This is the meaning.
(240) *liṭaḷbhyāsasyobhayeṣām* | Pāṇini 6.1.17. When the suffix *ṇal* is applied and reduplication has occurred, resulting in the form *yayāja*, [the rule] *liṭaḷbhyāsasyobhayeṣām* applies.

From the rule *ṭhṣyaṅḥ saṃprasāraṇam*, the term *saṃprasāraṇam* is understood to carry over. Both the roots mentioned in the sūtra *vacisvapiyajādīnām* and those mentioned in the sūtra *grahijyāvayi* are included by the word "both" (*ubhaya*). Thus he says: "of the *vaci*-class and the *grahi*-class."

And so on. Here, by the phrase "of *vaci* and the others," *vaci*, *svapi*, and the *yaj*-class verbs are intended. The *yaj*-class begins with "√*yaj* (to worship the gods)" and extends up to "√*ṭu o śvi* (in the senses of motion and growth).
As it has been said: "√*yaj*, √*vap*, √*vah*, √*vas*, as well as √*veñ* and √*vyeñ*."

"Hveñ, vadi, śvi, and these nine beginning with yaj—these are [the roots]. Because vaci and svapi are not included among those [nine], they are mentioned separately. By the phrase "of grahi, etc.," however, grah, jyā, vayi, vyadhi, vaś, vic, vṛśc, pracch, and bhṛjj are intended.

Regarding *iyāja*: the intention is that when the *y* of the reduplicated syllable undergoes *saṃprasāraṇa*, becoming *i*, the single-substitute form (*pūrvarūpa*) is applied by the rule *saṃprasāraṇācca*.
(241) *vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti* [Pāṇini 6.1.15].

When *yaja* is in the state of having undergone reduplication (*dvitva*), and after the semivowel *y* of the reduplicated syllable has been vocalized (*saṃprasāraṇa*) and the resulting form is *iyajatuḥ*, [the rule] *vacisvapiyajādīnām kiti* applies. In the rule *vacisvapi*, the mention of the letter *i* (in *svapi*) is for the sake of the sūtra; there is an absence of vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇābhāva*) by virtue of the sūtra itself. The word "etc. (*ādi*) is connected only with *yaji*, and not with the others.
Regarding the expression *vacisvapibhyām*: if that were the case, the meaning would be "of *vaci* and so forth, as well as *svapi* and so forth, and *yaj* and so forth.

If that were so, the separate mention of *svapi* would be redundant; for within the *ad*-class (*adādigaṇa*), starting from the root *vaca* (lug-vikaraṇa) meaning "to speak" up to the sixth root *ñi ṣvap* meaning "to sleep," [all would already be included].
This is because [the desired form] is already established by the inclusion of *vaci* and so forth; thus he says: "and of *vaci*, *svapi*, and the roots beginning with *yaj*.

Now, one might object: when the form *yaj-atus* is established, since *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization) occurs because it is subsequent to reduplication (*dvitva*), then according to the maxim "in a conflict of rules, that which is once superseded is superseded forever," reduplication would not take place.

Anticipating the question "How is this obtained?", he says: "Again, by occasion" (*punaḥ prasaṅga*). Regarding the form *ījatuḥ*: when *yajatus* is established, after the application of *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization) and the subsequent formation of the single substitute (*pūrvarūpa*), reduplication occurs, followed by the long vowel *savarṇadīrgha*;
this is the intended meaning. Thus, in this case, the rule *vacisvapi-* applies to the *liṭ* suffix that is *kit*, whereas [the rule *liṭyabhyāsasyobhayeṣām*] applies to that which is not *kit*.

Regarding the periphrastic perfect (*liṭ*), the established rule is the sūtra *liṭaḷbhyāsasya* [Pāṇini 6.1.17]. By the restriction of Bhāradvāja, there is optionally (*veṭ*) the augment *iṭ* after *thal*. Once reduplication has occurred, because the root is not marked with *k*, the rule *vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti* [Pāṇini 6.1.15] does not apply; thus, by *liṭaḷbhyāsasya*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the *yakāra* in the reduplicated syllable. This is what he expresses by saying *iyajitha*.

Regarding *iyaṣṭha*: in the alternative where the root is not treated as taking the augment *iṭ*, the substitution of *ṣ* for *j* occurs by the rule *vraśca* etc., and then *th* becomes *ṭh* by the rule *ṣṭuan*.

[The forms are] *ījathuḥ*, *īja*; *iyāja*—*iyaja*; *ījiva*, *ījima*. Regarding *īje*: because of the *kit* designation by the rule *ṭhasaṃyogā’d*, the semivowel substitution (*saṃprasāraṇa*) occurs by the rule *vacisvapī*, followed by reduplication and the lengthening of homogeneous vowels (*savarṇadīrgha*).
The verbal root *yaj* (to sacrifice). [In the perfect tense: *ījāte*, *ījire*—the augment *iṭ* is applied according to the rule for roots beginning with *krī*.
*Ījiṣe*, *ījāthe*, *ījidhve*; *īje*, *ījivahe*, *ījimahe*. Regarding *yaṣṭā*:

when the suffix *tās* is added, the *j* becomes *ṣ* by the rule beginning with *vraśca*, and the *t* becomes *ṭ* by the rule of *ṣṭu*. [In the future tense: *yakṣyati*, *yakṣyate*—here, the *j* becomes *ṣ* by the rule beginning with *vraśca*.
The intention is that by the rule *ṣṭhivuklamvācamāṃ śit* (Pāṇini 8.3.62), there is the substitution of *k* for *ṣ*, and then *ṣ*-hood for *s*. Regarding *ayākṣīt*:
in the *sic* suffix, there is the *vṛddhi* strengthening conditioned by a final consonant; the intention is that *j* becomes *ṣ*, *ṣ* becomes *k*, and *s* becomes *ṣ*. Regarding *ayaṣṭa*:

when the form *ayajsta* is established, the *s* is elided by the rule *jhalo jhali* (Pāṇini 6.4.10); then *j* becomes *ṣ*, and [the preceding *ṣ*] becomes *ṭ* by the rule *ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ* (Pāṇini 8.4.41).

The letter *takāra* becomes *ṭa*. [The forms are] *ayakṣātām*, *ayakṣata*; [the conditionals are] *ayakṣyat*, *ayakṣyata*. The root *ḍu vap* means "in the continuity of seeds"; that is to say, the sowing of seeds in fields for the purpose of sprouting.
Thus he says: "scattering in the field. [It is stated that] "the root *vapi* has the meaning of scattering."

Regarding the phrase "in the case of *sanyaṅe*," the *Bhāṣya* states: "and [the rite of] conception (*garbhādhāna*). The sense is that this is seen to be so in such passages as: "O vigilant ones, protect this thread; let not the seeds of others be sown in your field. The phrase "this [root √*sic*] also [means] cutting" has the word "occurs" (*vartate*) as its ellipsis.

"He shaves his hair" (*keśān vapati*) means "he cuts. This root is *aniṭ* (lacking the *iṭ* augment). Regarding *uvāpa*: the intention is that by the rule *liṭ-abhyāsasya*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the reduplicated syllable when the suffix is not *kit*. However, when it is *kit*, as in the case of *vacisvapi*, vocalization occurs before reduplication; thus [the forms] are *ūpatuḥ* and *ūpuḥ*.

*Upapitha*—*upatha*, *ūpathuḥ*, *ūpa*; *uvāpa*—*uvapa*, *ūpiva*, *ūpima*. *Ūpe*—*ūpāte*, *ūpire*; *ūpiṣe*, *ūpāthe*, *ūpidhve*; *ūpe*, *ūpivahe*, *ūpimahe*. *Vaptā*—*vapsyati*, *vapsyate*. *Vapatu*, *vapatām*; *avapat*, *avapata*; *vapet*.
*vapeta* (he should sow): from the root *vapi*, with the suffix *yāsuṭ* in the sense of a benediction (*āśis*), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule *vacisvapi-*.

*vapsīṣṭa*: this is the form with the suffix *sīyuṭ*. *praṇyavāpsīt*: in the *luṅ* tense, in the *parasmaipada*, with the suffix *sic*, there is vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*) conditioned by a consonant ending; the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* occurs by the rule *nergade*.

*avāptām*, *avāpsuḥ*. Regarding *avapta*: in the ātmanepada, there is elision of *s* by the rule "luṅlaṅlṛṅkṣv aḍudāttaḥ" [sic; actually referring to Pāṇini 6.4.71] and "jhalo jhali" [Pāṇini 6.4.10]. *Avapsātām*. Regarding the root *vah* in the sense of "carrying": this is aniṭ (does not take the iṭ augment). *Vahati*, *vahate*. *Uvāha*: the intention is that there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the reduplicated syllable when there is no *ak* suffix, according to the rule "liṭaḷbhyāsasyobhayeṣām" [Pāṇini 6.1.17].
When the semivowel substitution (*saṃprasāraṇa*) has been applied by the rule *ṭhvacisvapī*, reduplication occurs: *ūhatuḥ*, *ūhuḥ*.

According to the restriction of Bhāradvāja, there is optionally the augment *iṭ* in the case of the suffix *thal*; thus he says: *uvahitha*. Because of the prohibition *na śasadadeti*, the rule *thali ca seṭi* does not apply here. Now, in the case where *thal* lacks the augment *iṭ*:

He says: *sahivahorodavarṇasya*. The meaning is that for the vowel *o* of the roots *sah* and *vah*, there is the substitution of *ot* when *ḍh*, *ṛ*, *l*, or elision (*lopa*) follows. The intention is that the substitution of *ot* sets aside the rule for lengthening (*dīrgha*) prescribed by the rule *ḍhralopa*. Thus, in *uvoḍha*, there is the substitution of *ot* after [the application of] *ḍhatva*, *dhatva*, *ṣṭutva*, and the elision of *ḍh*.

And [in the case] of *lṛṭ* with *sya*, *h* becomes *ḍh*, which becomes *k*, and then *ṣ*-hood [is applied]. Thus he says: "he will carry" (*vakṣyati*), "she will carry" (*vakṣyate*). [Imperative: "let him carry" (*vahatu*), "let them carry" (*vaha-tām*). [Aorist: "he carried" (*avahat*), "they carried" (*avahata*). [Optative: "he may carry" (*vahet*), "he might carry" (*vaheta*). [Precative: "may he be carried" (*uhyāt*). Regarding "he carried" (*avākṣīt*): there is *vṛddhi* by the rule for stems ending in consonants (*halanta-lakṣaṇa-vṛddhi*), and *ḍh*, *k*, and *ṣ* as before. Regarding "they two carried" (*avoḍhām*): [the rule applies to] *jhal*.
The idea is that when the *s* is elided by the rule "jhalī" (Pāṇini 8.2.26), there is the substitution of *ḍha*, *dha*, *ṣṭu*, and the elision of *ḍha*, as well as the substitution of *o*.
Thus, [we have] *avākṣuḥ*. In the case of *usi* and *sic*, there is vṛddhi, followed by the substitutions of *ḍha*, *ka*, and *ṣa*. [The forms are] *avoḍhāḥ*, *avoḍham*, *avoḍha*;
*avākṣam*, *avākṣva*, *avākṣma*. [The form] *avoḍhe* is in the *luṅ* [lakhāra] for the *ātmanepada*.

In the third person singular (*prathamapuruṣaikavacana*), when *ava-hs-ta* is established, there is the elision of *s* (*salopaḥ*), followed by the substitution of *ḍha* for *ha*, the substitution of *dha* for *ṣa*, the substitution of *ṣṭu* for *ṭa*, the elision of *ḍha* (*ḍhalopaḥ*), and the substitution of *o* for *a*. Thus, *avakṣātām* [is formed]; the intention is that *ḍha* replaces *ka* in *ātām* after *sic*. As for *avakṣata*, the substitute *at* is applied according to the rule "in the *ātmanepada*, [for the final *a*] of that which does not end in *n*" (*ātmanepadeṣvanataḥ*).

*avoḍhām*, *avakṣi*, *avakṣvahi*, *avakṣmahi*; *avakṣyat*, *avakṣyata*. Thus, the roots ending in *vah* have been explained as having a circumflex (*svarita*) accent. The root *vas* is *aniṭ* (lacking an *iṭ* augment). When a *kit* suffix follows in the *liṭ* (perfect), there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the reduplication according to the rule *liṭaḷbhyāsasya*. Therefore, he says: *uvāsa*. In the case of a *kit* [suffix],...
However, when the *saṃprasāraṇa* has been applied by the rule *vacisvapi...* and reduplication (*dvitva*) and so forth have occurred,

the rule *liṭaḷbhyāsasya...* would not apply to the reduplication because it does not form part of either a substitute (*ādeśa*) or an affix (*pratyaya*), and thus the application of *ṣatva* (the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*) would not otherwise be obtained.

(241) *śāsivasighasāṃ ca* | Pāṇini 8.3.60. The words *śāsi*, *vasi*, and *ghasi*: from the rule *saheḥ sāḍaḥ saḥ*, the genitive form *saḥ* is understood to carry over. Furthermore, the governing rules *iṇkoḥ* and *apadāntasya mūrdhanyaḥ* are also in force.

Regarding this, he says: "by means of the root *iṇ* and the *ka*-class [of consonants]. Considering that there is an option for *iṭ* (*veṭ*) before the suffix *thal* according to the rule of Bhāradvāja, he says:

*uvasthitha*, *uvastha*. Because of the prohibition "not after *śas*, *sad*, or *ad*," the rule "also before *thal* when it has *iṭ*" does not apply. [The forms are: *ūṣathuḥ*, *ūṣa*, *uvāsa* (or *uvasa*), *ūṣiva*, *ūṣima*.
The augment *iṭ* is applied by the rule *krādiniyamāt*. When the form *vas sya ti* is established, he says: *saḥ syārddhadhātuke*.

The meaning of this is that the *s* is replaced by *t*. Thus we have *vasatu*, *avasat*, *vaset*, and *uṣyāt*. In the case of the benedictive (*āśīrliṅ*), because the suffix *yāsuṭ* is marked as *kit*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the *vas* by the rule *sāsivasīṣu*.

The intention is that [the change] becomes *ṣ*. Regarding *avātsīt*: when the suffix *sic* is added, there is the *vṛddhi* substitution conditioned by a final consonant, and the *s* of the root becomes *t*.

Regarding *avātām*: when the form *avas + tām* is established, after the *vṛddhi* substitution, the *s* is elided by the rule "jhalo jhali" (Pāṇini 8.2.26). Then, relying on the designation of the suffix (*pratyayalakṣaṇa*), because an *ārddhadhātuka* suffix beginning with *s* follows, the *s* of the verbal root [becomes *ṣ*].
In the form *saḥ si*, the *t* is [retained]. In reality, however, [the forms are] *avātsva*, *avāsma*, and *avatsyat*.

The root *veñ* is *aniṭ*. Because it has the marker *ñ*, it is *ubhayapadī* (active and middle). *Tantusantānaḥ* refers to the specific act of spreading threads crosswise for the purpose of weaving cloth. [Thus one says] *vayati* or *vayate*; in the presence of the *śap* suffix, there is the substitution of *ay*.
*veño vayiḥ*. He explains the sūtra by supplying the remainder of the text: *vā syālliṭi*.
The intention is that this is because the word *anyatarasyām* is understood from the previous rule, *liṅyanyatarasyām*.
[He says] "for the purpose of pronunciation" (*uccāraṇārtha*); the intention is that if the vowel *i* were marked with the *it*-designation, the augment *num* would occur.

Regarding the word *uvāca*: in the case of the root *vac*, because it belongs to the *yajādi* class, when the *liṭ* suffix follows that is not marked with *k*, there is *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization) of the *v* by the rule *liṭaḷbhyāsasya*, and subsequently the *upadhā-vṛddhi* (penultimate vowel strengthening); this is the intended meaning.
However, there is no *saṃprasāraṇa* of the *y* here, according to the rule *liṭi vayo yaḥ*.

The intention is that the negation of that [substitution] will be stated immediately hereafter. Although, even in the absence of the substitution of *vay* for *vye* before the suffix *ṇal*, the form *uvāya* could be established— by doubling the root, applying *saṃprasāraṇa* to the reduplicated syllable, applying the *vṛddhi* augment by the rule "aco ñṇiti," and then applying the *āy* substitute— nevertheless, [the rule is necessary] for the sake of forms such as *ūyatuḥ*.
Because the substitution of *vay* is necessary, it is appropriately introduced here as well.
When *ve-atus* is established, and the substitution of *vay* has been applied, [Pāṇini 6.1.16] states:
"In place of the roots *grah*, *jyā*, *vay*, *vyadh*, *viṣṭhiv*, *vicat*, *vṛśc*, *pṛcch*, and *bhṛjj*, [the substitution of *saṃprasāraṇa* occurs] before an affix marked with *ṅ*."
And [the word *kiti*] from Aṣṭādhyāyī 6.1.16 is understood here;
by the word *ca*, the term *kiti* from the rule *vacisvapiyajādīnām* (6.1.15) is conjoined. The phrase *ṣyaṅḥ saṃprasāraṇam* (6.1.13) is also carried over. Thus he says: "of these," and so forth.

In this context, because of the association with *grah* and other roots that take the *parasmaipada* (active voice), there is no inclusion of the *ātmanepada* (middle voice) root *vay* listed as "ṭhaya vaya paya gatau" (to go). Since the vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of *vay* is already established by its belonging to the *yajādi* group, the explicit mention of *vay* here is for the sake of clarity; this is clear from the Bhāṣya.

"Regarding the possibility of the substitution of *y* for *i*": this means that since the rule "there is no substitution of a semivowel (*saṃprasāraṇa*) when a semivowel [is already present]" serves as an indicator (*liṅga*), it is understood that the semivowel substitution occurs before the final semi-vowel; thus, there arises the possibility of substituting the semivowel *i* for the letter *y*.

(243) *liṭi vayo yaḥ* |6|1|38|. Regarding *liṭi vayo*: "There is no *saṃprasāraṇa*"—the intention is that this follows from the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the rule *na saṃprasāraṇe saṃprasāraṇam*. And thus, for the letter *yakāra*...

The intention is that, although the *saṃprasāraṇa* is prohibited [in general], the *saṃprasāraṇa* of the letter *v* does take place; thus he says: *ūyatuḥ*. (244) *vaścāsyānyatarasyāṃ kiti* | Pāṇini 6.1.39.

The rule "vaścāsyāṭṭliṭi vayo yaḥ" (Pāṇini 6.1.38) continues [from the previous sūtra]. Therefore, he says: "of *vayi*, etc. Regarding *uvayitha*: because it is not marked with *k* (*akit*), *va* does not [substitute for *y*]. Having raised the doubt that there might be an optional *iṭ* augment in *thali* due to the root ending in a vowel (*ajanta*) and having the letter *a*, he says: "Because there is no *tās-* [augment] after *vayi*, there is invariably *iṭ* in *thali*."
Since [the root] is prescribed specifically for the *vayerliṭ* (periphrastic perfect), it does not occur in the *tās* (the conditional suffix).

Consequently, because the prohibition of *iṭ*—as in the rules "after a root ending in *ṭh*" (*ṭhacaḥ*) and "after a root that is short *a* in its original form" (*upadeśe 'tvataḥ*)—does not apply here, the meaning is that it is invariably *niṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*) from the class beginning with *kram*. Thus, it is said: "that which exists in the *tās* and is invariably *niṭ*."

The commentary [states]: *ūyathuḥ*, *ūvathuḥ*; *ūya*, *ūva*; *uvāya*, *uvaya*; *ūyiva*, *ūviva*; *ūyima*, *ūvima*. Now, one might ask: since the root *vay* is not marked with Ñ (añit), how can it belong to both voice classes (*ubhayapada*)? To this he replies: "by virtue of the status of being a substitute" (*sthānivadbhāvena*). Thus: *ūye*, *ūve*. [This is so] by the rule: *vaścāsyānyatarasyām*.
There is no substitution of *v* for *va*. In the absence of *v*, there is a prohibition of *saṃprasāraṇa* for the letter *y* by the rule "ṭhliṭi vayo yaḥ".
For the letter *v*, there is *saṃprasāraṇa* either by the rule "ṭhgrahijye" or "ṭhvacisvapī". [The forms are:
*ūyāte*, *ūyire*; *ūyiṣe*, *ūyāthe* [or *ūyiḍhÂaveṭ*, *ūyidhve*].

*ūye*, *ūyivahe*, *ūyimahe*. The augment *iṭ* is applied according to the rule for roots beginning with *krī*. Similarly, there are forms such as *ūvāte* and *ūvire*. Regarding the phrase "in the absence of the substitution of *vay*" (*vayādeśābhāve*), the remainder [of the meaning] is: "when, because the root belongs to the *yajādi* class, the substitution of semivowels for vowels (*saṃprasāraṇa*) would have been required by the rules *liṭabhyāsasya* and *vacisvapi*."

(245) *veñaḥ* |6|1|40|. From the rule *liṭi vayo yaḥ*, the word *liṭi* is understood; from the rule *na saṃprasāraṇe saṃprasāraṇam*, the phrase *na saṃprasāraṇam* is also understood. Thus he says: *veñaḥ*.
"No," [it is said]. Here, the word *kit* does not recur. Thus he says: "vavau.
In the case of the *ṇal* suffix, because the substitution of semivowels (*saṃprasāraṇa*) is prohibited, the substitution of *ā* by "ādeca upadeśe" (Pāṇini 6.1.45) applies;

then, by "āta au ṇalaḥ" (Pāṇini 7.1.34), the substitution of *au* for *ā* occurs, and finally, by "vṛddhireci" (Pāṇini 6.1.88), the *vṛddhi* increment is applied to form the word. As for "vavatuḥ," [the rule] "ādecaḥ" [applies].

Thus, by the rule "āto lopaḥ" [Pāṇini 6.4.64], there is elision of the long *ā* in the present tense (*ātve*). Similarly, we have *vavuḥ*. According to the restriction of Bhāradvāja, there is optionally *iṭ* in *thal* (the second person singular perfect ending); since the root *veñ* is *aniṭ* before the affix *tās*, [there is no *iṭ* in that case]. Therefore, he says: *vavitha* or *vavātha*. In the alternative where *iṭ* is present, even though the affix is not *akit*, the elision of the long *ā* occurs because of the subsequent presence of *iṭ*. Thus: *vavathuḥ*, *vava*, *vavau*, *vavima*.

*vavima*. By the rule *krādiniyamādiṭ*, [the augment] *iṭ* is applied: *vave*. [In the dual: *vavāte*; [in the plural: *vavire*. [In the middle voice: *vaviṣe*, *vavāthe*, *vavidhve* (with the optional *iṭ*), *vave*, *vavivahe*, *vavimahe*. In the periphrastic future (*luṭ*), by the rule *tāsi*, there is *ātvam* (substitution of *ā* for the root vowel): *vāsyati*, *vāsyate*. [In the imperative: *vayatu*, *vayatām*. [In the imperfect: *avayat*, *avayata*. [In the optative: *vayet*.
*vayeta* means "he should weave. This is the optative (āśīr-liṅ) with the suffix *yās* and the augment *iṭ*;

because it is *kit*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule *vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti*, followed by the formation of the single substitute [of the preceding and following vowels] (*pūrvarūpa*), and then lengthening by the rule *akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ*.
*Vāsīṣṭa* is the middle voice (ātmanepada) optative; the form is derived from the addition of *sīyuṭ* and the substitution of *ā* for *i*.

*vāsīyāstām* (they two should have dwelt). *avāsīt* (he dwelt): when the substitution of *ā* has been made, the option for *iṭ* applies; with the form *avās i s īt* established, there is the elision of the *sij* suffix by the rule "ṭhiṭa īṭi. *avāsiṣṭām*, etc. In the Ātmanepada: *avāsta*, *avāsātām*, etc. [The conditional forms are] *avāsyat*, *avāsyata*. [Next is the root] *vyeñ*.

Regarding the entry *saṃvaraṇe*: because it has the marker *ñ*, it is conjugated in both voices (*ubhayapadī*) and is *aniṭ*. Thus, we have *vyayati* and *vyayate*; with the suffix *śap*, there is the substitution of *ay*. However, in forms beginning with *ṇal* and so on, one might expect *vivyau*, *vivyatuḥ*, and so forth, due to the substitution of *ā*. [To prevent this: (246) *na vyo liṭi* | Pāṇini 6.1.46: [The substitution of *ā* does not take place for the root *vyā* in the *liṭ* tense.]

Regarding this, he says: *na vyo liṭi* (Pāṇini 6.1.46). The term *vya* is a genitive-form citation (*ṣaṣṭhyanta*) of the root *vyai*, which has undergone the substitution of *ā* (i.e., *vya*). The phrase "the substitution of *ā*" is stated because the word *āt* is understood from the previous rule *ādeca upadeśe* (Pāṇini 6.1.45); this is the intended meaning. The phrase "vṛddhi" refers to the rule *aco ñṇiti* (Pāṇini 7.2.115), which applies when the form *vye a* is present in the *ṇal* suffix.

The meaning is "vṛddhi. Thus, the form *vyai-a* is established. Now, one might object: if there is doubling [of the root], then by the rule *liṭ-abhyāsasya*, the semivowel *y* in the reduplicated syllable undergoes *saṃprasāraṇa*; following this, the *pūrvarūpa* (single substitution of the preceding vowel) occurs, and then the *āy-ādeśa* is applied to the subsequent portion, resulting in the form *vivyāye*. This is incorrect, because [the *āy-ādeśa*] would apply prior to the *saṃprasāraṇa*.

Since the letter *y* would be eliminated by the rule *halādiśeṣaḥ* due to its being subsequent [to the preceding consonant], and since the letter *v* would undergo *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization) into *u*, the form *uvyāya* would result; therefore, he says: "Even though it is subsequent" (*paramapi*). Regarding the phrase "of both" (*ubhayeṣām*):
the meaning is that this is due to the force of including the term "of both" (*ubhayeṣām*) in the rule *liṭaḷbhyāsasya*.
He establishes that very point with the words "otherwise" (*anyathā*).

Since [the desired forms] would already be established here through the recurrence (*anuvṛtti*) of the rules *vacisvapiyajādīnām* and *grahijyāvayivyadhiviṣṭivicativṛścatipṛccchatibhṛjjatīnām* solely by virtue of their being marked with the svarita accent, [the mention of those rules] again in the rule *liṭi abhyāsasya*...

The mention of "both" (*ubhayeṣām*) is for the purpose of re-enacting the rule. Thus, it results in a double prescription: that there shall be vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) both of the *vacy*-class verbs and the *grah*-class verbs in the *liṭ* [perfect tense]. Among these, the second prescription is for the purpose of restriction: "for both classes, there is vocalization of the reduplicated syllable only."

It might be argued that [the rule] "not the other" (na itaraḥ) implies that when this *saṃprasāraṇa* occurs in the case of reduplication (*abhyāsa*), the prevention of other operations is established. Thus, he states the resulting forms—*vivyatuḥ*, *vivyuḥ*—once the *saṃprasāraṇa* of the *yakāra* of the reduplication has been accomplished in the present instance, by means of the rule "vacisvapi... (*vacisvapi-*) [Pāṇini 6.1.15].
The intention is that when there is *saṃprasāraṇa* and doubling, the rule *yaṇ* applies.

Regarding the *thali* suffix, having raised the doubt concerning the optional application of *iṭ* by the restriction of Bhāradvāja, he says: *iḍatyarti*. As for *vivyayitha*, the intention is that because it is not *akit*, there is *saṃprasāraṇa* of the reduplicated syllable. [The forms are] *vivyathuḥ*, *vivyatha*, and *vivyāya*.

Regarding *vivyaye*: because the root is not marked with *k*, there is *saṃprasāraṇa* of the reduplication; due to the optional nature of the *ṇit*-affix, there is an option regarding the *vṛddhi* increment—this is the intended meaning. [The forms] *vivyiva*, *vivyima*, and *vivye* are derived as follows: because the root is marked with *k*, there is *saṃprasāraṇa* by the rule *vacisvapi-*; following the formation of the single substitute (*pūrvarūpa*), there is reduplication of the syllable *vī*, and then the *yaṇ* substitution [of *i* for *v*]. [The form] *vivyāte*.

vivyire; vivyiṣe, vivyāthe, vivyiḍhve; vivye, vivyivahe, vivyimahe. Regarding *vyātā*: there is the substitution of *ā* for the vowel *e* in the form *tās*. [The forms are] *vyāsyati*, *vyāsyate*. [Imperative: *vyayatu*, *vyayatām*. [Aorist: *avyayat*, *avyayata*. [Optative: *vyayet*.

*vyayeta*—meaning "he would perish. This is the optative (*āśīr-liṅ*) with the suffix *sīyuṭ*, where *ātva* (the substitution of *ā*) occurs. *avyāsīt*—this is the aorist (*luṅ*) with the suffix *sic*;

after *ātva*, there is the elision of *sic* due to the presence of *iṭ* and *sak*. *avyāsiṣṭām* and so forth follow similarly. [The root] *syat*. The root *hveñ* is without *iṭ*. Because it has the marker *ñ*, it is conjugated in both voices (*ubhayapadī*). [The rule] "and in the sense of calling" indicates the meaning of summoning.

The word intended here is "ṭhāgacchet" and so forth. In the forms *hvayati* and *hvayate*, there is the substitution of *ay* for the root vowel by the rule *śapi*. When suffixes beginning with *ṇal* follow that are not *kit*, the rule *liṭ-abhyāsasya* would require the samprasāraṇa (vowel substitution) of the reduplicated syllable itself; however, this is the case [only] when such suffixes follow.

(247) *abhyastasya ca* |6|1|33|. The phrase "of the reduplicated (*abhyasta*) [root]" is understood. From the rule *hvaḥ saṃprasāraṇam*, the word *hvaḥ*—which is the genitive form of *hve* after the vowel substitution (*ātvam*) has occurred—is carried over. Thus, when the root *hveñ* has become reduplicated, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇam*).

Since the prohibition "there is no *saṃprasāraṇa* when there is already a *saṃprasāraṇa*" would apply once the practice (*abhyāsa*) of the first half has been formed, he says: "it will become reduplicated" (*abhyastībhaviṣyataḥ*). [Objection:
But if there is *saṃprasāraṇa* of the root *hveñ* while it is about to become reduplicated, then [the rule for] doubling (*dvitva*) would be sublated.

Since the semi-vowel *saṃprasāraṇa* occurs first due to its higher priority, then by the maxim "that which is superseded once is superseded for good," the doubling (*dvitva*) would not take place; therefore, he says:
"Then [comes] doubling. This means that doubling occurs after the *saṃprasāraṇa*, and again—

The intended meaning is "due to the cognition [of the rule] by way of logical consequence" (*prasaṅga-vijñānāt*). And so, when *ātvam* has been applied in the case of *ṇal*, after the *saṃprasāraṇa* and the subsequent single-substitute (*pararūpa*) operation, there is doubling of the element *hu*. Then, by the rule *kuhoścuḥ*, there is the substitution of *c* for that [h], followed by the substitution of the *jaś* sound [k].
Finally, by the rule *aco ñṇiti*, there is *vṛddhi*, and after the substitution of *ava*, the final form is established.

He states the form *rūpam*—namely, *juhāva* and *juhuvatuḥ*. In the case of the suffix *atus*, after the substitution of *ā* for *u* (the *ātvam*), the elision of *āl* (*allopa*) is set aside by the rule "of the reduplicated [root]" (*abhyastasya ca*) because it is internal (*antaraṅga*).

Then, due to the non-universality (*anityatā*) of the principle "an operation concerning a vowel (*āṅgam*) is stronger than one concerning a phoneme (*vārṇam*"), the single-substitute *pūrvarūpa* occurs first because it is internal.

The meaning is that when the doubling [of the root] has occurred, *uvaṅ* is substituted. Although this form is established even by means of the *saṃprasāraṇa* [substitution] prescribed for roots ending in *k* in the rule *vacisvapi-vaci-*, nevertheless, it should be understood that because the rules *akiti* and *abhyastasya ca* are more fundamental (*nyāyyatvāt*), they also apply here. Thus, *juhuvuḥ*.
According to the rule of Bhāradvāja, there is optionally *iṭ* before *thal*. Thus he says: *juhotha* or *juhavitha*. [The forms are: *juhuvathuḥ*, *juhuvathuḥ*;

*juhuvathuḥ*, *juhuvathuḥ*; *juhuvathuḥ*, *juhuvathuḥ*; *juhuvathuḥ*, *juhuvathuḥ*; *juhuvathuḥ*, *juhuvathuḥ*; *juhuvathuḥ*, *juhuvathuḥ*. [In the middle voice: *juhuve*, *juhuvāte*, *juhuvire*; *juhuviṣe*.
juhuvāthe, juhuviḍhve, juhuvidhve; juhuve, juhuvivahe, juhuvimahe. [In the periphrastic future] *hvātā*—here there is the substitution of *ā* [for *i*]. *hvāsyati*, *hvāsyate*. *hvayatu*, *hvayatām*.
*ahvayat*, *ahvayata*. *hvayet*, *hvayeta*. *hūyāt*—this is the benedictive (*āśīr-liṅ*).

The intention is that when *yāsuṭ* is in the *ātmanepada*, because it is *kit*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule "vacisvapi... followed by the formation of the single substitute [of the preceding and following vowels] (*pūrvarūpa*), and then lengthening by the rule "akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ". As for *hvāsīṣṭa*, this is the form in the *āśīrliṅ* (precative) with *sīyuṭ*. He states the specific rule for the *luṅ* (aorist):
(248) *lipisicihvāśca* |3|1|53| The term *lipisici* is a singular neuter compound (*samāhāra-dvandva*) formed from the roots *lip*, *sic*, and *hvā*.
[The word *cleḥ*] is supplied from the rule *cleḥ siC* [Pāṇini 3.1.44], and [the word *aṅ*] is supplied from the rule *asyativaktikhyātibhyaḥ* [Pāṇini 3.1.52].
And it follows [from this]. Thus he says: "from these. This refers to the domain of *parasmaipada* (active voice), because an option is prescribed for the *ātmanepada* (middle voice). Thus he says:
(249) *ātmanepadeṣv anyatarasyām* |3|1|54|.

In the *ātmanepada* [forms]: when "āto lopaḥ" (Pāṇini 6.4.64) applies, the sequence is *ahvā-a-t*, at which point the meaning is that the elision of *ā* occurs by "āto lopa iṭi ca" (Pāṇini 6.4.64). Thus: *ahvad*, *ahvatām*, *ahvann*, and so forth.
For the *ātmanepada* in the *luṅ* [aorist], the form is *aṅ*; thus: *ahvata*, *ahvetām*, *ahvanta*, and so forth.
Regarding the alternative view that there is no *aṅ* substitution, he says: *ahvāsta*, *ahvāsātām*, *ahvāsata*, and so forth;

as well as *ahvāsyat*, *ahvāsyata*. [The root] *vad* means "in distinct speech"; that is to say, in clear articulation through the distinction between vowels (*ac*) and consonants (*hal*). This [root] is *seṭ* (possessing the *iṭ* augment). [Examples include: *acccha vadati* ("he speaks clearly"), and *ṭhacche*.

The word *accha* is an indeclinable used in the sense of "facing" (*abhimukhya*). Its meaning is "speaking towards. The intention is that, because it functions as a *gati* (preverb) according to the rule *accha gatyarthavadeṣu*, it must be placed before the verbal root. Considering that there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the reduplicated syllable of the perfect tense (*liṭ*) by the rule *liṭaḷbhyāsasya* when followed by an affix beginning with a non-guttural (*akit*), he says: *uvāda* (in the case of an *akit* affix).
Regarding the *liṭ* [perfect] tense, however, one should consider that since the rule "vacisvapiyajādīnām" (Pāṇini 6.1.15) applies, the *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization) occurs before reduplication;
thus, after reduplication, a long vowel by *savarṇadīrgha* (Pāṇini 6.1.101) results. With this in mind, he says: *ūdatuḥ*. As for *uvaditha*:
the intention is that the *saṃprasāraṇa* of the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) occurs after reduplication. *Ūdathuḥ*, *ūda*, *uvāda*—*uvada*, *ūdiva*.
We have spoken [ūdim]. In *vadita*, the suffix *iṭ* is added. *Vadiṣyati*. *Vadatu*.
*Avadat*. *Vadet*. Regarding *udyāt*: because the *yāsuṭ* of the āśīr-liṅ (precative) is *kit*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to the rule *vacisvapi-*.
As for *avādīt*, although the prohibition *neṭ* applies to the *vṛddhi* prescribed by *halanta-lakṣaṇa*, [the substitution occurs] due to *ataḥ*.

Anticipating the objection that there might be an optional *vṛddhi* by the rule "halādi" (Pāṇini 7.2.7), and intending to state that *vṛddhi* occurs because the root *vad* is mentioned separately [from the group of roots ending in *jhal*], he says: "By the rule 'vada-vraja-' (Pāṇini 7.2.3), there is *vṛddhi*.
