The word *añcu* [takes the suffix *kvip*] except when there is an *apādāna* [kāraka]; that is to say, provided there is no mention of an *apādāna*. (Pāṇini 7.2.15) *yasya vibhāṣā*: "When there is an option for a particular [element]."

The phrase *yasya vibhāṣā* means "of which there is an option. Regarding *yasya*, the sense is "from which. The intention is that the augment *iṭ* shall not be applied to the *niṣṭhā* [past passive participle] suffix; this is because the word *niṣṭhāyām* is understood from the rule *śvīdito niṣṭhāyām*, and the word *neṭ* is understood from the rule *neḍ vaśi*. Now, one might ask: since the root *añc* is invariably accompanied by the augment *iṭ*, how can [the prohibition apply to it]?

In some places, because of the state of being "veṭ" (having the augment *iṭ*), he says: "or *udita*. Regarding "samanka": the meaning is "joined together" (*saṅgata*). This is the past passive participle (*kta*) from the root *añc* preceded by the prefix *sam*. There is a prohibition of the *iṭ* augment that would otherwise apply by the rule *ārddhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ*. By the rule *aniditāṃ hala upadhāyāḥ kṅiti*, there is the elision of the nasal (*n*). By the rule *cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ*, there is the substitution of *k* for *c*. [Thus] *udakta* means water that has been drawn up.

"From the well" (kūpāt) means "drawn out. The point here is that because there is the co-occurrence of an ablative case (apādāna), the substitution of *na* does not apply. Regarding the root *vraścū* in the sense of "cutting," it is indicated by its *ścutva* [substitution of *ś* for *s*]. From this root, the suffix *kta* is added; there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to the rule *grahijyā*; and since it is marked with *ū*, it optionally takes *iṭ*, whereby [the rule] *yasya*... [applies].

In the case of *vibhāṣe*, there is no *iṭ* augment; by the rule *ca-koḥ*, the *ca* becomes *ka*; by the rule *ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ*, the *ṣṭu* (the *ṣ*) of the *niṣṭhā* suffix becomes *ṇa*; and because that [change] is considered asiddha, the *sa* of the root is elided by the rule *skoḥ saṃyogādyor ante ca* due to being followed by a *jhal* letter, resulting in the form *vṛkṇa*. This is the established conclusion. In that context, because the change to *ṇa* is asiddha, [the rule] *vraśca-* applies due to being followed by a *jhal* letter.

To address the possibility that there might be *ṣatva* (the substitution of *ṣ* for *s*), he says: "The substitute *niṣṭhā* [is treated as] *ṣatva*. Thus, when *ṣatva* is to be applied by the rule *ṭhvraścabhrasjāṃ saṭi*, since the *natva* (substitution of *n* for *t*) is not considered *asiddha* (non-existent), the condition of being followed by a *jhal* consonant is absent; therefore, there is no *ṣatva*. Examples regarding accentuation (*svara*), suffixes (*pratyaya*), and the application of *iṭ* are clear in the Bhāṣya.

(834) *pariskandaḥ* in the speech of the Easterners and the Bharatas. 8|3|75. *pariskandaḥ* in the speech of the Easterners and the Bharatas. This sūtra occurs under the governing rule (*adhikāra*) "a cerebral [substitute] is substituted for [an al] not at the end of a word" (*apadāntasya mūrdhanyaḥ*).
"By the preceding" refers to the preceding sūtra, *pareśca*. [The meaning is: after the prefix *pari*, [the *s* of] the root *skand* [is optionally replaced by a cerebral].

The meaning of that [sūtra] is "it may be *sasya* or *ṣa*. By this, since an option for *ṣatva* (the substitution of *ṣ*) would otherwise apply, the absence of *ṣatva* is prescribed (*nipātyate*) among the Eastern Bharatas; such is the meaning. Regarding *pariskanda*: from the root *skand* preceded by *pari*, there is the elision of the letter *t* in the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*).

(835) *divo 'vijigīṣāyām* | 8|2|49|. The analysis of the rule is: *divaḥ*, *a-vijigīṣāyām*. In the case of *dyaūnaḥ*, the meaning is "praised. By the rule *cchvoḥ śūḍanunāsike ca*, *ūṭh* is substituted [for the *v* of *div*]. However, when there is a desire for victory (*vijigīṣā*), it is *dyaūtam*—that is, gambling for the sake of victory.
The sense is "of the process" (*pravṛtteḥ*).
[The rule] *nirvāṇo’vāte* [is stated]; the agent is not [the referent]. The verbal root preceded by the prefix *nir-* signifies destruction.

It occurs [in the sense of] proceeding and ceasing. Regarding that meaning of the verbal root (*dhātvartha*), if the wind is the agent, then the suffix *naṭ* (the past passive participle suffix *kta*) is not applied; this is the meaning. [Examples are: "the fire has been extinguished" (*nirvāṇo 'gniḥ*) or "the sage has ceased [from worldly activity]" (*nirvāṇo muniḥ*). The meanings are, respectively, "destroyed" (*naṣṭa*) and "ceased" (*uparata*).
The suffix *kta* is applied in the sense of the agent according to the rule "gatyarthākarmaka... (Pāṇini 3.4.72). [The example is: "the wind has subsided" (*nirvāto vātaḥ*). In this case...

The intention is that [the word *vāta*] does not undergo the substitution of *na* because it functions as the agent (*kartṛ*). However, in the expression "the lamp is extinguished by the wind" (*nirvāṇo dīpo vātena*), since the wind is intended to be the instrument (*karaṇa*), it lacks the status of an agent; therefore, the substitution of *na* must be applied. But in the sense of a state (*bhāva*), one says "windless" (*nirvātam*) [meaning "by means of the wind"].

(837) *śuṣaḥ kaḥ* | Pāṇini 8.2.51. Regarding *śuṣaḥ kaḥ*: [the phrase] "from the rule *niṣṭhātaḥ*" [is understood]. The resulting meaning is that the suffix *ka* shall replace the *t* of the *niṣṭhā* [suffixes *kta* and *ktavatu*] following the root *śuṣ*.

(838) *paco vaḥ* | Pāṇini 8.2.52. The meaning of *paco vaḥ* is that the substitute *va* shall occur for the *niṣṭhā* [kṛt suffix -ta] following the root *pac*. Thus, in the form *pakva*, because the substitution of *va* is considered *asiddha* (not yet established), the substitution of *ku* [i.e., *ka*] takes place.

(838) *kṣāyo maḥ* | Pāṇini 8.2.53. The meaning is that for the root *kṣai* in the sense of "wasting away" (*kṣaye*), the letter *m* replaces the *t* of the *niṣṭhā* suffix. Thus, *kṣāma*. The substitution of *ā* [for *ai*] is by the rule *ādeca upadeśe 'śiti*. The *kta* suffix is used in the sense of the agent (*kartari*) because the root has a motion as its meaning and lacks an object (*akarmaka*). [The form is] *kṣīṇa*.
This is the meaning. When the causative sense (*ṇyartha*) is inherent, the meaning is "destroyed" (*kṣapita*).
(839) *styaḥ prapūrvasya* |6|1|23|. Regarding *styaḥ prapūrvasya*: the form *stya*, which is the genitive singular of *styai* after its vowel has been changed to *ā*, is used here.

The term *saṃprasāraṇa* is understood from the rule *ṭhṣyaṅḥ saṃprasāraṇam*, and the term *niṣṭhāyām* is understood from the rule *ṭhsphāya sphī*. Thus he says: "prādityādi" (beginning with *pra*). When the semivowel has been replaced by its corresponding vowel (*saṃprasāraṇa*), the preceding form (*pūrvarūpa*) is applied, and then by the rule *ṭhalaḥ*, the lengthening occurs; thus, the form *prastītaḥ* is established.

(840) *prastyo 'nyatarasyām* | 8.2.54. The word *prastyaḥ* is a locative (*pañcamī*). The meaning is "from the root *syai* preceded by *pra*. The remainder of the rule is *niṣṭhātasya maḥ* ("the *t* of the *niṣṭhā* [past participle] suffix becomes *m*"). Thus, we have *prastīmaḥ*.
The meaning is "become associated.
(841) *anupasargāt phulla-kṣība-kṛśa-ullāghāḥ* | Pāṇini 8.2.55. [The word] *anupasargāt*: these [words] are irregularly formed (*nipātyante*) provided they do not follow a prefix (*upasarga*).

The meaning is that the substitution of *ṭh* for *t* is established by the rule "ṭhāditaśca," which results in the absence of the augment *iṭ*, and the substitution of *u* for *ṛ* is established by the rule "ti ca. However, the root *phal* in the sense of "ripening" (*niṣpatti*) is not included here, because that would entail the necessity of also prescribing the absence of *iṭ* as a nipātana (irregularity). Now, one might ask: how is the form *phullavān* derived when the suffix *ktavatu* is applied?
Since the suffix *ktavatu* is not included by the word *phulla* because the *kta* portion [of *ktavatu*] is devoid of meaning, he says:

"even of a single part of *ktavatu*. Regarding "in *kṣība*, etc.," the meaning is "in *kṣība*, *kṛśa*, and *ullāgha*. Regarding "only of the suffix *kta*," the meaning is "but not even of a single part of *ktavatu*," because [the latter] is devoid of meaning.

"Bhāvaḥ" (the state). "Tasya" (of that) means "of the elision of *tal*. "Kṣībo mataḥ" (drunk is considered): [this is] the suffix *kta* added to the root *kṣīb*, with the elision of *tal* and the absence of the augment *iṭ*. Here, the meaning is precisely "considered" (*mata*) and so forth, by virtue of the irregularity (*nipātana*). [The question] "Why [is it said] 'not preceded by a prefix'? is intended to provide the counter-example "praphulla" in this context.

He states an exception: (842) *āditaśca* |7|2|16|. [The word] "from roots beginning with *ā*" [is understood]. [The meaning is: the suffix *niṣṭhā* (the past passive participle suffixes *-ta* and *-tavant*) shall not have the augment *iṭ*. [This is understood] from the rule *śvīditaḥ* [in 7.2.14], where the word *niṣṭhāyām* [is supplied].

The intention is that "neṭ" (the prohibition of the augment iṭ) is understood from the rule "ṭhneḍvaśi" and continues [into the present context]. Regarding "ti ca": having considered the continuation of the rule "caraphalośca," he says "caraphaloḥ. Regarding "ata utsyāt": the intention is that this is due to the continuation of [the portion] "utparasyātaḥ" from that same rule. Regarding "kiti": [this refers to the condition of being followed by a kṛt suffix marked with the marker K].
The intention is that [the condition] "after *iṇ* when followed by a *kit* suffix" (Pāṇini 7.2.35) is carried over here by means of a "frog-leap" (*maṇḍūkapluti*).

However, in reality, the carry-over of the term "when followed by a *kit*" is both baseless and fruitless; for since those two [roots, *śās* and *vaca*,] are *seṭ* (possessing an *iṭ* augment), there is no suffix beginning with *t* other than the *niṣṭhā* (past participle) suffixes. How then [is it explained]?

The point is that because the word *praphulla* contains a prefix (*pra*), the substitution of *l* for the *t* of the past passive participle suffix (*niṣṭhā*) is impossible. He provides the solution: "phulleti. Now, since the form *phulla* is established simply by adding the suffix *ac* (in the sense of the agent) to the root *phull*, the specific grammatical rule (*nipātana*) for *phulla* is redundant; to this he replies: "sūtraṃ tviti" (but as for the rule...).

Regarding the words *utphulla* and *saṃphulla*: the remainder of the rule is "the substitution of *l* for the final *t* of the *niṣṭhā* suffix. This statement is made for the sake of including the forms with prefixes (*upasarga*).
(843) Pāṇini 8.2.56: *nudavidondatrāghrāhrībhyo 'nyatarasyām*.

Regarding *nudavidonda*: since [the suffix] has not been prescribed for the root *hrī*, and since it is invariably prescribed for the others, this option (*vikalpa*) applies specifically to the ending in *-nta*. "The root belonging to the *raudhādika* class" means the root *vid* in the sense of "investigation" (*vicāraṇe*). "But of *veti*" means of the root *vid* in the sense of "knowledge" (*jñāne*); this [latter root] is *seṭ* (possessing the augment *iṭ*).

Because it is not included among the roots that do not take the augment *iṭ*. Thus he says: "viditaḥ" (known). The point here is that because the *t* of the *niṣṭhā* suffix is separated from the root by the *iṭ* augment, the substitution of *n* for *t* does not occur. Regarding "vinnaḥ" from the root *vid*: this root *vid* meaning 'to exist' is one that does not take *iṭ*; therefore, by the rule "radābhyām," the substitution of *n* for *t* occurs invariably.
*undīti*: This indicates an example.
(844) *śvīdito niṣṭhāyām* | Pāṇini 7.2.14. Regarding *śvīdito niṣṭhāyām*: [The compound] *śvi-īdit* is a collective dvandva; from this, the ablative case is formed.
From the rule "ṭhneḍvaśi," the word "na iṭ" (no *iṭ*) does not cease to apply. Therefore he says: "of the root *śvi*.

(845) *Na dhyākhyāpṛmūrccchimadām* | 8|2|57|. "Not [after] *dhyai*, *khyai*, *pṛ*, *mūrch*, *mad*. The genitive case is used in the sense of the ablative. Therefore he says: "from these. Regarding *dhyāta*: from the root *dhyai*.

The suffix *kta* is applied. By the rule "ādeca upadeśe 'śiti," there is the substitution of *ā*. Here, the substitution of *ṇatva* (nasalization) prescribed by the rule "saṃyogāder ātaḥ" does not occur. Thus, we have *khyātaḥ*. In the alternative view where *khyāñ* is the substitute, because it contains a semi-vowel (*yaṇ*), the *ṇatva* prescribed by "saṃyogāder ātaḥ" does not occur. However, if the *ś* of the substitute *khyā* undergoes *yatva* (substitution of *y*), then [the rule applies].

Since the substitution of *ṇatva* (nasalization) occurring in the section on *ṇatva* is considered *asiddha* (non-existent for the purposes of subsequent operations), the quality of being preceded by a *saṃyoga* does not exist; therefore, there is no possibility of the application of the rule *saṃyogāder ātaḥ*. Furthermore, since the root *khyā*, which is inherently established, has no usage whatsoever in the *ārddhadhātuka* domain, the mention of *khyā* [in the rule] is indeed redundant. Regarding the form *pūrta*: it is derived from the root *pṛ* with the suffix *kta*.

In the case of *mūrch*, the augment *iṭ* is not applied by the rule *ṛt-śyukaḥ kitī*. The substitution of *u* [for the root vowel] occurs by the rule *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya*, followed by the replacement of *u* with *ra*. Here, the substitution of *n* [for *m*] which would have been applicable by the rule *radābhyām* does not take place. Regarding the suffix *kta* after the root *murch*, he says: *rāllopaḥ*. The meaning is that there is elision of the letter *ch*.
Thus, we have *mūrtaḥ*. The augment *iṭ* is not applied here by the rule *āditaśca*. This is because of the elision of *ch*.
The substitution of *n* [for *ṇ*] which would have been required by the rule *ṛtābhyām* does not occur here. There is a lengthening [of the vowel] by the rule *hali ca*. Regarding the word *mata*:

it is derived from the root *madī* (meaning "joy" and "intoxication") with the suffix *kta*; the augment *iṭ* is not added because of the rule *śvīditaḥ*. Here, the substitution of *n* [for *ṇ*] which would have been required by the rule *ṛtābhyām* does not occur.

(846) *vitaḥ* [is substituted for the root *vid*] when followed by the suffixes *bhoga* and *pratyaya*. (Pāṇini 8.2.58). *Bhoga* means that which is enjoyed (*bhujyate*), i.e., an object of enjoyment. *Pratyaya* means that which is recognized (*pratīyate*), i.e., well-known. It is clear from the Bhāṣya that only the root *vid* (in the sense of "to find") is intended here. Thus he says:

Regarding "vidante": this is a nipāta (an irregularly formed word). The meaning is that it is an irregular formation (nipātana) intended to prevent the optional substitution of *n* for *d*, which would otherwise be required by the rule *nudavidonde*. Thus, the meaning is that the substitution of *n* never occurs for the *d* in this word in the senses of "enjoyment" (*bhoga*) and "cognition" (*pratyaya*). Regarding "pratīte": the meaning is "well-known. Regarding "vitaḥ puruṣaḥ": [this refers to a person who is well-known].

The meaning is "renowned. Regarding the term *vinna*, the meaning is "one who has been caught," such as a thief or the like. Here, he establishes the prohibition of the suffix *iṇ* by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*; it should also be understood that this is because of the prohibition [of *iṇ*] by the rule *ekācaḥ*.

(848) *bhītam* [is used for] *śakalam* | Pāṇini 8.2.59. *Bhītam* [is used for] *śakalam*. When the meaning "fragment" (*śakala*) is to be expressed, the absence of the substitution of *n* for the *t* of the suffix *kta* is prescribed as an irregularity (*nipātana*). This word is a conventional term (*rūḍha*) denoting a part characterized by the genus "fragment-ness" (*śakalatva*), without regard for its etymological meaning as a "split. Consequently, and so forth...

Because *bhīta* and *śakala* are synonyms, they are not used together. However, it is clear in the Bhāṣya that when the action of splitting (*bhidikriyā*) is intended, the forms *bhītam* and *bhinnaṃ* both occur.
(849) *ṛṇam ādhamarṇye* | 8|2|60| [The word *ṛṇa* is neuter when it signifies debt.]

"Debt" (*ṛṇa*) [is used] in the sense of "being a debtor" (*ādhamarṇya*). "Being a debtor" (*ādhamarṇya*) is the action of one who is a debtor; it refers to the legal proceeding concerning debt. And that [proceeding] consists of a formal agreement (*saṃvit*) in the form: "The property belonging to another, having been taken, shall be returned after such a time with such an amount of interest. The meaning is: "in that context. "Anything else is *ṛta*."
The meaning is "truth.

(850) *sphāyaḥ sphī niṣṭhāyām* | 6|1|22|. [Sūtra: For the root *sphāy*, there is *sphī* before the suffix *niṣṭhā*. [Commentary: For the root *sphāyī* in the sense of "increase," there shall be the substitution of *sphī* when the suffix *niṣṭhā* follows.
This is the meaning.
(851) *iṇniṣṭhāyām* |7|2|47|. The rule *niraḥ kuṣaḥ* is understood to follow here. Therefore, he says: "after *nir-*".
Now, one might ask: since the form is already established by the rule *ārddhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ*, what is the purpose of this sūtra? To this he replies:

*yasyeti*. Because the root *kuṣ* optionally takes the augment *iṭ* before suffixes such as *tṛc* by the preceding rule *niraḥ kuṣaḥ*, this [sūtra] is intended to set aside the prohibition of *iṭ* that would otherwise apply by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*.

Furthermore, the meaning here is "prescription" (*vidhāna*). Although *iṭ* is already understood from the context, the repetition of *iṭ* is for the purpose of terminating the recurrence of the option (*vā*) mentioned in the rule *svarati-sūti-*.
(852) *vasati-kṣudhor iṭ* (Pāṇini 7.2.52).
The suffix *iṭ* is applied after the roots *vas* and *kṣudh*. The genitive case (*ṣaṣṭhī*) is used in the sense of the ablative (*pañcamyarthe*). Regarding the phrase "after *ktvā* and *niṣṭhā*":

the intention is that this is due to the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the rule "after *kliś*, [the suffix *iṭ* is applied] before *ktvā* and *niṣṭhā*" (*kliśaḥ ktvāniṣṭhayoḥ*). Regarding the word "always" (*nityam*):

since the term *iṭ* was already being carried over (*anuvartamāne*), the mention of *iṭ* once again is for the purpose of excluding [the optionality] derived from the rule "after *svarati*, *sūti*, etc. (*svaratisūtītyataḥ*).

The intention is that [the word] *vā* is used for the purpose of both continuing and discontinuing [the application of previous rules]. This sūtra is intended to override the prohibition of *iṭ* prescribed by the rule *ekāca upadeśe*. Regarding *uṣitaḥ*:
there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) because it belongs to the *yajādi* group, and the retroflex *ṣ* occurs according to the rule *śāsivasighasīnāṃ ca*.

(853) *añceḥ pūjāyām* | Pāṇini 7.2.53. Regarding the rule *añceḥ pūjāyām*: since the suffix *ktvā* would optionally take the *iṭ* augment by the rule *udito vā*, and the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) would be subject to the prohibition of *iṭ* by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*, this sūtra is stated [to provide for the mandatory application]. Thus, we have *añcitaḥ*.
In the rule *nāñceḥ pūjāyām*, there is a prohibition against the elision of the nasal (*nalopa*).
(854) *Lubho vimohane* | 7.2.54. Regarding *lubho vimohane*: the word *lubhaḥ* is in the ablative case. The root *lubh* meaning "to delude" belongs to the *tudādi* class.

The commentary states: "Ṭhvi-mohanaṃ vyākulīkaraṇam" (Ṭhvi means delusion, i.e., causing confusion). The root *lubh* belongs to the Divādi class [meaning 'desire']. Here, only the Taudādi root is intended, because only that has the meaning of 'delusion'; not the Daivādi root, because that has the meaning of 'desire'. Thus he says: "but not in the sense of desire."

Regarding the rule *ṭhtīṣasaha-*: since the suffix *ktvā* would optionally apply [by the previous rule], and since the suffix *niṣṭhā* (the past passive participle suffixes *kta* and *ktavatu*) would be prohibited by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*, this statement [is made]. *Lubhitaḥ* means "deluded. However, in the sense of greed (*gārdhya*), it is *lubdhaḥ*; that is, "one who desires intensely."
In the rule *ṭhmatibuddhipūjārthebhyaśca*, the suffix *kta* is used in the sense of the agent (*kartari*).

(855) *kliśaḥ ktvāniṣṭhayoḥ* | 7|2|50|. Regarding the rule *kliśaḥ ktvāniṣṭhayoḥ*, the remainder [of the sūtra] is: "the augment *iṭ* may optionally occur. This is derived from the rule *svaratisūtisūyatidhūñūdito vā*.

The meaning is that [the word] "veti" (or "vā") is understood by way of *anuvṛtti*. "Always obtained" means by the rule *ārddhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ*. "Established as an option" means because it is marked with the *u* vowel (*ūdit*). "When a prohibition is obtained for the *niṣṭhā* suffix" refers to [the rule] *yasya...* [etc.].
The sense is that it is called *vibhāṣā* because one may optionally [apply] this [rule].
(856) *pūṅśca* | 7.2.51 | "And after the root *pūṅ*. [This refers to the rule regarding] *ktvā* and *niṣṭhā*. [From the rule] *kliśaḥ*...
The intention is that this [term] follows from the rule "ktvāniṣṭhayoḥ. Regarding "iḍ vā":

the intention is that the word "vā" (or) is carried over from "svarati-sūti... and the word "iṭ" is carried over from "iṇ-niṣṭhāyām. Since the prohibition by the rule "śyukaḥ" would otherwise apply, [the option is stated].
This is an alternative view.
(857) Pūṅ-ktvā ca | 1.2.22 | After the root *pūṅ*, the suffix *ktvā* [is optionally seṭ]. From the rule "na ktvā seṭ" [1.2.18], the phrase "not seṭ" (*na seṭ*) is understood to carry over here.
From the rule *ṭhasaṃyogā’d* [Pāṇini 1.2.5], it is understood that the suffix is *kit*; and from the rule *niṣṭhā śīṅ* [Pāṇini 1.2.19], it is understood that the term is *niṣṭhā*.

Therefore, he says: "The suffixes *ktvā* and *niṣṭhā* after the root *pūṅ*, etc. Now, since the desired result would already be established by the rule *na ktvā seṭ* [Pāṇini 1.2.18], for what purpose is the mention of *ktvā* here? To this he replies: "The mention of *ktvā* is for the sake of the subsequent rules."
He establishes that very point: "not because of the condition (upadhā) here.

For in that [context], only the suffix *ktvā* is intended to recur. However, if it were stated simply as "pūṅśca," then only the mention of *niṣṭhā* from the rule "niṣṭhā śī" would continue to recur; such is the intention.

(858) *niṣṭhā śīṅ-svidi-midi-kṣvidi-dhṛṣaḥ* |1|2|19|. From the rule *na ktvā seṭ*, the phrase *na seṭ* is understood to follow. And from the rule *asaṃyogāt*, the word *kit* is also understood. Therefore, he says: "after these [roots], [the suffix] *niṣṭhā* is *seṭ*. [The root] *śīṅ*.

He states the result of the suffix *ṅ* with the words "anubandha" etc. The meaning is that [the suffix] is for the purpose of prohibiting [the application of] *yaṅ*, as per the rule "ṭhśtipā śap". Regarding the form "seśyitavān": here, because there is no prohibition of *kit*-status, there is no *guṇa* substitution due to its being *kit*; this is the intended sense. The statement "the *niṣṭhā* [suffixes] should be stated [to apply] in the sense of the commencement of an action" refers to an action that has been occupied over a long period of time.

The "commencement of action" (*ādikarma*) is that portion of the activity of producing a mat or the like which is characterized by its initial moment. The meaning is that the *niṣṭhā* suffixes should be prescribed after a verbal root when [the action] exists therein. In that case, even though the first moments of the action have already passed, because the action as a whole has not yet reached the state of being completed (*bhūtatva*), the *niṣṭhā* suffixes prescribed for the past tense do not apply.
The section beginning with *prāpta* is commenced.

(859) *ādikarmaṇi ktaḥ kartari ca* | 3|4|71|. Regarding the rule *ādikarmaṇi ktaḥ kartari ca*: because of the word *ca* ("and"), it is understood that the suffix *kta* is also applied in the sense of the abstract action (*bhāva*) and the object (*karman*). [As stated in the commentary: "only in those two... (*tayoreva*).

The sense is that [the action] continues excessively toward the object to be accomplished (*kṛtya*). The *Bhāṣya* provides the examples: "Devadatta has begun the mat" (*prakṛtaḥ kaṭaṃ devadattaḥ*) and "Devadatta has commenced the mat" (*prakṛtavān kaṭaṃ devadattaḥ*).
The understanding is that it refers to the action of the process of undertaking (*ārabhyamāṇa-karaṇa-kriyā*).

(860) *vibhāṣā bhāvādikarmaṇoḥ* | 7.2.17. "Optionally [the suffix] *iṭ* [is added] after the first vowel in the case of the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) when used in the sense of the abstract action (*bhāva*) or the beginning of an action (*ādikarman*). This is derived from the word *āditaḥ* in the rule *āditaśca* and the mention of *niṣṭhā* in the rule *śvīditaḥ*.

The intention is that the word "na" (not) is understood as a carry-over from the rule "ṭhneḍvaśi". Because the prohibition is optional, the augment *iṭ* is permitted in one alternative case. Regarding the example *prasveditaścaitraḥ*: the meaning is an action of perspiring currently being commenced, with Caitra as the agent. Regarding *ñīd-bhiḥ*: those which have *ñi* or *it* [as their indicatory letters] are called *ñītaḥ*.
The meaning of "by those beginning with mid" is that it should be understood that this subject matter concerns the prohibition of *kit* status.

As for "svidyate": the meaning is that in the rule prescribing the prohibition of *kit* status, only the root belonging to the *divādi* class—namely, "ñi-ṣvidā gātra-prakṣaraṇe"—is intended to be included. Thus, [the form] is *sviditaḥ*.

In the alternative view provided by the rule *vibhāṣā bhāve*, the augment *iṭ* is applied. Because the root *svid* is not included in the prohibition of *kit*-affixes, there is no *guṇa* substitution due to its *kit* status. Here, the *iṭ* is prohibited for roots beginning with *svid* by the rule *āditaśca*. However, in the cases of the abstract action (*bhāva*) and the reflexive-passive (*ādikarman*), the *iṭ* is optionally applied.

(861) *mṛṣaḥ titikṣāyām* |1|2|20|. *mṛṣaḥ titikṣāyām*: "titikṣā" means patience (*kṣamā*). "Is it not [the case that] the *niṣṭhā* suffixes are excluded?"—this is a supplement to complete the sense. [The rule] "the *niṣṭhā* suffixes are *śī* and *ṅ*" indicates that the *niṣṭhā* suffixes are intended; [and the rule] "not [before] *ktvā*" [is also relevant].
The intention is that "seṇ" is understood from the rule *seḍiti*, and "kit" is understood from the rule *ṭhasaṃyogādiḥ*; thus, [the sūtra] reads:
(862) *udupadhādbhāvādikarmaṇoranyatarasyām* || 1.2.21 ||.

[The rule] *udupadhādbhāvādikarmaṇoḥ* [states: "After a root having *u* as its penultimate letter, the suffix *kta* is used in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*) or an initial action (*ādikarman*). He gives examples for the abstract action (*bhāva*): *muditam*, etc. He gives examples for the initial action (*ādikarman*): *pradyotitaḥ* and *sādhu pradyotitaḥ*. In the case of the initial action, the suffix *kta* is used in the sense of the agent (*kartari*). Why "having *u* as its penultimate letter"? Consider *viditam*; this is from the root *vid* (in the sense of "knowing").
*Rūpam* [is derived from the root] *gudh*, as in *gudhitam*. The root *gudh* (belonging to the *divādi* class) is *seṭ* (taking the augment *iṭ*). [The rule applies] by *Niṣṭhāyāṃ seṭi* 6.4.52:
"When a *niṣṭhā* suffix with the augment *iṭ* follows, there is the elision of *ṇi*. This [sūtra] is a supplement to the rule regarding the presence of *iṭ*.

The sense is that the word *ṇeḥ* is understood from the rule *ṭhṇeraniṭi*, and the word *lopaḥ* is understood from the rule *āto lopaḥ*. This [rule] is commenced because it would otherwise not apply due to the prohibition by the phrase *aniṭi*. Regarding the root *ṭu o śvi gativṛddhyoḥ*, he states that the augment *iṭ* is not applied in the past passive participle (*kta*) because of the rule *śvīdito niṣṭhāyām*.

Regarding the term *saṃprasāraṇa*: the intention is that [the root] belongs to the *yajādi* group. When *saṃprasāraṇa* has occurred, after the formation of the single substitute (*pūrvarūpa*), the long vowel is applied by the rule *halaḥ*, and then the rule *oditaśca* applies the substitution of *ṇatva* (nasalization) for the *niṣṭhā* suffix; thus he states the form as *śūna*.
Although in the root text under the rule *oditaśca* the example *ucchūna* was indeed cited, nevertheless—

However, it is presented here again with the intention of specifying a particular case. In this instance, although it is governed by the rule for *al* (the general vowel), its status as a *saṃprasāraṇa* is established solely by the force of the introduction of the rule "hal" (Pāṇini 6.1.71). Nor can it be argued that because the *saṃprasāraṇa* and the subsequent *pūrvarūpa* (single-substitute formation) are both obligatory, the rule "śyukaḥ kiti" (Pāṇini 6.1.13) alone would suffice.

It should not be said that the mention of *śvi* is redundant because the prohibition [of *guṇa*] is already established; for in the rule *ṛt-śyukaḥ kiti*, the term *upadeśe* (in the original enunciation) is understood from the preceding rule *ekāca upadeśe*. Thus, since there is no status of having a long vowel (*ugantatva*) in the original enunciation, the prohibition does not apply, and therefore the mention of *śvi* is necessary. For this very reason, in forms such as *stīrtvā*, etc., [the prohibition applies].

It is sufficient to note that in the *Upadeśa* (the original list of roots), by taking the form as ending in *u*, the prohibition of *iṭ* is established. He gives an example of a root marked with *ī*: *dīpta*.
The root *dīpī* meaning "to shine" belongs to the *divādi* class; because it is marked with *ī*, there is no *iṭ*. Regarding *gūḍha*:
because it is marked with *ū*, it optionally takes *iṭ*; thus, by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*, there is no *iṭ*.

[The rules concerning] the substitution of *ḍha* for *dha*, *ṣṭu* for *ṣṭa*, the elision of *ḍha*, and the lengthening [of vowels]: *vanu-vataḥ*, *tanu-tataḥ*. Because the suffix *ktvā* optionally takes the augment *iṭ* by the rule "udito vā," the augment *iṭ* is not applied here by the rule "yasya vibhāṣā.
By the rule "anudātopadeśa," there is the elision of the nasal (*na*). Regarding the form *pateḥ sani*: this refers to the root *patlṛ* in the sense of "going."

Regarding the statement "the addition [of the rule] for *tan*, *pat*, and *daridrā*," since there is an option (*veṭ*) regarding the suffix *san*, the prohibition of *iṭ* in the case of the *niṣṭhā* suffix follows from the rule "yasya vibhāṣā. Thus, one would expect that another justification must be stated to establish the form *patita* in the word *patita*, yet such a justification is not possible. For these...
Because of the rule *ṭhse'sici kṛtacṛtachﬁadatṛdanṛtaḥ*, the augment *iṭ* is optional (*veṭ*) before suffixes beginning with *s*; consequently,

since the prohibition of *iṭ* in the *niṣṭhā* (past participles) by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā* would not be established as permanent, the fact that these roots are marked with the indicator *īt* implies that the prohibition of *iṭ* by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā* is not universally obligatory.

It is understood as follows: since there is a possibility that the prohibition of *iṭ* by the rule "of that which has an optional [prohibition]" (*yasya vibhāṣā*) would not apply to *kṛta* and other such words, the designation *īdit* in the rule "after *śvi* and those marked with *ī*" (*śvīditaḥ*) is meaningful for the purpose of prohibiting *iṭ*. And thus, in the word *patita*, [the rule] "of that which... [applies].

The meaning is that [the rule] does not apply because of the non-universality (*anityatva*) of the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*. Regarding the word "tena" (by that): it means by making known the non-universality of the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*. Regarding the word "dhāvitam": although there is an option for the augment *iṭ* for the root *dhūñ* by the rule *svaratisūtisūyatidhūñūdito vā*, the prohibition of *iṭ* in the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*) applies by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*.
To address this, he says: "In the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*," etc.

*kṣubdha-svānta-dhvānta-lagna-mliṣṭa-viribdha-phāṇṭa-bāḍhāni mantha-manas-tamaḥ-sakta-avispaṣṭa-svara-anāyāsa-bhṛśeṣu* || Pāṇini 7.2.18 [The forms] *kṣubdha*, *svānta*, *dhvānta*, *lagna*, *mliṣṭa*, *viribdha*, *phāṇṭa*, and *bāḍha* [are established as correct] in the senses of churning (*mantha*), mind (*manas*), darkness (*tamas*), stuck (*sakta*), indistinct (*avispaṣṭa*), voice (*svara*), lack of effort (*anāyāsa*), and intense (*bhṛśa*) respectively.

*kṣubdhasvāntadhvāntalagnamliṣṭaviribdha-phāṇṭabāḍhāni* is the nominative plural of a dvandva compound consisting of these eight words: *kṣubdha*, *svānta*, *dhvānta*, *lagna*, *mliṣṭa*, *viribdha*, *phāṇṭa*, and *bāḍha*. It refers to the following eight meanings respectively: *mantha* (churning), *manaḥ* (mind), *tamaḥ* (darkness), *sakta* (attached), *avispaṣṭa* (unclear), *svara* (sound), *anāyāsa* (effortless), and *bhṛśa* (intense); this is the locative case of a dvandva compound consisting of these eight.

The correspondence is according to the respective order. Regarding the phrase "by the whole": these terms are conventional (*rūḍha*) in reference to the *mantha* and other such objects; one should not insist upon their etymological meanings. Thus he says: "substance-substance," etc. In this matter, the established usage of the ritualists (*yājñika*) alone must be taken as the refuge. And [the term] "churning-stick" (*manthāna-daṇḍa*).

Regarding the word *mantha*: Amara states, "The *manthāna*, *manthā*, *mantha*, and *daṇḍaka* [are synonyms] for the churning-stick (*vaiśākha*). Regarding *kṣubdha*: from the root *kṣubh* in the sense of "to shake" or "to agitate," the suffix *kta* is applied;

the absence of the augment *iṭ* is established by nipātana (irregular derivation). By the rule *jhaṣastathordho'dhaḥ*, the *t* is replaced by *dh*, and then *jaśtva* (the substitution of the voiced unaspirated stop) applies.
Regarding *svāntam*: from the root *svan*, the suffix *kta* is applied, and [the lengthening of the vowel] occurs by the rule *anunāsikasya kvī*.

The vowel is long by virtue of a specific grammatical rule (*nipātana*), and there is no *iṭ* augment. Amara states: "Ṭh-svānta, hṛt, mānasa, and manas [are synonyms for the heart]. Regarding *dhvānta*, it means darkness; it is derived from the root *dhvan* with the suffix *kta*.

The vowel is long according to the rule *anunāsikasya kvī*. Amara states: "Andhakāra (masculine/neuter), dhvānta, tamisra, timira, and tamas [are synonyms for darkness]. *Lagna* means attached or clinging.

The meaning is "connected. [The form] *lagna* is derived from the root *lag* with the suffix *kta*; there is an absence of the augment *iṭ*. Then, since it is not preceded by *ra* or *da*, how is the substitution of *ṇ* for *t* (niṣṭhā-natva) achieved? To this he says: "by irregular derivation" (*nipātanāt*). *Mliṣṭam* means "unclear. In the absence of *iṭ*, the *ṣ* is substituted [for *s*] by the rule *vraśca-*; the *t* becomes *ṭ* by the rule *ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ*.

According to Amarasimha, *mliṣṭam* means "indistinct" (*avispaṣṭam*). Regarding the term *virabdhaḥ*, it refers to a particular tone (*svara*); the meaning is a specific modulation of voice. [The root] *rebhṛ* is used in the sense of "sound. From this root, the suffix *kta* is applied; in the absence of the augment *iṭ*, the rule *jhaṣastathordho'dhaḥ* changes the *t* to *dh*. Demonstrating the actual form of the roots in both cases, he says: "of these two, *mleccha* and *rebhṛ*."
"itvamapi" means that there is also the absence of *iṭ*. Regarding "phāṇṭam":

the suffix *kta* is applied to the root *phaṇ*, with the absence of *iṭ* and the substitution of *ṭ* for the *t* of the *niṣṭhā* suffix being irregularly prescribed (*nipātita*). Because that [substitution] is treated as not having taken effect (*asiddha*), the lengthening [of the vowel] occurs by the rule "anunāsikasya". Amara states: "Phāṇṭa is that which is prepared without effort."

He states the opinion of the author of the *Vṛtti*: "A particular kind of decoction (*kaṣāya*)," etc. In the *Vṛtti*, it is established that: "That which is neither boiled nor ground, and whose taste is slightly distinct from water merely through contact with water, and which is somewhat warm—that is called sour (*āmla*). He says this in the *Vedabhāṣya*: "That indeed becomes fresh butter (*navanīta*)."

The meaning is that [the author] says this during the occasion of the commentary on the *Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa*: "Clarified butter (*ghṛta*) indeed belongs to the gods, while a thin gruel (*phāṇṭa*) belongs to humans. Regarding the word *bāḍham*, it means "exceedingly" or "intensely.

It is derived from the root *bāhṛ* in the sense of "effort," with the suffix *kta*, the absence of the augment *iṭ*, and the application of the rules for changing *ha* to *ḍha*, *ḍha* to *dha*, *ḍha* to *ṭha*, and the elision of *ḍha*. The phrase "but elsewhere" refers to other instances.
The meaning is that there is no denotability (*vācyatva*) for *mantha* and so forth. (865) *dhṛṣi-śasī vaiyātye* | Pāṇini 7.2.19.
*dhṛṣi-śasī*: *viyātaḥ* means one who is *avinītaḥ* (ill-mannered); its state is *vaiyātyam*. In that regard, [the suffix] *ñi-*...

The prohibition of *iṇ* for the root *dhṛṣ* (meaning "to be bold") is established by the rule *āditaśca*. However, for the root *śasu* (meaning "to injure"), since it optionally takes *iṭ* in the *ktvā* suffix according to the rule *udito vā*, the prohibition of *iṇ* is established by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*. Therefore, he states that [the present rule] is for the purpose of restriction (*niyamārtha*), namely: "only in the sense of 'lack of discipline' (*avinaya*)."

*Dhṛṣṭa* means *viśasta*; the meaning is "undisciplined. *Anyatra* means "in the absence of impudence" (*vaiyātya*). *Dharṣita* means "overpowered by force. *Visasita* means "injured. The point here is that because there is an absence of impudence, the prohibition of the suffix *iṇ* does not apply. [Objection: But...

Since the root *dhṛṣ* belongs to the *ad*-class, the rule *vibhāṣā bhāvādikarmaṇoḥ* applies, resulting in an option (*vikalpa*) regarding the augment *iṭ* in the sense of abstract action (*bhāva*) and the beginning of an action (*ādikarman*). Therefore, let this present rule (*vidhi*) serve to make [the absence of *iṭ*] obligatory in those two cases. Consequently, in instances other than abstract action and the beginning of an action, even in the absence of audacity (*vaiyātya*), there is simply the prohibition of *iṭ* by the rule *āditaśca*.
To address this, he says: "But in the case of the action [expressed by] the root *bhū* and the passive... He says "it does not exist," the implication being that it is not so expressed.
In this regard, he cites the consensus of the elders:

"For this very reason," meaning precisely because the root *dhṛṣ* is not expressed in the sense of the action or the passive. Otherwise, since *dhṛṣ* belongs to the first class (*ādi*), [the rule would apply].

The sense is that, although the option (*vibhāṣā*) regarding the suffix *iṭ* for the abstract action (*bhāva*) and the initial action (*ādikarman*) would apply by the rule "vibhāṣā bhāvādikarmaṇoḥ," this [prohibition] is prescribed for the sake of making it obligatory (*nitya*) in those specific cases.

As for the remark "it should be considered" (*cintyam*): indeed, the status of *dhṛṣ* as belonging to the first class (*ādi*) is not for the purpose of prohibiting the suffix *iṇ* (which is conditioned by being in the first class) in the sense of "impudence" (*vaiyātya*).

Since [the form] is already established by the rule "dhṛṣi-śasi vaiyātye," nor is it for the purpose of prohibiting the suffix *iṣ* under the condition of being an initial [root] in cases other than insolence (*vaiyātya*), because there is no prohibition of the suffix *iṣ* under the condition of being an initial [root] in cases other than that, given the restriction that for the root *dhṛṣ*, *iṣ* is prohibited only in the sense of insolence; nor is it for the sake of [prohibiting it] in the sense of insolence for the root *dhṛṣ*.

The meaning is that Haradatta says that the inclusion of *dhṛṣ* at the beginning [of the list] is useless; for, regarding the scope of the rule "optionally [the suffix *iṭ* is added] in the sense of the abstract action (*bhāva*) and the beginning of an action (*ādikarman*)"—that is, for the purpose of optionally adding *iṭ* by the rule *vibhāṣā bhāvādikarmaṇoḥ*—there is no mention of *dhṛṣ* in the sense of impudence (*vaiyātya*) when it occurs in the abstract or as the beginning of an action.
Therefore, [Haradatta's view is that] the status of *dhṛṣ* as being at the beginning is redundant. As for Mādhava, however... [he says].

The meaning is that there is no evidence for the non-expression of the sense of "boldness" (*avaiyātya*) in either the state (*bhāva*) or the incipient action (*ādikarman*). Regarding that, he gives an example for the state of boldness: *dhṛṣṭam* and *dharṣitam*.
He gives examples for the incipient action: *pradhṛṣṭaḥ* and *pradharṣitaḥ*.
(866) *dṛḍhaḥ sthūlabalayoḥ* |7|2|20|.

The word *dṛḍha* [is used] in the senses of "thick" (*sthūla*) and "strong" (*bala*). The word *bala* here ends in the suffix *ac* according to the *arśa-ādi* group, and thus refers to one who possesses strength (*balavat*). Therefore, he says: "and when it means strong. Regarding the phrase *tasya*: the meaning is that the substitution of *ḍha* for the *ta* of the *niṣṭhā* suffix is prescribed as an irregularity (*nipātana*).

Regarding "hasya lopaḥ" (the elision of *h*): the remainder [of the rule] is "it is treated as an irregularity (*nipātyate*). Regarding "idita" (having *i* as its *it* marker): the intention is that for roots not having *i* as their *it* marker (*anidit*), the elision of the nasal (*nalopa*) is already established. Now, one might object: if *ḍhatva* is applied to *h*, then by the rule "jhaṣas tathoḥ dho 'dhaḥ," the *t* would become *dh*; then, by the rule "ṣṭuan," that *dh* would become *ḍh*; and finally, by the rule "ḍho ḍhe," there would be the elision of the first *ḍh*, resulting in *dṛḍha*. [This objection is answered as follows:]...

If it is argued: "Let *iḍ* simply not occur [in this case], and let there be neither the elision of the letter *h* nor the substitution of *ḍh*, then what need is there for these rules?"—do not say so. For if that were the case, in forms such as *draḍhiyān*, the elision of *ḍh* would be considered *asiddha* (non-existent) for the purposes of the preceding rule; consequently, the vowel *ṛ* would still be followed by a *saṃyoga* (conjunct consonant), and this elision of the *hal* (consonant) [would not apply].
This is clear from the Bhāṣya, which states that there is no lack of established proof (*asiddhatva*) because [the rule] belongs to the seventh chapter (*sāptamika*).

(867) *prabhau paribṛḍhaḥ* | 7|2|21|. Regarding *prabhau paribṛḍhaḥ*: "as before" means that the substitution of *ḍha* for *ta*, the doubling of the consonant, and the elision of the vowel (*halopa*) apply.

(868) *Kaṣa* [takes the affix *khal*] when *kṛcchra* and *gahana* are the objects. /7/2/22/ Regarding *kṛcchra* and *gahana*: the word *kṛcchra* refers to suffering (*duḥkha*) as well as its cause. *Kaṣṭam* means suffering, and it also means the cause thereof. It is said: "It would be *kaṣṭam*..."
The statement from the *Amarakośa* is: "kṛcchra means ābhīla. He provides an example for the sense of a cause of suffering:

"moha (delusion) is kaṣṭa. He provides an example for the sense of being impenetrable: "the śāstra (scripture) is kaṣṭa. He explains the word *gahana* [which is synonymous with *kaṣṭa*]: "duravagāha (difficult to fathom)."

(869) *ghuṣir aviśabdane* | Pāṇini 7.2.23. Regarding *ghuṣir aviśabdane*: "the rope is *ghuṣṭā*" means it has been produced [as such] or it has been stretched. *Viśabdana* is the manifestation of an intention by means of sound. Thus he says: "by means of sound."

(870) *arddeḥ saṃnivibhyaḥ* | Pāṇini 6.1.139. Regarding *samarṇa*: when *sam* and *ard* are combined as *sam arda*, by the rule *radābhyām* (Pāṇini 8.2.42), there is the substitution of *ṇ* for the final *t* of the suffix *niṣṭhā* and for the preceding *d*. This results in the form *samarṇa*. The change to *ṇ* is applied.

(871) *abheścāvidūrye* | Pāṇini 7.2.25. "And after *abhi*, [the substitution of *ar* for *ṛ* occurs] when non-proximity (*avidūrya*) is intended. Non-proximity is the state of being not distant; that is *āvidūryam*. When this is to be understood, the root *ṛd* (meaning "to go") following *abhi* is replaced by *ar*, provided it is anit (lacking the augment *iṭ*). It was not stated simply as "in proximity" (*sāmīpye*), because [proximity] does not necessarily exclude what is not very far (*anatidūra*).
Because it would otherwise not be included [in the category of *kṛt* suffixes]. Indicating this, he says: "not too far" (*nātidūram*).

(872) *ṇeradhyayane vṛtam* | Pāṇini 7.2.26. Regarding *ṇeradhyayane*: [the rule] "and there is elision of *ṇi*" (*ṇiluk ca*) applies. However, if there were elision of *ṇi* (*ṇilopa*), the *guṇa* substitution for a light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*) would occur.
The meaning is as follows: regarding the word "adhīyamāne" [in the rule], the intention is that in the sūtra the word *adhyayana* ends in the suffix *lyuṭ* used in the sense of the object (*karman*).

(873) *Śṛtam pāke* | 6.1.27. Regarding *śṛtam pāke*: the root *śrā* in the sense of cooking belongs to the *ghaṭādi* group; from it, with the causative suffix *ṇic* and the augment *puṅ*, [the form *śrāpayati* is derived].
The established rule is that because the root *mī* is short, it becomes *śrā* before the suffix *śru*. Regarding the phrase "of *śrā* and *śrapaya*":
this means [the application] of both the non-causative (*aṇyanta*) and the causative (*ṇyanta*) forms of the root *śrā*. Regarding the phrase "of milk and oblation" (*kṣīrahaviṣoḥ*):
this is obtained from a Vārttika. He explains the non-causative form: "cooked by itself."

The root *śrā* (to cook) occurs in the sense of cooking (*pāka*). Here, "cooking" is intended to mean only the state of being softened (*viklitti*), and not even the activity conducive to that. Thus, since the root *śrā* is intransitive when meaning "softening," the suffix *kta* is applied in the sense of the agent according to the rule *gaty-arthā-karmaka-* (Pāṇini 3.4.72).

And thus, milk is the substratum of the process of softening; therefore, from the root *śrap*—which has the same meaning as *pac*, signifying an activity conducive to softening—when the suffix *kta* is applied in the sense of the object, the result is stated as "cooked" (*pakva*). And this...

This is clear from the Bhāṣya and Kaiyaṭa. As for Amara’s statement, "The [words] *kṣīra*, *ājya*, and *havis* [take the suffix *kta*] in the sense of *śṛta*," that is indeed an error, because it contradicts the Vārttika rule: "In the case of *kṣīra* and *havis*.
(874) *vā dānta-śānta-pūrṇa-dasta-spasta-channa-jñaptāḥ* | Pāṇini 7.2.27.

The term *ṇeḥ* (of the causative suffix) is understood from the rule *dāmnī-śasa-yu-yuja-stu-tuda-si-sica-miha-pata-daśāṃ ca* (Pāṇini 3.2.182). Regarding the roots *damu* and *śamu* in the sense of "to pacify," the absence of the augment *iṭ* is prescribed as a nipātana (irregularity). The lengthening of the vowel is by the rule *anunāsikasya kvi-jhaloḥ kṅiti*.

The elision of the causative suffix (*ṇilopa*) is not treated as *sthānivadbhūta* (as if it were the original element), because of this specific nipātana and because the prohibition of such treatment applies to the prescription of lengthening.

*Dāntaḥ* (tamed), *śāntaḥ* (calmed). From the root *pṝ* in the sense of "to fill" (*āpyāyane*), the suffix *kta* is applied; the absence of *iṭ* is prescribed by rule (*nipātita*), and there is the elision of the causative marker *ṇi*. Because it follows a letter other than *r*, the substitution of *n* for *ṇ* occurs, resulting in *pūrṇaḥ* (filled/full).
By this [explanation], the objection that the mention of *pūrṇa* is redundant—since the form would already be established by the rule "na dhyākhyāpṛmūrchī"—is refuted.

Because the root *pṝ* (to fill), when followed by the causative suffix *ṇi*, has the sense of "becoming full," [the form *pūrṇa* is derived]. From the root *dasu* (to perish) with the causative suffix *ṇi*, the absence of the augment *iṭ* is prescribed as a nipātana, as is the absence of vṛddhi in the penultimate vowel; there is then the elision of the *ṇi* suffix. From the root *spaś* (to afflict) with the causative suffix *ṇi*, the suffix *kta* is added, the absence of the augment *iṭ* is prescribed as a nipātana, as is the absence of vṛddhi in the penultimate vowel; there is then the elision of the *ṇi* suffix.

This is clear. [The root] *chad* is used in the sense of "covering" (*apavāraṇe*). The suffix *kta* is added after the causative form (*ṇyanta*). The absence of the augment *iṭ* and the absence of *vṛddhi* are treated as irregularities (*nipātana*).
There is the elision of the causative marker *ṇi*. By the rule *radābhyām*, there is the substitution of *na* for the final radical, resulting in *cchannaḥ*. Regarding *jñaptaḥ*:

Kaiyaṭa states that the suffix *kta* is added after the causative form of the root *jñap* (belonging to the *curādi* class) in the sense of "making known. There is the absence of the augment *iṭ* and the elision of the causative marker *ṇi*. In this alternative view (*pakṣa*), [the form is derived thus].
Thus [it is said]. This means the alternative view in which there is no irregular derivation (*nipātana*). "Damitaḥ," "śamitaḥ":

because they end in *am*, they have the designation *mit*, and therefore the vowel is shortened. "Jñāpate": this is the form belonging to the non-causative group (the *jñā* root not belonging to the *cur*-class).
However, for the causative group (*cur*-class), the form is only "jñapitaḥ."

(875) *ruṣyamatvarasaṅghuṣāsvanām* | 7|2|28| The compound *ruṣyamatvarasaṅghuṣāsvanām* is a *dvandva* consisting of *ruṣi*, *ama*, *tvara*, *saṅghuṣ*, and *āsvan*. The word *ṇeḥ* ("after the causative suffix *ṇic*") is no longer in force. The genitive case is used in the sense of the ablative. Thus he says: "after these. "It may be optional" (*vā syāt*)—this refers to the rule "optionally" (*vā*).
The intention is that [the suffix] *kta* follows from the word "dānte" (in the rule *dānta-śānta-pūrṇa-dasta-spṛṣṭaḥ*). Regarding "ruṣṭaḥ" and "ruṣitaḥ":
since the root *ruṣ* optionally takes *iṭ* by the rule *tīṣasaha*, this option applies even though the prohibition [of *iṭ*] would otherwise have been obtained by the rule *yasya vibhāṣā*.

Regarding "āntaḥ" and "amitaḥ": the suffix *kta* is applied to the root *am* in the sense of "motion" and so forth. In the alternative where *iṭ* is absent, [the lengthening of the vowel occurs] by the rule *anunāsikasya...*.

*Dīrghaḥ*, *tūrṇaḥ*, and *tvaritaḥ*. [The word] *tvarita* is derived from the root √*tvar* (meaning "to hasten" or "agitation") with the suffix *kta*; in the alternative where the augment *iṭ* is absent, the substitution *ūṭh* applies by the rule *jvaratvaretyūṭh*. Then, by the rule *radābhyām*, there is the substitution of *n* for *t*, followed by the substitution of *ṇ*. Regarding the rule *āditaśca*, although a permanent prohibition of *iṭ* would have applied, this [present rule] provides an option; however, as for the status of being "beginning with a vowel" (*āditva*), [it remains].

The result is solely the *ātmanepada* [voice]. Thus he says: "The result of its being *ādi* (beginning with a vowel) is that it is slow. And so, the intention is that it is more logical for it to have a short indicatory vowel (*hrasvānubandhatva*), just like [the roots] *ṭedha* (in the sense of growth) and others.
Regarding the forms *saṃghuṣṭaḥ* and *saṃghuṣitaḥ*: [this is derived] from the root *ghuṣ*, preceded by *sam*, according to the rule "ghuṣir aviśabdane" (Pāṇini 7.2.23).
Since the prohibition of *iṭ* would apply permanently [by the previous rule], this is an optional provision (*vikalpa*). Examples are *āsvāntaḥ* and *āsvanitaḥ*.
The suffix *kta* is added to the root *svan-* preceded by the prefix *āṅ*. In the alternative where *iṭ* is absent, there is lengthening according to the rule *anunāsikasya*.
However, the specific grammatical prescription (*nipātana*) regarding *kṣubdha-svānta-* does not apply to *svan-* when it is preceded by *āṅ*.

They say that because this very option applies due to its subsequent position; however, in the Bhāṣya on the sūtra "na veti," it is stated that regarding the roots *saṃ-ghuṣ* and *ā-svan*, there is an option in both cases. (876) *hṛṣer lomasu* 7.2.29.

Regarding the rule *hṛṣer lomasu*: it should be understood that "when the body hairs (*loman*) are the agents" [the suffix *kta* is used]. This is clear from the *Bhāṣya* on the rule *ṭha-ja-ra-yaḥ*. Thus, *hṛṣṭam* and *hṛṣitam* mean "the hair. The suffix *kta* is applied in the sense of the agent (kartr) according to the rule *gaty-artha-akarmaka-* (Pāṇini 3.4.72).

The meaning is "that which has become bristling with hair. Also, regarding the phrase *vismita-pratighātayoś ca*: [the suffix *kta* is applied in the sense of the agent when the roots *hṛṣ* and *ghuṣ* denote astonishment and anger, respectively].
This is a *vārttika*. The remainder of the rule is "there is optionally an augment *iṭ* after the root *hṛṣ* in the *niṣṭhā* [past participles]. Regarding the phrase "because it is marked with *u*":

since there is an optional *iṭ* for the suffix *ktvā* by the rule "optionally after a root marked with *u*," there is no *iṭ* for the *niṣṭhā* by the rule "there is no *iṭ* when the option has been provided. Thus, in the sense of "untrue" (*alīka*), one says simply *hṛṣṭa*; the meaning is "he spoke falsely" (*mṛṣoktavān*).

Regarding *iṭ*: the meaning is that after the root *hṛṣ* (in the sense of "satisfaction"), only *iṭ* occurs when the suffix *kta* follows; thus, *hṛṣitaḥ* means "satisfied. However, in the senses of "astonishment" and "obstruction," the application [of the suffix] is due to the polysemous nature of roots.

In those cases—namely, regarding body hair, as well as astonishment and obstruction—the form is derived from the root *hṛṣu* (in the sense of "falsehood"). As for [the rule] *yasya*... [text continues].

The term *vibhāṣā* [is used] here because the prohibition of *iṭ* would otherwise apply invariably; this is an optional rule (*vibhāṣā*). The distinction is that while *iṭ* would invariably apply after the root *hṛṣ* in the sense of "joy" (*tuṣṭau*), this is made optional. (877) *apacitaś-ca* | Pāṇini 7.2.30.

"And *apacita*. The *Bhāṣya* states: "The substitution of *ci* for the root *ci* preceded by *upa*, when it is in its causative (*ṇyanta*) form, is irregularly prescribed (*nipātana*) in the case of the past passive participle (*niṣṭhā*). Thus he says: "This is an irregular form (*nipāta*) of the root *cāy*. (878) *pyāyaḥ pī* 6.1.28.

"Of *pyā*, there may be *pī* in the *niṣṭhā* [suffixes]. This is a supplement to the rule. The sense is that "optionally" (*vibhāṣā*) is carried over from the rule "optionally after [the root] preceded by *abhi* or *ava*," and "in the *niṣṭhā*" is carried over from the rule "of *sphā*, *sphī*. Thus, it is an option governed by specific conditions (*vyavasthitavibhāṣā*). In this case—
The commentary itself is the refuge. This is clear from the Bhāṣya, beginning with "not [the substitution] of the root *nī* when preceded by a preposition," and so forth.
(879) *hlādo niṣṭhāyām* | 6|4|95|. Regarding *hlādo niṣṭhāyām*: "there shall be a short vowel. This is a supplement to the remaining portion [of the rule]. [Cf. *khaci hrasvaḥ*.
The sense is that [the rule] follows from that. Regarding *prahlanna*: [the root] *hlādī* is used in the sense of "pleasure.

The suffix *kta* is applied; by the rule *śvīditaḥ*, the augment *iṭ* is not added; and by the rule *radābhyāṃ ṇaḥ*, the substitution of *ṇa* for *na* occurs. Furthermore, by the rule *dyatisyatimāsthāmiti kiti*, [the substitution of *ī* for *ā* takes place].

The genitive case is used after these four [roots] in a copulative compound (*dvandva*). The form *dyati* is the citation for the root *do* in the sense of "cutting" (*avakhaṇḍana*), while the form *syati* is the citation for the root *ṣo* in the sense of "concluding" (*antakarmaṇi*). The analysis of the sūtra is *it-ti-kit-i*. Regarding the term *ītve*: the substitution of *ī* [for the vowel of the root] occurs by the rule *ghumāsthāgāpājahātisām hali*, and the substitution of *dadh-* [for *do*] occurs by the rule *do dadghoḥ*.
The meaning is that the substitution of *d* for *t* is an exception (*apavāda*) to the [substitution of] *l*, as far as possible. He provides an example of the root *dā*:

"ditaḥ. [He includes] *mā*, *māṅ*, and *meṅ*; the intention is that this is because of the statement: "In the case of the mention of *gā*, *mā*, and *ā*, there is no distinction [between the various forms]."
(881) *śācchāer anyatarasyām* | 7|4|41| Regarding *śācchāeḥ*: [the roots] *śo* in the sense of "making thin" (*tanūkaraṇe*) and *chāe* in the sense of "cutting" (*chedane*).

These two are mentioned here with their *ātv* (vowel substitution) already applied. An *ikāra* (the vowel *i*) may optionally be the substitute for the final letter of these two before suffixes beginning with *ta*.
The meaning is "how much? Regarding the term *vyavasthitā* (restricted/established), this is clear in the Bhāṣya.
(882) *dadhāter hiḥ* | 7|4|42|.
[The rule] *dadhāter hiḥ* [is explained as follows]: "before an affix beginning with *t* that is marked with *k*. This is a supplement to the rule (*śeṣapūraṇam*).

The intention is that [the rule] *ṭhdyatīstayatī* follows from that [previous context]. In the rule *do daddhoḥ*, *da* is in the genitive case (*ṣaṣṭhyanta*). Thus he says: "of *dā*. The analysis is *dath*. Thus he says: "there shall be *dath*. This substitute ends in the second letter of the dental class (*tavarga*). [Regarding the expression] *tādau kitīti*: *ti*...

The intention is that [the rule] *kiti* continues [from the previous sūtra]. Regarding *cartvam*: the meaning is that the letter *th* is changed to *t* by the rule *khari ca*. Regarding *dāta*: this is the form of the roots *dāp* and *dai*.
Because of the statement *adāp*, there is no substitution of *d* for *dh* due to the absence of *ghu*-status. Regarding *tānto vā*: [this refers to the alternative view].

The meaning is "ending in the first letter of the *tavarga* (the dental class). But if this were the case, then in examples such as *vidati*, there would be the undesirable consequence of lengthening the upasarga *dasti*; for in that instance, the genitive *daḥ* is used in the sense of the locative, meaning that the vowel of an upasarga ending in an *ik* (i, u, ṛ, or ḷ) should be lengthened when followed by a root beginning with *d* (specifically, the root *dadāti*).

Anticipating this objection, the author says: "And it is not so. This means: provided that the substitute (ādeśa) begins with the first letter of the *tavarga* (the dental class). Regarding the phrase "at the beginning of a word starting with *t*": in the word *dasti*, the genitive case ending in *da-* connects with the word *ti-*.
Thus, there would be lengthening of a prefix ending in *i* or *u* when followed by a subsequent member (*uttarapada*) beginning with the substitute *da-* and starting with *t*.

This is the meaning. Because of the governing rule concerning the "subsequent member" (*uttarapada*), the intention is that since the subsequent member here does not begin with the letter *t*, there is no lengthening of the vowel. "Ending in *d* or ending in *dh*" means that this substitute ends either in the third letter of the dental class (*tavarga*) or the fourth. "And not... [etc.].

The syntactical connection is as follows: one should not suspect the application of *niṣṭhānatva* (the substitution of *ṇ* for *n*) when the suffix ends in *d*, nor the application of *dhatva* (the substitution of *dh* for *t*) under the rule *ṭhjhaṣastathoḥ* when the suffix ends in *dh*. Regarding the term *saṃnipāta*:
because the substitutes for *d* and *dh* depend upon the suffix beginning with *t* and so forth, they [the substitutes] would obstruct the *natva* and *dhatva* that cause those suffixes to arise.
The sense is that [the suffix] cannot have a cause (*nimitta*).
(883) *aca upasargāt taḥ* | Pāṇini 7.4.47. In the rule *aca upasargāt taḥ*, the vowel *a* in *taḥ* is for the sake of pronunciation (*uccāraṇārtha*). The term *aca* is repeated.

The first [term] is a qualifier of the prefix (*upasarga*), while the second provides the original form (*sthānin*). Thus he says: "from that which ends in a vowel" (*ajantāt*); "ghoḥ" means "of a portion of *ghu*"; "taḥ syāt" means "the letter *t* should occur. This is an exception to the substitution of *d*. Regarding "the substitution of *c*" (*cartvam*): this occurs when the sequence *pra dā taḥ* is established.
The meaning is that when *ā* follows *da*, *ta* is substituted for *da*, and by the rule of *cartya* (the substitution of *ca* sounds), *ta* is substituted for *da*.

"Avadataṃ vidataṃ ca" is a verse found in the Bhāṣya. Here, the term *ādikarmaṇi* (in the sense of the beginning of an action) connects only with *pradattam*. This [rule] is not an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule "ṭhaca upasargāt" (Pāṇini 7.4.47).

Thus he says that one should not be confused, adding "by the word 'ca', as it occurs [in the original rule]. The meaning is that, accordingly, even the substitution of *da* for *dā* is sometimes obtained in words such as *avadātā*.
For this very reason, in the commentary (*bhāṣya*) on the present sūtra, there is scope for the rule "after a prefix, *at* is substituted for *aca*"—as in *pratam* and *avata*.
The sense is that it "comes together" (*saṅgacchate*).
(884) *da-sti* | 6|3|124|. Regarding *da-sti*: from the rule *ikaḥ kāśe*, the word *ikaḥ* is understood; and from the rule *upasargasya ghañyamanuṣye*.

In the rule *upasargasya*, the word *dīrghaḥ* (long vowel) is understood from the previous rule *ḍhralope*. The governing term *uttarapade* (in the following member) is qualified by the word *ti*. This is a rule concerning the initial element of that [member]. The genitive case in *daḥ* is construed with *ti*; thus, it means "when the following member begins with a *t* that is a substitute for the root *dā*."

Thus it is obtained. He says this with the words *iganta-* and so forth. Now, one might object: when *ni* and *dātṛ* are in the state *nidātṛ*, by the rule *upasargādṛti dhātau*, the *ā* of the root *dā* following the *t* of the prefix is replaced by *t*; then, by the rule *khari ca*, the *t* undergoes *cartva* (substitution by the first letter of its class) to become *d*;
and finally, by the present sūtra, the long vowel is substituted for the prefix, resulting in the form *nīttṛ*. This is what he will state.

That is incorrect; for if *cartva* (the substitution of *ca*) were considered *asiddha* when the lengthening (*dīrgha*) was to be performed, then after the substitution of *da*, there would be no subsequent word beginning with *ta*. To this, he says: "The *cartva* is established by virtue of its basis. When the lengthening is being prescribed based on the *takāra* resulting from the substitution of *da*, the *cartva* is not *asiddha*.

The meaning is that [the substitution] occurs by relying on the letter *t*, which is established as a *cartva* (a substitute for *c*), through the force of the grammatical rule (*vidhi*). However, the statement "it has been produced" (*sūtam*) is to be considered; for in the *Bhāṣya* and *Vārttika* on the sūtra *gatiśca*, it is explained in detail that in the case of the word *sudataḥ*, when the substitution of *t* is to be applied by the rule *aca upasargāt taḥ*, the prefix *su-* does not possess the status of an *upasarga*. Now...

Regarding the forms *dheṅkta* and *pādhukta*, he says [the rule] *ghumāsthā...* [applies]. Thus we have *dhītam*. In the rule *dadhāter hiḥ*, because of the mention of the *ślu*-affix (*śluvikaraṇa*), the substitution of *hi* does not occur here.
(885) *ado jagdhir lyapi kiti*: In place of the root *ad*, the substitute *jagdhi* occurs before the suffix *lyap* and before suffixes having a *k* or *ṅ* as an indicatory letter (*kit*).

*ado jagdhiḥ*: "The substitution of *jagdhi*" means that when the form *jagdha* is established, the letter *t* is replaced by *dh* according to the rule *jhaṣas tatho 'dhaḥ*. *Jharo jhari*: this means that the optional elision of the letter *dh* occurs by this rule. *Ādikarmaṇi ktaḥ*: this has been explained previously; [it is mentioned here] with the intention of providing another example.

The term *punarupanyāsaḥ* (re-introduction) means "what is that which has begun (*prakṛtaḥ*)? The sense is: "he has begun to make. Because the object (*karman*), namely the mat (*kaṭa*), is not expressed [by a case ending], the second case (*dvitīyā*) is used. Because the agent (*kartṛ*) is expressed [by the suffix], the first case (*prathamā*) is used after the word *tat*. By the word "and" (*ca*), it is stated that [the suffix] occurs in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāva*) and the passive (*karmaṇi*). Among those, he gives an example for the passive: *prakṛtaḥ*.
"Kaṭas tena" means "the mat was made by him. "Prakṣīṇaḥ saḥ" means "he has perished"; here the suffix *kta* is used in the sense of the inception of an action (*ādikarman*).
(Vārttika 886: *vā’krośadainyayoḥ* | The phrase *vā’krośadainyayoḥ* follows from the rule *aṇyadartha*. The term *aṇyadartha* is understood [to apply here]. The meaning of *ṇyat* is...

It was stated [in Pāṇini 3.4.69] that [the suffix *kta* is used] for the state (*bhāva*) and the object (*karman*). He gives an example for the sense of "abuse" (*ākrośa*): *kṣīṇāyurbhava* ("May you be one whose life is exhausted").

Here, the suffix *kta* is used in the sense of the agent (*kartṛ*) according to [Pāṇini 3.4.72] *gatyarthākarmaka-*. He gives an example for the sense of "wretchedness" (*dainya*): *kṣīṇo 'yaṃ tapasvī* ("This poor man is wasted away"). The meaning is "emaciated."

(887) *ninadībhyāṃ snāteḥ kauśale* |8|3|89|. [The meaning is: After the words *ni* and *nadī*, the *s* of the root *snā* shall become *ṣ* when denoting skill (*kauśala*). The sense is that from the rule *sahe sāḍaḥ saḥ* [8.3.56], the word *saḥ*—standing in the genitive case—is understood to carry over, and the governing heading *apadāntasya mūrdhanyaḥ* [8.3.55] is also applicable.

"Niṣṇāta" means "skilled. Regarding "nadīṣṇa," the analysis of the compound is: "one who bathes skillfully in a river. Regarding "supi," the meaning is that the suffix *ka* is applied by means of the separation of the rule (*yogavibhāga*) from the rule "supi sthaḥ."

(888) *gatyarthākarmakaśliṣaśīṅsthāsavasajanaruhajīryatibhyaśca* || 3.4.72 || The compound consists of these ten: roots having the sense of motion (*gatyartha*), intransitive roots (*akarmaka*), and the roots *śliṣ*, *śīṅ*, *sthā*, *ās*, *vas*, *jan*, *ruh*, and *jīryati*. [The word] "in the sense of the abstract action" (*bhāve*) is supplied from the rule *laḥ karmaṇi ca bhāve ca*.

Regarding the term *karmaṇi*: from the rule "the suffix *kta* is used in the sense of the beginning of an action (*ādikarmaṇi*) and also in the sense of the agent (*kartari*)," the word "in the sense of the agent" (*kartari*) is understood to carry over. Thus he says [the author of the commentary] by the words "from these," etc. Since only "in the sense of the agent" (*kartari*) were carried over, [the suffix would] not occur in the sense of the state (*bhāva*) or the object (*karman*); therefore, those two are also carried over. For example: *gaṅgāṃ gataḥ* ("he has gone to the Gaṅgā").

The suffix *kta* is used in the active sense (*kartari*). In the example "he has reached the Gaṅgā" (*gaṅgāṃ prāptaḥ*), the root *āplṛ* (meaning "to pervade") functions in the sense of "motion" due to the influence of the prefix. He gives an example of an intransitive verb: "withered" (*mlānaḥ*). The meaning is "diminished. The substitution of *ṇatva* for *n* occurs by the rule "after a conjunct beginning with a consonant" (*saṃyogādeḥ*). [He gives another example: "embraced" (*āśliṣṭaḥ*).

The meaning is that he embraced her. Now, one might object that since this is already established by the fact that the roots are intransitive (*akarmaka*), the separate mention of *śīṅ* and the others is redundant; to this, he says: "He lay upon the remainder" (*śeṣamadhiśayita*). The meaning is that he lay upon the remainder (*śeṣe śayitavān*). According to the rule *adhi-śīṅ-sthāsām karmam*, the "remainder" (*śeṣa*) is the object (*karman*). Therefore...

The sense is that there is no application [of the rule] here because [the root *sthā*] is not intransitive (*akarmaka*). "Residing in Vaikuṇṭha" means staying in Vaikuṇṭha. According to the rule *adhi-śīṅ-sthāsām*, *vaikuṇṭha* is the object (*karman*).
Therefore, there is no application [of the rule] here due to its being intransitive. "He worshipped Śiva" means Śiva...

The meaning is that he "has attended upon. The point is that although the root *ās* (to sit) is intransitive when it has the sense of "sitting," here, due to the influence of the prefix (*upa*), it takes an object in a different sense; therefore, the rule regarding intransitive roots (*akarmaka*) does not apply.
In the example "he fasted on the day of Hari" (*haridinamupoṣitaḥ*), the augment *iṭ* is applied by the rule *vasatikṣudhoḥ*.

There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) due to its inclusion in the *yajādi* group. By the rule "śāsī," there is the substitution of *ṣ*. The meaning is: "he did not eat on the day of Hari. According to the rule "upānvadhyāṅvasaḥ," the day of Hari is the object (*karman*).
Consequently, because the verb is not intransitive (*akarmaka*), the [prohibition of the *ātmanepada*] does not apply. [The example is: "born after Rāma" (*rāmamanujātaḥ*).
The meaning is "he has imitated" (anukṛtavān). Or, it means "having followed, he was born" (anusṛtya jātavān).

Consequently, because there is an absence of intransitivity (*akarmakatva*), [the rule] does not apply. "Mounted upon Garuḍa" (*garuḍam ārūḍha*) means "he has ascended above. "He has aged after the universe" (*viśvam anujīrṇa*) means "he has destroyed it" (*hatavān*).

Or [it may mean] "he has pervaded. Since there is an absence of intransitivity (*akarmakatva*), [the rule for the *kta* suffix] does not apply. The suffix *kta* occurs after the root *jṛ* in the sense of the agent. By the rule *ṛtaḥ*, the substitution of *i* for *ṛ* takes place; then the substitution of *ra* for *ṛ*; then the lengthening by the rule *hali ca*; then the substitution of *na* for *d* by the rule *radābhyām*; and finally the substitution of *ṇa*. "In the alternative case" means in the case where there is no suffix denoting the agent.

(889) *kto'dhikaraṇe ca dhrauvyagatipratyavasānārthebhyaḥ* |3|4|76|. "The suffix *kta* [is applied] also in the sense of the locus (*adhikaraṇa*), after roots whose meanings are 'stability' (*dhrauvya*), 'motion' (*gati*), and 'consumption' (*pratyavasāna*). The analysis (*vigraha*) is: "those whose meanings are stability, motion, and consumption. That is to say: after roots meaning stability, after roots meaning motion, and after roots meaning consumption.
"Up to... and as it has been attained" means that this applies to the relationships of object and agent as well, according to the possibility.
"Permanence" (*dhrauvya*) is explained as "stability" (*sthairya*); that is, becoming firm, which refers to actions such as sitting or lying down. "This is the sitting of Mukunda."

This is a verse. "Āsitam" means that in which one sits; it signifies a seat. This is an example of the sense of stability. "Idaṃ yātaṃ ramāpateḥ" is an example of the sense of motion. "Yātam" means that in which one goes or is traversed; it refers to a path.
This is the meaning. Regarding the phrase *bhuktametadanantarasya*: that in which one eats is called *bhuktam*;

thus, it means a place of eating. In all three cases, the genitive case (*ṣaṣṭhī*) is used for the agent according to the rule *adhikaraṇavācinaśca*. Regarding the word *pakṣe*: this means in the alternative case where there is no suffix denoting the locus (*adhikaraṇa*).

"Because [the root] *ās* is intransitive (*akarmaka*). And thus, the meaning is that the suffix *kta* does not occur in the sense of the object (*karman*). "Mukunda has sat" (*āsito mukundaḥ*) means "he has sat" (*āsitavān*). "He has sat" (*āsitam tena*) is an example in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāva*). Regarding the rule "after roots meaning 'to go'": because those [roots] are transitive (*sakarmaka*), the suffix *kta* occurs in the sense of the agent (*kartṛ*) and the object (*karman*), but not [in the sense of the abstract state].
The meaning is "in the sense of a state" (bhāve), because [the suffix] is not seen in the rule *laḥ karmaṇi ca* (Pāṇini 3.4.69); this is the intention. Regarding *bhujeḥ karmaṇi*:

the suffix *kta* is applied to the root *bhuj* in the sense of the object (*karman*) when it means "eating," but not in the sense of a state (*bhāve*), because a suffix in the sense of a state is not seen for transitive roots in the rule *laḥ karmaṇi ca*. Nor is it [applied] after roots signifying "consuming" (*pratyavasāna*).

The meaning is that [the suffix] does not apply in the sense of the agent (*kartari*), because it is not so prescribed. Why? Because it has already been stated that the *kta* suffix does not occur after the root *bhuj* in the sense of the agent; this is the intended sense. He provides the resolution: "They have eaten" (*bhuktamasti eṣām*).

For after roots meaning "to go" (*gatyartha*), the *kta* suffix certainly occurs even in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāve*), since there is no distinction made, as in the case of the word *ajaryam*.

This is because the *bhāṣya* on the sūtras "saṃgatam" and "anekam anyapadārthe" accepts the application of the *kta* suffix in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāva*) after roots meaning "to go"; this is explained in detail in the *Śabdenduśekhara*. Regarding the phrase "having taken [this] as the governing rule": this is understood by skipping over [the intervening rules], like a frog's leap (*maṇḍūkapluti*), from the rule "the *laṭ* suffix is used for the present tense."

The meaning is "continuing" (*anuvartamāna*), for it is stated in the commentary (*bhāṣya*) on the sūtra *bhūte* that affixes such as *cānaś* have all three times (*sarvakālatā*). (890) *ñītaḥ ktaḥ* | 3.2.187 | [The suffix *kta* is applied after a verbal root ending in *ñi* or *ī*].

*Ñītaḥ ktaḥ*: The meaning is that *kta* is applied after a root (*dhātu*) that has *ñi* as its augment (*it*), provided that the action is occurring in the present. This rule is formulated because, according to the rule "tayoreva kṛtyaktakhalarthāḥ," the suffix *kta* prescribed for the past tense applies only to the meanings of the abstract state (*bhāva*) and the object (*karman*); it would not otherwise apply to the present tense. Thus, [the rule] is commenced. In *kṣviṇṇa*, the augment *iṭ* is not inserted by the rule "ādiśca. In *iddha*, [the same applies].
By the rule *śvīditaḥ*, the augment *iṭ* is prohibited.

(891) *matibuddhipūjārthebhyaśca* [Pāṇini 3.2.188]. The analysis of the compound is: those whose meanings are *mati*, *buddhi*, and *pūjā*. [The suffix *kta* is applied] in the sense of the present tense.

Thus [is] the remainder. "Of those two alone" means of the *bhāva* (action/state) and *karman* (object) alone. "Considered" (*mataḥ*) means desired (*iṣṭa*). The suffix *kta* is applied to the roots *man* and *iṣ*, which have the sense of "desiring. Because the rule "tīṣasaha" allows for the optional application of *iṭ*, the rule "yasya vibhāṣā" prevents the insertion of *iṭ*. "Cultivated" (*śīlita*) and "protected" (*rakṣita*)—this is a verse found in the Bhāṣya.
Regarding the phrase "ityādi" (and so forth): by the word "ādi," the following summary is included: "Both *ruṣṭa* and *ruṣita* are also [declared] as *abhivyāhṛta*.

Likewise, *hṛṣṭa* and *tuṣṭa*, as well as *ākānta*; both *saṃyata* and *udyata*. 'It will be painful (*kaṣṭam*),' they say; *amṛta* is remembered as being like the former. Thus is the summary. The word *kaṣṭa*...
It will come to pass; the meaning is that the word *amṛta* applies to the present time.
(892) "The suffix *kta* is used in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) when it is neuter" (Pāṇini 3.3.114). Regarding this [rule]: "in the generality of time."

The intended meaning is that [the action] is not included within the scope of the present tense and so forth. It is clear from both the *Bhāṣya* and Kaiyaṭa on the sūtra "ṇeradhyayane vṛttaḥ" that the suffix *kta* occurs only after intransitive verbs (*akarmaka*) in the sense of the impersonal abstract noun (*napuṃsake bhāve*), and not after transitive verbs (*sakarmaka*). Making this point clear, he provides examples only from intransitive verbs:

Regarding the passage beginning with "jalpitam" (spoken) and so forth: in cases such as "gataṃ" (gone) and "bhuktam" (eaten), one should understand that they are treated as intransitive because their objects are not intended to be expressed. For this very reason, in examples such as "gataṃ haṃsasya" (the going of the swan) and "bhuktam odanasya" (the eating of the rice), the genitive case is used to express the sense of residual relation (*śeṣatva*). This is the general direction.

(893) *suyajo-ṅvanip* | 3|2|103|. The meaning is: after the roots *su* (to press) and *yaj* (to sacrifice), the suffix *ṅvanip* occurs. The genitive case is used in the sense of the ablative (*pañcamyarthe ṣaṣṭhī*). The intention is that this [suffix] falls under the governing rule for the past tense (*bhūte*).

Having heard [the rule], "sutvā" and "sutvāna" are formed. In the suffix *ṅvanip*, the markers *ṅ* and *āp* are elided; the vowel *i* is for the sake of pronunciation. Because of the marker *ṅ*, there is no *guṇa* substitution. (894) *jīryater atṛn* 3.2.104. [The suffix *atṛn* is added after the root *jṝ* to form a noun denoting the agent.]

Regarding the rule *jīryateratṛn*: the meaning is that the suffix *atṛn* occurs after the root *jṛ* when it denotes a past (bhūta) sense. The letters *ṛ* and *n* are elided; thus, the suffix *at* remains. From *jaran*, the nasal augment *num* is added because the suffix is marked with the *u* indicatory letter (*ugit*). From *jīrṇa*, the substitution of *ṛ* for *ṛt* applies, followed by the substitution of *ra* for the semivowel, and then the doubling of the consonant according to the rule *hali ca*.
