The term *sakhā ca panthāśca* is a *dvandva* compound. The suffix *a* is applied, and by the rule *ṭhnastaddhite*, there is elision of the final vowel (*ṭilopa*). However, in the reading *sakhipatha*, it is a *tatpuruṣa* compound meaning "the path of a friend" (*sakhyuḥ panthā*).
As for *ramyapatha*, the analysis (*vigraha*) is "one whose path is beautiful" (*ramyaḥ panthā yasya*).
(929) *ac* [is added] after *sāman* and *loman* when preceded by *prati*, *anu*, or *ava*.

[The sūtra states: *ac-pratyaya-anv-ava-pūrvāt-sāma-lomnaḥ*. This means "preceded by these"—that is, preceded by *prati*, *anu*, or *ava*. For example, *pratisāmam*: the analysis (*vigraha*) is "the *sāman* has returned" (*pratigataṃ sāma*). [The suffix] *ac* is applied; [this is governed by the rule] *ṭh-nas-taddhite*.

There is the elision of the suffix *ṭi*. Regarding *anusāma*: the analysis is "that which has followed the *sāman*"; [the suffix] *ac*; elision of *ṭi*. Regarding *avasāma*: the analysis is "that which is drawn down from the *sāman*"; *ac*; elision of *ṭi*. Regarding *pratiloma*: the analysis is "that which has gone against the hair (*loman*)"; *anuloma* [is analyzed similarly].

The analysis (*vigraha*) of *anugataṃ loma* is "hair following [the grain]. The analysis of *avaloma* is "hair gone against the grain. In all these cases, the suffix *ac* is applied, with the elision of the *ṭi* portion. Regarding the term *kṛṣṇodak*, this is not a Vārttika; rather, it is a statement by an authoritative scholar based on a formal separation (*yogavibhāga*) of the rule *ac* into *a* and *j*. As for *kṛṣṇa*: [End of excerpt]

The analysis [of the compounds] is as follows: "that whose ground is black," "that whose ground is northern," "that whose ground is white," "that which has two grounds," and "that which has three grounds. In all cases, "palace" (prāsāda) is the head-word (viśeṣya).
Regarding the rule "after a numeral" (*saṅkhyāyāḥ*): this too is based on a formal split (*yogavibhāga*) of the rule *aj-*. [The rule applies] after a numeral.
The meaning is that it will be understood by means of the two words "para" (the other) and "nadī" (river), as well as the word "godāvarī.
Regarding "pañcanadam": the analytical derivation (*vigraha*) is "the collection of five rivers. Regarding "saptagodāvaram": the analytical derivation is "the collection of seven Godāvarīs."
The compound *nadībhiśca* is an *avyayībhāva*. By the rule *aci yasyeti ca*, there is elision [of the final vowel of the first member].
By the rule *nāvyayībhāvāt*, [the feminine suffix] *ām* is not applied. Regarding the phrase "even elsewhere": the word *aj* (in the neuter) is to be understood as the remainder. As for *padmanābha*:
the analysis (*vigraha*) is "one who has a lotus (*padma*) in the navel (*nābhau*). In reality, however, [this is an example of] the division of the rule (*yogavibhāga*).
Since it is not seen in the Bhāṣya, it is more appropriate to treat it as belonging to the *pṛṣodarādi* group.

(930) *Akṣṇo 'darśanāt* |5|4|76|. [The word] *akṣi* [is formed] from *adarśana*. The analysis is: *adarśanāt*. [It is derived from the root *dṛś*, with the suffix *in* in the sense of] "that by which something is seen" (*dṛśyate 'nena*).
"Darśana" means the eye; the suffix *lyuṭ* is used in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇa*). Thus, it results that [the term applies] to what does not denote the eye.

He states this with the words "from a synonym for non-eye. In the phrase "like the eye of cows," the word *akṣi* (eye) is used with the particle *iva* to indicate that it is used figuratively (*lākṣaṇika*) for something resembling an eye; it is not used in its primary sense (*mukhyavṛttyā*).

[The word *akṣi* is not included in this list] because it lacks the sense of "expressing vision" (*cakṣurvācakatvābhāvāt*). Its masculine gender is established by common usage (*lokāt*). (931) *acatura-avicaturasucatura-strīpuṃsa-dhenu-anaḍuh-ṛksāma-vāṅmanasa-akṣibhruvadāra-gava-uṣṭhīva-padaṣṭhīva-akta-nakta-diva-rātri-diva-aha-rātra-ajas-rajas-niḥśreyasa-puruṣāyuṣa-dvyāyuṣa-trayāyuṣa-ṛgyajuṣa-jātokṣa-mahokṣa-vṛddhokṣa-upaśuna-goṣṭhaśvāḥ* || Pāṇini 5.4.77. [In these compounds, the final member retains its original form. The following are the examples: *acatura*, *avicatura*, *sucatura*; *strīpuṃsa*; *dhenu*, *anaḍuh*; *ṛksāma*; *vāṅmanasa*; *akṣibhruva*; *dāragava*; *uṣṭhīva*, *padaṣṭhīva*; *akta*, *nakta*, *diva*, *rātri*, *diva*, *rātri*, *diva*, *aha*, *rātra*, *aja*, *rajas*, *niḥśreyasa*, *puruṣāyuṣa*, *dvyāyuṣa*, *tryāyuṣa*, *ṛgyajuṣa*, *jātokṣa*, *mahokṣa*, *vṛddhokṣa*, *upaśuna*, and *goṣṭhaśva*.

"Acaturaḥ": the first three are *bahuvrīhi* compounds; that is to say, they are exclusively *bahuvrīhis*. This is a statement from the Bhāṣya. Regarding "acaturaḥ": by the rule "naño'styarthānām," there is the elision of the word expressing existence (*asti-pada*). Regarding "vicaturaḥ": it means "one from whom four have departed."
The analysis [of the compound] is as follows: *sucatura* means "one whose four are very beautiful" (*su-śobhanāni catvāri yasya*).
The prohibition [stated in Pāṇini 5.4.69], "not after a word of worship," is set aside.
[Accordingly,] the suffix *aji* is applied to the word *catur* when preceded by the two words *tri* and *upa*.

"From *tri* and *upa*"—this is a Vārttika. It means that the suffix *ac* will be applied after the word *catur* when it follows *tri* or *upa*. Thus, *tricaturaḥ*. The analysis (*vigraha*) is "three or four. This is a *bahuvrīhi* compound according to the rule *saṅkhyā-vyaya-āsanna...*. [In the section on] *bahuvrīhi*:
In the case of a numeral (*saṅkhyeya*), by the rule *ḍa’jiti*, the suffix *ḍac* is superseded by *ac*. If *ḍac* were applied, however, there would be elision of the final syllable (*ṭilopa*).
Thus we have *upacaturāḥ*, meaning "three or five. This is a *bahuvrīhi* compound according to the rule *saṅkhyayāvyaye*.
Then, by the rule *ac*, [the suffix *ac* is added]. From that, it follows that there are eleven *dvandva* compounds; the meaning is that they are indeed *dvandvas*. This also [is so].

This is a statement from the Bhāṣya: "strīpuṃsau" (woman and man). The analysis (*vigraha*) is "strī ca pumāṃśca" (a woman and a man). [The suffix] *ac* is applied. Thus, the form "dhenvaḍvāhau" does not occur. However, in the case of a collective copulative compound (*samāhāradvandva*), it is already established by the rule "dvandvāccudaṣahāntāt. As for "ṛksāme," the analysis is "ṛk ca sāma ca" (the Ṛgveda and the Sāmaveda).

The analysis (*vigraha*) is: *ac* [suffix], with the elision of the *ṭi* portion. Thus, it does not become *ṛksāmanī*. For *vāṅmanase*, the analysis is: *vāk* and *manaḥ*. [With the suffix] *ac*, it does not become *vāṅmanasī*.
For *akṣibhruvam*, [with the suffix] *ac*, there is singular number (*ekavadbhāva*) because they are parts of a living being (*prāṇyaṅga*). It does not become *akṣibhru*.
Regarding "dāragavam": this is formed with the suffix *ac* from a collective (*samāhāra*) *dvandva* compound; thus, it does not become "dāragu.

However, in an associative (*itaretarayoga*) *dvandva*, it would be "dāragāvaḥ. Regarding "ūrvaṣṭhīvam": because these are parts of a living being (*prāṇyaṅga*), they are treated as a singular unit. *Ūru* refers to the thighs; *aṣṭhīvantau* refers to the knees.

Regarding this, Amara states: "The word *sakthi* is neuter; *rū* is masculine," and "the knee (*jānu*), the thigh (*ūru*), and the joint of the knee (*aṣṭhīvat*) are not feminine. Now, one might ask: since [the suffix] *ṭhañ* has been elided and the word ends in *an*, how can there be the elision of the *ṭi* (the final vowel and following consonant)? To this he says: "By way of irregular derivation (*nipātana*), there is the elision of the *ṭi*. Thus we have *paṭ-aṣṭhīvam*. And the two feet are the two *aṣṭhīvants*.

The suffix *ac* is applied after this *dvandva* compound. Because it denotes a part of a living being (*prāṇyaṅga*), it is treated as a singular. Now, one might ask: since the word *pāda-* does not end in the vowel *a*, how can it undergo the substitution of *pad-* here? To this he says: "by means of an irregular derivation" (*nipātana*). *Naktam* is an indeclinable ending in *m*; *divā* is an indeclinable ending in *ā*. The form *naktamdiva* is derived from the *dvandva* [of *nakta-* and *divā-*, with the elision of the final *ā*] by means of the suffix *ac*.

By the rule *yasyeti ca*, there is the elision of the vowel *ā*; by the rule *avyayībhāvaśca*, it acquires the status of an indeclinable (*avyaya*) as well as neuter gender. By the rule *nāvyayībhāvāt*, the substitution of *am* occurs. Regarding the statement "the finality of *m*" (*māntatvam*): when the compound *rātrau ca divā ca* (night and day) is formed as a *dvandva*, after the elision of the case-ending (*sup-luk*), the finality of *m* for the word *rātri-* is prescribed as a grammatical irregularity (*nipātana*).

This is the meaning. By the rule *yasyeti ca*, there is the elision of the vowel *ā* and the substitution of *ambhāva*. Now, one might object: since the referent of the word *ahar* (day) and the referent of the word *divā* (by day) are identical, there is an absence of co-occurrence (*sāhitya*); how, then, can there be a *dvandva* compound here?
Even if a *dvandva* were applicable by taking into account the difference between individual instances of "day," [the following applies]: "Even for words that are dissimilar..."

Since the *ekaśeṣa* (retention of one) rule would be unavoidable for words having the same meaning, he says: "The *dvandva* is prescribed by way of exception (*nipātana*) in the sense of distributive repetition (*vīpsā*).

The meaning is that when the doubling (*dvirvacana*) has been applied in the sense of distributive repetition according to the rule *nityavīpsayoḥ*, the *dvandva* is prescribed by way of exception, thereby setting aside the *ekaśeṣa*. [The example is] *sarajasam*.

The compound *rajo'pyaparityajya* has its constituent members not separated (*asvapadavigraha*). *Rajaḥ* means dust. The indeclinable *saha* forms an *avyayībhāva* compound with the word *rajas* in the sense of totality. According to the rule *avyayībhāve cākāle*, the substitution of *sa-* for *saha* occurs. The suffix *ac* is applied because it is an *avyayībhāva*; this is stated in the Bhāṣya.
The intention is that by such a statement, the *avyayībhāva* compound is included. Regarding the example *sarajaḥ paṅkajam* (a lotus with pollen):
the analysis (*vigraha*) is "together with dust" (*rajobhiḥ parāgaiḥ saha*). This would otherwise form a *bahuvrīhi* by the rule *tena saheti tulyayoge*.
However, by the rule *vopasarjanasya*, the substitute *sa-* is applied for *saha-*. Because it is a *bahuvrīhi*, the feminine suffix *āP* does not apply.
Regarding "niḥśreyasam": the suffix *ac* is applied after a *karmadhāraya* compound; the intention is that it occurs only after a *tatpuruṣa*, as indicated by the Bhāṣya. Regarding "niḥśreyān":

since this is a *bahuvrīhi* compound meaning "one for whom there is certain (*niścita*) welfare (*śreyaḥ*)," the suffix *ac* does not apply. Furthermore, because of the prohibition in the rule "ṭhīthasaśca," the suffix *kap* is not added.

Regarding the term *puruṣāyuṣam*: the *Bhāṣya* states that this is a genitive compound (*ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa*) ending in the suffix *ac*. Then, regarding *dvigū*, this is a statement from the *Bhāṣya*. As for *dvyāyuṣam* and *tryāyuṣam*, the analytical explanations (*vigraha*) are "the collection of two lifespans" and "the collection of three lifespans," respectively. [This falls under the rule] *taddhitārtha...* [Pāṇini 2.1.51].
Thus ends the section on *dvigu* compounds ending in *-ac*. Then follows "then the *dvandva*," which is a statement from the *Bhāṣya*. Regarding "the *ṛgyajuṣam*":

it is a collective *dvandva* (*samāhāra-dvandva*) meaning the collection of both *ṛc*s and *yajus* verses. Then follow three instances of *karmadhāraya* compounds; such is the sense, as it is stated in the *Bhāṣya*. Regarding "the *jātokṣa*": [it is formed by the same principle].

The analysis (*vigraha*) is: "he is born and he is a bull" (*jātaś cāsāv ukṣā ca*). When the suffix *ac* is present, there is the elision of the *ṭi* in the word *ukṣan*. Thus, *mahokṣa*: the analysis is "he is great and he is a bull" (*mahāṃś cāsāv ukṣā ca*). By the rule "after *mahat*, [the substitution of] *āt* [occurs]," there is the substitution of *āt*; when *ac* follows, there is the elision of the *ṭi*. *Vṛddhokṣa*: the analysis is "he is old and he is a bull" (*vṛddhaś cāsāv ukṣā ca*). When *ac* follows...

There is elision of the *ṭi* [the final vowel and following consonant]. Thus, we have *upaśunam*. This is because the suffix *ac* is applied after an *avyayībhāva* compound, according to the Vārttika. Now, one might ask: why does the elision of the *ṭi* not occur here by the rule *ṭhnastaddhite*? [The answer is: because of the exclusion (*paryudāsa*) by the phrase *ataddhite* [in that rule]. Furthermore, how is there vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule *śvayuvamaghonāmataddhite*?
To this he says: "The elision of the suffix *ṭi* and the *saṃprasāraṇa* are treated as irregular (*nipātana*).

Thus we have *goṣṭhaśva*. According to the *Bhāṣya*, [the suffix] *ac* is applied after a locative compound (*saptamīsamāsa*). For this very reason, it is a locative compound. There is an elision of the suffix *ṭi*; however, because of the prohibition "not before a *taddhita* suffix," [the elision does not apply here].

There is *saṃprasāraṇa* [of the semivowel]. However, in a *ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa* compound, as in *goṣṭhaśva* ("a horse in a cow-pen"), there is no such change. (932) *brahmahastibhyāṃ varcasaḥ* (Pāṇini 5.4.78). Regarding the word *brahma*: he explains the sūtra by supplying the missing portion, stating that *ac* [the suffix *ac*] should be applied. Thus, we have *brahmavarcasam*.
The analysis [of the compound] is *brahmaṇo varcaḥ*. In the case of *hastivarcasam*, the analysis is *hastino varcaḥ*.
It should be stated that [the suffix *aC* is applied] after the words *palya* and *rājan* as well.

Regarding the phrase "by *palya* and *rājan*": the meaning is that it should be stated that the suffix *aj* is also applied after the word *varcas* when these two precede it. Thus, *palyavarcasam*. Here, *palya* means flesh (*palam*); one who deserves that is a *palya*, meaning a meat-eater. The analysis (*vigraha*) of the compound is "the splendor (*varcas*) of that [meat-eater]. Similarly, *rājavarcasam* [is analyzed as] "the splendor of kings."
The analysis [of the compound] is *varcas*.

(933) *avasamandhebhyastamasaḥ* | Pāṇini 5.4.79. [The suffix *aṇ* is applied after the word *tamas* when it follows the words] *ava*, *sam*, and *andha*. [That is to say, the suffix is applied] after these: *ava*, *sam*, and *andha*.
The meaning is that the suffix *ac* occurs after the word *tamas*. Regarding *avatamasam*: the analysis (*vigraha*) is "that from which darkness has departed" (*ava-hīnaṃ tamas*);
it is a *prādi* compound. Regarding *saṃtamasam*: the analysis is "continuous darkness" (*saṃtataṃ tamas*);
it is a *prādi* compound. Regarding *andham* in the sense of "it blinds": the root *andh* (meaning "to impair vision") belongs to the *curādi* class.

The meaning is that it obstructs vision. Regarding "pacādyaj": the meaning is that the suffix *ac* is applied because [the root] belongs to the *pacādi* class, according to the rule "nandi-grahi-pacādibhyaḥ lyu-ṇini-ac-aḥ. When the suffix *ac* is present, the form *andha* arises through the elision of the *ṇi* [augment]. It means "intensely" (*gāḍham*). It bears fruit; [namely,] of that very dense darkness...
Because it obstructs vision. Regarding the term *andhatamasam*: the suffix *ac* is applied after a *karmadhāraya* compound.
(Pāṇini 5.4.79). Regarding the rule *śvasovasīyaśśreyasaḥ* (5.4.80): after the indeclinable (*avyaya*) *śvas*, there follows the word *vasīyas* and the word *śreyas*.
Therefore, the meaning is "he would become an *ṛc*. The word *vasu* denotes that which is praiseworthy;
this is because we observe such usage in passages like, "Whomever one might desire: 'May he become more prosperous (*vasīyān*),' and so forth. Regarding the term *tataḥ*:
in the analysis (*vigraha*) as "one who is exceedingly *vasu*," the suffix *iyasun* is applied by the rule *dvivacanavibhajyopapade*.

With the continuation of the rule *ṭhṭhuriṣṭhemeyassu*, the elision of the *ṭi* portion by the rule *ṭer* results in the word *vasīyas*. Regarding the word *śvas*: although the word *śvas* denotes a specific time, nevertheless, due to the inherent nature of the word's expressive power (*śabda-śakti-svabhāva*) in this context, it conveys the excellence residing in the meaning of the subsequent member (*uttarapada-artha*), which is the object of the benediction (*āśīr-viṣaya*).
The meaning is "it illuminates. *Āśīrviṣayaḥ* is a genitive compound (*ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa*) meaning "the object of a benediction" (*āśiṣo viṣayaḥ*).

It is an adjective qualifying "praise" (*praśaṃsā*). Because the word *viṣaya* is invariably masculine, it does not take the feminine gender. Thus, the word *śvas* (tomorrow) is an indicator (*dyotaka*) of the excellence inherent in the meaning of the final member of the compound.

The meaning is established. Now, one might object: "In that case, even though the word *śvas* indicates excellence residing in the meaning of the subsequent member (*uttarapada*), how can there be a *viśeṣaṇa-samāsa*, given the absence of grammatical coreferentiality (*sāmānādhikaraṇya*) with the subsequent member? To this he says: *mayūra-*. Thus, intending that its correctness occurs only in usage such as the benedictive optative (*āśīr-liṅ*) and so forth, he provides the example: *śvovasīyasam*. The meaning is "exceedingly excellent. Regarding *śvaḥśreyasam*: in the analytical explanation (*vigraha*) "exceedingly excellent," the suffix *īyasun* is added to the word *praśasta*, [resulting in] *praśasyasya śraḥ*.

Because of the rule *ṭhprakṛtyaikā'c* (Pāṇini 6.4.163), there is no elision of the suffix *ṭi* due to the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*). By the rule *ādguṇaḥ* (Pāṇini 6.1.87), the form *śreyas* is established. The word *śvas*, however, indicates praise pertaining to the meaning of the subsequent member (*uttarapada*). As Amara states: *śvaḥ-śreyasaṃ śivaṃ bhadram*. The phrase *te bhūyāt* ("may it be yours") is connected with both: *śvovasīyasaṃ te bhūyāt* and *śvaḥ-śreyasaṃ te bhūyāt*. (935) *anvavataptādrahasaḥ* (Pāṇini 5.4.81). [The analysis is: *anu*, *ava*, *tapta*—this is a collective dvandva compound. From these [words], when followed by...

The meaning is that the suffix *ac* is applied after the word *rahas*. *Rahaḥ* means a non-public place. Regarding *anurahasam*: the analysis (*vigraha*) is "that which has approached (*anugata*) a secluded place (*rahaḥ*). Regarding *avarahasam*: the analysis is "a secluded place (*rahaḥ*) that is not abandoned (*avahīnam*). In both cases, it is a *prādi*-compound (a compound with an indeclinable as the first member). Regarding *taptarahasam*: [the analysis is] "a heated secluded place."

Such is the analysis (*vigraha*). Regarding *praterurasaḥ*: it is called "standing in the locative" (*saptamīstha*) because it occurs as an indicator (*dyotaka*) for the sense of the locative case. The meaning is that the suffix *ac* shall be applied after the word *uras*, provided it follows the prefix *prati* when the latter indicates the sense of the locative. By the phrase "on the chest" (*urasīti*), exactly that which is stated [by the rule] is expressed.
The meaning is that this is expressed by the word *pratyurasam*. The prefix *prati* indicates the sense of the locative case.

Since it occurs in the sense of a case ending, the compound is formed as an *avyayībhāva* according to the rule "an indeclinable [is compounded] with a word ending in a case suffix," and so forth; this is the intended sense.

(936) *anugavamāyāme* | 5|4|83|. Regarding *anugavamāyāme*: this means that the word *anugavam* [is a *nipātana*]. The meaning is that when length (*dīrghatva*) is to be indicated by the prefix *anu*, it is prescribed as a *nipātana* ending in the suffix *ac*. The word *āyāma*...
The meaning is "one that is long. Regarding the term *anugavam-yānam*: the meaning is that the vowel substitution (*av-ādeśa*) occurs after the word *anugu* when the suffix *ac* is applied.

Regarding the phrase *yasya ca*: this refers to the *avyayībhāva* compound according to the rule *yasya cāyāmaḥ*. Thus, the resulting sense is "a vehicle whose length is that of a cow. This is the intended meaning.

(937) *dvistāvā tristāvā vediḥ* |5|4|84|. "Twice as large" (*dvistāvā*). "As large as in the archetype" (*yāvatī prakṛtau*). Since there is an extended application (*atideśa*) of the entire collection of constituent parts (*aṅgakalāpa*), that is the archetype (*prakṛti*). The Agniṣṭoma is the archetype of the Aśvamedha.

In that regard, because of the extended application (*atideśa*) [of rules] from the Aśvamedha sacrifice, the collection of subsidiary parts (*aṅga-kalāpa*) prescribed therein [is applied]. This has been stated in the Kalpasūtra: "The Agniṣṭoma is the archetype (*prakṛti*) of all Soma sacrifices.
In that Agniṣṭoma, the measurement of the altar (*vedi*) is heard in scripture; and therein, it is said: "three hundred steps..."

In the archetype (prakṛti), the measurement of the altar is stated as: "The side-steps (prakrama) are thirty-six to the west and across; forty-four to the east; and thirty-six to the front across. However, for this [specific] altar, the measurement of the area is stated as being double and triple that [of the archetype].
In the *Kalpasūtras* it is stated: "The *Māhāvedi* is eight thousand minus twenty-eight *padas*.

Here, the mention of *pada* is also an elliptical indication (*upalakṣaṇa*) of the *prakrama*. Thus, in the archetype (*prakṛti*), the *agniṣṭoma*, the altar (*vedi*) is twice or thrice as large as that [of the *agniṣṭoma*] in rituals such as the *aśvamedha*.
In that context, regarding the altar for the horse sacrifice (aśvamedha) which is to be described, the meaning is that it becomes "twice that" (dvistāvat) and "thrice that" (tristāvat).
According to the rule "kṛt-suc after a numeral when counting the repetition of an action" (*saṅkhyāyāḥ kriyābhyāvṛttigaṇane kṛt-suc*) and the rule "suc after the words dvi,
tri, and catur" (*dvitricaturbhyaḥ suc*), the suffix *suc* is applied to the word *dvi* to denote the repetition of an action.

The forms are *dvis* and *tris*. In this context, *tāvatī* means "that which has the original measure (*parimāṇa*)," that is to say, "having the original measure. The word *dvis* connects with the original measure, which is the meaning of the pronoun *tat*. The analysis (*vigraha*) is: *dvis-tāvatī*, meaning "repeated twice" (*dvirāvṛtam*).

The meaning is that the sacrificial altar (*vedi*) of the Aśvamedha is of the same measure as that which is prescribed for the Prākṛta [sacrifice]. Precisely because of this irregular formation (*nipātana*), there is a compound; the suffix *ac* is applied, and by the rule "bhasyāḍhe" (Pāṇini 1.2.48), the word *tāvatī* undergoes masculine substitution (*puṃvat*).
Consequently, the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is removed. Even though the suffix is not *ḍit*, the base does not end in a long vowel *ā*.

There is elision of the suffix *ṭi*. [In the examples] "a rope twice as long" (*dvistāvatī*) and "a rope three times as long" (*tristāvatī*), the meaning is that because the application [of the rule] does not occur with respect to the sacrificial altar (*vedi*), the suffix *ac*, the elision of *ṭi*, and the compound formation do not take place. Thus, in the counter-example, the word "dvi" is a separate word.

(938) *upasargād adhvanaḥ* | Pāṇini 5.4.85. The meaning of *upasargād adhvanaḥ* is that the suffix *ac* shall be applied after the word *adhvan* when it follows a prefix (*upasarga*). For example: *prādhvo rathaḥ*. Here, the suffix *ac* is applied to the compound according to the rule *atyādayaḥ*.
There is elision of the *ṭi* [the final vowel and following consonant] by the rule "ṭhnastaddhite" (Pāṇini 6.4.143).

(939) "Not after a word expressing praise" (na pūjanāt 5.4.69). The phrase "after others" (*parebhyaḥ*) is to be supplied [to the sūtra]. [This refers to] the section on "suffixes at the end of compounds" (*samāsānta*).
The preceding sūtra is carried over [into this one]. Thus he says: "from the root meaning 'to honor' (*pūjanārtha*).
With the intention of the Vārttika—"the inclusion of *su* and *ati* must be made [in the rule] regarding honoring"—he provides the examples:
*surāja* and *atirāja*. *Surāja* means "a beautiful king" and is a *prādi*-compound (prepositional compound). *Atirāja* means "one who is highly honored."

The meaning is "king. In both cases, the suffix *ṭac* is applied by the rule *rājāhaḥsakhibhyaṣṭac*. "Only after *su* and *ati*" means that it occurs only after the word *rājan* when it follows *su* or *ati*; such is the sense according to the Vārttika. "Not here" implies "in the case of prohibition," as is understood from the context.

Regarding *paramarāja*: the analysis (*vigraha*) is "he who is both supreme (*parama*) and a king (*rājā*). Regarding *atigava*: the compound is formed by the rule "atyādayaḥ" (Pāṇini 2.2.18). Since the prefix *ati-* does not have the sense of "reverence" (*pūjana*), the prohibition of the suffix *ṭac* does not apply.
The same applies to *paramarāja*. As for the phrase "prior to this": it refers to the mention of the term *bahuvrīhi* occurring earlier [in the sūtras].

This is a summary of the meaning of the *vārttika*: "it should be applied. Regarding the examples *susakthaḥ* and *svakṣaḥ*: the analysis is "one whose two thighs (*sakthinī*) are very beautiful" and "one whose two eyes (*akṣiṇī*) are very beautiful.
The suffix *ṣac* is applied by the rule *bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇor ac*. Regarding the rule *kimaḥ kṣepe*: [the examples are] *kiṃrājā* ("what a king! and *kiṃsakhā* ("what a friend!").
In this case, the suffix *ṭac* is applied by the rule "rājāhaḥsakhibhyaṣṭac," and the compound is formed by the rule "kiṃ kṣepe" (the word *kim* is compounded when used in a derogatory sense).
Thus we have *kiṃrājaḥ* and *kiṃsakhaḥ*. Here, the word *kim* is used in the sense of a question; the analysis (*vigraha*) is either "whose king? or "what kind of king?"

(940) *Nañastatpuruṣāt* |5|4|71|. Since no censure is understood, there is no prohibition of the suffix *ṭac*. [The rule] *Nañastatpuruṣāt*—he explains the sūtra by supplying the missing words: "the compound-final suffix (*samāsānta*) is not [added]."

The result is that there is no application of the compound-final suffix (*samāsānta*) after a *tatpuruṣa* compound whose prior member is the negative particle *nañ*. For example, in the case of *adhuraṃ śakaṭam* ("a cart without a yoke"), the analysis is "that of which the yoke (*dhur*) does not exist. Even though the prior member is the negative particle *nañ*, because it is not a *tatpuruṣa* [in this specific sense], the compound-final suffix prescribed by the rule *ṛkpūrabdhūḥpathāmānakṣe* does not apply.
The prohibition [of the suffix *ṭac*].
(941) *patho vibhāṣā* |5|4|72|. Regarding "from *pathas*": this means from the word *pathin*. As in *apathim* ("not a path"). Not [the other case].

In the analysis (*vigraha*) as *apatha*, it is a negative compound (*nañ-tatpuruṣa*). When the suffix *ap* is applied by the rule *ṛkpūḥ*, the elision of the final vowel occurs by the rule *na-staddhite*. Neuter gender is established by the rule *pathaḥ saṅkhyāvyayādeḥ*. Thus, *apathaḥ* is the form when the suffix *ap* is absent.
The phrase "only from a *tatpuruṣa*" is understood to carry over [from the previous rule]. Regarding the example "an inaccessible region" (*apatha*):

the analysis of the compound is "that which has no path" (*avidyamānaḥ panthā yasya*). Because it is a *bahuvrīhi*, there is not even an optional prohibition of the suffix *ap* (as prescribed by the rule *ṛkpūr-*) [which would otherwise apply].
Thus ends the section on compound suffixes (*samāsānta*) in the *Bālamanoramā*.
Now follows the rule based on compound formation:

(969) *gharūpakalpacelaḍbruvagotramatahateṣu ṅyo'nekāco hrasvaḥ*. In the presence of the suffixes *gha*, *rūpa*, *kalpa*, *celaṭ*, *bruva*, *gotra*, *mata*, and *hata*, the penultimate vowel of a word ending in the feminine suffix *ṅī* that has more than one syllable is shortened.

[6.3.43] Now, the rules dependent on compound formation (*samāsāśrayavidhi*) are examined: *gharūpa*. The governing term "in a subsequent member" (*utarapade*) applies to *celaḍ* and the others, but not to *gha*, *rūpa*, and *kalpa*, because the suffixes *tarap* and *tamap* are what is denoted by the word *gha*.

And because [the suffix] *kalpa* is a condition (*pratyaya*). Nor should it be argued that when there is a reference to that which ends in [the suffix], the status of being a subsequent member (*uttarapadatva*) is impossible for those [suffixes]; for it has been stated in the Bhāṣya regarding the rule *hṛdayasya hṛllekha* that, within the governing context of "subsequent member" (*uttarapada*), there is no inclusion of that which ends in [the suffix] when a suffix (*pratyaya*) is being referred to. [The rule continues: *striyāḥ*.

From the rule *puṃvat* (Pāṇini 6.3.34), the phrase *bhāṣitapuṃskāt* is understood [as a qualifier]. The mention of *ṅī* [in the rule] is intended to include that which ends in *ṅī*, because the suffix *ṅīp* alone cannot consist of more than one syllable (*anekāctva*). Thus he says: "from a word denoting a male (*bhāṣitapuṃska*) which has the suffix *ṅī*. It is for this very purpose that the term *bhāṣitapuṃskāt* is included in the rule *striyāḥ puṃvat*.

In that context, the word *bhāṣitapuṃskāt* is used in the ablative case (*pañcamyantam*) in the rule "from a word denoting a male (*bhāṣitapuṃska*), [the feminine suffix] *ṅīp* [is elided]. It is for this very purpose that the term *bhāṣitapuṃskāt* is employed in the ablative case in the rule "of the feminine (*striyāḥ*), [there is] the masculine form (*puṃvat*). In that context, it is stated:

"from a word denoting a male (*bhāṣitapuṃskāt*), [the feminine suffix] *ṅīp* [is elided]. It is for this very purpose that [the term *bhāṣitapuṃskāt*] is employed in the ablative case in the rule "of the feminine (*striyāḥ*), [there is] the masculine form (*puṃvat*)."

The term *bhāṣitapuṃskāt* is used here in the ablative case (*pañcamyanta*). If, however, it were used in the genitive case as *bhāṣitapuṃskāyāḥ*, then its reference (*anuvṛtti*) would not apply here, because that is impossible. For the suffix *ṅīp* itself, nor that which ends in it, possesses the quality of having a corresponding masculine form (*bhāṣitapuṃskatva*). Nor even in that [other] case...

It should not be argued that [the rule] would not apply because, by the exclusion (*paryudāsa*) "not ending in *ūṅ*," the feminine suffix is obtained, and thus that which ends in it lacks the quality of having been previously mentioned as masculine (*bhāṣitapuṃska*). For in that context, since the word "of the feminine" (*striyāḥ*) is not marked with a svarita accent, it has been stated that there is no inclusion of the feminine suffix itself. [Example: *brāhmaṇitarā*.

The form *brāhmaṇitama* occurs; the suffixes *tarap* and *tamap* are used in the sense of excellence (*atiśāyana*). Nor is there a removal of the feminine suffix *ṅīp* by virtue of the rule *tasilādiṣu*, because that rule is prohibited by the rules *saṅkhyāḥ* and *jāteśca*.
In the form *brāhmaṇirūpā*, the suffix *rūpap* is used in the sense of praise (*praśaṃsā*). [Likewise] *brāhmaṇikalpā*.

The suffix *kalpa* is applied by the rule *ṭhīṣadasamāptau*. Regarding *brāhmaṇicelī*: from the root *cila* (meaning "to wear"), the suffix *aca* is added, and *celaḍ* is listed among the roots in the *pacādi* group; because it has the marker *ṭi*, the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied. Regarding "and so forth": [examples include] *brāhmaṇimatā* and *brāhmaṇihatā*. Regarding *brūñ*: when the suffix *ac* is added to the root *brūñ*, [the form *brū* is derived].

The meaning is that in the case of *vāci*, there is the prescribed substitution (*nipātana*) of the absence of both the replacement by *vāc* and the *guṇa* substitution of the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*).

Regarding "the words *celaṅ* and so forth": in the domain of compound formation (*samāsavṛtti*), since the subsequent members *celaṅ*, *bruvan*, *gotra*, and *hatā* denote contempt, [the rule] "contemptuous things [are compounded] with contemptuous words" (*kutsitāni kutsanaiḥ*) applies.

The meaning is that it is a *karmadhāraya* compound. Regarding the term *āmalakītara*: since the word *āmalakī* denotes a tree and is invariably feminine (*nityastrīliṅga*), it lacks the quality of being "originally masculine" (*bhāṣitapuṃska*); therefore, by the rule [Pāṇini 6.3.43], there is no shortening of the vowel—this is the intended sense.
Now, an objection might be raised: in the *Mahābhāṣya* on the sūtra "not at the end of a word" (*na padānte*), the words *bimba*, *badarī*, and *āmalaka*...

Because it is understood that [the word] has already been used as masculine, one might ask how the word *āmalakī* can have an obligatory feminine gender (*nityastrīliṅgatva*) when referring to a specific tree; expressing dissatisfaction with this, he says: "the other *kuvalī*. The intention is that this word is obligatorily feminine when denoting a tree. However, Amara [states]: "The *karkandhū*, the *badarī*, and the *kolī*..."
The word *ghoṇṭā* is stated to be neuter in the sense of "the *kubala* fruit.

(970) *nadyāḥ śeṣasyānyatarasyām* | 6.3.44. [The suffix *ṅīp*] is optionally applied after the remainder (*śeṣa*) of a feminine stem ending in a *nadī* vowel. The "remainder" (*śeṣa*) refers to that which is other than what was mentioned [in the preceding rules]. This follows from the previous rule: *ṅyantasyānekācaḥ*.

That otherness [of the case] is possible even when there is no status of being a stem ending in a *ṅī* suffix with more than one vowel (*anekāc*), provided that the stem ending in *ṅī* lacks more than one vowel. Thus he says:

"of a feminine stem (*nadyāḥ*) not ending in *ṅī*, and of a monosyllabic stem (*ekācaḥ*) ending in *ṅī*. In the word *brahmabandhūḥ*, the suffix *ūṅ* is applied according to the rule "after *ūṛ* and *u*" (*ūṛutaḥ*).
Intending that the phrase "of that which has the masculine form" (*bhāṣitapuṃskasya*) does not carry over here, he provides the example: *stritarā*.
[The suffix] is not applied after a word ending in a *kṛt* affix or a nadī stem.
"Kṛnnādyā na" means it should be stated that the short vowel [substitution] does not apply to a *nadī* (feminine noun) ending in a *kṛt* suffix.
Regarding "lakṣmītara": the word *lakṣmī* is a *kṛdanta* because the suffix *ī* with the augment *muṭ* is applied to the root *lakṣ* by the rule "ṭhlakṣermuṭ ca. This is the intended meaning.

(971) *ugitaśca* | 6|3|45 | "And [the feminine suffix] *nīp* is applied after a stem ending in an *ugit* vowel. For example, *viduṣitarā*. Here, the suffix *vasu* is applied by the rule *videḥ śaturvasuḥ*.

This [stem *vidvas-*] ends in an *ugit* vowel (*u*). Since it consists of more than one syllable (*anekāc*), the application of the elision (*śeṣatva*) of the suffix *nīp* would not otherwise be obtained; this is the intended meaning.

Regarding "vidvatareti": the meaning is that when the *puṃvat* (masculine) substitution applies and the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is removed, the form becomes "vidvataretī. Regarding "that is without foundation": the meaning is that the *puṃvat* substitution is unavoidable. The *Vṛtti* states: "The *puṃvat* status for 'vidvat' and 'śreyas' need not be stated. However, this statement...

The sense is that this [interpretation] is to be disregarded because it is not seen in the Bhāṣya. Here, the root text—"after an *ugit* [stem], the following *nadī*"—is intended to convey the view that the designation *nadī* applies only to the two vowels (*varṇau*). (972) *hṛdayasya hṛllekhayadaṇlāseṣu* (Pāṇini 6.3.50).

Regarding *hṛdaya*: the meaning is that in these subsequent [forms] such as *hṛllekha*, there is the substitution of *hṛd* for *hṛdaya*. *Hṛllekhaḥ* means "one who writes the heart" (*hṛdayaṃ likhati*), with the suffix *aṇ* by the rule *karmaṇyaṇ*. *Hṛdyam* means "dear to the heart"; here the suffix *yat* is applied by the rule *hṛdayasya priyaḥ*. *Hārdam* means "belonging to that"; here the suffix *aṇ* is applied by the rule *tasyedam*.

The substitution of *hr̥d* [for *hr̥daya*] occurs. Regarding the term *hallāsa*, the intention is that this word ends in the suffix *ghañ*. As for the inclusion of *lekha* as ending in the suffix *aṇ*, the ancient commentators maintain it is due to the co-occurrence (*sāhacarya*) with the suffix *aṇ*. However, the truth is that it is due to the specific explanation (*vyākhyāna*). If that is so, then the mention of *lekha* would be useless, since the form is established even by the suffix *am*; to this he replies: "It is an indicator" (*jñāpaka*).

He states the portion to be made known: "In the governing rule for subsequent members (*uttarapada-adhikāra*), there is no application of the rule regarding that which ends with such a member (*tadanta-vidhi*). The result of this, however, is the absence of *tadanta-vidhi* when the terms *gha*, *rūpa*, and *kalpa* are mentioned.

(973) *vā śokaṣyañrogeṣu* || 6.3.51 || *vā śoka*: *sauhārdyam*—here, because the word belongs to the *brāhmaṇa*-group, the suffix *ṣyañ* is applied in the sense of abstract state (*bhāva*), and by the rule *ṭhhṛdbhagasindvante*, there is vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*) in both parts of the compound. *Sauhṛdayyam*—here, likewise, the suffix *ṣyañ* is applied in the sense of abstract state.

The intention is that because the word *hṛd* lacks the sound *ś*, there is initial *vṛddhi* [by P. 7.2.117], and then the form is derived by the elision [of the final syllable] according to P. 6.4.148 (*yasyeti ca*). (974) *pādasya padājyātigopahateṣu* | 6.3.52. [The substitute] *pada* replaces *pāda* before *āji*, *ati*, *ga*, and *upahata*. The word *pade* is a separate word with the nominative case elided. "Before these" refers to *āji*, etc.

The meaning is: "in these [roots], namely *āp*, *gam*, and *upahata*. Regarding "ending in *ad*": the intention is that since the subsequent sūtra specifies *pad* as having a consonant (*hal*) at its end, this [restriction] applies here. Regarding "he goes" (*ajati*): [the root is] *ṭhaja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ* (DhP 1.234).
Regarding "pedātir" (*padāti*): the analysis is "one who goes by means of the feet" (*pādābhyām atati*). [The root is] *ata gatau* (DhP 2.37), [along with] *aj* and *ati*.

The meaning of that [sūtra] is that the affix *iṇ* occurs when *pāda-* is the upapada, whether the root is *aja-* or *ata-*. Anticipating the objection that the rule "ṭhājī" would require the substitution of *vy* for *aj* (by the rule "ajervyaghañapoḥ"), he says: "The substitution of *vy* for *aj* is due to nipātana. This means it is because of the specific mention (*nirdeśa*) of the form "ājī. [The example] is *padagaḥ*, [meaning] one who goes by means of two feet (*pādābhyām*).

The meaning is "he goes. By the *vārttika* "it is seen after other [roots] as well," which is attached to the rule *gamaśca* (Pāṇini 3.2.47)—specifically to the portion *antātyantādhvadūrapārasarvānanteṣu ḍaḥ*—the suffix *ṅa* is applied to the root *gam*.
When the word *ga*, ending in that suffix, follows, the substitution of *pada* for the final syllable of *pāda* occurs. However, if the substitution were to end in *d*, [the following would apply].

It would be *ṭhpadga* [instead of *pādaga*]. [The form] *padopahata* [is derived as follows]: the analysis (*vigraha*) is "struck by the feet" (*pādābhyām upahataḥ*). Here too, if there were a substitution of a *d*-final [suffix], it would be *ṭhpadupahata*.
(Pāṇini 6.3.53) *padyatyatadarthe* ("[The suffix *yat* is applied after the root *pad*] when not in the sense of 'fitting'").

The analysis of *padyati* is as follows: the division is *pada-yati-atadarthe*. Regarding *padyā*: the suffix *yat* is applied according to the rule *vidhyaty-adhanuṣā*. Regarding *pādyam*: the suffix *yat* is applied according to the rule *pādārghābhyāṃ ca* in the sense of "for the sake of" (*tādarthye*).
[Addendum: An inclusionary statement (*upasaṅkhyānam*) should be made for the suffix *ika* in the sense of "moving upon."

Regarding the rule *i ke caratau*: the meaning is that there is an extension (*upasaṅkhyāna*) stating that when the substitute *ik* occurs in place of the suffix *ṣṭhan* prescribed in the sense of "moving" (*carati*), the word *pād* should replace *pāda* before that [substitute].
(976) *himakāṣihatiṣu ca* | 6.3.54 | [The substitution of *pād* for *pāda* occurs] also before the words *hima*, *kāṣin*, and *hati*.
*Himakāṣī*: when these [words] follow, *pāda* becomes *pat*; this is the meaning. *Paddhimam*:

the analysis (*vigraha*) is "the snow of the foot" (*pādasya himam*). *Patkāṣī*: the meaning is "one who scrapes with the feet" or "one who scrapes by means of the feet. The suffix *ṇini* is applied according to the rule *supyajātau*. *Paddhati*: it is that which is struck (*hanyate*).

*hṛtiḥ* [is derived as follows]: the suffix *ktin* is applied in the sense of the object (*karman*). The analysis (*vigraha*) is "striking with the feet" (*pādābhyāṃ hṛtiḥ*). The compound is formed by Pāṇini 2.1.32, *kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulam*. (977) *ṛcaḥ śe* (Pāṇini 6.3.55).

Regarding the word *ṛcaḥ*, it is explained with the intention that the locative case is used because it is an imitation (*anukaraṇa*) of the single portion of the suffix *śas* belonging to the root *śas*. Thus, he provides the example: *pacccha* (verse by quarter).
According to the rule *saṅkhyaikavacanācca vīpsāyām*, the suffix *śas* is added after the word *pāda* to express distributive repetition (*vīpsā*).

And because it ends in *taddhita* and lacks all case-endings (*asarvavibhakti*), it possesses the status of an indeclinable (*avyaya*); however, there is no inclusion here of the group beginning with *loman*, because the word *pāda* is not recited among those beginning with *loman*. [The example is: "He gives a *kārṣāpaṇa* by the quarter" (*pādaśaḥ kārṣāpaṇaṃ dadāti*).
This means he gives a specific measure of value called a *kārṣāpaṇa*—such as gold coins and the like—quarter by quarter (*padaṃ padam*).
The meaning is "he gives.
(978) *vā ghoṣamiśraśabdeṣu* | 6|3|56|. Regarding *vā ghoṣa*: he explains the sūtra by supplying the remainder [of the rule], namely: *pādasya pada*.
And it should be stated: "also before *niṣka*.
Regarding "also before *niṣka*," the remainder [of the rule] is "for *pāda*, *pad*" (Pāṇini 6.3.52).
(979) *udakasyodaḥ saṃjñāyām* (Pāṇini 6.3.57): "In the sense of a name (*saṃjñā*), *uda* is substituted for *udaka*."

*Udaka* becomes *uda*. The meaning is that the word *udaka* undergoes the substitution *uda* when followed by another word (*uttarapada*) in the context of a proper name (*saṃjñā*). For example, *udamegha*: this is a name for someone because of his resemblance to a cloud filled with water.
It should be stated: "and [the substitution applies] to the final member.

Regarding the phrase "and to the final member": the meaning is that for the word *udaka* occurring as the final member, the substitute *uda-* shall take its place when it forms a technical name (*saṃjñā*). For example, *kṣīroda*: that of which milk (*kṣīra*) stands in the place of water (*udaka*).
[The compound] *vigrahaḥ* [is explained as follows]: the form *kṣīrodaṃ saraḥ* ("the milk-ocean lake") is incorrect, because it is not a conventional name (*asaṃjñātvāt*).

(980) *peṣaṃvāsavāhanadhiṣu ca* | Pāṇini 6.3.58. Regarding *peṣaṃvāsa*: *peṣam* is an indeclinable (*avyaya*) ending in the suffix *ṇamul*. In that case, [the final vowel of the preceding word is lengthened] before *vās*, *vāhana*, and *dhi*.

The meaning is that after the word *udaka*, *uda* shall occur [in place of *udaka*]. This statement is for the purpose of excluding its use as a technical name (*saṃjñā*). For example: *udapeṣaṃ pinaṣṭi*. The meaning is "he grinds with water. The suffix *ṇamul* is applied by the rule *snehane piṣaḥ*. In the case of *kaṣādi* roots, there is the subsequent employment (*anuprayoga*) according to the original form of the verb. As in *udavāsaḥ*: this means "the dwelling in water" (*udakasya vāsaḥ*).
The analysis [of the compounds] is as follows: *udavāhana*—the suffix *lyuṭ* is used in the sense of an instrument (*karaṇe*); thus, the meaning is "one who carries water.

*udadhiḥ ghaṭaḥ*—the analysis is "that in which water (*udaka*) is placed (*dhīyate*). The suffix *ki* is applied by the rule "after a word denoting the object, when the sense is that of a location" (*karmaṇy adhikaraṇe ca*). The word "jar" (*ghaṭa*) is used as the substantive (*viśeṣya*) to indicate that this is not a technical name (*asaṃjñātva*).

Regarding "samudre tu": the meaning is that since the word *udadhi* is a technical name (*saṃjñā*), the substitution of *uda-* for *udaka-* is already established by the preceding rule, "udakasyodaḥ" (Pāṇini 6.3.58). (981) Pāṇini 6.3.59: "In a word beginning with a single consonant, when it denotes something to be filled, [the substitution of *uda-* for *udaka-*] may optionally take place."

In the case of a single consonant at the beginning [of a word], since the substitution of *h* for *has* is already established by the fact that it is a property of each individual phoneme (*varṇa*), the explicit mention of "single" (*eka*) allows one to understand that it must be uncombined (*asaṃyukta*). "To be filled" (*pūrayitavya*) refers to things like jars (*kumbha*) which are fit to be filled.
When a word denoting something to be filled begins with an uncombined consonant as the following member (*uttarapada*), the word *udaka* becomes *uda*.
The meaning is that such an injunction (*ādeśa*) should take place.

(982) *Manthaudanasaktuvinduvajrabhārahāravīvadhagāheṣu ca* | 6|3|60|. In the case of *mantha*, *odana*, etc., the remainder of the rule is: "there is optionally the substitution of *ud* for *udaka*" (*udakasya udādeśo vā*). This is for the purpose of filling out the sense.

The word is *udamantha*, meaning "water-mash. The analysis (*vigraha*) is "a mash mixed with water" (*udakamiśro manthaḥ*). A *mantha* is parched grain flour (*saktu*) mixed with a liquid substance; specifically, *saktu* refers to the flour of roasted barley. [The term] *udaudana* means "water-rice"; the meaning is "mixed with water. The phrase "and so forth" includes *udasaktavaḥ* ("water-grain-flour").

*udaka-saktavaḥ*, *udabindavaḥ*, *udakabindavaḥ*; *udavajraḥ*, *udakavajraḥ*; *udabhāraḥ*, *udakabhāraḥ*; *udahāraḥ*, *udakahāraḥ*; *udavīvadhaḥ*, *udakavīvadhaḥ*; *udagāhaḥ*, *udakagāhaḥ*. A *vīvadha*, however, is a carrying-pole suitable for fetching water and the like, having two loops at both ends and slung over the shoulder externally.
A specific type of wood.

(983) *iko hrasvo’ṅyo gālavasya* | P. 6.3.61. The analysis is: *ikaḥ* [the short vowel] *hrasvaḥ* [is substituted], and *aṅyaḥ* [provided it is not part of a compound ending in *aṅ*]. For example, *grāmaṇīpatraḥ*. This is a *karmadhāraya* compound.
Or it is a genitive compound (*ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa*). The meaning is that this *ī* belongs to the root *nī*, and not the feminine suffix *ṅīp*.
Now, one might ask: why could the mention of Gālava not signify an option?
To this he replies: "because of the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the term *anyatarasyām*."

The rule "na" (negation) should be stated for those [stems] that undergo the substitution of *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ*, as well as for indeclinables. Regarding the phrase "of those that undergo *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ*": the meaning is "of those [stems] that are eligible for them. In the example "śrīmad-bhrūbhaṅgaḥ," the point is that the words *śrī-* and *bhrū-* are eligible for the substitutions *iyaṅ* and *uvaṅ* when followed by a suffix beginning with a vowel (*aj-ādi*).
Regarding the term *śuklībhāva*: when the suffix *cvi* is applied in the sense of "becoming that which it was not," the substitution of *ī* for *ṭha* occurs by the rule *ṭhasya cvau*.

Then, by the rule *ṭhcvau*, lengthening (*dīrgha*) takes place. The intention is that its status as an indeclinable (*avyaya*) follows from its being a particle (*nipāta*) according to the rule *ūryādicviḍācaśca*.
It should be stated as "of *abhrū*, *kuaṃsa*, and so forth.

Regarding "of *abhrū*, *kuaṃsa*, and so forth": since the word *bhrū* is subject to the substitution of *uvaṅ*, a prohibition of shortening (*hrasva*) would otherwise apply; the meaning is that this [prohibition] does not take effect. By this [rule], the vowel *a* [is substituted]. Thus: "of *abhrū*, *kuaṃsa*, and so forth."

In the *Vārttika*, "ṭha" is a separate word with the nominative case elided. Thus, the meaning is that there is another interpretation according to which the vowel *a* is the final substitute for the word "bhrū" when it is a member of a compound such as *bhrūkuaṃsa*. [The resulting form is] *bhrukuṃsa*, meaning "one who speaks with his eyebrows."

The meaning is: "the making known of such-and-such a thing. Amara states: "Bhrūkuṃsa, bhrukuṃsa, and bhrūkuṣa refer to a dancer," and also: "Bhrukuṭi, bhruṃkuṭi, and bhrūkuṭi are feminine [terms for a frown]. (984) *Ekataddhite ca* | Pāṇini 6.3.62.

"Also in a *taddhita* [suffix], when *eka* [is present]. The word "eka" here has its genitive case ending elided. Thus he says: "of the word *eka*. The remainder [to be supplied] is "ending in a feminine suffix," for otherwise the rule prescribing the short vowel would be redundant. "And when it is a subsequent member (*uttarapada*)"—the sense is that by the particle *ca*, the preceding [condition] is drawn forward. "Uniformity" (*ekarūpyam*).
The suffix *rūpya* is optionally applied after words ending in *hetu* and *manuṣya*. For example: *ekakṣīram*. The analysis (*vigraha*) is: "the milk of one woman" (*ekaśyāḥ kṣīram*).
(Pāṇini 6.3.63): "In names and in Vedic literature, the elision of the feminine suffixes *ṅī* and *āp* occurs diversely."

"Of *ṅī* and *āp*"—the remainder [of the rule] is that there shall be a short vowel (*hrasva*) in the subsequent member (*uttarapada*). For example: *revatiputraḥ*. This is the name of a certain person. Now, he gives an example from the Veda (*chandas*): *ajakṣīram*. The analysis (*vigraha*) is "the milk of a goat. As it is said in the Taittirīya: "This is indeed the supreme milk, namely the milk of a goat."
Regarding *tve ca*: he explains the sūtra by supplying the missing portion—when the suffix *tvap* follows, there is optionally shortening (*hrasva*) of the feminine suffixes *ṅī* and *āp*.

Thus: "the state of being unborn" (*ajatvam*) and "the state of being Rohiṇī" (*rohiṇitvam*). Because it lacks the status of a technical term (*saṃjñātva*), this [suffix] occurs only in the Vedic language; such is the commentary (*vṛtti*). This statement is for the sake of the subsequent rule. (987) Pāṇini 6.1.13: *ṣyaṅḥ saṃprasāraṇaṃ putrapatyostatpuruṣe* ("In a Tatpuruṣa compound, there is vocalization of the semivowel in the element ending in *ṣyaṅ* when followed by *putra* or *pati*").

There is *saṃprasāraṇa* for *ṣyaṅ*. By the paribhāṣā regarding the mention of a suffix (*pratyayagrahaṇaparibhāṣā*), the term "ṣyaṅ" includes that which ends in it. Thus he says: "of the preceding member ending in *ṣyaṅ*. The intention is that although this rule occurs within the governing heading (*adhikāra*) concerning the "subsequent member" (*uttarapada*), the status of being a "preceding member" (*pūrvapada*) is obtained through the mention of the *tatpuruṣa* compound.

Regarding the phrase "in the case of the two latter members": this too is obtainable from the term *tatpuruṣa*. Alternatively, by virtue of the governing heading (*adhikāra*) concerning the "latter member" (*uttarapada*), the "former member" (*pūrvapada*) is implied.

(988) *saṃprasāraṇaṃ putrapatyostatpuruṣe* | 6|1|13| [In a *tatpuruṣa* compound, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the vowels of the words *putra* and *pati* when they are the former members.]
"Of the *saṃprasāraṇa*, there is lengthening. The sense is that this is because of the continuation (*anuvṛtti*) of that [rule] from "when there is elision of *ṭh*, *ḍh*, or *r*.
"In the subsequent member (*uttarapada*)"—the sense is that this is because of the governing scope (*adhikāra*) of "elision when there is no subsequent member.
"The son of Kaumudagandhyā"—this is an analytical sentence (*vigrahavākya*). Like the fragrance of a water-lily (*kumuda*).

He whose scent is that [of the kumuda] is "kumudagandhi. This is a *bahuvrīhi* compound according to the rule: "A *bahuvrīhi* is to be stated for a word preceded by a locative case or a word denoting a standard of comparison (*upamāna*), with the optional elision of the final member.
Thus, in the first part of the compound *kumudagandha*, there is the elision of the subsequent member, the word *gandha*.

The substitution of *it* occurs after a word ending in *ṭhu*. In the sense of "the female offspring of Kumudagandhi," the suffix *aṇ* is applied by the rule *tasyāpatyam*. By the rule *aṇiñoś cānārṣayor gura-vato 'striyām*, this *aṇ* is replaced by *ṣyaṅ*.
By the rule *yasyeti ca*, the vowel *i* is elided. There is initial vṛddhi strengthening. Finally, the feminine suffix *cāp* is added after *ṣyaṅ*.

The intended meaning is the word *kaumudagandhyā*. [In the analysis] "the son of *kaumudagandhyā*," it is a genitive compound (*ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa*). When the case endings have been elided (*subluk*), and the form *kaumudagandhyā-putra* has been established, the semivowel *ya* undergoes vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) to become *i*. Then, for that [vocalized *i*] and the subsequent vowel *ā*, [the substitution of *vṛddhi* occurs].
The intended meaning is that, by the rule *saṃprasāraṇācca*, the vowel *i* is replaced by its former form (*pūrvarūpa*), and by the rule *saṃprasāraṇasya*, the long vowel is applied,

resulting in the form *kaumudagandhīputra*. However, the application of the long vowel by the rule *halaḥ* is not relevant here, because [the rule *halaḥ* applies] to a consonant (*hal*) preceding the *saṃprasāraṇa*.
Because there is an absence of any limb or constituent part specified as having undergone *saṃprasāraṇa*.
Regarding the example *kaumudagandhīpatiḥ*: the analytical derivation (*vigraha*) is "the husband of Kaumudagandhyā.
The grammatical formation (*prakriyā*) is as before; however, by the rule *ṭhiko hrasvo'ṅgyo gālavasya*, the short vowel is optional.

Fearing that [the vowel] might be short, he says: "By the rule of *vyavasthita-vibhāṣā* (optional restriction), it is not short. In this matter, however, the commentary itself is the sole refuge. This may be so:
*karīṣaṃ* means the dung of cows, buffaloes, and so forth; [the word *karīṣagandhi* refers to one] whose scent is like the scent of *karīṣa*.
*Karīṣagandhi*—the feminine descendant of that [man] is *kārīṣagandhyā*; she who is both supreme (*paramā*) and *kārīṣagandhyā* is *paramakārīṣagandhyā*; her son is *paramakārīṣagandhīputra*.
In this case as well, there is the *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization) of the suffix *ṣyaṅ*, and its lengthening.

[The rule regarding] *sthiti* [is as follows]: here, *saṃprasāraṇa* is difficult to obtain. Since the suffix *ṣyaṅ* is prescribed only after the word *karīṣagandhi*, the preceding member of the compound *paramakārīṣagandhyā* does not end in *ṣyaṅ*. According to the principle that "when a suffix is mentioned, it refers to that which begins with the element after which it is prescribed and ends with it," [the condition for *saṃprasāraṇa* is not met].

To address the objection beginning with "because of the inclusion [of the base]," he says: "and when there is a feminine suffix (*strīpratyaya*). Since *ṣyaṅ* is prescribed for the feminine, it is a feminine suffix.

Consequently, according to the maxim of the later grammarians—"and when there is a feminine suffix that is not a subordinate member (*anupasarjana*), [the rule applies] to what begins with that"—there is an absence of the restriction that the suffix must apply only to what begins with the base;
thus, even the word *paramakārīṣagandhyā* ends in *ṣyaṅ*. Therefore, in that case...
The intention is that when there is *saṃprasāraṇa* and the subsequent lengthening, the form is "paramakārīṣagandhīputra.

This *paribhāṣā* is cited in the Bhāṣya on the current rule, "ṣyaṅḥ saṃprasāraṇam. Regarding that, he states the purpose of the inclusion of the term "anupasarjana" (non-derivative): "But in the case of a derivative (*upasarjana*), however..."

In the compound *atikārīṣagandhyaḥ* (meaning "one who has surpassed Kārīṣagandhyā"), the feminine suffix is elided by the rule *atyādayaḥ*, and the preceding vowel is shortened as it is an *upasarjana*. His son is *atikārīṣagandhyaputraḥ*. In this case, the prohibition—"the restriction regarding the initial element [of the compound] does not apply when a feminine suffix is present"—does not take effect, because that rule applies only when the suffix is not an *upasarjana*.

Because that prohibition applies when a feminine suffix (*strīpratyaya*) follows; however, this *ṣyaṅ* suffix here is merely a subordinate element (*upasarjana*). Therefore, since the rule regarding the initiality of the stem (*tadādiniyama*) applies there, the word *atikārīṣagandhya* does not end in *ṣyaṅ*, and thus there is no vowel substitution (*saṃprasāraṇa*). This is the intended meaning.

(989) *bandhuni bahuvrīhau* | 6|1|14 | Regarding the rule "in a *bahuvrīhi* compound when [the final member] is *bandhu*": as in *kārīṣagandhībandhuḥ*. Since there is no subsequent member *pati* and no *tatpuruṣa* compound, the application of the preceding rule does not occur here.

"Or in *mātañ*, *mātṛka*, and *mātṛ*. This is a *vārttika*. The meaning is that when *mātañ*, *mātṛka*, or *mātṛ* follow, the *saṃprasāraṇa* of *ṣyaṅ* should optionally be stated. [In the case of] *mātañ*:

He provides examples: *kārīṣagandhīmātaḥ* and *kārīṣagandhyāmātaḥ*. Here, the word *mātṛ* undergoes the substitution of *māta*. This form ends in the vowel *a*. He provides examples for the suffix *-mātṛka*: *kārīṣagandhīmātṛkaḥ* and *kārīṣagandhyāmātṛkaḥ*.

The suffix *kap* is applied by the rule "nadītaśca. He provides examples for the word *mātṛ*: *kārīṣagandhīmātā* and *kārīṣagandhyāmātā*. These forms occur when the secondary (*śaiṣika*) suffix *kap* is absent. Now, one might ask: what is the authority for the substitution of *mātṛj* for the word *mātṛ*, given that the suffix *kap* is prescribed as obligatory by the rule "nadītaśca" and not merely optional?

Because [the form] is difficult to obtain, he says "for this very reason. He explains that this [suffix] occurs only in a *bahuvrīhi* compound, because the intention is that this *vārttika* is recited in the rule *bandhuni bahuvrīhau*.
He states that the addition of the *c* marker in *mātaj* is for the sake of accent (*svara*), saying "by virtue of the power of the *c* marker."

(990) *iṣṭakeṣīkāmālānāṃ citatūlabhāriṣu* || 6.3.65 || The words *iṣṭaka*, *iṣīkā*, and *mālā* [undergo *puṃvadbhāva*] when followed by the words *cita*, *tūla*, and *bhārin* respectively. The governing rule "in a subsequent member" (*uttarapade*) is understood here.
That which was obtained as the preceding member is qualified by the words *iṣṭaka* and so forth. This is a rule of *tadanta-vidhi* (application to that which ends with the specified word).

Their inclusion occurs by virtue of the principle of *vyapadeśivadbhāva* (treating a thing as identical to what it designates). Alternatively, their inclusion may occur because the governing rule for the "subsequent member" (*uttarapada*) is accepted as being a governing rule for the "word" (*pada*), or by the explicit statement: "In the governing rules for *pada* and *aṅga*, [the operation applies] to that and to what ends with it. From the rule "the short vowel for *ika*" (*iko hrasvaḥ*), the word "short" (*hrasva*) is understood to carry over (*anuvartate*).
Thus he says: "of *iṣṭakā* and so forth, ending with that. Regarding *iṣṭakacitam*:
the analysis (*vigraha*) is "piled by means of bricks and so forth" (*iṣṭakādibhiścitam*). This is a compound formed according to the rule *kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulam*.
He states the purpose of the rule for [compounds] ending in that: *pakveṣṭakacitam*. [And as an example: *iṣīkātūlam*.
The analysis of the compound is *iṣīkāyās tūlam* (the tuft of a reed). *Tūla* means the tip; others say it means *śaṣpa* (young grass). The analysis of *muñjeṣītātūlam* is *muñjeṣīkāyās tūlam*.
In the word *mālabhārī*, the suffix *ṇini* is applied according to the rule *supyajātau* (Pāṇini 3.2.78). [In the sūtra, it says *āriṣu*...]
Alternative reading:
(991) *kāre satyāgadasya* | 6|3|70|. Regarding the rule *kāre satyāgadasya*, he explains the sūtra by supplying the missing portion: "the suffix *mum* shall be applied."

The intention is that this [suffix] is understood from the rule *ṭhād dviṣat* (Pāṇini 5.4.120). The resulting meaning is that the augment *mum* occurs when the word *satya* or *agada* is followed by the suffix *kāra*. In *mum*, the letter *m* is the *it* (the marker indicating the position of the augment), while the letter *u* is for the sake of pronunciation (*uccāraṇārtha*).

Because it is marked with *m* (*mit*), it is placed after the final vowel. Thus, we have *satyaṅkāraḥ*. Here, the suffix *ghañ* is used in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāve*); it is the act (*kāra*) of truth (*satyasya*).
Such is the analysis [of the compound]. The meaning is "the making of an oath. Regarding the term *agadakāra*: *gada* means disease;

its absence is *agada*. Since it is stated that a *tatpuruṣa* compound may optionally take the place of an *avyayībhāva* when expressing the absence of something, the meaning here is "one who performs the act of healing" (*agadakāra*).

It should be stated that [the suffix] *mu* is applied after the word *astu*. Regarding "after *astu*": the remainder is that the suffix *mu* is added to the syllable *kāra*. Thus, it becomes *astuṅkāra*.
The indeclinable *astu*, which is a formal derivative (*pratirūpaka*) of a verbal form ending in a *tiṅ* suffix, is used in the sense of assent (*abhyupagama*).

[In the case of] *dhenubhavyā*. Regarding "of *dhenu*": the remainder [of the rule] is "the suffix *mum* should be stated. Thus, *dhenubhavyā*. This expression refers to the period prior to her first calving; the meaning is "a cow that is about to become one. [This is governed by the rule] *bhavyadeya*.
The kṛtya suffix occurs here by way of an irregular derivation (*nipātana*) in the sense of the agent. The analysis of the compound is: "she who is both a cow (*dhenu*) and auspicious (*bhavyā*).
The word *bhavyā* is placed last according to the *mayūravyaṃsakādi* class.
[She is] for the fulfillment of the world.

"‘For the filling of the world’ (lokasya pṛṇe); the remainder [of the compound] is ‘ṭhumvaktavyaḥ’ (the suffix ṭhu must be stated). Now, one might object: if the analysis is *lokaṃ pṛṇati* (it fills the world), then by the rule *karmaṇyaṇ*, with the guṇa substitution for the light penultimate vowel and the replacement of the vowel by *ra*, the form would be *parṇa*; to this he replies:
‘Because it belongs to the class beginning with *mūlāvibhuja* (roots that grow outwards), the suffix *ka* is applied.’"

Thus, regarding *anabhyāśam itya*: the remainder [of the rule] is "the suffix *mum* should be stated. *Anabhyāśam itya* means: *abhyāśaḥ* is proximity; *anabhyāśam* is distance. This is the accusative case ending. [It is derived] from the root *iṇ*.

The suffix *kyap* is applied to the root *prāp* (in the sense of "reaching") by the rule *ṭhetistuśā'sityādi*; then, by the rule *gamyādīnāmupasaṅkhyānam*, a compound with a word in the accusative case is formed. When the case-endings (*sup*) are elided, the augment *mum* is inserted. Keeping in mind the meaning—"one who is to be brought to a distance, and not to a near place"—he says: *dūrataḥ*.
"It must be avoided.
[In the case of] *bhrāṣṭrāgnyor indhe*, [the form] *bhrāṣṭrāgnyor indhe* [is derived]. The remainder [of the rule] is "the augment *ṭhmuṃ* should be stated. Thus, [the form] *bhrāṣṭram indhaḥ*.

A vessel for roasting grain and the like is a *bhrāṣṭra*; one who kindles or heats that is a *bhrāṣṭramindhah*. [The suffix] *aṇ* is applied by virtue of the rule *karmaṇyaṇ*, followed by a compound with an *upapada*. Upon the elision (*luk*) of the case-ending, the augment *mum* is inserted.
Regarding *agnimindhah*: it means "one who kindles the fire."
Regarding *gile'gilasya*:

the analysis is *gile'gilesya*. [The word] *agilasya* is to be separated as *a-gilasya*. The meaning is that when *gila* follows, the augment *mum* may optionally be applied to that which is different from *gila*. In the example *timiṅgila*, [the root is] *gṛ* in the sense of "swallowing."
*Timi* is a particular kind of fish. [The term *gilagila*] is derived from the root *gṛ* (to swallow) with the suffix *ka*, according to the rule for words beginning with *mūlavibhuja* and others.
By the rule "ṭhAñta iddhātoḥ," the substitution of *ra* occurs, and by the rule "aci vibhāṣā," the substitution of *la* occurs; this forms an *upapada* compound.
With the elision of the case-ending (*subluk*), the augment *mum* is added, resulting in *gilagila*. This, too, is a particular kind of fish.
And regarding *gilagile*:
[the word] *gilagile* means that the suffix *mum* should be stated after *agila*. Thus, *timiṅgilagila*:
[it is derived as] "one who swallows a *gila*" (*gilaṃ gilatīti*); *gilagila* is the term, and the analysis (*vigraha*) is "the *gilagila* of whales" (*timīnāṃ gilagilaḥ*).

The genitive case (*ṣaṣṭhī*) is used in the sense of a general relationship. Alternatively, *timiṣu gilagila* is a locative of specification (*nirdhāraṇasaptamī*). The compound is formed by the rule "in the sense of a technical name" (*saṃjñāyām*), which prescribes the locative compound (*saptamīsamāsa*).
[This applies] when *uṣṇa* and *bhadra* function as instruments (*karaṇe*).

Regarding the rule *uṣṇabhadrayoḥ karaṇe*: the meaning is that [the suffix] *mum* is to be elided. "The making hot" (*uṣṇaṅkaraṇam*) and "the making auspicious" (*bhadraṅkaraṇam*) are genitive compounds (*ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa*). (Pāṇini 6.3.72) *rātreḥ kṛti vibhāṣā*.

The word *kṛti* [is used here] because it stands under the governing heading (*adhikāra*) concerning the final member of a compound. However, the rule "when a suffix (*pratyaya*) is mentioned, that which ends with it is also included" does not apply here. Since a *kṛt* suffix has a verbal root (*dhātu*) as its base, it is impossible for the word *rātri-* to be followed by a *kṛt* suffix;
therefore, intending to indicate that this is a reference to what ends in such a suffix (*tadantavidhi*), he says: "when a word ending in a *kṛt* suffix follows."

The meaning is that *mum* should be applied after *rātreḥ*. Thus we have *rātriñcaraḥ* and *rātricaraḥ*. When a word ending in a case-suffix (*sup*) is the governing term (*upapada*), the suffix *ṭa* is added to the root *car*; this forms an *upapada-compound*, and when the case-suffix is elided (*luka*), *mum* optionally appears. [Similarly,] *rātrimaṭaḥ* and *rātryaṭaḥ*: when a word ending in a case-suffix is the governing term, the suffix *ka* is added because [the compound] belongs to the class beginning with *mūlavibhuja*; this forms an *upapada-compound*, and when the case-suffix is elided, [the form is established].

*mum* [is applied] in *rātrimaṭaḥ* and *rātryaṭaḥ*. When a *sup*-ending word is the *upapada*, the suffix *ka* is added because [the compound] belongs to the class beginning with *mūlavibhuja*; this is an *upapada-samāsa*. In the alternative where the elision (*luk*) of the *sup* occurs, *mum* is applied. Now, one might object: "In the case of *rātrimmanyaḥ* as well, there would be an optional application of *mum*. To this he says: "for the sake of excluding *khid*" (*akhidartham*). [This is stated] because when there is *khid*, [the rule does not apply].

The meaning is that, having set aside this option (*mum-vikalpa*), the rule "ṭharurdviṣadajantasya" will prescribe the *mum* suffix invariably under the heading of *kṛt*-suffixes by means of a prior prohibition (*pūrvavipratiṣedha*). As for the example *rātirammanyaḥ*: the suffix *khaś* is applied by the rule "ātmamāne khaśca. [Regarding] *khaś*...

Because it has the marker *ś* (śitva), it is a *sārvadhātuka* affix; when this follows, [the rule] "śyan after *div* and so forth" (*divādibhyaḥ śyan*) applies, and because it has the marker *k*, [the rule] "optionally *khaś* in the sense of self-reflexive action" (*ātmamāne khaśca*) applies, resulting in *khaś*. Because *khaś* has the marker *ś* (śitva), it is a *sārvadhātuka* affix; when this follows, [the rule] "śyan after *div* and so forth" (*divādibhyaḥ śyan*) applies.
The sense is that one should always utter "mum.

(993) *sahasya saḥ saṃjñāyām* | 6|3|78|. [The rule] "saḥ replaces saha" applies when there is a subsequent member (*uttarapada*). This is stated by supplying the remainder of the sūtra. "sa" is the substitute for "saha."
The meaning is that this substitution (*ityādeśaḥ*) occurs when there is a subsequent member (*uttarapada*). It is an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule *vopasarjanasya*.
The example *sapalāśam* is a *bahuvrīhi* compound formed according to the rule *tena saha*. This is the name of a particular forest.
In the example *sahayudhva*, the suffix *kvanip* is applied by the rule *sahye ca*; because it is not a technical name (*asaṃjñātva*), the substitution of *sa-* does not take place.

(994) *granthāntādhike ca* |6|3|79|. "And after [words meaning] the end of a book (*granthānta*) and after [the word] *adhika*. This is a collective copulative compound (*samāhāra-dvandva*) consisting of *granthānta* and *adhika*. The phrase "in these two meanings" implies the remainder of the rule, namely *vidyamānasya* ("of that which exists"). The example is *samuhūrtaṃ* ("having lasted for a short time").
The meaning is that he has studied the science of astrology (jyotiḥśāstra) up to the limit of a treatise on the rules for auspicious moments (muhūrta).

The compound is an avyayībhāva used in the sense of "limit" (anta). Regarding the form *sadroṇā khārī*, although the substitution of *sa-* [for *samāna-*] would not have applied here because the rule *avyayībhāve cākāle* excludes time (*kāla*), the inclusion of the term "treatise" (*grantha*) [in the sūtra] serves to include this case as well. Thus, "a khārī containing one droṇa."
The meaning is that it exceeds the measure of a *droṇa*.
Because it belongs to the class beginning with *mayūravyaṃsaka*, there is a compound of the word *saha* used here in the sense of "exceeding," and the substitution of *sa-* for *sa-* occurs.
(995) *dvitīye cānupākhye* |6|3|80|.
And regarding the second [type], which is "inexpressible" (*anupākhyā*): the word "second" is used figuratively for that which is non-primary and lacks a companion.

That which is expressed, understood, or perceived is "expressible" (*upākhyā*), meaning "perceptible"; the opposite of that is "inexpressible" (*anupākhyā*), which is to say, "inferable. Thus he says: "the inferable."
The meaning is: when a word expressing a companion occurs as the final member of a compound. Regarding the example *sarākṣasīkā*:

this is a *bahuvrīhi* compound formed according to the rule *tena saha*. The suffix *kap* is applied by the rule *nady-utaś-ca*. The meaning is: "the night accompanied by an inferable Rākṣasī. Thus he says: "the Rākṣasī is present."

(996) *samānasya chandasy amūrdhaprabhṛtyudarkaṣu* | 6|3|84 | [The word] *samāna* [is substituted for *sa-*] except when followed by *mūrdhan*, *prabhṛti*, or *udarka*. That is to say, the substitution does not occur when these follow. *Sagarbhya* means "born from the same womb" (*samāne garbhe bhavaḥ*). *Sayūthya*.

Thus: the meaning is "one who exists in the same herd. Regarding *sanutya*: the meaning is "one who exists in the same dwelling (*nut*). In all these cases, the substitution of *sa-* for *samāna-* occurs within a compound by the rule *taddhitārtha*.
Regarding *samānamūrdhā*: the analysis (*vigraha*) is "one whose head (*mūrdhan*) is the same. [The same applies to] *samānaprabhṛtayaḥ*.

Thus [it is said]. The analysis of the compound is: "those whose initial members (*prabhṛti*) are the same. Regarding *samānodarkāḥ*: the analysis is "those whose final parts (*udarka*) are the same. In the Taittirīya [Saṃhitā], it says: "In harmony with the seasons (*sajūrṛtubhiḥ*), in harmony with the sacrificial ordinances (*sajūrvidhābhiḥ*), in harmony with the Vasus (*sajūrvasubhiḥ*), in harmony with the Rudras (*sajūrudraiḥ*), in harmony with the Ādityas (*sajūrādityaiḥ*)."

The five mantras—“In harmony with all the gods; in harmony with the gods; in harmony with the gods who bestow vital strength; for Agni Vaiśvānara, may the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryus, settle thee here; settle thee”—are recited as a composite whole. In all five of these mantras, [the phrase] “in harmony with the seasons” [is included].
The initial portion, "sajūrvidhābhiḥ," and the final portion, "sajūrdevairvayonādbhiḥ," are common [to all]; furthermore,
for each of the five [formulas] beginning with "sajūrvasubhiḥ," there is respectively one [formula] in the middle of each mantra.

"Placement" (niveśa) refers to the established convention of the ritualists (*yājñika*). Now, one might ask: how is there the substitution of *sa-* for *samāna-* in worldly words such as *sapakṣa* and others? To this he says: "The connection is divided. Thus, a separate rule is formed: "There shall be *sa-* in place of *samāna-*. And since the restriction "in Vedic usage" (*chandasi*) is absent there, it applies even in the world.
The meaning is that it is obtained [from the statement] "it exists in some cases.

Regarding "sapakṣa": the analysis of the compound is "that which has a similar (samāna) side (pakṣa). Regarding "sādharmya": that which has a similar (samāna) property (dharma) is "sadharmā"; the substitution of *sa* for *sama* occurs; the state of being that is "sādharmya" (homogeneity).

The suffix *ṣyañ* is applied because [the word] begins with *brāhmaṇa* and so forth. Regarding the term *sajātīya*: the analysis (*vigraha*) is "that which has a common (*samāna*) genus (*jāti*). The substitution of *sa-* for *samāna-* occurs [by Pāṇini 6.3.84]. The suffix *cha* is applied by the rule *jātyantāc cha bandhuni*. The phrase "and so forth" includes [the formation of] *sagrāma* and other such examples. This is due to the separation of the rules (*yogavibhāga*).

Because it is not seen in the Bhāṣya, he states another reasoning, beginning with "Or rather" (*athavā*). Regarding the phrase "by that" (*tena*): the connection is that [the compound] is a *bahuvrīhi* by means of that word "similar" (*sadṛśa*). And thus, the intention is that the substitution of *sa-* for *saha-* occurs according to the rule "vopasarjanasya. Now, one might ask: how can the analysis (*vigraha*) be "that which has the same side as this"? For it is the word *saha* itself [that is used].

Because it is appropriate for [the word *saha*] to enter into a compound (*vigraha*), he says: "not in its own form" (*asvapade*). The intention is that the word *saha* signifies "similarity" (*sadṛśa*) only when it occurs within a compound (*vṛtti*).
Pāṇini 6.3.86: *jyotirjanapadacaraṇe brahmacāriṇi*. (In a Bahuvrīhi compound, the final vowel of the first member is lengthened before the words *jyotis*, *janapada*, *caraṇa*, and *brahmacārin*.)

The rule *jyotirjanapada* (Pāṇini 6.3.85) is stated for the sake of excluding the meaning of *chandah* (Vedic meter). The term *sajyotiḥ* is analyzed as "that which has the same *jyotis*" (*samānaṃ jyotiryasya*). The same applies to *sajanapada* and so forth. [Examples include: *sarātriḥ*, *sanābhiḥ*, *sanāmā*, *sagotraḥ*, *sarūpaḥ*, *sasthānaḥ*, *savarṇaḥ*, *savayāḥ*.
*sa-vacanaḥ*, *sa-bandhuḥ*.

(998) *caraṇe brahmacāriṇi* | 6|3|86|. In the case of *caraṇa* [meaning a Vedic school] and *brahmacārin* [meaning a student], [the substitute *sa-* is applied]. The words *samānasya* and *sa-* are understood from the preceding rules. This applies when it occurs as a subsequent member (*uttarapada*).
This is the subject under discussion. Thus he says: "When *brahmacārī* follows as the subsequent member [of a compound], there shall be *sa* for *samāna*.
The locative case in *caraṇe* connects with *samānasya*; the meaning is "occurring in *caraṇa*. He states the resulting sense: "when *samāna* is understood as referring to a *caraṇa* (Vedic school)."

Therein, he explains the term *caraṇa*: "The *caraṇa* is the branch (*śākhā*). The basis for this is indeed Vedic tradition. To provide an etymological derivation (*nirvacana*) for the word *brahmacārin*, he says: "Brahman is the Veda. [As Amarasimha states: "The Veda, reality, and austerity are *brahman*. Regarding the phrase "for the sake of that *caraṇa*": the *caraṇa* of that Veda is its study (*adhyayana*).

The meaning is that both that conduct (*caraṇa*) and the vow (*vrata*) are intended by the word *brahman*. The phrase "by means of a secondary figurative application" (*gauṇyā vṛttyā*) is to be supplied. "He practices that" means that the word *brahmacārī* has the sense of one who practices—that is, performs—that vow. The suffix *ṇini* is applied according to the rule *supyajātau*. [Regarding the form] *samānasya sa*: [the rule is] *samāna...* [etc.]

The meaning is that when *brahmacārī* is a *karmadhāraya* compound, the form *sabrahmacārī* arises according to the present sūtra through the substitution of *sa-* for *samāna-*. This commonality (*sāmānya*) is to be understood as being by way of the Veda; thus, the resultant meaning is "one who observes the vow for the purpose of studying the same Veda. However, in the Bhāṣya...

It has been stated that in the sense of "one who performs the vow (*vrata*) in the same sacred knowledge (*brahman*)," the suffix *ṇini* is applied to the root *car*, and the elision of the word *vrata* is here prescribed as a grammatical anomaly (*nipātana*).
(999) *tīrthe ye* (Pāṇini 6.3.87).

Regarding the word *tīrthe*: from the word *ya*, which ends in the vowel *a*, the seventh case singular (*saptamyekavacana*) is taken; the vowel *a* is not intended to be significant (*na vivakṣita*). The term "suffix" (*pratyaya*) is to be supplied as the qualifier (*viśeṣya*). By the rule "an operation [applies] when something is present," there is an extension of the rule to that which begins with it (*tadādividhi*). Thus he says: "in a suffix beginning with *y*" (*yādau pratyaye*). It does not apply here to a suffix ending in *ya*.

It can be explained that [the suffix] occurs when the word *tīrtha* follows; for the rule "one who dwells at the same *tīrtha*" (*samānatīrthe vāsī*) prescribes the *ya*-suffix in the sense of a secondary derivative (*taddhita*) precisely from the compound word *samānatīrtha*. And that *ya*-suffix is applied only after the internal substitution of *sa* for *sama* has already taken place.
