"For the sake of restriction" means that the sense is that [the suffix is applied] only when it refers to something other than a foot-soldier, provided it follows *sālva*. (1340) *Goyavāgvośca* (Pāṇini 4.2.136).
"And [the suffix] after *go* and *vāgv-*. The meaning is: when these two are intended to be expressed as having the nature of "born" (*jāta*) and so forth.

(1341) *gartottarapadāc chaḥ* | 4.2.137. "[The suffix] *cha* after a word ending in *garta* as its final member. [The word] "in the sense of a place" (*deśe*) is supplied to complete the rule; that is, it applies to words denoting a place.
Up to "vṛkagartīya" [the rule applies]. *Vṛkagarta* is the name of a region; the meaning is "that which exists there.

Now, one might object: since the mere addition of the suffix *cha* after *garta*—by the rule *gartāc cha*—is sufficient to establish that the word *garta* alone does not denote a region, and since the formation would already be accomplished by the rule *gartottarapadāt*, why is the term *uttarapada* (subsequent member) mentioned?
To show that [the previous rule] would be redundant, he says: "The mention of the subsequent word.
(Pāṇini 4.2.138) *gahādibhyaśca* ("and from *gaha* and so forth"). *Gahīyaḥ*: *gaha* is a particular region. *Mukhapārśva*.
The *gaṇasūtra* beginning with *gaha*: the word *mukhapārśve* is a term with its sixth case ending elided;

there is also elision of the final phoneme of these two [words] ending in *tas*. Because of the word *ca*, the suffix *cha* is also included. Since it is impossible here, the phrase *janapadasya* (of the country) is not connected [to this rule]. *Kugjanasya* is a *gaṇasūtra*.

The augment *kuk* shall be added to the words *jana* and *para*. Because of the word *ca* (and), *cha* is also included. Here too, the word *deśa* (place) is not connected [to the rule]. And [the suffix applies] to *deva*. This is also a *gaṇasūtra*; because of *ca*, both *kuk* and *cha* are included.
It is an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule "after *deva*, the suffixes *yañ* and *añ*. As in the example: *daivānugraha*.

The form *daivam* is also correct due to its usage in the Bhāṣya. Regarding *svakīyam*: the suffix *cha* is applied because it belongs to the *gaha*-class, and there is also the augment *kuk*. The word *sva* is also included in the *gaha*-class; thus, by the non-obligatory nature (*anityatva*) of the rule concerning augments, we have *svīyam*. (1343) *prācāṃ kaṭādeḥ* | Pāṇini 4.2.139.

[The suffix *cha* is applied] after words beginning with *kaṭa* when they denote an eastern region. For example: *kaṭanagarīyā*. *Kaṭanagara* is the name of an eastern country. (1344) *rājñaḥ ka ca* | 4.2.140. [The suffix *cha* is applied] after *rājan*, and there is also the substitution of *ka* for the final phoneme. That is to say, the suffix *cha* is applied after the word *rājan*, and the letter *k* is substituted for the final phoneme [of *rājan*].

(1345) *vṛddhādakekāntakhopadhāt* | Pāṇini 4.2.141. [The suffix *cha* is applied] after a word that has a *vṛddhi* vowel in its first syllable, ends in *aka*, *ika*, or *anta*, or has *kha* as its penultimate letter. For example: *brāhmaṇakīya*. Here, *cha* is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *aṇ* for words ending in *k*. Similarly: *śālmalikīya*. This refers to a region named Śālmalika; the meaning is "that which exists there."

This is an exclusive example. It is an exception to [the suffix] *aṇ* when the penultimate vowel is *o*. In the case of *ayomukhīya*, the suffix *cha* is an exception to the *ṭhañ* and *ñiṭha* prescribed by the rule "bāhīkagrāmebhyaśca" (Pāṇini 4.2.118).
(1346) Pāṇini 4.2.142: [The suffix *cha* is applied] after words ending in *kanthā*, *palada*, *nagara*, *grāma*, or *hrada* as the final members of a compound.

*Kanthāpalada*: This is an exception (*apavāda*) to [the suffixes] *ṭhañ* and *iṭha*. In the case of "at the end of a city name," it is an exception to *vuñ* [by the rule] *ṭhropadheto'ra*; in the other case, it is an exception to *ṭhañ* and *iṭha* [by the rule] *bāhīkagrāmebhyaśca*. Such is the distinction.

(1347) *parvatācca* |4|2|143|. The rule beginning with *parvatācca* is clear. Regarding *yuṣmadasmado*: because the words *yuṣmad* and *asmad* here refer to the actual form of the words themselves (*śabdasvarūpaparatvāt*), the rule "the *tyad*-class [words] are always [retained] when followed by any [other word]" (*tyadādīni sarvair nityam*) does not apply, and thus there is no *ekaśeṣa* (single-remainder retention).
The genitive case is used in the sense of the ablative. The meaning is that the suffix *khañ* is applied after the words *yuṣmad* and *asmad* in the sense of "born from" (*jāta*) and so forth.

By the word *ca* ("and"), the suffix *cha* is also included; the meaning is that *cha*, which was previously governed by the rule "after a compound whose final member is *garta*," is conjoined here by the letter *ca*.

(1348) *vibhāṣāmanuṣye* |4|2|144|. The sense is that the suffix *aṇ* is optional (*pakṣe*) because of the inclusion of the term *anyatarasyām*. Here, the rule *yuṣmadasmador ari* is divided; the meaning is that the suffix *cha* occurs after these two [words]. And [the rule] *khañ ca* [follows].
This refers to another rule (*yogāntara*): the meaning is that the suffix *khañ* also occurs after these two. "Or else" (*anyatarasyām*) is another rule:

the meaning is that after these two, the suffixes *cha* and *khañ* optionally occur, while in the alternative case, the suffix *aṇ* applies. Thus, it is clear in the *Bhāṣya* that there is no correspondence according to the order of enumeration (*yathāsaṃkhya*).

(1349) *yuṣmadasmador anyatarasyāṃ khañ ca* [Pāṇini 4.3.1]: From the words *yuṣmad* and *asmad*, the suffix *khañ* may optionally be applied. Thus, *yuṣmadīya*. From forms ending in the dual or plural, the suffix *cha* is applied; *īya* is the substitute for this.
Upon the elision (*luk*) of the case-ending (*sup*), the substitutes *yuva-* and so forth cease to apply, because they are prescribed only when a case-suffix (*vibhakti*) follows.

Even when the case-ending is elided, provided there is oneness of meaning for the base, the substitution of *tvā* and so forth will be taught. "Belonging to us" (*asmadīya*) means "this belongs to the two of us" or "this belongs to us.
(Pāṇini 4.3.2) "In that [context], and when the suffix *aṇ* follows, *yuṣmāka* and *asmāka* [are substituted]."

Now he states the distinction regarding *khañ* and *aṇ*: "In that *aṇ* as well. The suffix *khañ*, which was specified in the preceding rule, is referred to by the word "that" (*tat*). Thus he says: "In *khañ* and in *aṇ*.
Here, the correspondence is between the two original bases (*sthānin*) and their two substitutes (*ādeśa*), and not between the two subsequent causes (*paranimitta*).

In that [rule], because of the separate mention of *aṇ*, [the forms] *yauṣmākīṇa* and *āsmākīna* are derived as follows: The analysis of *yauṣmākīṇa* is "this belongs to you two" (*yuvayoḥ*) or "this belongs to you all" (*yuṣmākam*). [The suffix] *khañ* is applied; there is the substitution of *īn* for [the final vowel and consonant of the base]; the substitution of *yuṣmākā-* [for *yuṣmad-*]; initial *vṛddhi*; and the substitution of *ṇa* for *na*.
The analysis of *āsmākīna* is "this belongs to us two" (*āvayoḥ*) or "this belongs to us all" (*asmākam*). [The suffix] *aṇ* is applied.
He provides an example: *yauṣmākaḥ* and *āsmākaḥ*.

(1351) *tavaka-mamakau ekavacane* | 4|3|3|. [The words] *tavaka* and *mamaka* [are substituted for *yuṣmad* and *asmad* respectively] when the singular number is expressed. The phrase "when the singular number is expressed" (*ekavacane*) is an adjective qualifying the bases *yuṣmad* and *asmad*.

The term *ekavacana* means "the utterance of one"; it is understood as "of two [words] being employed in the expression of one. Thus he says: "of two that denote a single object. Regarding the word *tu* ("but"): the ellipsis is "a distinction between those two that function with a single object will be stated."

(1352) *pratyayotarapadayośca* | 7|2|98 | This [sūtra] belongs to the seventh chapter (*sāptamika*). The phrase "in the singular" (*ekavacane*) from [sūtra 7.2.97] *tvamāvekavacane* is understood to carry over (*anuvartate*). [It also carries over] from [sūtra 7.2.90] *yuṣmadasmadoranādeśe*.
The phrase *yuṣmadasmadoḥ* (of *yuṣmad* and *asmad*) is understood [from the previous rule]. The term *maparyantasya* (of that which ends in *m*) is the governing heading (*adhikṛtam*).

Thus he says: "of those ending in *m*" and so forth. In the forms *tvadīyaḥ* and *madīyaḥ*, when the suffix *cha* is elided by *subluk*, *tavad* and *mavad* are replaced by the substitutes *tvad* and *mad* respectively, once *tavamama* have been removed, leaving only the portions ending in *m*.

Because there is an absence of being followed by a case-ending (*vibhakti*), there is no elision (*lopa*) of the final phoneme in the sense of "remainder" (*śeṣa*). However, when a subsequent member of a compound (*uttarapada*) follows, examples such as *tvatputraḥ* ("your son") and *matputraḥ* ("my son") occur.
(1353) *ardhād yat* | Pāṇini 4.3.4. [The suffix *yat* is applied after the word *ardha* to form a feminine noun denoting a portion].

From *ardha*. Regarding *ārdhya*: the meaning is "born in the half" (*ardhe jātaḥ*) and so forth. The Vārttika, "The suffix *ṭhañ* should be stated after a word preceded by another member," is established in the Bhāṣya. Example: *bāleyārdhikaḥ* ("one born in the half belonging to Bāleya").
(1354) [Also] from words preceded by *para*, *avara*, *adhama*, and *uttama*. 4.3.5.
The word *parāvara* [is formed] from *ardha*, etc.; this is the remainder [of the rule]. The word *avara* has the dental labial *va* in its middle.
(1355) *dikpūrvapadāṭ ṭhañ ca* |4|3|6|. From a compound whose first member is a direction-word, the suffix *ṭhañ* is also applied; [the condition] "from *ardha*" (*ardhāt*) applies here as well.
Whatever [suffix] was [prescribed] by the previous rule from the words *parāvara*, *pūrva*, and *ardha*, [remains so], because it has been specifically prescribed.

(1356) *grāma-janapada-ekadeśād-añ-ṭhañ-au* |4|3|7|. [The sūtra states: "From a part of a village or a country, the suffixes *añ* and *ṭhañ*. [Objection: But surely, by merely stating *añ ca* ("and *añ*"), the attraction (*anukarṣa*) of *ṭhañ* would be established through the force of the particle *ca*.

The inclusion of the term *ṭhañ* is redundant; therefore, he says: "the inclusion of *ṭhañ*. Now, one might object that even when it is said "and *añ*," the attraction (*anukarṣa*) of *ṭhañ* by means of the letter *ca* is quite clear; to this he replies: "when it is said 'and *añ*'," and so forth. (1357) *madhyān maḥ* |4|3|8|.
*madhyān maḥ*. This is clear.

(1358) *a sāṃpratike* |4|3|9|. [The word] *a* [is used] in the sense of "not being appropriate. The term *ṭha* is in the nominative case with its case-ending elided. The word *madhyāt* is understood from the previous rule.

He says this with the words "from the word *madhya*" and so forth. The indeclinable *saṃprati* occurs in the sense of equality (*sāmya*), which consists in being devoid of excellence or deficiency; as it is said in the Taittirīya [Saṃhitā]:
"The four-night sacrifice is deficient, the six-night sacrifice is excessive; indeed, this [five-night sacrifice] is the sacrifice that is *saṃprati* (just right)."

Because it is seen thus in the passage "yatpañcarātraḥ," the meaning is that the *pañcarātra* is neither deficient nor excessive, but equal (*sama*). From the word *samprati*, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied in the sense of the base itself according to the rule for the *vinaya*-group, resulting in *sāmpratika*. However, when the suffix *aṇ* is applied in the same sense according to the *prajñādi*-group, the form *sāmpratam* also occurs.

The words *ṭha*, *itarhi*, and *samprati* are used in the sense of "now" (*idānīm*) according to the *Kośa* and other authorities; however, in the present context, it is equality (*sāmya*) that is intended to be expressed.
(1359) [Pāṇini 4.3.10: After the word *dvīpa*, the suffix *yañ* is applied in the sense of "along the ocean."

Regarding *dvīpādanu*: the compound *anusamudram* is an *avyayībhāva* used in the sense of proximity (*sāmīpye*), as in the expression "near the ocean. The form *anusamudram* ends in the locative case; the word *vidyamāna* ("situated") is to be supplied. Thus he says: "in the vicinity of the ocean. Regarding *dvaipya*: the suffix *ṅīp* does not apply here by the rule *hyañaśca*, because [the word *dvīpa*] falls under the restriction "not when [the suffix] occurs outside the scope of *apatya*" (*anapatyādhikārasthāt*).
Because of its exclusion [from the previous rule].
(1360) *kālāṭ ṭhañ* | Pāṇini 4.3.11. Regarding *kālāṭ ṭhañ*: it is not only the word *kāla* itself that is taken as the referent, but rather the entire category of words denoting time (*kāla*).

And the inclusion of words expressing specific times is clear from the Bhāṣya on the two sūtras "tadasya parimāṇam" and "saṅkhyāyāḥ. Thus he says: "from words denoting time," as in *sāyaṃprātikaḥ* (belonging to evening) and *paunaḥpunikaḥ* (repeated). The elision of the suffix *ṭi* occurs by the rule "avyayānāṃ bhamātre" (there is elision of the *ṭi* of indeclinables when a *bha*-affix follows).

Regarding "sāyañciram," the suffixes *āyuṭ* and *āyuc* do not apply; this is because such usage is observed in the commentary (*bhāṣya*) on the rule *na-staddhite*. As for the word *śārvarasya*, the meaning is that it should be understood as being simultaneous with or prior to [the night]. Regarding the term *prāmāṇikāḥ*, some say *amukaḥ*.

They say that these words (*purataḥ*, *paredyavi*, etc. are also unanalyzed (*avyutpanna*), or that they are correct as *pṛṣodarādi* [irregular] formations. The phrase "up to this point" (*iti yāvat*) implies [the rule] is established through such an explanation. (1361) *śrāddhe śaradaḥ* | 4.3.12 | [In the sense of] "at the Śrāddha," [the suffix *aṇ* is added] after the word *śarad*. [The form is *śāradaḥ*].

Regarding the word *śaradaḥ* [in the rule for the Śrāddha]: it means that the suffix *ṭhañ* should be applied. This is a supplement to the rule [to complete its meaning]. Now, one might ask: since the form is already established by the rule *kālāt ṭhañ*, what is the purpose of this [separate mention]? To this he says: *ṛtvaṇaḥ*. The meaning is: [it is to prevent the application] of the suffix *aṇ* which will be taught later in the rule *saṃdhivelsādyṛtunakṣatrebhyo 'ṇ*. Thus, the form is *śāradikam*.
The meaning is "that which occurs in the season of autumn. If the word *śarad* were to denote a year (*saṃvatsara*), however, it would already be established by the preceding rule.
(1362) *Vibhāṣā rogātapayoḥ* |4|3|13|. [This rule provides for] the optional application [of the suffix *aṇ*] in the case of *roga* (disease) and *ātapa* (heat).

The *vibhāṣā* (optionality) applies to the words *roga* and *ātapa*. The suffixes *ṭha*, *ṭhañ*, and *añ* are understood from the previous rule, as is the word *śarad*. Thus, we have *śāradaṃ dadhi* ("autumnal curd"). The point is that the suffix *añ* is applied because it is marked with *ñ*. (Pāṇini 4.3.14: "Also after *niśā* and *pradoṣa*."

"And from *niśā* and *pradoṣa*, the suffix *ṭhañ* may optionally be applied. This is a supplement to the rule. Since the suffix *ṭhañ* would necessarily apply by the rule "kālāṭ ṭhañ" [Pāṇini 4.3.11], this present rule provides an option.
(1364) "And after *śvas*, there is the augment *tuṭ*. [Pāṇini 4.3.15]
"śvas-tuṭ ca" [Pāṇini 5.4.80]. Regarding "tasya": this means "of the suffix. In the augment *tuṭ*, the letter *ṭ* is the *it*-marker; the letter *u* is for the sake of pronunciation.
(1365) "And [the augment *tuṭ* is added] after *dvārā-* and so forth" [Pāṇini 7.3.4].

And regarding *dvāra* and the others: the rule *ṭhna yvābhyāṃ padāntābhyām* (Pāṇini 7.3.3) follows [from the previous rules] with the exception of the phrase *padāntābhyām*, and the word *vṛddhiḥ* is carried over from the rule *mṛjervṛddhiḥ* (Pāṇini 7.2.114). Thus he says: "For these, there is neither *vṛddhi* nor the substitution of *aij*. For *dvāra* and the others, there is no *vṛddhi* of the initial vowel.
However, the meaning is that the augment *ai* occurs before the letters *ya* and *va*.
Since *ya* and *va* are not at the end of a word (*apadānta*) in this context, the rule "na yvābhyām" (Pāṇini 7.3.3) does not apply; therefore, this specific statement is made.

Regarding the form *śauvastikam*: from the indeclinable *śvas*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is added in the sense of "belonging to the future," followed by the substitution of *ik* and the addition of the augment *tuṭ*.
Before the letter *va*, the augment *aiC* (*ai*) is applied by way of *āgama*, resulting in the vowel *au*. There is no *vṛddhi* substitution for the vowel *a*.

(Pāṇini 4.3.16) "The suffix *aṇ* [is applied] after words denoting a junction (*saṃdhi*), a time (*velā*), etc., as well as seasons (*ṛtu*) and lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*). Regarding the example *saṃdhivelām*, it is because the rule "after words expressing time" (*kālāt*) is understood here through the recurrence (*anuvṛtti*) from the rule "the suffix *ṭhaÑ* after a word denoting time" (*kālāṭ ṭhañ*).
This is the sense. It is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *ṭhañ*. Regarding the form *taiṣam*: the meaning is "that which occurs during Tiṣya.

[The rule] *ṭhtiṣyapuṣyayornakṣatrāṇī* [prescribes the elision of the final vowel]. There is the elision of *y*. Regarding the sense "born under Tiṣya," the elision (*luk*) will be stated by the rule *śraviṣṭhāphalgunī*. [One should consult] the *saṃdhivelādi* group.
He recites: *saṃdhivelā* and so forth; and *saṃvatsarāt phalapaurṇamāsyām*.
This is a *gaṇa-sūtra*. (1367) *prāvṛṣa eṇyaḥ* 4.3.17.

*prāvṛṣ-eṇyaḥ*. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *ṛtvaṇ*. Regarding *prāvṛṣeṇya*: *prāvṛṭ* is the rainy season (*varṣartu*). The meaning is "that which exists therein" (*tatra bhava*), and so forth. However, regarding the sense of "born there" (*jāta*), the suffix *ṭha* will be taught [later]. The vowel *ṇa* is pronounced for the sake of brevity in grammatical derivation (*prakriyālāghava*).

(1368) *varṣābhyaṣṭhak* | Pāṇini 4.3.18. Regarding the suffix *ṭhak* after the word *varṣā*: the words *tṛtīya-ṛtu-* and *varṣā-* are always plural in form, according to the rule on gender (*liṅgānuśāsana*) which states: "The plurality of *ṛtu*, *apsu*, *manas*, *samā*, *sikatā*, and *varṣā* [is inherent]."
According to Amarasimha: "The word *strī* [is used] for the rainy season (*prāvṛṭ*), and *varṣāḥ* in the plural.
The suffix *ṭhak* is added to the word *varṣā* in the sense of "born therein" and so forth. "Beneficial in the rains" means one who acts for the welfare [of others].

Now, one might ask: since the section on "beneficial" (*sādhv-adhikāra*)—specifically the rule "fit for that place" (*tatra sādhuh*)—is largely subsumed under the general section on "remainder" (*śeṣa-adhikāra*), how [is this derived]?
Since this suffix is prescribed in the sense of "skillful" (sādhv-artha), he says: "from time" (kālāt). Regarding "in the sense of skillful":

the meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is also used in the sense of "skillful. The intention is that this [suffix] is included within the secondary (śaiṣika) suffixes in the senses of "born from" (jāta) and so forth.

(1369) *sarvatrāṇ ca talopaśca* || 4.3.22 || The term *sarvatra* ("everywhere") is included for the purpose of terminating the recurrence (*anuvṛtti*) of the word *chandasi* ("in the Veda"). The meaning is: "in both common usage (*loka*) and in the Veda (*veda*). From the preceding rule, *hemantāt* ("after *hemanta*") is carried over (*anuvartate*). Thus, the suffix *aṇ* is applied after *hemanta*, and there is the elision (*lopa*) of the *t* sound.

He says this with the words beginning "hemanta-āditya" and so on. Now, one might object: since the form is already established by the rule "sarvatrāṇ talopaśca," the first *ca* (and) is redundant; to this he replies: "by virtue of the *ca*. In the word *haimanam*, in the context of the term *hemante*, the *anusvāra* and its subsequent *parasavarṇa* [the nasal *m*] stand in place of the *n* that precedes the *t*.

In that regard, according to the view that there is the elision (*lopa*) of the entire combination of the letter *t* and the vowel *a*, there is no elision of the *ṭi* (the first vowel) because of the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*) by the rule *ṭhaniti*. However, according to the view that there is the elision of the letter *t* alone, there is likewise no elision of the *ṭi* because the elision of the vowel *a*— by the rule *ṭhyasyeti ca*— is either considered non-existent (*asiddha*) due to being an *ābhīya* operation, or because it functions as if it were still present (*sthānivadbhāva*).

Regarding *haimantam*: this is a form derived with the suffix *ṛtvaṇ*. Here, there is no elision of the final *t*, because that [elision] is prescribed as being conditioned by the co-occurrence (*saṃniyoga*) with the suffix *aṇ* specifically mentioned in this rule.

(1370) Pāṇini 4.3.32: *sāyaṃ-ciraṃ-prāhṇe-prage’vyayebhyaṣṭyu-ṭyulau tuṭ ca*. [The suffixes] *ṭyu* and *ṭyul* are added after the indeclinables *sāyam*, *ciram*, *prāhṇe*, and *prage*, and the augment *tuṭ* is also applied.

Regarding "sāyaṃ-ciram": the meaning of "from four" is "from these [words], namely sāyaṃ, ciram, prāhne, and prage. Regarding "expressing time": the intention is that this follows from the recurrence of the rule "kālāṭ ṭhañ" (Pāṇini 4.3.11). Regarding "of those two": the meaning is "of ayuṭ and ayul. Now, one might ask: how is it in cases such as "sāyaṃtana"?
The substitution of *an* for *yu* and *vu* [is not applied here]. For the rule "ṭhyuvoranākau" (Pāṇini 7.1.1) occurs within the governing context (*adhikāra*) of the "stem" (*aṅga*).

It prescribes that *an* and *ak* are substituted for *yu* and *vu* when they follow a stem. In the present case, however, because the augment *tuṭ* is internal (*antaraṅga*), and because [the suffix] does not follow a stem due to the presence of *tuṭ*, the substitution of *an* does not take place.

It is possible [to object] as follows: "One should not say that because of the maxim *tadāgamāstadgrahaṇena gṛhyante* (substitutes with their augments are included by the mention of the original element), the form *tyu* is also included by the mention of *yu*, and thus its status as following the *aṅga* is beyond reproach. This is because of the paribhāṣā *nirdiśyamānasyādeśā bhavanti* (substitutes take the place of what is explicitly mentioned).

Since the substitution (*ādeśa*) would have been obtained even earlier, and because that [substitution] is separated by the augment *tuṭ*, it does not follow after the stem (*aṅga*); therefore, he says: "The substitution occurs before *tuṭ*.
To the question "Why?", he says: "Because of the specific mention (*nirdeśāt*). By the word "etc. (*ādi*), [the rule] *ṭh-ghakālataneṣu* is included.

The word *tana* should be understood as that which is to be grasped (*grāhya*). Regarding the term *sāyaṃtanam*: from the verbal root *ṣo* in the sense of "concluding" (*antakarman*), the noun suffix *ghañ* is applied, and the word *sāya* is conventionally established (*rūḍha*) in the sense of the end of the day. From that [root], the suffixes *ṭyuṭ* and *ṭyul* are added; when there is no substitution for those two, the augment *tuṭ* is inserted, and the final *m* of the base is prescribed by rule (*nipātita*). As for the form *sāyam*:
The word *svarādi* is listed among the indeclinables (*avyaya*); precisely because it is an indeclinable, the suffixes *ṭaḷ*, *uṭaḷ*, and *ul* are established [after it].

Regarding the form *ciraṃtanam*: here too, the fact that the base ends in *m* is treated as an irregularity (*nipātana*). From this very indicative mark (*liṅga*), it is understood that the inclusion of *ciras* among the indeclinables is not authoritative (*aprāmāṇika*).

Regarding *prāhṇetana*: the analysis of the compound is *prāhṇaḥ soḍho 'nena* ("that by whom the forenoon was endured"), because the meaning "that which has been endured by him" is what is about to be specified [by the rule *tadasya soḍham*]. However, in the sense of "born in the forenoon" (*prāhṇe jātaḥ*), the form ending in *-et* is established simply through the elision (*aluk*) prescribed by the rule *ghakālataneṣu*. Regarding *pragetanam*: [it is derived from *prage* with the suffix *-tana*].

*Pragaḥ* means "one who goes forward"; the meaning is "born at that time" (*tasmin jātaḥ*). As for the indeclinable *prage*, which ends in *e* and signifies "at dawn," its formation is established simply by virtue of its being an indeclinable. He gives an example from the indeclinables: *doṣātanam*. *Doṣā* ending in long *ā* is an indeclinable meaning "at night."

Regarding *divātana*: *divā* is an indeclinable ending in the vowel *-ā*, meaning "during the day. Regarding *ciraparut*: the meaning is that the suffix *tnap* is applied after the words *cira*, *parut*, and *parāri*. Regarding *ciratna*: this is a statement [of a rule] concerning the application of the suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ṭyul*; in the case of the suffix *tnap*, there is no final *m*.

[The suffix] *bhavati* [is applied], because it is taught as being in obligatory association (*saṃniyogaśiṣṭa*) with *ṭaḷu* and *ṭaḷul*. The indeclinables *ṭhparuṭ* and *ṭhparārī* respectively denote the preceding year and the year prior to that.
[The suffix] *ḍimac* is added after [stems ending in] *agra* and so forth, and after words ending in *paścāt*.

"From *agra* and so forth"—this is a Vārttika. The meaning is that the suffix *ḍimac* is applied after the words *agra*, *ādi*, and *paścāt*. Regarding the form *paścimam*: there is elision of the *ṭi* by the rule "of indeclinables, when a *bha*-stem suffix follows. (1) Also from *anta*.
And from the end [of the commentary]: this is also a *vārttika*.
(1371) *Vibhāṣā pūrvāhṇāparāhṇābhyām* | Pāṇini 4.3.24.
"Optionally after *pūrvāhṇa*. Since it is optional, [the suffix] *ṭhañ* applies; in that case, there is no *tuṭ* augment, because of that [rule].
The meaning is that [the suffix] is taught as being invariably connected with *ṭha* and *yuṭ*. Thus,

(1372) *tatra jātaḥ* 4|3|25. Now, he begins to demonstrate the specific meanings of those suffixes and the specific case-endings of their bases: "born there" (*tatra jātaḥ*), [derived] from a base ending in the seventh case.

The meaning is "from that which ends in the seventh case (locative) after sandhi has been applied. The intention is that by the word *tatra* ("therein"), that very [base] ending in the seventh case is indicated as the first member [of the compound]. Regarding "the suffixes beginning with *aṇ*":
the meaning is that they are common to all meanings from "descendant" (*apatya*) up to "modification" (*vikāra*). Regarding "the suffixes beginning with *gh*": [the same applies].
The meaning is that [the suffixes] are specifically prescribed by rules such as "ṭhrāṣṭrāvārapāre" and others.

(1373) *prāvṛṣaṣṭhap* | 4.3.26 | The suffix *ṭhap* is added after *prāvṛṣ*. The fact that *ap* is marked with the indicatory letter *p* is for the sake of its own accent, according to the rule "anudātau suppitau."

Regarding the word *eṇyasya*: this means [the suffix] prescribed by the rule *prāvṛṣa eṇyaḥ*. Thus, it follows that the rule *prāvṛṣa eṇyaḥ* results in a suffix for meanings other than "born" (*jāta*). (1374) *saṃjñāyāṃ śarado vuñ* |4|3|27|. This means: the suffix *vuñ* is applied after the word *śarat* when it forms a proper name (*saṃjñā*). For example: *śāradaka* (a festival occurring in autumn). The mention of *saṃjñāyām* is for the sake of restriction; otherwise, the suffix would apply even in non-proper-name contexts, such as *śaradi bhavaḥ* = *śāradaḥ* (autumnal). The suffix *vuñ* is not applied in cases like *śaradbhavaḥ* (occurring in autumn), because the suffix *aṇ* is prescribed by the rule *sāyaṃciram...* etc., which takes precedence over *vuñ*. The suffix *vuñ* is applied after [a word ending in] *śarat* when it forms a name (*saṃjñā*). Regarding the statement "when it forms a name," some [commentators], such as the author of the Vṛtti, maintain that this term governs the entire section up to the rule *kṛtalabdhakrīte* (Pāṇini 4.2.10). (1375) *Uttarapadasya* (7.3.10).
"Of the second member. This is a governing heading (*adhikāra*). These initial rules belong to the section on initial *vṛddhi* in the seventh book. (1376) *Avayavād ṛtoḥ* | Pāṇini 7.3.11.

Regarding "from a part of a season" (*avayavād ṛtoḥ*): the phrase "from a preceding word" (*pūrvapadāt*) is understood; the remainder is "of that which follows" (*ṭhparasya*). Regarding "denoting a season" (*ṛtuvācinaḥ*): the phrase "of the subsequent member" (*utarapadasya*) is understood. In the example *pūrvavārṣikaḥ*, the word *varṣāḥ* is always feminine and plural when referring to a specific season. [Thus: the first of the rains is *pūrvavarṣāḥ*; therein—

The meaning is "born. In the compound *pūrvāparādharottaram*, there is an *ekadeśisamāsa* (partitive compound). Regarding *aparahaimana*: the latter part of winter is *aparahemanta*; the meaning is "one born therein," etc. There is an *ekadeśisamāsa*. [Regarding] *aparahaimana*: the latter part of winter is *aparahemanta*.

In that context, the meaning is "born there and so forth. This is an *ekadeśisamāsa* (partitive compound). According to the rule *sarvatrāṇ ca talopaśca*, the suffix *aṇ* is applied, with the elision (*lopa*) of the suffix *tal*, and the initial vowel of the subsequent member (*uttarapada*) undergoes vṛddhi.
Regarding the expression *pūrvāsu varṣāsu*: this is a compound formed by the rule *taddhitārtha*. There is only the initial vṛddhi, and not [the other].
There is Vṛddhi substitution for the initial vowel of the second member (*uttarapada*), because the first member lacks the status of being a constituent part (*avayava*).
Regarding the rule *ṛtor vṛddhimat-vidhāv avayavānām*, there is a *tadanta-vidhi* (application of a rule to that which ends in such a form) in the preceding case.

Now, one might ask: how is it that here [in the word *vārṣika*], the suffix *ṭhak* is applied by the rule *varṣābhyaṣ ṭhak*? [This is so] because the suffix is prescribed [by a rule governing a specific stem].

Because of the prohibition against [applying] the rule regarding the end of that (tadantavidhi), he says there: "from ṛtu. This refers to the rule *yena vidhis tadantasya* (Pāṇini 1.1.72), which means that when a suffix caused by vṛddhi is to be prescribed after words denoting parts of a season, the rule regarding the end of that [word] must be stated.

The meaning is that, according to the statement found in the Sūtra-bhāṣya, in the examples cited previously, there is the rule of *tadanta-vidhi* (application of a suffix to a word ending in a specified stem). Thus, in the examples "pūrvavārṣikaḥ" and "pūrvahaimanaḥ," the suffix *ṭhak* is applied by the rule "varṣābhyaṣṭhak," and the suffix *aṇ* is applied by the rule "sarvatrāṇ ca."

In that case, both the elision of the suffix *aṇ* and the elision of the final syllable (*atalopa*) are established; however, here they are not. The meaning is that in the counter-example (*pratyudāharaṇa*), there is no rule of extension (*tadantavidhi*) because, through grammatical coreferentiality (*sāmānādhikaraṇya*), the word "prior" (*pūrva*) does not function as denoting a part (*avayavavṛtti*). Consequently, in the counter-example...

In the case of *paurvavārṣika*, the suffix is *ṭhañ* by the rule *kālāṭ ṭhañ*, and not *ṭhak*; there is a difference in accent. The intention is that in *paurvahemantika* as well, it is indeed *ṭhañ*.
(1377) *susarvārdhāj janapadasya* [Pāṇini 7.3.12].

The meaning is that [the suffix *kan* is applied] after the words *su*, *sarva*, and *ardha* when they precede a word denoting a country (*janapada*). "Vṛddhi of the final syllable" is the completion of the rule. *Supāñcālaka* means "born in the excellent Pañcālas. Regarding the term *janapada*: [it refers to a country].

With the phrase "from a word ending in *ṭha* or *japa*, and from that which has *avadya*" continuing [from the previous rule], the meaning is that the suffix *vuñ* is applied even after a non-*vṛddha* [word] when it refers to a plural object.
Now, one might ask: in the prescription of a suffix by the rule "even after a non-*vṛddha*," how can there be an extension of the rule to include words ending in those [terms]?
To this, he says: "from *su*, *sarva*, *ardha*, and directional words. That is, from these—*su*, *sarva*, *ardha*, and words denoting direction.

The meaning is that there is an application of the rule *tadantavidhi* (the rule applies to words ending with the specified term), according to the statement cited in the Bhāṣya on the sūtra *yenavidhistadantasya*, which conveys that when a suffix is prescribed after a word denoting a foreign country (*parasya janapadavācinaḥ*), the rule applies to what ends with that [foreign country name].
(1378) *diśo'madrāṇām* 4.2.107. [This sūtra provides for the addition of the suffix *añ* after words denoting directions, except for those denoting Madra.]

"Diśo'madrāṇām" (from the word *diś*, [the suffix *añ* is applied] for those other than the Madras). The analysis is "ṭhamadrāṇām. Regarding "digvācakāt" (from a word denoting a direction), the remainder [of the rule] is "after that which follows [the word *diś*]. Regarding "janapadavācinaḥ" (denoting a country), it should be understood that this also excludes words denoting the Madras. Regarding "vṛddhiḥ" (vṛddhi [vowel substitution]), the remainder is "of the initial [vowel]" (*āder*). In the example "paurvapañcālaḥ," here—

The intention is that the word *pūrva* denotes time. Regarding the form *paurvamadra*: the suffix *añ* is applied by the rule *madrebhyo 'ñ*. Now, one might object: "Why not simply have a single sūtra, *su-sarvārdha-diśo janapadasyāmadrāṇām*? To this, he replies: "There is a division of the yoga (*yogavibhāga*)."

Regarding the phrase "for the sake of the subsequent rule": the meaning is that this is for the purpose of ensuring that the connection [with the word *diś*] occurs only with the subsequent sūtra, "of villages and cities of the Easterners" (*prācāṃ grāmanagarāṇām*). For if they were part of a single sūtra, there would result the undesirable consequence of excluding the word *madra*, even when it follows words such as *su* or *sarva*.
Some say that the meaning here is also [the same].

(1379) *prācāṃ grāmanagaragāṇām* | 7|3|14|. [The rule] "of the villages and cities of the Easterners. Regarding the word *diśaḥ*: those words denoting Eastern villages which follow the word *diś* (direction).

The meaning is that there should be *vṛddhi* (vowel strengthening) of the first vowel of those [words] denoting an eastern city which serve as its constituent parts. In the example *pūrveṣukāmaśamī*, the compound is formed by the rule *diksaṃkhye saṃjñāyām*. The suffix *aṇ* is applied because it is a proper name (*saṃjñā*). The suffix *ñya* is not applied by the rule *dikpūrvapadāt* because the whole [compound] is a proper name.
Even though it is the name of a village, since the latter member of the compound is also a village name, there is vṛddhi of the first vowel of the latter member.

"In a city" (*nagare*) indicates an example. "Former Pāṭaliputraka" (*pūrvapāṭaliputraka*) is a compound formed by the rule *pūrvāparaprathamā-*; the suffix *vuñ* is applied according to the rule *avṛddhādapī-*. Although...

When the word *pāṭaliputra* is the second member (*uttarapada*), there is indeed Vṛddhi of the initial [vowel] only; nevertheless, the purpose is the prevention of Vṛddhi for the first member (*pūrvapada*). (1380) [The suffix] *vuñ* is applied after *pūrvāhṇa*, *aparāhṇa*, *ārdrā*, *mūla*, *pradoṣa*, and *avaskara*. Pāṇini 4.3.28.

Regarding *pūrvāhṇāparāhṇa*: [the forms] *pūrvāhṇakaḥ* and *aparāhṇakaḥ* mean "born in the forenoon" and "born in the afternoon. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule *vibhāṣā pūrvāhṇāparāhṇābhyām*. The intention is that the optional application (*vikalpa*) of the suffixes *ṭyu*, *ṭyul*, and *ṭhañ* has scope (*sāvakāśa*) when the meaning is other than "born" (*jāta*).

*Ārdrakaḥ*, *mūlakaḥ*. The meaning is "born under the asterism Ārdrā" and "born in the month of Mūla. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *ṛtvaṇ*. *Pradoṣakaḥ*. The suffix *ṭhan* replaces the absence of *niśā*. *Ārdrakaḥ*, *mūlakaḥ*. The meaning is "born under the asterism Ārdrā" and "born in the month of Mūla. This is an exception to the suffix *ñatvaṇ*. *Pradoṣakaḥ*.
The form *avaskara* is an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule *ṭhañiśāpradoṣābhyām*.
It is also an exception to the general suffix *aṇ*. Regarding the word *patha*: after the stem *pathin*, the suffix *van* is applied, and the base is replaced by *pantha*.
(1381) Or [the suffix] after *amāvāsyā*. /4/3/30.
"Or after *amāvāsyā*"—the word *vuñ* is understood as the remainder. In the alternative case, the suffix *aṇ* applies because [the word] belongs to the *saṃdhivelādi* group.
By the principle of "modification of a part," this rule applies even from the form *amāvasyā*.

(1382) *a ca* | Pāṇini 4.3.31. *a ca*. This means that from the word *amāvāsyā*, the suffix *a* is also applied [after the suffix *ṭha*]. The absence of *vṛddhi* in the first syllable is the purpose [of this rule].
(1383) *kan* is added after *sindhu* and *apākara*. [Vt. 5 on Pāṇini 4.3.29] *sindhukaḥ*: meaning "born in Sindh.
Regarding *kacchādi*: [the suffix] *aṇ* is applied by the rule *kacchādibhyaśca*, and *vuñ* is applied by the rule *manuṣyatatsthayośca*.
The meaning is that this suffix *ṭhak* is prescribed when [the conditions for] *aṇ* have been reached. Regarding "in *apakara*": the meaning is "born in *apakara*.
Regarding "when *aṇ* has been reached": the remainder of the phrase is "the prescription of *ṭhak*. (1384) *aṇ-ñaś-ca* | 4.3.33 | [When the suffixes *aṇ* and *ñ* are to be applied].
And [the suffix] *aṇ*. "In sequence, *staḥ*" means that the remainder is supplied from the rule "*sindhvapakarābhyām*.

(1385) *Śraviṣṭhā-phalgunī-anurādhā-svāti-tiṣya-punarvasu-hasta-viśākhā-aṣāḍhā-bahulāl luk* || 4.3.34 || [The suffixes denoting asterisms are elided after the following words: Śraviṣṭhā, Phalgunī, Anurādhā, Svāti, Tiṣya, Punarvasu, Hasta, Viśākhā, Aṣāḍhā, and Bahulā.
"Śraviṣṭhā. Regarding "from these": this means from Śraviṣṭhā, Phalgunī, Anurādhā, Svāti, Tiṣya, Punarvasu, Hasta, Viśākhā, Aṣāḍhā, and Bahulā.
"In the sense of one born [under them]" is understood here from the context. The word *svāti* ends in a short vowel.

Kaiyaṭa and Haradatta [state this]. Mādhava [explains] that in the verbal root *ṭhata* (meaning "continuous movement"), it has a long vowel at the end (*dīrghānta*). The word *bahulā*, denoting a type of creeper (*kṛtikā*), ends in the feminine suffix *ṭāp*. In a collective *dvandva* compound, there is the mention of the short vowel. (1386) *luk taddhitaluki* | Pāṇini 1.2.49. [This rule prescribes the elision of the feminine suffix when a *taddhita* suffix is elided.]

Regarding *luk taddhitaluki*: this sūtra occurs in the second pāda of the first adhyāya. The meaning is that it refers to "the feminine suffix of an upasarjana," because of the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the rule *gostriyor upasarjanasya*. The example is *śraviṣṭhā*.

When there is elision (*luk*) of the *aṇ* suffix, there is the cessation of the feminine affix. In the rule "ṭh-luktaddhitalukī," the term *upasarjana* refers only to that which is non-primary (subordinate), and not to the technical grammatical *upasarjana*, because the latter is impossible here; this is the intended meaning.
Regarding the example *phalguna*: it means "born from the two Phalgunīs. When there is elision of the *aṇ* suffix, there is the cessation of the feminine affix.

"Regarding the phrase 'ityādi' (and so forth): one born under Anurādhā is called *anurādhaḥ*. When the suffix *aṇ* [denoting birth] following a lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*) is elided, the feminine suffix is also removed. Likewise, in the subsequent examples, when the suffix is elided, the feminine suffix is removed. "Regarding the phrase 'ityādi': one born under Anurādhā is called *anurādhaḥ*. When the suffix *aṇ* following a lunar mansion is elided, the feminine suffix is removed."

The same applies in the following cases as well. In such instances as "ṛtunū rādhān haviṣā vardhayantaḥ," the masculine gender is a Vedic (chāndasa) usage. One born under Svāti is called Svāti; one born under Tiṣya is called Tiṣya;
one born under the two Punarvasus is called Punarvasu; and one born under Hasta is called Hasta.

One born under the *viśākhā* [nakṣatra] is called *viśākha*; one born under the *aṣāḍhā* [nakṣatras] is called *aṣāḍha*; one born under the *bahulā* [nakṣatras] is called *bahula*. (1) An addition should be made for feminine names derived from *citrā*, *revatī*, and *rohiṇī*.
Regarding *citrā*: the meaning is that there is elision (*luk*) of the suffix denoting the sense of "born" (*jāta*) which follows words such as *citrā* when it has the form of a feminine.

In the case of *revatī* and *rohiṇī*, once the suffix *aṇ* (denoting birth) derived from a lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*) has been elided, and the feminine suffix of the base (*prakṛti*) belonging to the *gaurādi* group has ceased [to apply], the suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied again to express the femininity residing in the meaning of "born."

One might object: since *revatī* and *rohiṇī* are listed in the *gaurādi* group, why is the suffix *ṅīṣ* applied here when they denote the sense of "born under" (*jāta*)? To this he says: "from these two.
This means from the words *revatī* and *rohiṇī*. [The rule applies] to the subsequent [element].

The phrase "of the cognition of a meaning characterized by femininity and belonging to a genus" is the ellipsis [to be supplied]. Regarding the statement "because it belongs to the class of *ākṛtigaṇas*":

the authority for the inclusion of these two—[the suffixes] which function with meanings characterized by femininity and belonging to a genus—within the *pippalyādi* group is precisely the example cited in the Bhāṣya. As for the phrase "only when [the word refers] to a feminine": this is likewise because of the Bhāṣya.
[This is] the meaning: after the words *phalgunī* and *āṣāḍhā*, the suffixes *ṭa* and *an* respectively must be stated to express the sense of a feminine-specific genus (*jāti*). (That is to say:
after *phalgunī* and *āṣāḍhā*, the suffixes *ṭāp* and *aṇ* must be stated.
*Phalgunī*: the meaning is "born under the two Phalgunīs. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *aṇ* [prescribed after asterisms];

the suffix *ṭaP* is applied. By the rule *yasyeti ca*, there is the elision of the vowel *ī*. Since the sense is "born" and the gender is feminine, the suffix *ṅīp* is added because the suffix *ṭaP* contains the *ṭi*-marker.

*Aṣāḍhā*: the meaning is "born under the Aṣāḍhās. This is an exception to the suffix *aṇ* [prescribed after asterisms]; the suffix *an* is applied. By the rule *yasyeti ca*, [there is the elision of the final vowel].

And by the rule "ca," there is the elision of the vowel *ā*. In the sense of "born under" (*jāta*) and denoting femininity, the suffix *ṭāp* is applied. However, the elision of the *ṭā* and *an* [suffixes] by the rule "ṭh śraviṣṭhā-phalgunī...
does not occur here, because of the force of the specific injunction. It is stated that "the suffix *chaṇ* should be prescribed";
this is an exception to the suffix *aṇ* [prescribed after] *nakṣatra*. Due to the force of the injunction, there is no elision even for this suffix. [The term applies] even when not feminine.

The sense is that the term "in the feminine" (*striyām*) is not connected here, because it is so illustrated in the Bhāṣya. (1) The suffix *chaṇ* should be stated [after the words] *śraviṣṭhā* and *aṣāḍhā*.
Thus, *śrāviṣṭhīyaḥ*; the meaning is "born under the *śraviṣṭhā* [nakṣatra]. [The suffixes] *chaṇ*, *īya*, and *ṭhya* [are applied]. *Yasya* [is used to indicate the possessive relation].

There is the elision of the suffix *ca* (the syllable *itya*). Because the suffix is marked with *ṇ*, there is vṛddhi of the first vowel. Thus, *āṣāḍhaīya*. The meaning is "born under the asterism Aṣāḍhā.
(1387) *je proṣṭhapadānām* | Pāṇini 4.3.34. [The suffix *cha* is applied after the word *proṣṭhapadāḥ* when followed by the suffix *jya* (*je*)].

This sūtra occurs in the section on the initial *vṛddhi* [strengthening] for the word *proṣṭhapadā*, under the governing rule (*adhikāra*) "of the latter member" (*uttarapadasya*). Thus he says: "of the *proṣṭhapadās*. By the word *ja*, the suffix expressing the sense of "born" (*jāta*) is intended. Thus he says: "in the sense of being born. Regarding the plural number in "of the *proṣṭhapadās*":
He states the purpose [of the rule] with the words "bahuvacanena" (by the plural). Regarding "bhadrapāda": the meaning is "one born under the *bhadrapadā* [nakṣatra].
(1388) Pāṇini 4.3.35: *sthānāntagośālakharaśālācca*.
*Sthānānta-gośāla*: "From these" means from *sthānānta*, *gośāla*, and *kharaśāla*. *Gosthāna* means born in a cow-pen (*gosthāna*).
*Gośāla* means born in a cow-shed (*gośāla*). *Kharaśāla* is explained in the same way. In all these cases, there is the elision (*luk*) of the suffix *aṇ*.

There is no increase in the vowel length. Now, one might object that because the word *śālā* is feminine, the mention of a short vowel (*hrasva*) is inappropriate; to this he says: "optionally, as in the case of *senā*" (*vibhāṣā senā*). By the paribhāṣā regarding forms qualified by gender (*liṅgaviśiṣṭaparibhāṣā*), elision (*luk*) occurs even from the feminine form.

(1389) *vatsaśālā’bhijidaśvayukchatabhiṣajo vā* || 4|3|36 || *vatsaśālābhijit* | "From these" means from *vatsaśālā*, *abhijit*, *aśvayuj*, and *śatabhiṣaj*. The word "of the following" (*parasya*) is to be supplied. "And so forth" refers to *abhijiti*.
Born under Abhijit: *ābhijitaḥ*, *abhijit*. Born under Aśvayuj: *āśvayujaḥ*, *aśvayuk*.
Born under Śatabhiṣaj: *śātabhiṣajaḥ*, *śatabhiṣak*.
Regarding the sense of "born under," it should be stated that the suffix *aṇ* is optionally introduced with the augment *ḍi*.

Regarding the phrase "in the sense of being born" (*jātārthe*): the meaning is that the general suffix *aṇ*, which was set aside by the suffix *ṭhañ* in the rule *kālāṭ ṭhañ*, is raised again by the rule *saṃdhivelādi-sūtra*, and it should be stated that it optionally becomes marked with the *ḍit* designation. This Vārttika is seen in the Bhāṣya on the rule *dṛṣṭaṃ sāme*. [The example] *śātabhiṣaḥ* is formed with the suffix *aṇ*.
In the alternative case [of the suffix *ṇya*], there is elision of the *ṭi* portion.
(1390) Pāṇini 4.3.37: *nakṣatrebhyo bahulam*. From words denoting lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*), the suffix is applied diversely. For example, *rohiṇaḥ*, meaning "born under Rohiṇī."

When the *luk* elision occurs for the *nakṣatra-aṇ* suffix, the initial *vṛddhi* is precluded; consequently, by the rule "ṭh-luk-taddhita-lukī," there is the removal of the feminine suffix (*strī-pratyaya*). It should not be argued that if this were the case, the letter *takāra* would also be removed along with the *nakāra*; for this word *rohita* does not denote a specific color.
If it were derived from the root *sthā* with the suffix *ṅīp* according to the rule *ṭi-ṣṭhavarṇād-anudāttāt*, then upon the removal of *ṅīp*, the letter *t* would also have to be removed.

However, this word *rohiṇī* is an underived (avyutpanna) term conventionally established (*rūḍha*) for a specific lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*). The suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied by its inclusion in the *gaurādi* group according to the rule *rohiṇī nakṣatre*. For this very reason, it is said: "The lunar mansion is *rohiṇī*."

In cases such as *prajāpati-devatā*, the fact that the final syllable is heard to be udātta is not contradicted; otherwise, by rules such as "for words ending in *ṭha*, *ta*, *na*, *ti*, or *ni*, the acute accent falls on the first syllable," the initial syllable would instead be udātta. Enough of this. (1391) *kṛta-labdha-krīta-kuśalāḥ* | 4.3.28 | [The suffix *aṇ* is applied after a word denoting price when it signifies something made, obtained, bought, or skilled therein.]

*Kṛtalabdha* (Pāṇini 4.3.38). Regarding *tatrety eva*: the word *tatra* alone is carried over from the rule *tatra jātaḥ* (4.3.25); however, the word *jātaḥ* has ceased to apply. Thus, the meaning is that in the sense of "done," "obtained," "bought," or "skilled," the suffixes *aṇ* and others, as well as *gha* and others, should be applied respectively to a word ending in the locative case.
*snaughna*—the suffix *aṇ* is the general rule (*autsargika*). Examples such as *rāṣṭre kṛtaḥ* = *rāṣṭriyaḥ* (one made in the kingdom) should also be cited.
(1392) *prāyabhavaḥ* (Pāṇini 4.3.39).

"Prāyabhavaḥ" (originating mostly therein). Regarding "tatrety eva" (only [in the sense] "therein"): the meaning is that when the sense is "originating mostly therein," suffixes such as *aṇ* and others, as well as *gha* and others, should be applied respectively according to the rule.
The explanation of the word *prāya* is "mostly" (*bāhulyena*). It means simply "originating therein."
This has been rejected in the Bhāṣya because [the desired forms] are already established.

(1393) *upajānu-upakarṇa-upanīveṣṭhak* 4.3.40: after the words *upajānu*, *upakarṇa*, and *upanīvi*, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied in the sense of "mostly existing there" (*prāyabhava*). Thus, one obtains *aupajānuka*, *aupakarṇika*, and *aupanīvika*.
The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhac* is applied after these [words]. In cases such as *upajānu*, there is an *avyayībhāva* compound expressing proximity.
Regarding *aupajānuka*: "near the knee" is *upajānu*; the meaning is "that which generally exists therein.
Because it follows a word ending in *u*, the *ṭha* is replaced by *ka*. Regarding *aupakarṇika*: "near the ear" is *upakarṇa*.
The meaning is "mostly existing there. Regarding *aupanīvika*: *upanīvi* means "near the waist-cloth" (*nīvi*);
the meaning is "mostly existing there. (1394) *saṃbhūte* [Pāṇini 4.3.41].

In the case of *saṃbhūte*, it is simply "therein. The meaning is that after a word in the locative case (*saptamī*), when the sense is "produced therein" (*saṃbhūte*), the suffixes *aṇ* and others, as well as *gha* and others, shall apply according to their respective rules. *Saṃbhavaḥ* means possibility or probability. (1395) *Kośāḍ ḍhañ* [Pāṇini 4.3.42].

*Kośāḍḍhañ*: *kauśeyaṃ vastram* ("silk cloth"). This means "a product of the cocoon of a specific type of insect. This is according to the Vārttika rule: *ṭhvikāre kośāḍḍhañ* ("the suffix *ḍhañ* [which becomes *eyan*] is applied after *kośa* when a derivative [product] is denoted").
(1396) *Kālāt sādhupuṣpyatpacyamāneṣu* (Pāṇini 4.3.43): [The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word denoting time when it signifies that which blossoms well or ripens during that time].

"From time [expressed by a word ending in the locative case], [the suffix *yat*] is applied after [a root] meaning 'to flower well' (*sādhu-puṣpyat*). The meaning is that when the senses of "in that place," "well," "flowering," or "ripening" are intended, suffixes prescribed according to the rules beginning with *yathā* shall occur after a word ending in the locative case.
From the root *puṣp* (meaning "to blossom") belonging to the *divādi* class, the form *puṣpyat* is derived from the present participle (*laṭ*) in the *śatṛ* suffix. Thus, "puṣpyat" is obtained.
Regarding *haimanaḥ prāvāraḥ* (a winter cloak): by the rule *sarvatrāṇ ca talopaśca*, there is the suffix *aṇ* and the elision of the *tal*.

Regarding *vāsantyaḥ*: by the rule *ṭiḍḍhea*, the suffix *ṅīp* is applied. Regarding *śāradāḥ*: here the suffix *ṛtvaṇ* is used. The phrase *tatra bhavaḥ* ("occurring therein") continues to apply [from the previous sūtra] up to the limit of *kāla* ("time").

(1397) *upte ca* |4|3|43|. Also when [the action] is "sown. The word *tatra* (therein) is understood here as well. After a word denoting time ending in the seventh case (*saptamī*), the prescribed suffixes shall occur in the sense of "having been sown" (*upta*). [The word] "are sown" (*upyante*) is derived from the root *ḍu vap* in the sense of "the scattering of seeds" (*bījasantāna*).
The meaning is that the past tense is not intended to be expressed.
(1398) *āśvayujyā vuñ* | 4.3.45 | [The suffix] *vuñ* is applied after *āśvayujī*. It is governed by the rule "tatropya" (4.3.53).

The meaning is that the suffix *vuñ* occurs after the word *āśvayujī*, which ends in the seventh case (*saptamī*), when the sense of "sown" (*upta*) is expressed. It is an exception (*apavāda*) to *ṭhañ*;
that is to say, it supersedes the *ṭhañ* prescribed by the rule *kālāt ṭhañ*. The form *āśvayujakāḥ* means "those sown on the full moon day of Āśvayuja";
for *āśvayujī* refers to the full moon day joined with the month of Āśvayuja, and the sense is "sown therein."

(1399) *grīṣmavasantād anyatarasyām* |4|3|46|. From *grīṣma* and *vasanta*: the meaning is that the suffix *vuñ* is optionally applied after the words *grīṣma* and *vasanta* when they end in the locative case and denote something sown. (1400) *deyam ṛṇe* |4|3|47|. [The same suffix is applied] to a word ending in the locative case when it means "to be given" provided it refers to a debt.

Regarding the term *deyam* (to be given), it refers specifically to a debt (*ṛṇa*). The word *tatra* (therein) also continues [from the previous rule], while *vuñ* is discontinued. When a word denoting time ending in the seventh case is used, the suffixes prescribed by the rule for the sense of "to be given" (*deya*) shall apply, provided that the thing to be given is a debt. For example: *māsikam* (due within a month).
Regarding the sense of time (*kālaṭṭha*):
(1401) *kalāpy-aśvattha-yavabusād vun* |4|3|48|. From the words *kalāpin*, *aśvattha*, and *yavabusā*, which denote time, [the suffix *vun* is applied].

The meaning is that the suffix *vun* is applied in the sense of "a debt to be paid" when following words ending in the locative case (*saptamyanta*). Regarding *kalāpaka*: [the suffix] *vun* is added; there is the substitution of *a*; and by the rule *ṭnastaddhite*, there is the elision of the final vowel (*ṭilopa*). Regarding *aśvattha*:
the intention is that there is the elision (*luk*) of the suffix denoting a modification (*vikāra*) when it refers to the fruit. However, if the word *aśvattha* belongs to the *plakṣādi* group...

Therefore, by the rule *ṭhplakṣādibhyo 'ṇ* [Pāṇini 4.3.164], the suffix *aṇ* is prescribed for the fruit; since this prescription of *aṇ* prevents elision (*luk*), the word *aśvattha* is used figuratively (*lākṣaṇika*) for the fruit—this is the intended meaning.
(1402) *grīṣmā'varasamādvuñchaṇ* [Pāṇini 4.3.49].
The suffix *vuñ* is applied after the words *grīṣma* and *avarasamā*. The word *samā* is always feminine and plural when it means "year.

[The compound] *grīṣma-avarasamā* is a collective dvandva; from this, the fifth case ending is used. The meaning is that the suffix *vuñ* is added after these two in the sense of "a debt to be paid therein. Thus, *āvarasamakam* means "in the later years" (*avarāsu samāsu*).
The meaning is "that which is to be paid as a debt. This is a compound formed by the rule *taddhitārtha* (Pāṇini 2.1.51). (1403) *saṃvatsarāgrahāyaṇībhyāṃ ṭhañ ca* (Pāṇini 4.3.50):
after the words *saṃvatsara* and *āgrahāyaṇī*, the suffix *ṭhan* is also applied [in the sense of "to be paid as a debt"], provided that the word ending in the locative case follows.
The remainder [of the rule]: in the *saṃdhivelādi* group, it is read as "from *saṃvatsara*, [the suffixes *aṇ* and *ṭhañ* are applied] in the sense of fruit and festival.
Therein, when the fruit is intended to be expressed as a debt to be paid, the suffix *aṇ* which would otherwise apply is superseded by this *ṭhañ*.
(1404) *vyāharati mṛgaḥ* | 4.3.51 | [The suffix *aṇ* is applied after a word denoting a time to form a name of] a beast that cries out [at that time].
The animal speaks; in that case, it is simply "kālāt" (from time). The rule "ṭhdeyamṛṇe" is no longer applicable. (1405) *tadasya soḍham* |4|3|52|.
Regarding the sense "that has been endured by him," suffixes shall be applied as prescribed after a word in the nominative case.

The meaning of *soḍham* is "repeatedly practiced" (*abhyastam*). Regarding *naiśikaḥ* and *naiśaḥ*: the suffixes *ṭhañ* and *aṇ* are applied [respectively] by the rule "after *niśā* and *pradoṣa*" (*niśāpradoṣābhyāṃ ca*).
[The rule] "that which occurs therein" (*tatra bhavaḥ*) [is 4.3.53].

In this context, the word *bhava* [is used]. The term *kālāt* (from time) is excluded. The meaning is that in this sense, suffixes are applied as prescribed after a word ending in the locative case (*saptamī*). There is a distinction between *bhavanaṃ* (existence) and *jananam utpattiḥ* (birth or origination).
Regarding *sraughna*: the suffix *aṇ* is the general rule (*utsarga*). Regarding *rāṣṭriya*: the suffix *gha* is applied by the rule *rāṣṭrāvārapārād ghaḥ*.

(1407) *digādibhyo yat* | 4|3|54| The suffix *yat* is applied after words beginning with *diś* (direction), provided they are in the locative case; the ellipsis [to complete the rule] is "in the sense of 'being there' (*bhava*)."
*diśyam* means "pertaining to the direction" (*diśi bhavam*).

(1408) *Śarīrāvayavācca* [Pāṇini 4.3.55]: "And from parts of the body. The remainder of the rule is: "after words ending in the locative case, in the sense of 'being there' (*bhava*). Thus, *dantyam*.
The meaning is "occurring in *danta*. By the rule *yasyeti ca*, there is the elision of the vowel *a*. In the same way, [the forms] *kaṇṭhya* and so on are derived.
(1409) *prācām nagarānte* | 7|3|24|. Regarding the phrase *prācām nagarānte*: the term *aṅgasya* is supplied from the governing context, and the word *nagarānte* [specifies the condition].
In accordance with the locative case [of the previous rule], it is changed to the locative. "Of the second member" (*uttarapadasya*) is the governing heading (*adhikṛta*).
From the sūtra *ṭhhṛdbhagasindhvante*, the phrase "of the first member" (*pūrvapadasya*) is carried over (*anuvartate*). Thus, the meaning is as follows:
when a city of the Easterners (*prācām*) is at the end of a compound, [the substitution occurs] for both the first member and the second member.
"Vṛddhi shall replace the vowel of that which begins with *ac* before a *taddhita* suffix having the markers *ñ*, *ṇ*, or *k*.
Thus, "Suhmanagara" and "Puṇḍranagara" constitute the eastern boundary of the eastern region (*prāgdeśa*).
"Madranagara is in the north" means that there is a city named Madranagara in the northern region (*udagdeśa*).
The meaning is that there is some city.
(1410) *Vibhāṣitam apataram jaṅgaladhenuvalajāntasya* (Pāṇini 7.3.25). [The rule concerns] a stem ending in *jaṅgala*, *dhenu*, or *valaja*. That is, *jaṅgala*, *dhenu*, and *valaja*.
The meaning is "up to this point. Regarding "in Kurujaṅgala," the word "bhava" (originating from) is to be supplied.
Words such as *kurujaṅgala* refer to specific regions.
(1411) Pāṇini 4.3.56: *dṛtikukṣikalaśivastyastyaherḍhañ*.

*dṛtikukṣi*: [The suffix] *ḍhañ* is applied after *dṛti*, *kukṣi*, *kalaśi*, *vasti*, *asti*, and *ahi* in the sense of "being there" (*bhava*). The phrase "after words ending in the locative case" is understood as a remainder [from the previous rule]. *Dārteyam* means "that which exists in a leather bag" (*dṛtau bhavam*). [The suffix] *ḍhañ* is added, followed by *eya*, vṛddhi of the first vowel, and the substitution of *ra* for the final vowel. A *dṛti* is a leather water-bag.

Regarding the word *kaukṣeyam*: although the suffix *vuñ* would have been expected by virtue of its inclusion in the *dūma-ādi* group, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied instead. *Kaliśi* refers to a jar; the commentators on Amara state that "the *kalaśi* is a vessel for churning. According to Amara, "the *vasti* is the two [organs] below the navel. That which exists there is *bāsteya*. It is called *asti*.

The author of the Nyāsa and Haradatta state that *āsteya* is an indeclinable (*avyaya*) resembling a case-ending, meaning "in existence" (*satāyām*) or "in a cloud" (*ghane*). In this context, *āsteya* means "born therein. *Ahiḥ* means "a snake"; *āheya* means "born from that [snake].
(1412) *grīvābhyo’ṇ ca* [Pāṇini 4.3.57].
The suffix *aṇ* is also applied after the word *grīvā*; this is an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule [Pāṇini 4.3.55] beginning with *śarīrāvayavācca*.

This word *grīvā* refers to a cluster of vessels (*dhamanī-saṅga*). In that context, when there is an intention to express a connection involving distinct manifested parts, the suffix is applied to the form ending in the plural number.

The plural number is used to indicate [the collective sense]. However, when there is an intention to express the difference between the parts as being concealed (*tirohita*), the suffixes *aṇ* and *ḍhañ* indeed occur even after a word ending in the singular.
(Pāṇini 4.3.58) *gambhīrāñ ñyaḥ*.

[The suffix] *añ* occurs after [the word] *gambhīra*. Regarding "depth" (*gāmbhīrya*): if the rule for the suffix *yañ* were applied, then according to the rule "after a feminine [base], *ṣpha* is added [to form a feminine noun]; in the opinion of the Easterners, *ṣpha* is a *taddhita* suffix," the suffix *ṣpha* would have occurred. [However, this is not the case. Furthermore: "Also after an *avyayībhāva* compound, [the suffix *ṭac* is added]. (Pāṇini 4.3.59).
"And from an *avyayībhāva* compound. The word "the suffix *ñya*" is understood as the remainder [of the rule]. [This suffix] is desired only after words such as *parimukha*.
Regarding the phrase "after *parimukha* and so forth": although this *vārttika* is not seen in the *Bhāṣya*, nevertheless...

Following the recitation of the *dig-ādigaṇa*, it is understood by the force of the subsequent recitation of the *parimukha-ādigaṇa* that the term "avyayībhāva" here refers specifically to those beginning with *parimukha*; for there is no *parimukha-ādigaṇa* in the *Aṣṭādhyāyī*.
There is another purpose [for this rule]. In the case of *āṭpakūla*, the meaning is "be near the bank" (*upakūlaṃ bhava*).

Even though it is an *avyayībhāva* compound, the suffix *ñya* does not apply because it is not included among the group beginning with *parimukha*. (Pāṇini 4.3.60: *antaḥpūrvapadāt ṭhañ* ("The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word preceded by *antaḥ* as its prior member").
The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a compound whose prior member ends in *antaḥ*. For example: *antarveśmam* (within the house). This is an *avyayībhāva* compound in the sense of a case ending.

By the rule *ṭhanaśca*, the suffix *ṭac* is applied [to form *antarveśman*]. In the case of *āntarveśmikam*: the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied; the *ika* portion is elided; the case-ending (*su*) is dropped (*subluk*); the *ṭi* portion is elided (*ṭilopa*); and the initial vowel undergoes vṛddhi strengthening (*ādivṛddhi*). In the case of *āntargaṇikam*: *antargaṇam* means "within a group" (*gaṇe*). In that context...
The meaning is "existence. Regarding the term *ādhyātmika*: *adhyātma* means "in the self" (*ātmani*); the meaning is "that which exists therein.
[This is because] the suffix *-iṣṭhañ* is prescribed after *adhyātma* and other such words.
"Internal" (*ādhyātmika*) means "pertaining to the self" (*ātmani*), that is, *adhyātma*. The meaning is "that which exists therein.

(1416) *anuśatikādīnāṃ ca* | 7|3|20|. And for the *anuśatika* group and others: in the section concerning initial *vṛddhi*, [the rule applies] to the final member of the compound and to the initial member.
This sutra occurs in the section concerning the "cetas" (the mind). Thus he says: "of these. Regarding the term *ādhidaivika*:
it means "pertaining to the gods" (*adhideva*), that is, existing therein; the suffix *ṭhañ* causes the vowel increase (*vṛddhi*) of both members of the compound.
Regarding the term *ādhibhautika*: it means "pertaining to beings" (*adhibhūta*), that is, existing therein.

*Aihalaukika* means "pertaining to this world" (*iha loke bhavam*). *Pāralaukika* means "pertaining to the next world" (*paraloke bhavam*). In all these cases, by the suffix *ṭhañ*, there is vocalic strengthening (*vṛddhi*) of both members of the compound.
(1417) Pāṇini 7.3.1: [The substitution of *ai* for *ā* occurs] after *deva*, *kāśi*, *śiṃśapā*, *āditya*, *vāḍ*, *dīrghasatra*, and *śreyas*.

*Devikā*. This sūtra belongs to the section concerning initial *vṛddhi*. Regarding the word "of those ending in -ṣ" (*ṣām*): this means [the application of the rule] to these—namely, *devikā*, *śiṃśapā*, *dityavāhū*, and *dīrghasatra*.

Regarding the phrase "when there is the occurrence of *vṛddhi*": when there is the occurrence of initial *vṛddhi*, the letter *ā* is substituted for the initial vowel as an exception (*apavāda*) to that [general rule].
The meaning is "it might be. Regarding *dāvikam*: the river named Devikā; the meaning is "that which exists in it.

Regarding *dāvikākūlāḥ*: this is an example provided to dispel the misconception that there is a vṛddhi [substitution] in the final member of the compound, because the sense is that this rule falls outside the scope of that specific governing heading (*adhikāra*). Regarding *śāṃśapaḥ*.

The vowel *ā* replaces the *i* of *ikāra*; this is a *vṛddhi* substitute according to the rule *añ-ṇ-i-vṛddhiḥ*. Since the word *śiṃśapā* is listed among the words beginning with *palāśa*, the suffix *ñañ* is optionally applied; in its absence, the suffix *aṇ* applies—this is the meaning. Regarding the form *dātyauha*:
from the word *dityavāh*, the suffix *aṇ* is added by the rule *tasyedam*, and then there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the *vāh* by the rule *vāha ūṭh*.

The original form is *pūrvarūpa*. By the rule "ṭhetyedhatyūṭhasu," there is *vṛddhi*. The letter *ā* is an exception to the initial *vṛddhi* of the vowel *i*. Regarding the term *dīrghasūtram*: by the rule "tasyedaṃ," there is the suffix *aṇ*, and the initial vowel *ī* becomes *ā*. Regarding *śrāyasam*: by the rule "tatra bhavaḥ," there is the suffix *aṇ*, [and the vowel *e* becomes *ai*].
The suffix *ṭhañ* shall be applied after the word *grāma* when it is preceded by *pari* or *anu*. This is the meaning. (1418) *Grāmātparyanupūrvāt* |4|3|61|.
The suffix *ṭhañ* shall be applied after *grāma* when it is preceded by *pari* or *anu*. This is the rule.
The intention is that [the suffix *cha*] follows from the recurrence of the rule "when the first member ends in *ṭha*" (*ṭhantaḥ-pūrvapadāt*).

(1419) *jihvāmūlāṅguleś-chaḥ* | 4.3.62 | The suffix *cha* is applied after *jihvāmūla* and *aṅguli*. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *ya*, which would have been applied by the rule "after a word denoting a part of the body" (*śarīrāvayavāt*).

(1420) *vargāntācca* |4|3|63|. [The suffix *cha*] also follows a word ending in a class-consonant (*varga*). For example, *kavargīya* ("belonging to the *ka*-class"). The meaning is "that which exists in the class beginning with *ka*. (1421) *aśabde yatkhāvanyatarasyām* |4|3|64|. [The suffixes *yat* and *kha* are optionally used after a word ending in a class-consonant when it does not denote a linguistic sound.]

In the absence of a specific rule, the remainder is supplied by the sūtra *ṭhVargāntāc chaḥ*. Thus we have *madvargyaḥ* and *madvargīṇaḥ*, meaning "one who belongs to my group" or "one who is on my side. (1422) *Karṇalalāṭātkan alaṅkāre* [Pāṇini 4.3.65]: The suffix *kan* is added after the words *karṇa* and *lalāṭa* when the sense is "ornament."
[The suffix *kan* is applied] after *karṇa* and *lalāṭa*, as an exception (*apavāda*) to [Pāṇini 4.3.55] *śarīrāvayavācca*. Thus, we have *karṇikā* and *lalāṭikā*. The meaning is:

"an ornament located on the ear" or "on the forehead. The feminine gender is established by common usage (*lokāt*). When the feminine suffix *ṭāp* is added, the shortening of the vowel occurs by [Pāṇini 7.3.44] *pratyayasthāt...*.

(1423) *tasya vyākhyāna* [is formed] from the name of that which is to be explained; 4.3.66. Also, in the case of *tasya vyākhyāna*. A "commentary" (*vyākhyāna*) is a book by which something is explained (*vyākhyāyate*);
the suffix *lyuṭ* is used in the sense of the instrument (*karaṇe*). In the analytical construction (*vigraha*), it is *tasya vyākhyānaḥ*.

The meaning is that suffixes are applied as prescribed after a word ending in the sixth case (*ṣaṣṭhī*) which denotes the text to be explained, and after a word ending in the seventh case (*saptamī*) in the sense of "occurring therein" (*tatra bhavaḥ*). The particle *ca* serves to include the rule "tatra bhavaḥ. Regarding *saupa*: [the suffix] *añ* is the general rule. Regarding *taiṅ*: [the suffix] *ñyaṅ*.
The meaning is that it is a work consisting of an explanation (*vyākhyāna*) of verbal suffixes (*tiṅ*). Regarding *kārta*: the meaning is "one who has made an explanation" (*kṛtā vyākhyāna*).

When the suffix *aṇ* is applied, there is vowel strengthening (*vṛddhi*) of the first vowel, followed by the substitution of *ra* for the semivowel. He gives an example in the sense of "belonging to that" (*bhavārtha*)—namely, *saupam*.
And this is clearly stated in the Bhāṣya by the two rules: "this belongs to that" (*tasyedam*) and "originating therein" (*tatra bhavaḥ*).

(1424) *bahvaco'ntodātāṭṭhañ* | 4|3|67 | From a polysyllabic word that has the udātta accent on the final syllable, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied in the aforementioned scope. This is an exception to *aṇ*.

(1425) And from words denoting *kratu* and *yajña*. [Pāṇini 4.3.68] Regarding "from words denoting *kratu* and *yajña*": the meaning is that the words *kratu* and *yajña* are well-known to denote rituals in which the *soma* creeper is the sacrificial substance (*dravya*). If that is so, then the inclusion of the word *antara* (in the previous rule) is redundant, because of the use of the plural number.
To the objection that this would result in the cessation of the apprehension of their own nature, he says: "Therein" (*tatra*). Regarding the phrase "they are apprehended":

the intention is that here the word *kratu* refers to Soma sacrifices, while the word *yajña* refers to sacrifices other than those. And thus, [the term applies] to those denoting specific Soma sacrifices as well as those denoting specific sacrifices other than them.
The meaning is that the suffixes *ṭhak* and *chañ* are applied to the aforementioned subjects. Regarding "pākayājñika":

*pākayajñas* are sacrifices such as the *pārvaṇasthālīpāka* and others, which are accomplished by means of the *aupāsana* fire; it refers either to a treatise explaining those [sacrifices] or to one who exists within them. Regarding "nāvayajñika": this refers to the sacrifice called *āgrayaṇa*, which consists of fresh [grain].

[The term] *navayajña*. Now, one might ask: since this is already established by the previous rule, for what purpose is this stated? To this he replies: "It is for the sake of making it oxytone. The word *vājapeya* is well-known in the Taittirīya and other texts as being circumflex-accented on the middle syllable (*madhyodātta*). Although the word *agniṣṭoma* is indeed seen in the Taittirīya as being oxytone (*antodātta*), [this rule is necessary to ensure its correct accentuation here].

The term *navayajña* is also a genitive compound (*ṣaṣṭhīsamāsa*) and, by the accentuation rule for compounds, would necessarily be oxytone; nevertheless, there is no fault, because this [present rule] applies even to oxytones for the sake of another purpose, since it is subsequent [in the order of rules]. (1426) *adhyāyeśvevarṣeḥ* | Pāṇini 4.3.69.

The suffix occurs after the word *ṛṣi* when it refers to chapters (*adhyāya*). The mantra "Vasiṣṭha" [is used as an example] by way of metaphorical indication (*lakṣaṇā*); this is the intended meaning.

"A chapter belonging to Vasiṣṭha" (*vāsiṣṭhika*) refers to a specific type of literary work. As for "a ṛc verse belonging to Vasiṣṭha" (*vāsiṣṭhī ṛk*), the intention is that the suffix *ṭhañ* does not apply here because a ṛc verse lacks the designation of being a "chapter."
(1427) *pauroḍāśapuroḍāśāt ṣṭhan* |4|3|70|.
[The word] *pauroḍāśa* [is formed]. The phrase "in the sense mentioned" is to be supplied as the remainder. Regarding *puroḍāśa*:
the meaning is that a mantra accompanied by the word *puroḍāśa* is, by way of indication (*lakṣaṇayā*), called *puroḍāśa*.
"That very thing is *pauroḍāśa*. The intention is that the suffix *aṇ* is applied in its own sense (*svārthe*) according to the rule beginning with *prajñādi*.

*Pauroḍāśika* is the form derived from *pauroḍāśa* with the suffix *ṭhan*. *Puroḍāśika* is the form derived from the word *puroḍāśa* with the suffix *ṭhan*; because the suffix is marked with *ṣ*, the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied.
*pauroḍāśikī*—[derived from] *puroḍāśa*.

(1428) *cchandaso yadaṇau* | 4|3|71|. [The suffixes] *ya* and *aṇ* are applied after *chandas*. The remainder [of the rule] is: "in the sense of 'an explanation thereof' (*tasya vyākhyāne*) and 'existing therein' (*tatra bhavaḥ*). [Thus,] *chāndasa*.

*Chāndasa*: [This term means] one who explains the *chandas* (Vedic meters), or that which exists therein; it is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *ṭhak* characterized by two syllables, which will be mentioned later. (1429) *Dvyaj-ṛd-brāhmaṇa-ṛk-prathama-adhvara-puraścaraṇa-nāma-ākhyātāt ṭhak*.
Pāṇini 4.3.72: After words consisting of two syllables, after *ṛt*, *brāhmaṇa*, *ṛc*, *prathama*, *adhvara*,
*puraścaraṇa*, *nāman*, and *ākhyāta*, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied in the sense of "a commentary on that" (*tasya vyākhyāna*) and "occurring therein" (*tatra bhava*).

"Śaiṣika" means that which pertains to a "śeṣa," i.e., a commentary (vyākhyāna) or something occurring therein. "Pāśuka" refers to a text expounding the animal sacrifice (paśuyāga); it means a commentary on or something pertaining to the "paśu. Because [the suffix] *uka* follows, the *ṭha* is replaced by *ka*. "Ṛtaḥ" means "is cited as an example."

"Cāturhotṛka" refers to the meaning of the exposition or that which pertains to the *caturhotṛ* mantras— namely, the mantras beginning with "The altar is the ladle" (*citiḥ sruk*)— which are well known in the Taittirīya [Saṃhitā]. Similarly, "Brāhmaṇika" and "Ārcika" refer to the *brāhmaṇas*.

The *brāhmaṇa* portions are those parts of the Veda distinct from the *mantras*, or the explanation of those *ṛks*; "that which exists therein" is the meaning. Thus, one is called *brāhmaṇika* or *ārcika*. The *brāhmaṇas* are the parts of the Veda distinct from the *mantras*, or the explanation of those *ṛks*; that which exists therein [is the *brāhmaṇika*].

The meaning is "he knows" (*vetti*). Regarding the phrase "and so forth": [the suffixes denote] one who studies the *Prāthamika*, the *Ādhvarika*, the *Pauraścaraṇika*, the *Nāmika*, and the *Ākhyātika*.
(1430) Pāṇini 4.3.73: *aṇ ṛgayanādibhyaḥ* ("The suffix *aṇ* is applied after [words such as] *ṛgayan* and others").
[The suffix is applied] after words such as *ṛgayanādi*. The remainder [of the rule] is: "in the sense of 'an explanation thereof' (*tasya vyākhyāna*) and 'occurring therein' (*tatra bhava*).

Regarding *ārgayana*: *ṛgayanam* means the *Ṛksaṃhitā*; the meaning is "an explanation thereof" or "occurring therein. Although the suffix *ṭhañ* would have been expected by the rule "after a polysyllabic word with an udātta on the final syllable," the suffix *aṇ* is used. Thus, *aupaniṣada*.
Thus [it is said]. The meaning is: "that which exists in the commentary on the Upaniṣads. Similarly, one is called a *vaiyākaraṇa* (grammarian).

By the rule *na yvābhyām*, the diphthong *ai* is substituted. They say, however, that the mention of the suffix *aṇ* is for the purpose of precluding the suffix *cha*; otherwise, once *aṇ* has been applied, *cha* would be unavoidable.
(1431) *tata āgataḥ* | Pāṇini 4.3.74. The meaning is: in this sense—that "he has come from that"—affixes are applied as prescribed after a word ending in the fifth case (*pañcamī*).
For example, *sraughnaḥ*: here the suffix *aṇ* is applied according to the general rule (*autsargika*).
(1432) *ṭhagāyasthānebhyaḥ* | Pāṇini 4.3.75.

[The rule] *ṭhagāyasthānebhyaḥ*: the remainder [of the meaning] is "that which has come from that" (*tata āgataḥ*). Revenue (*āya*) is the share to be taken by the owner in markets and such places; that in which it is collected is the "place of revenue" (*āyasthāna*), and [the suffix *ṭhak* is applied] after words denoting such places.
This is the meaning.

(1433) *Śuṇḍikādibhyo 'ṇ* | Pāṇini 4.3.76: The suffix *aṇ* is applied after words beginning with *śuṇḍika*. [The rule] "from that which has come" (*tata āgata*) applies here as well. *Śuṇḍika* refers to a particular type of tavern or place for drinking.

This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *ṭhak* prescribed by the preceding sūtra. Regarding *kārkaṇa*: the remainder [of the rule] is "come from *kṛkaṇa*"; it is an exception to the suffix *cha* prescribed by the rule "after *kṛkaṇa* and *parṇa*, when [the descendant is] Bhāradvāja. Regarding *tairtha*: it is an exception to the suffix *vuñ* prescribed for the group beginning with *dhūma*. Regarding *āudapāna*: here, because it begins with *ut*, the suffix *añ* would have been applicable, but [it is not].

It occurs again because of the inclusion of *añ*; otherwise, if the rule were applied exactly as it was obtained [from the previous sūtra], *añ* alone would apply, overriding the suffixes *-īya*, *-sthāna*, and *-ṭhak*. (1434) Pāṇini 4.3.77: The suffix *vuñ* is added after words denoting a relationship by knowledge (*vidyā*) or by birth (*yoni*).

[The suffix] *vidyāyoni* [is applied]. It is simply [the sense of] "derived from that" (*tata āgata*). For example: *aupādhyāyakaḥ*, *paitāmahakaḥ*. The meaning is "derived from a teacher" (*upādhyāya*) and "derived from a grandfather" (*pitāmaha*).
(1435) *ṛtaṣṭhañ* | Pāṇini 4.3.78.

*Ñataṣṭhañ*: This means [the suffix *ṭhañ*] is applied after a word ending in *ṛt* that denotes a relationship by learning (*vidyā*) or by birth (*yoni*). It is exactly as in the rule "from that, it has come" (*tata āgataḥ*). For example: *hautṛkam*, *bhrātṛkam*. Because the suffix *uka* follows, the *ṭh* of *ṭhañ* is replaced by *ka*. (1436) *Pituryaśca*: [The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after the word *pitṛ*, and furthermore, the suffix *ya* is also applied. 4.3.79.
And [the suffix] *putuḥ* is also [used]. He demonstrates the grammatical derivation (*prakriyā*) with the words "from *rīñ* [comes] *rāyaḥ*.
(1437) *gotrādaṅkavat* | Pāṇini 4.3.80.

From a *gotra* [name], as in the case of the *aṅka* [suffixes]. Whatever suffixes are used after a *gotra* [name] in the sense of "marked" (*aṅka*), those same suffixes are used in the sense of "come from that" (*tata āgataḥ*).
The meaning is "they come to be. "Coming from the Bidas" (*bidebhya āgatam*) is an illustration of the analytical derivation (*vigraha*).
Here, because the suffix *añ* is elided in the plural by the rule *ṭhyañañośca*, the form *bidebhyaḥ* is used as the designation.
[The derivative form is] *baidam*.
