(1526) *prāgvahateṣṭhak* | 4|4|1 | Regarding *prāgvahateṣṭhak*: the word "vahati" is used here as a partial reference (*ekadeśa*) to the entire sūtra *tadvahati rathayugaprāsaṅgam*. With this intention, he says: "from the [sūtra] *tadvahati* onwards."
Regarding this, he says: there is an addition [to the rule] from words such as *mā* and so forth.
"He says that" (*tadāha*). The word *iti* is to be understood as displaced [in the sūtra], following immediately after the word *tat*.
The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after words such as *mā*, *svāgata*, and others, in the sense of "he says that. (*tadityāha*) means "he says 'mā'," etc.

The syntactical connection is with the word *upasaṅkhyānam* (supplementation). By the word *ṭhta*, the meaning of the sentence (*vākyārtha*) is intended to be expressed. The particle *iti* indicates that this sentential meaning functions as the object (*karman*).
In such cases as "He said, 'Do not make a sound,'" the word *māśabda* [is used] because it is a constituent part of that sentence.

From the word "ityādi" (and so forth) up to "ṭhag" [is the suffix]. Regarding "māśābdika": the construction is "mā śabdam kārṣīḥ" (do not make a sound). The suffix *luṅ* is used in the sense of the imperative (*loṭ*) by the rule "māṅi luṅ. The augment *aṭ* is prohibited by the rule "na māṅyoge. The meaning is "do not make a sound. Here, the word "āha" (says) [is used].
With respect to the action of speaking clearly the meaning of the verbal root *brūñ* (to speak), the sentence-meaning "Do not make a sound" (*mā śabdaṃ kārṣīḥ*) is the object (*karman*).
The aggregate consisting of the single portion of that sentence, namely the word *mā*, is [the base]. Therefore, this suffix follows that which lacks a case-ending.
For there is no case-ending after the aggregate consisting of the word *mā*. And thus, [it is established that] *māśabda*—

From the compound *samudāya* with the suffix *ṭhak*, the form *māśabdika* is derived. However, if the reading is *ṭhamā śabdaḥ kāri*, then *kāri* is the *luṅ* (aorist) in the sense of the object (*karman*), meaning "one for whom sound is not to be produced. Furthermore, one should not accept the literal rule *māśabdādibhyaṣṭhak* in the sense of "one who says that," [but rather apply it] in the sense of "one who says 'māśabda'," and so forth.

One might ask why it is not explained that the suffix *ṭhak* is applied directly after words such as *māsa* ending in the accusative case; the point is that if this were the case, the subsequent *vārttika*, "ṭhāhau prabhūtādibhyaḥ," would become redundant.
(1527) And [the augment *it* is applied] after the words beginning with *svāgata* [before the suffix *aṇ*]. Pāṇini 7.3.7. In the *svāgatādi* group, the words *svāgata* and *svadhvara* are recited;

regarding them, he states the specific rule: "And for the words beginning with *svāgata*, [the augment *it* is applied]. [The previous rule was: "Not [after a vowel] followed by *y* or *v* that stand at the end of a word, but rather before them..."

This is the sūtra following "na karmavyatihāre" within the section beginning with "tābhyāmaic. It means that *aij* should not occur. This is a supplement to the rule. The meaning is that although [the substitution of] *aij* would have been obtained by the rule "na yvābhyāṃ padāntābhyāṃ pūrvau tu tābhyāmaic," it should not take place.

*svādhvarikaḥ*: the meaning is that he is called *svadhvara*. Now, he provides examples for the remainder of the *svāgatādi* group—starting with *svaṅgasya*. *Vyāṅgiḥ*: the analysis (*vigraha*) is "the offspring of *vyaṅga*. *Vyaḍasya*: one who does not possess a *ḍa*.
*aḍaḥ*; *vyaḍaḥ* means that which is devoid of *aḍ*. Regarding the term *svāpateyam*:

by the rule *pathyatithivasatisvapater ḍhañ*, the suffix *ḍhañ* is applied. Because [the word *svapati*] belongs to the *dvārādi* group, the substitution of *ai* and *oc* (i.e., *vṛddhi*) is prohibited.
[The suffix *ṭhañ*] is applied after [words] such as *prabhūta*, etc., in the sense of "having said" (*āha*).
Regarding the term *āha*: the vowel *ā* in the word *āha* is indicated for the purpose of pronunciation; it refers to the initial portion of the word *āha*.
The word *tat* is carried over from the preceding *vārttika*. Thus, the suffix is applied after words ending in the accusative case in the sense of "having said."
The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is optionally prescribed after words such as *prabhūta*. *Pāryāptika* means "one who says [it is] sufficient.
After the verb *pṛcchati* ("he asks"), [the suffix is applied] after words such as *paradāra*.

"Regarding the word *pṛcchatau* (in the sense of 'he asks'): the term *ṭhañ* is understood to follow from the previous rule. The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is prescribed after words such as *susnāta* when they are in the accusative case and signify 'one who asks. In the example *saukhaśāyanikaḥ*, the meaning is 'one who asks about a comfortable bed. Regarding the phrase *anuśatikādiḥ*: the remainder [of the explanation] is that the word *sukhaśayana* belongs to the *anuśatikādi* group."
And thus, by the rule "and in the case of *anuśatika* and so forth," the meaning is that there is vṛddhi of the initial vowels of both the preceding and following members [of the compound].
[The suffix] *gacchati* [is applied] after words such as *paradāra*.

"From *gacchati* [the suffix is added]. The word *tat* (from the previous rule) is understood here. The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is added after words ending in the accusative case, such as *paradāra*, when the sense is "he goes to. Thus, *pāradārikaḥ* means "one who goes to another's wife. *Gaurutalpikaḥ* means "one who goes to the bed of the teacher"; *gurutalpa* refers to the teacher’s wife (*gurustrī*).

(1528) *tena dīvyati khanati jayati jitam* || 4.4.2 || The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is added to a word ending in the third case when it occurs in the analytical explanations (*vigraha*) "he plays with that," "he digs with that," "he wins with that," or "it has been won by that. For example: *pāradārikaḥ*.

The meaning is "he goes to another's wife. *Abhriḥ* means a spade or hoe. However, in the expression *devadattena jitam* ("conquered by Devadatta"), the suffix *ṭhak* is not applied, because that rule [for *ṭhak*] is prescribed only after a word ending in the instrumental case denoting an instrument (*karaṇa*).
*Sanskṛtam*: The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word ending in the third case in the sense of "prepared by that.
However, in the rule *saṃskṛtaṃ bhakṣāḥ*, the prescription of *aṇ* and other suffixes is from a word ending in the seventh case. *Mārīcikam* means "prepared with rays" (*marīcibhiḥ saṃskṛtam*).
(1530) *Kulatthakopadhād-aṇ* [Pāṇini 4.4.4].
Regarding the rule *kulatthakopadhād-aṇ*: the remainder [of the sūtra] is "the suffix *aṇ* follows a word ending in the third case when the sense is 'prepared with' (*saṃskṛtam*).
For example, *tintiṇīkam*; the meaning is "prepared with *tintiṇī*."

(1531) *tarati* |4|4|5|. The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is applied after a word ending in the third case when the sense is "he crosses" (*tarati*). (1532) *gopucchāṭ-ṭhañ* |4|4|6|. [The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after the word *gopuccha* in the same sense.]
The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after *gopuccha*. The remainder of the rule is that *ṭhañ* is added in the sense of "crosses by means of" (*tarati*) after a word ending in the third case.
(1533) *naudvyacaṣṭhan* |4|4|7|. [The rule] *naudvyacaṣṭhan*: the analysis is *na-ud-dv-acaṣ-ṭhan*. The *ṣ* in *ṭhan* is due to the substitution of *ṣ* for *s* by the rule *ṣṭuan*.

The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhan* is added after a word ending in the third case, provided it consists of two syllables, when the sense is "he crosses by means of. Thus, *nāvikaḥ* means "one who crosses by boat" (*nāvā tarati*). *Ghaṭikaḥ* means "one who crosses by means of a jar" (*ghaṭena tarati*).
Regarding *bāhukā strī*: because the suffix *uka* follows, the *ṭha* of *ṭhan* is replaced by *ka*; and because it ends in a short vowel (*adanta*), the feminine suffix *ṭāp* is applied.

(1534) *carati* |4|4|8|. It means "he moves" (*gacchati*) or "he eats" (*bhakṣayati*). The sense is that the verbal root *car-* has two meanings, as it is used in the senses of "moving" and "eating. Regarding the form *hāstika*: [it is derived] with the suffix *ṭhan* and the feminine suffix *ikā*.
By the rule "ṭhanas taddhite," there is elision of the suffix *ṭi* (Pāṇini 6.4.143).
[Pāṇini 4.4.9 states: "The suffix *ṣṭhal* is added after *ākarṣa*. This is used in the sense of "one who moves by means of that."
The meaning of *ṣṭhal* is derived from the word *ākārṣa*, which ends in the third case (*tṛtīyānta*).

(1536) *parpādibhyaḥ ṣṭhan* | 4.4.10. From *parpa* and others, the suffix *ṣṭhan* is applied. The analysis is *ṣṭhan*. It is applied after words ending in the third case in the sense of "he moves" (*carati*).

This is the remainder [of the rule]. He states that the designation *ṣit* is for the purpose of [introducing] the suffix *ṅīṣ*: namely, *parpikī*. Regarding *aśvikaḥ*, the meaning is "one who moves about with a horse.
(1537) *śvagaṇāṭ ṭhañ ca* [Pāṇini 4.4.11].
"And [the suffix] ṭhañ after *śvagaṇa*. The phrase "in the scope where *ṭhak* was mentioned" is the ellipsis.
The meaning is that after the word *śvagaṇa*, ending in the third case, the suffixes *ṭhañ* and *ṣṭhan* are applied in the sense of "one who moves with [that].
He will give *śvāgaṇika* as an example; in that case, because the word *śvan* belongs to the *dvāra*-group, there is the augment *aij*.
When [the suffix] *iñ* follows: (1538) *śvāder iñi* | P. 7.3.8.
After words beginning with *śvan*, [the substitution of *u* for *ūṭh* does not take place] when *iñ* follows; the word *na* ("not") is understood from the preceding rule, *na karmavyatihāre*.
The term *aṅgasya* (of the base) is understood [from the previous rule]. The analysis of the compound is: "that whose beginning is the word *śvan*.
The meaning is that when the suffix *iñ* follows, the augment *naij* is added to the base whose prior member is the word *śvan*. For example: *śvāmitriḥ* [is derived] by [the rule] *ata iñ*.
*Śvādaṃṣṭriḥ* [is derived] by [the sense] "the offspring of Śvadaṃṣṭra. Now, [an objection:]...

Only the word *śvan* is recited in the *dvārādi* group, and not the word *śvabhastra*; therefore, since the latter does not belong to the *dvārādi* group, there is no possibility of the substitution of *aij*. To this, he says: "In the rule regarding [substitution] of that which begins with it.
Even though the word *śvan* is included in the *dvārādi* list, it is precisely because of this prohibition [that the substitution does not apply].
The meaning is that the *aṅga* preceded by the word *śvan* is understood to be included in the *dvārādi* group.

The result of this is that the city named Śauvavahāna—which means "belonging to one who carries a dog"—is formed. It should be stated that [the suffix applies] when an *ikāra* vowel (*i*, *ī*, *u*, *ū*) follows.
Now, one might object: "Since the suffix *iñ* does not apply to the word *śvāgaṇika* in the present context, how can this prohibition apply?

To this, he says: "It should be stated that [the suffix applies] when preceded by the letter *i*. The meaning is that, setting aside the rule for *iñ*, it should be stated that [the suffix applies] when preceded by the letter *i*. In the case of *iḍhi*, however, there is the status of being "preceded by *i*" by virtue of its designation (*vyapadeśitva*). [Thus, the suffix applies to] *śvāgaṇika*.

Thus, with the suffix *ṭhañ*, there is vṛddhi of the first vowel; hence *śvagaṇikaḥ*. With the suffix *ṣṭhan*, the form is *śvāgaṇikaḥ*. *Śvagaṇikī* is formed by adding *ṅīp* to the word ending in *ṭhañ* according to the rule *ṭiḍḍhāṇañ...*. *Śvagaṇikī* is formed by adding *ṅīṣ* because the suffix is marked with *ṣ*.
(1539) *padāntasyānyatarasyām* | 7|3|9|. [The final vowel of a word ending in *pad* optionally takes vṛddhi before the suffixes *ṭhak* and *ṭhañ*.]

He states this as a corollary: *padāntasyānyatarasyām*. This sūtra follows immediately after *śvāderiñī*. The analysis of the compound is: "that which has the word *pada* at its end. Thus he says: "of that which ends in the word *pada*, [the substitution of] *aij* optionally [occurs]. Since there is an option regarding the prohibition, [the rule applies].

This is a case of a grammatical option (*vidhivikalpa*). The sense is that [the result] has borne fruit. Regarding the term *śvāpada*: the analysis (*vigraha*) is "that whose foot (*pada*) is like the foot (*pada*) of a dog (*śvan*). The lengthening of the vowel occurs by the rule *śuno dantadaṃṣṭrā-* etc.
Thus we have *śauvāpada*. The suffix *aṇ* is applied by the rule *tasyedam*; however, the suffix *cha* (which would yield *śauvāpada*) is not applied by the rule *vṛddhāc chaḥ*.

They say [the suffix *aṇ* does not apply] because it is not so prescribed. Others, however, state that when there is an absence of lengthening—as in the case of a dog's tail—the suffix *aṇ* is applied.

(1540) Pāṇini 4.4.12: *vetanādibhyo jīvati*. From words beginning with *vetana*, the suffix [is applied] in the sense of "one who lives by. The remainder of the rule is: the suffix *ṭhak* is added after words ending in the third case (*tṛtīyāntebhyaḥ*) in the sense of "he lives by" (*jīvatītyarthe*).

*Vaitanikaḥ*: the meaning is "one who lives by means of wages. *Dhānuṣkaḥ*: the meaning is "one who lives by means of a bow. Because it follows a word ending in *uṣ*, the *ṭha* is replaced by *ka*. The substitution of *ṣ* for *ṭha* is according to the rule "ṭhiṇaḥ ṣaḥ. (1541) Pāṇini 4.4.13: *vasnakrayavikrayāt ṭhan*. The suffix *ṭhan* is added [to the words *vasna*, *kraya*, and *vikraya*] to denote one who lives by that. (1542) Pāṇini 4.4.14: *āyudhād ikaḥ*. The suffix *ika* is added [to the word *āyudha*] to denote one who lives by that. (1543) Pāṇini 4.4.15: *śilpam*. The suffix *ṭhak* is added [after a word denoting an art or craft] to denote one who is skilled therein. (1544) Pāṇini 4.4.16: *mṛdastikan*. The suffix *takan* is added [after the word *mṛd*] to denote something made from that. (1545) Pāṇini 4.4.17: *saṃjñāyāṃ kan*. The suffix *kan* is added [after a word denoting a material] to denote an object made from it when it is a name. (1546) Pāṇini 4.4.18: *kuśalajñātyor ṅīp*. The feminine suffix *ṅīp* is added [after the words *kuśala* and *jñāti*] when they denote a skill or a kinsman. (1547) Pāṇini 4.4.19: *ākrośe 'vanyoḥ*. The suffix *kan* is added [after the words *ava* and *ani*] when used in the sense of abuse. (1548) Pāṇini 4.4.20: *gotracaraṇāc chlāghātyākāratadaveteṣu*. The suffix *kan* is added [after a word denoting a *gotra* or a *caraṇa*] to express praise, censure, or the state of being that. (1549) Pāṇini 4.4.21: *hotrābhyaś chaḥ*. The suffix *cha* is added [after words denoting the names of officiating priests] to denote the office of that priest. (1550) Pāṇini 4.4.22: *brahmaṇas tvaḥ*. The suffix *tva* is added [after the word *brahman*] to denote the office of that priest. (1551) Pāṇini 4.4.23: *ātharvaṇikasyekalopaś ca*. For the word *ātharvaṇika*, the suffix *tva* is added and the syllable *ika* is elided. (1552) Pāṇini 4.4.24: *chandaso yadaṇau*. The suffixes *ya* and *aṇ* are added [after the word *chandas*] to denote what belongs to it. (1553) Pāṇini 4.4.25: *dvyacaś chandasaḥ pragātheṣu*. The suffix *ya* is added [after a word consisting of two syllables denoting a Vedic hymn] to denote the *pragātha* composed from it. (1554) Pāṇini 4.4.26: *vāmadevād yaḍḍyau*. The suffixes *yaṅ* and *ya* are added [after the word *vāmadeva*] to denote what belongs to it. (1555) Pāṇini 4.4.27: *parivṛto rathaḥ*. The suffix *aṇ* is added [after a word denoting the price] to denote a chariot covered with that. (1556) Pāṇini 4.4.28: *paryāhitāliṅgāt krītaḥ*. The suffix *aṇ* is added [after a word denoting the price] to denote something bought with that. (1557) Pāṇini 4.4.29: *tatroddhṛtam amatrebhyaḥ*. The suffix *aṇ* is added [after words denoting vessels] to denote what has been taken out from them. (1558) Pāṇini 4.4.30: *maṇivac ca bhakṣāḥ*. The suffix *aṇ* is added [after words denoting vessels] to denote foodstuffs, and the word *maṇi* is treated as an example. (1559) Pāṇini 4.4.31: *śūlokhādyat*. The suffix *yat* is added [after the words *śūla* and *ukhā*] to denote what has been cooked on or in them. (1560) Pāṇini 4.4.32: *daṇḍavyavasargayoś ca*. The suffix *yat* is added [after the word *śūla*] also to denote punishment or abandonment. (1561) Pāṇini 4.4.33: *kṣetre 'ñ*. The suffix *añ* is added [after the word *śūla*] to denote a field. (1562) Pāṇini 4.4.34: *vibhāṣā havirapūpādibhyaḥ*. The suffix *añ* is optionally added [after words denoting sacrificial offerings and cakes] to denote what has been cooked on or in them. (1563) Pāṇini 4.4.35: *saṃskṛtam*. The suffix *aṇ* is added [after a word denoting a vessel] to denote what has been prepared therein. (1564) Pāṇini 4.4.36: *kulatthakopadhād añ*. The suffix *añ* is added [after a word ending in *kula* or having *ka* as its penultimate letter] to denote what has been prepared therein. (1565) Pāṇini 4.4.37: *odanāsūpamaṇḍasaktuvindutimāṃsaudanāṭ ṭiṭṭhann anyatarasyām*. The suffixes *ṭiṭṭhan* are optionally added [after the words *odana*, *sūpa*, *maṇḍa*, *saktu*, *vindu*, *timāṃsa*, and *audana*] to denote what has been prepared therein. (1566) Pāṇini 4.4.38: *ṭiḍḍhāṇañdvayasajdaghnañmātractayapṭhakṭhañkañkvarapaḥ*. The feminine suffix *ṅīp* is added after words ending in the suffixes *ṭi*, *ḍha*, *añ*, *dvayasa*, *daghnac*, *mātra*, *tayap*, *ṭhak*, *ṭhañ*, *kañ*, and *kvarap*. (1567) Pāṇini 4.4.39: *īkak ca*. The suffix *īkak* is also added [after the words *odana*, *sūpa*, *maṇḍa*, *saktu*, *vindu*, *timāṃsa*, and *audana*] to denote what has been prepared therein. (1568) Pāṇini 4.4

The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhan* occurs after words such as *vasna* ending in the third case when the sense is "he lives by means of. The phrase "for the sake of [applying the suffix to] both the compound and its separated elements" implies that this is based on the [author's] explanatory commentary (*vyākhyāna*).

(1542) *āyudhāc cha ca* |4|4|14|. From the word *āyudha*, when meaning "he lives by means of," the suffix *cha* is applied after a word ending in the third case; that is to say, both *cha* and *ṭhan* may be applied.
(1543) *haratyutsaṅgādibhyaḥ* | 4|4|15|. The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is applied after words such as *utsaṅga* ending in the third case, in the sense of "carries" (*harati*).

(1544) *bhastrādibhyaḥ ṣṭhan* | Pāṇini 4.4.16. The analysis of the sūtra is *bhastrādibhyaḥ* and *ṣṭhan*. The meaning is that the suffix *ṣṭhan* occurs after words such as *bhastṛ* when they are in the third case, in the sense of "carrying. Regarding the mention of its being *ṣit*: the remainder [of the rule] is that the suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied.

(1545) *vibhāṣā vivadhāt* | 4.4.17. Regarding the rule *vibhāṣā vivadhāt*: the remainder [of the sūtra] is that the suffix *ṣṭhan* is applied after a word ending in the third case when the sense is "he carries. (1546) *aṇ kuṭilikāyāḥ* | 4.4.18. [The suffix *aṇ* is applied after the word *kuṭilikā* in the same sense.]

The suffix *aṇ* is applied after the word *kuṭilikā* in the sense of "he carries. This means that the suffix *aṇ* occurs after the word *kuṭilikā* ending in the third case when the meaning is "he carries. A *karmāra* is a blacksmith; [the object referred to is] that which is an instrument for seizing glowing coals, heated iron, and so forth, consisting of a wrought-iron modification belonging to him.
It has the alternative name *sandaṃśa*, which means "the crooked" (*kuṭilikā*).
(1547) Pāṇini 4.4.19: *nirvṛte’kṣadyūtādibhyaḥ*.
[The suffix *aṇ* is applied] after words such as *akṣadyūta* in the sense of "accomplished by" (*nirvṛtam*).
The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is added after words such as *akṣadyūta* when they end in the third case.
(1548) *trermamnityam* | 4.4.20 | "The suffix *man* is always applied after [words ending in] *tri*. This is for the sense of "produced by that," according to the rule *ṭhḍvitaḥ kriḥ*.

The meaning is that after a word ending in a *kṛt* suffix, the suffix *map* must invariably (*nityam*) occur. This is because the inclusion of the word "invariably" (*nitya*) serves to exclude the major optionality (*mahāvikalpa*) prescribed by the rule *samarthānāṃ prathamādvā*. Consequently, it is clear from the *Bhāṣya* that in this sense, there is no usage of a word ending in a *kṛt* suffix without the suffix *map*.

And thus, he demonstrates here the analysis [of the compound] where the constituent words do not stand independently (*asvapadavigraha*): "accomplished by means of *kṛti*. In this analytical sentence (*vigrahavākya*), this word *kṛti* ends in the suffix *ktin*, according to the rule *striyāṃ ktin*.
Regarding *kṛtrimam*: it is derived from the verbal root *ḍukṛñ* (meaning "to make") by the rule *ḍvitaḥ kriḥ*.

The suffix *map* is added after a word ending in a *kṛt* suffix. For example, *pakrimam*. This is a non-elliptical analysis (*asvapadavigraha*): "accomplished by cooking" (*paktyā nirvṛtam*). The suffix *map* is added after the root *pac* (meaning "to cook") which ends in a *kṛt* suffix. It should be stated that the suffix *imac* is applied; the remainder [of the rule] is that this applies after a word ending in the third case when the sense is "accomplished. In this context, the term "always" (*nityam*) does not apply.
Intending to show that [the suffix] is connected [to the sense], he demonstrates the analysis of its own word according to common usage: "produced by cooking" (*pākena nirvṛtam*).
(1549) *Apamitya* and *ayācita* take the suffixes *kak* and *kan* respectively: Pāṇini 4.4.21.

Regarding the forms *apamitya* and *ayācitvā*: [the derivation of] *lyab-anta* is as follows. From the root *dāṇ* (in the sense of "giving")—specifically from its meaning of "exchange" (*vinimaya*)—the suffix *ktvā* is applied by the rule *udīcāṃ māṅo vyatihāre*.

This results in a *gati*-compound, after which the suffix *lyap* is applied. Finally, by the rule *mayater id anyatarasyām*, the vowel *i* is substituted for the *ya* of *maya*. Thus, the form *apamitya* is derived. Similarly, *ayācitvā* is formed from the root *yāc* with the suffix *ktvā* and the subsequent application of *lyap*.

The meaning is that, due to the occurrence of the *tuɡ* augment by the rule *ṭhhrasvasya pitī*, the word *apamitya* is an indeclinable (*avyaya*), as stated by the rule *ktvātosunkasunaḥ*. In the sense of "obtained" (*nirvṛtam*),
the suffix *kak* is applied after the indeclinable *apamitya* ending in the nominative case, and also after the word *yācita* ending in the instrumental case.

The meaning is that [the suffixes] should apply respectively. Regarding the portion *apamitya*, since it is impossible for it to be in the instrumental case (*tṛtīyānta*), and since the word *yācita* is in the nominative (*prathamānta*), the meaning is that the suffix *kan* and [the suffix *ka*] should apply respectively from the instrumental forms. Regarding the portion *apamitya*:
Since it is impossible for [the word] to end in the third case, it is understood that it must end in the first case.
(1550) *saṃsṛṣṭe* |4|4|22|. Regarding *saṃsṛṣṭe*: the meaning is that the suffix *ṭhañ* is added after a word ending in the third case when the sense is "mixed together" (*saṃsṛṣṭam*).

(1551) *cūrṇādiniḥ* |4|4|23|. [The suffix] *ini* is added after *cūrṇa* and others. The remainder [of the rule] is: "after a word ending in the third case, in the sense of 'mixed with' (*saṃsṛṣṭam*)". (1552) *lavaṇālluk* |4|4|24|. [The suffix *ini* is elided (*luk*) after *lavaṇa* in the same sense].
*Lavaṇāt luk*: The remainder [of the rule] is "of that which was prescribed by the preceding sūtra.
(1553) *Mudgād-aṇ*: [The suffix] *aṇ* after *mudga*. The remainder is "after a word ending in the third case, in the sense of 'mixed with that' (*tena saṃsṛṣṭam*)."

*Maudga odanaḥ* means "rice mixed with mung beans. [Pāṇini 4.4.26] *Vyañjanair upasikte*: after words ending in the third case, [the suffix *aṇ* is applied] in the sense of "sprinkled with" (*upasikta*) condiments (*vyañjana*).

The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is applied after words denoting condiments (*vyañjana*). "Sprinkling" (*upaseka*) refers to the softening [of food] by means of pouring. Although the formation would have been established simply by the word "mixed" (*saṃsṛṣṭa*), this sūtra is for the purpose of restriction—namely, that [the suffix is applied] only after words denoting condiments when they mean "sprinkled.
Therefore, it does not apply here: *sthālī saṃsṛṣṭā sūpena* ("a pot mixed with soup").

(1555) *ojaḥ-saha-ambhasā vartate* |4|4|27|. The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is added after the words *ojas*, *sahas*, and *ambhas* when they appear in the third case, provided that the sense is "it operates" (*vartate*) or "it is engaged in" (*vyāpriyate*). For example, *aujasikaḥ* means "one who operates by means of *ojas*, i.e., strength."

"Engages" means he is occupied with battle. "A daring one" (sāhasika) means he is occupied with theft by means of rashness, namely, by accepting the risk of loss of life. "An aquatic one" (āmbhasika) means he is occupied with movement by means of water.

(1556) *tatpratyanupūrvamīṣallomakūlam* |4|4|28|. The rule *tatpratyanupūrva* [is explained as follows]: the word *tad* is an imitation (*anukaraṇa*) of a word ending in the accusative case. The suffix *ṭhak* is applied after words ending in the accusative case preceded by *prati*, *anu*, or *pūrva*, when they are followed by the words *īṣat*, *loma*, or *kūla*, provided that the sense is "behaving toward" (*vartate*).

The meaning is "it may be so. Now, one might ask: since the verb *vartate* ("to exist" or "to proceed") is intransitive in the upcoming analyses such as *pratīpaṃ vartate*, how can there be an accusative case? To this he replies: "because it functions as an adverbial modifier (*kriyāviśeṣaṇatvāt*).
This point has already been established in the section defining the grammatical factors (*kāraka*). [As stated: "Of adverbial modifiers..."

However, in the *Śabdenduśekhara*, it is stated that this [view] is contrary [to the truth], namely that [the word *prati*] ends in *t*. [The derivation is as follows: *Prati* is a *bahuvrīhi* compound meaning "that in which waters (*āpaḥ*) have gone back" (*pratigatāḥ*). The suffix *a* is added as a compound-final element (*samāsānta*) by the rule *ṛkpūrabdhūḥpathāmānakṣe*.
Then, by the rule *dvyantarupasargebhyo'pa īt*, the substitution of *ī* for *ap* occurs. [Similarly, *anūpa* means] "that in which waters have followed" (*anugatāḥ*).
Following that, [we have] *anvīpa*. The substitution of *ū* by *ūT* (as in *ṭhūdanordeśe*) does not apply here, because it is not a location (*adeśatvāt*).
For the words *pratīpa* and *anvīpa* are conventional (*rūḍha*) synonyms for "contrary" and "favorable" respectively;
one should not insist upon their etymological meanings.
(1557) *parimukhaṃ ca* |4|4|29|.
And *parimukham*. From this [word] ending in the second case, the suffix *ṭhak* is applied in the sense of "being there.
Because of the word *ca* ("and"), which serves to include what has not been mentioned, the suffix *ṭhak* is also applied after *paripārśvam*.
Pāripārśvika:
(1558) *prayacchati garhyam* |4|4|30|.
[The word] *garhyam* [is used]. The word *tat*, ending in the accusative case, is understood from the previous rule. *Garhyam*...

The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhac* is applied after a word ending in the accusative case in the sense of "he gives. In the example to be cited later, "dvaiguṇika" (one who deals in double), the word "dviguṇa" refers to the substance intended for the purpose of doubling. Thus, the meaning is: "he gives that [substance] which is for the purpose of doubling; hence, he is a 'dvaiguṇika'."

The meaning is that one lends one's own wealth as a loan so that it may double; the sense is that this is censurable here because it contradicts the Dharmaśāstras, such as the rule: "The interest on a secured loan shall be one-eightieth part [of the principal] month after month."
The substitution of *vārdhuṣi* for *vṛddhi* should be stated [in the rule].

Regarding "from *vṛddhi*": the meaning is that when the suffix *ṭhak* is applied in the sense already expressed by the word *vṛddhi*, the base (*prakṛti*) should be declared as having the substitute *vārdhuṣi*. The meaning is that from the word *vṛddhi* (interest), the suffix *ṭhak* is added in the sense of "one who gives that," resulting in the substitution of *ik* for the final vowel; thus, the base *vṛdh* undergoes the substitution of *vārdhuṣi*. As for the statement "*vṛddhyājīvastu vārdhuṣiḥ*," it is simply an error.

(1559) *kusīda-daśaikādaśāt ṣṭhan-ṣṭhacau* || 4.4.31 || From the words *kusīda* and *daśaikādaśa*, when they signify something censurable (*garhya*), the suffixes *ṣṭhan* and *ṣṭhac* respectively occur after them in the accusative case, in the sense of "he gives" (*prayacchati*). That is to say, "he gives. Now, he shows the worldly analytical sentence (*laukika-vigraha-vākya*):

"he gives ten and eleven. Regarding the phrase "here too": just as in the analytical sentence the creditor (*uttamarṇa*) is indicated as the primary element, so too in the compound, it is the creditor alone [who is the primary].
The meaning is that the word *ṛṇadātṛ* itself is the primary sense of the secondary derivative (*taddhita*).

The meaning is that there is a grasping [of the specific form], but not of words such as *animiṣa* (the blinkless). This point is also established in the *Bhāṣya* on the rule *svaṃ rūpam*. Regarding the term *pākṣika*: it is an example of the word’s own form (*svarūpa*). Regarding *śākunika*:
it is an example of a synonym for "bird" (*pakṣin*). Regarding *māyūrika*: it is an example of a specific type of bird. Likewise...

*Mātsyikaḥ*, *mainikaḥ*, and *śākalikaḥ* are, respectively, examples of the base form (*svarūpa*), its synonym (*paryāya*), and its specific variety (*viśeṣa*). Likewise, *mārgikaḥ*, *hāriṇikaḥ*, and *sāraṅgikaḥ* are, respectively, examples of the base form, its synonym, and its specific variety.

(1565) *mātha-uttarapada-padavy-anupadaṃ dhāvati* | Pāṇini 4.4.37.

(Pāṇini 2.4.31). [The sūtra] "He enters into associations" (4.4.43): from words expressing "association" (*samavāya*) ending in the second case.

"Lālāṭika" means a servant; the meaning is that standing at a distance, he merely gazes at the forehead of his master, but does not engage in any work. (1575) *tasya dharmyam* | 4|4|47 | Regarding *tasya dharmyam*: that which is not departed from dharma is *dharmyam*, meaning that which is fit to be practiced.

(Pāṇini 4.4.50) *avakrayaḥ*. The word "of that" (*tasya*) is understood to carry over. Thus he says: "from [a word] ending in the sixth case."

Thus it is said: because of the marker *ṣ*, the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* is added.

If "that" (*tat*) were not carried over [into the rule], then because the word "object" (*karman*) alone is explicitly mentioned in the nominative case in the sūtra, the suffix would arise from that [word] itself, and not from the word expressing its qualificand (*viśeṣya*), since [the latter]...
Intending to show that [the word *ekānya*] lacks the status of being "first mentioned" (*prathamānirdiṣṭa*), he provides an example: *etamanyadvṛtamasyaikānyikaḥ*.

The intention is that in the compound formed by the rule *taddhitārtha* (Pāṇini 2.1.51), the suffix *ṭhak* is applied after the word *ekānya*. Thus we have *dvaiyanyikaḥ* and *traiyanyikaḥ*; the specific difference here is the augment *aij*.

(1593) *bahvac-pūrvapadāt ṭhac* | 4|4|64 | [The suffix] *ṭhac* [is applied after a compound] having a multi-syllabic prior member. The phrase "when it has been chosen for this as its task/study" (*tad-asya karma-adhyayane vṛtam*) is understood [from the previous rule]. Thus he says: "in the domain previously [mentioned]. An example is *dvādaśānyikaḥ*. This is a compound formed according to the rule *taddhitārtha-* (Pāṇini 2.1.51).
Thus, there is an increase of thirteen [suffixes] beginning with *anya*.
(1594) *hitaṃ bhakṣāḥ* |4|4|65|.
"That which is beneficial" (*hitam*) and "foods" (*bhakṣāḥ*). The phrase "that belongs to him" (*tad asya*) is understood [from the previous rule]. In that context, the genitive case [is used].

The fourth case [is used] because it is conducive to welfare (*hitayogāt*). In the sense of "that which is beneficial for this," the suffix *ṭhak* shall occur after a word ending in the nominative; the meaning is that these are edible items (*bhakṣāḥ*) which are beneficial. This is to be explained in the same way as [the rule] "prepared as food" (*saṃskṛtaṃ bhakṣāḥ*). For example: "eating cake" (*apūpabhakṣaṇam*). By this—

It is indicated that the word *apūpa* is used figuratively (*lākṣaṇika*) in the sense of "eating cake. However, the suffix *ṭhak* is not applied in the sense of "cake is beneficial" (*apūpo hitaḥ*), because of the inherent nature of linguistic usage (*abhidhānasvābhāvya*); this is the intended meaning. (1596) *tadasmai dīyate niyuktam* [Pāṇini 4.4.66].
That [thing] is invariably given to him; in this sense, the suffix *ṭhak* is added to a word ending in the nominative case.
(1597) Pāṇini 4.4.67: *śrāṇāmāṃsaudanāṭṭiṭhan*. [The words] *śrāṇā* and *māṃsa* [are the bases]. "That is invariably given to him"—this rule remains in force. *Śrāṇā* means barley-gruel (*yavāgū*).

"Ṭhyavāgū, uṣṇikā, śrāṇā, vilepī, and taralā are synonyms for gruel," says Amara. The presence of the marker *ṭ* is for the purpose of applying the feminine suffix *ṅīp*. Thus he says: "śrāṇikī. [The mention of the group] "saṅghāta-vigṛhītārtha" means that although the suffix *ṭhak* would have sufficed, a different suffix is prescribed in the case of "audanika" to prevent the initial *vṛddhi* (vowel strengthening).

The suffix *aṇ* is optionally applied after *bhakta* [in the sense of "that which is given to him regularly"]. This is exactly as in the rule: "That which is given to him regularly" (*tadasmai dīyate niyatam*).

(1599) *tatra niyuktaḥ* |4|4|69|. The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is added after a word ending in the locative case (*saptamī*) in the sense of "appointed there" (*tatra niyuktaḥ*). "Appointed" (*niyuktaḥ*) means authorized (*adhikṛtaḥ*), that is to say, one who has been impelled toward such tasks as guarding and so forth. For example: *ākarikaḥ*.

*Ākara* means a source or place of origin for jewels and the like. (1600) *Agārāntāṭ ṭhañ* [Pāṇini 4.4.80]: after a word ending in *agāra*, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied. This applies specifically in the sense of "appointed to that. Because the suffix is marked with *ṇi*, there is vṛddhi substitution for the initial vowel.
Thus he says: "devagārika" (a temple-attendant).

(1601) *adhyāyinyadeśakālāt* | Pāṇini 4.4.71. Regarding the phrase "adhyāyinyadeśakālāt," [the word] "niṣiddha" (prohibited) is understood from the term "adeśakāle" (in an improper place or time), where the negative particle *nañ* signifies prohibition.

The sense is that it "occurs. [The examples] *śmāśānikaḥ* and *cāturdaśikaḥ* are given; the point is that if one were to explain [the rule] as "from what differs in place and time," then this would not apply here. (1602) *kaṭhināntaprastārasaṃsthāneṣu vyavaharati* |4|4|72|.

*kaṭhināntaprastāra*. In this context, the meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is applied after these words—*kaṭhinānta*, *prastāra*, and *saṃsthāna*—when they end in the locative case (*saptamī*). He explains the word *vaṃśakaṭhina*: "bamboo" (*vaṃśāḥ*).
"Transaction" (*vyavaharaṇa*) means appropriate action. He states this with the words: "in which place" (*yasmin deśe*).
The words *prastāra* and *saṃsthāna* are synonyms for the arrangement of parts.
(1603) *nikaṭe vasati* |4|4|73|. Regarding the sense "he dwells near," the meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is added to the word *nikaṭa* ending in the locative case (*saptamī*) in this sense.

Regarding the term *naikaṭika* bhikṣu: the sense is that this suffix *ṭhak* is applied to one who dwells in close proximity (*nikaṭa*), having transgressed the scriptural rule that a bhikṣu must reside within one *krośa* of a village. In this matter, the commentary itself is the authority.

(1604) *āvasathāt ṣṭhal* | Pāṇini 4.4.74. The suffix *ṣṭhal* is added after the word *āvasatha*. The meaning is that *ṣṭhal* is applied to a word ending in the seventh case (*saptamī*) in the sense of "dwelling there. *Āvasatha* means a house. The presence of the marker *ṣ* is for the purpose of [triggering] the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*. Thus he says: *āvasathikī*.

From *ākarṣa*, *parpa* and so forth, from *bhastrā* and so forth, from *kusīda-sūtra*, and from *āvasatha*, *kisara* and so forth—these six [suffixes] ending in *ṣit* belong to the section governed by *ṭhak*.
"From *ākarṣa*" and so forth: this is a verse-commentary (*ślokavārtika*) concerning the rule "before *vahati*, the suffix *ṭhak*" and others.
In order to remove the doubt that "ṭhag" or "ṣṭhag" might mean "cutting," the *Sūtrabhāṣya* reads "ṭhākarṣāt ṣṭhal. In this context, by the word "ākarṣāt," the sūtra "ṭhākarṣāt ṣṭhal" is intended;
and by the phrase "ṭh parpādibhyaḥ," the sūtra "ṭh parpādibhyaḥ ṣṭhan" is intended.

By "sūtraṃ vipakṣitam," the sūtra *bhastrādibhyaḥ ṣṭhan* is intended. By "kusīdasūtrāt," the sūtra *kusīdadaśaikādaśāt ṣṭhanṣṭhacau* is intended. By "āvasathāt," [the sūtra *āvasathāt ṣṭhal* is intended].

By "ṭhāvasathāt ṣṭhal," the rule *ṭhāvasathāt ṣṭhal* is intended. By "kisarādeḥ," the rule *ṭhkisarādibhyaḥ ṣṭhan* is intended. The meaning is that the six suffixes prescribed by these rules under the governing heading *prāgvahateṣṭhak* are termed *ṣit*. Now, [one might ask]:

Regarding the question, "How is it that there are six *ṣit* [roots], given that seven suffixes are obtained from these six sūtras because two suffixes are prescribed in the sūtra *ṭhkusīdaḥ*?"—the author says: "Six," etc.
The intention is that by the word "six" (*ṣaḍ*), the number six intended by the sūtras is what is meant to be expressed.
Thus ends the section on *prāgvahatīya* suffixes in the *Bālamanoramā*.
Now begins the section on the suffix *ṭhañ*.
(1712) [Pāṇini 5.1.72: The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after the words *pārāyaṇa*, *turāyaṇa*, *taṇa*, and *cāndrāyaṇa* when they mean "one who performs" (*vartayati*).

Now, within the section on *taddhita* suffixes beginning with *ṭhañ*, the section on time (*kāla*) is examined—starting from here, it is understood that the suffix *ṭhañ* alone applies. Regarding the meanings of the *ārhīya* group, there are exceptions to the *prāgvatīya-ṭhañ* such as *ṭhak* and others belonging to the *ārhīya* class. Once the meanings of the *ārhīya* group have been examined, [the discussion] proceeds beyond that.
The meaning is that because the suffixes *ṭhak* and others cannot recur [from the previous rule], only the suffix *ṭhañ* belonging to the *prāgvatīya* group recurs. Regarding *pārāyaṇa*:

the meaning is that the suffix *ṭhañ* shall be applied after words such as *pārāyaṇa* ending in the second case, in the sense of "one who performs" (*vartayati*). Thus: "one who performs the *pārāyaṇa*" (*pārāyaṇaṃ vartayati*).

*Pārāyaṇa* means the study of the Veda. The sense is that one who performs or causes that [study] to be performed is a *pārāyaṇika*, as in "a student who completes the *pārāyaṇa*. However, this suffix is not applied when the word *guru* refers to the teacher, because of the lack of conventional usage (*anabhidhāna*); such is the intention. In the case of "a *taurāyaṇika* sacrificer," this refers to the officiating priest (*ṛtvij*).
The meaning is that there is no suffix because it is not so expressed. Regarding "cāndrāyaṇika": *cāndrāyaṇa* is a specific type of ascetic penance (*kṛcchra*).
(1713) *saṃśayamāpannaḥ* (Pāṇini 5.1.73).
"Having fallen into doubt" (*saṃśayamāpannaḥ*). The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhak* is applied after a word ending in the accusative case, such as *saṃśaya*, in this sense.

Here, in the word *āpanna*, the suffix *kta* has the sense of the agent (*kartari*). By virtue of the prefix (*upasarga*), the meaning is "attained as an object"; thus, it refers to an object that has become the subject of doubt. Through that [suffix], by way of inherence (*samavāyena*)...
The sense is that this cognition is not one belonging to a doubter (*saṃdegdhr*) when there is a basis for doubt. However, Amara says:
"One who is *sāṃśayika* is one whose mind is possessed by doubt. (1714) [The suffix *ṭhak*] is added after *yojana* in the sense of "going" (*gacchati*). Pāṇini 5.1.74.
It goes for a *yojana*. The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after the word *yojana* ending in the second case (*dvitīyā*) in the sense of "going.
(1) There is an extension [of this rule] to the cases of "one hundred *krośas*" and "one hundred *yojanas*."

Regarding "krośaśata": the meaning is that there is an addition (*upasaṅkhyāna*) of the suffix *ṭhañ* after these two words ending in the accusative case when the sense is "he goes. Regarding "krośaśatāt": this is the ablative case used with the elision of the suffix *lyap*;
the meaning is "having passed beyond a hundred *krośas*."

(1715) *pathaḥ ṣkan* | 5|1|75 | The analysis of *pathaḥ ṣkan* is *pathaḥ* and *ṣkan*. The meaning is that the suffix *ṣkan* is applied after the word *pathin* ending in the accusative case, in the sense of "one who goes."

(1716) *pantho ṇa nityam* | 5|1|76 | The word *pathaḥ* is understood [from the previous rule], as is the word *gacchati*. The term *nityam* ("always") is connected with *gacchati*; it is intended as part of the meaning of the suffix (*pratyaya-artha*), and not as being connected with the actual formulation of the rule (*vidhāna*).

This is for the purpose of excluding the *Mahāvibhāṣā*. The meaning is that after the word *pathin* ending in the second case, the suffix *ṇa* should always occur in the sense of "one who goes," and there should be the substitution of *panth* for the base. However, in the *Bhāṣya*, the mention of "always" (*nitya*) has been rejected.

(1717) And [the suffix] is added after *uttarapatha* in the sense of "brought by" (5.1.77). That is to say, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after the word *uttarapatha* ending in the third case, in the sense of "brought," and also in the sense of "going."
In the section concerning derived forms (*āhṛta-prakaraṇa*), there is an addition [to the rule] regarding words preceded by *vāri*, *jaṅgala*, *sthala*, and *kāntāra*.

Regarding "preceded by *vāri* and *jaṅgala*": from the word *pathin* when preceded by these—namely *vāri*, *jaṅgala*, *sthala*, and *kāntāra*—the sense is "brought" (*āhṛta*) or "gone" (*gacchati*) by means of that which ends in the third case.

The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied in the sense of "in the matter of. It means "one who goes by way of water" or "that which is brought by way of water. Examples are: *jāṅgalapāthikaḥ*, *sthālapathikaḥ*, and *kāntārapathikaḥ*. (1718) [The suffix *ṭhañ* is applied] after a word denoting time. 5.1.78.
"From time" (*kālāt*). The sense is that this is prior to [the rule concerning] "from here onwards" (*itaḥ prāk*), according to the explanation.

(1719) *tena nivṛtam* | 5|1|79 | "Completed by means of that. The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhañ* shall be applied after a word ending in the third case in the sense of "completed by means of that."
Regarding the term *āhnika*: because of the restrictive rule (*niyama*) "only after *ahan* [the suffix] *ṭhak* or *kha*," there is no elision of the *ṭi* portion.

(1720) *tam adhīṣṭo bhṛto bhūto bhāvī* | 5.1.80. The meaning is that the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied after a word ending in the second case when it signifies one who has been appointed (*adhīṣṭa*), hired (*bhṛta*), past (*bhūta*), or future (*bhāvī*).

"Vyāpārita" means "impelled. "Tādṛśa eva" means "precisely such [a time] as is being pervaded by its own existence. In expressions such as "māsam adhīṣya" (having studied for a month), the accusative case is used according to the rule *kālādhvanor atyantasamyoge*.

(1721) *māsādvayasi yat-khañau* |5|1|81|. Regarding *māsād-vayasi*: here, the word *bhūte* (in the sense of "occurred") is understood to carry over [from the previous rule], according to the explanation.
When the meaning is "occurred" (*bhūta*) following the word *māsa* in the accusative case, the suffixes *yat* and *khañ* are applied if "age" (*vayas*) is implied.
This is the meaning. (1722) *dvigoryap* |5|1|82|.
The term *dvigoḥ* [“after a *dvigu* compound”] is understood [to carry over]. It means that after a *dvigu* compound ending in *māsa*, the suffix *yap* is applied in the sense of “become” (*bhūta*).
The meaning is: "if the age is such that it can be reached [in that time]. (1723) *ṣaṇmāsāṇṇyac ca* |5|1|83|.
Here, because of the word *ca* ("and"), there is an attraction (*anukarṣaṇa*) of the immediately preceding suffix *yap*; thus, only *ṇyat* and *ya* would occur, and not [the others].

"Also *ṭhañ*. But *ṭhañ* is also desired. To this he says: "Even though [the previous suffix] continues," meaning that it continues because it is marked with a svarita accent. If so, for what purpose is the particle *ca*? To this he says: "*caṭṭhañ*" (and by *ca*, *ṭhañ*). Thus, three suffixes are established: *ṇyat*, *yaP*, and *ṭhiñ*.

(1724) *avayasi ṭhaṃśca* | Pāṇini 5.1.84. The meaning is: after the word *ṣaṇmāsa* ending in the accusative case, the suffix *ṭhan* as well as *ṭhañ* may be applied when [the action] occurred at a time that is not yet old age (*avayasi*).

(1725) *samāyāḥ khaḥ* | 5|1|85 | [The suffix] *kha* is added after *samā*. By means of the "frog-leap" (*maṇḍūakapluti*), the entire preceding rule— *"tam adhīṣṭo bhṛto bhūto bhāvī"*— is understood to follow here as well.

The meaning is that the suffix *kha* occurs after the word *samā* ending in the accusative case when used in the senses of "appointed for" (*adhīṣṭa*) and so forth. (1726) *dvigor vā* | 5.1.86 | [The rule] *dvigor vā* means that *kha* is added to *samā* alone; and thus:

The result is that the suffix *kha* (which becomes *īna*) may optionally occur after the word *samānta* ending in the second case (*dvitīyā*), and in the alternative case, the suffix *ṭhañ*. This is established by the rule on gender: "The words *ṭhaka*, *apsu*, *manas*, *samā*, *sikatā*, and *varṣā* are plural. And Amara states: "*Samā*, *hāyana*, and *śarat* are not feminine. [Regarding] *samām*:
From the sūtra "samāṃ vijāyate," there is also the use of the singular number. Regarding the phrase "in five":
this means that [the suffix] occurs in these five cases—namely, *nirvṛtam*, *adhīṣṭaḥ*, *bhṛtaḥ*, *do* (dātavya), and *bhāvī*.
Their connection [to the base word] is according to their respective application. Regarding the term *dvaisamika*: when *kha* is absent, the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied as before.
(1727) *rātryahaḥsaṃvatsarācca* 5.1.87.

[The word] *rātryahaḥ* [is a compound]. "Only after a *dvigu*"—this is the meaning: after a *dvigu* compound ending in *rātri*, *ahan*, or *saṃvatsara*, the suffix *kha* may optionally be applied in the senses beginning with "produced therefrom" (*nirvṛta*).

The suffix *iṭhañ* is applied in the sense of "belonging to a fortnight" (*pakṣe*). Regarding the example *dvirātra* ("lasting two nights"): in senses such as "produced by two nights" (*dvābhyāṃ rātribhyāṃ nirvṛtaḥ*) or "studied for two days" (*dve ahanī adhīṣṭaḥ*), the suffix *kha* is applied to the *dvigu* compound by the rule *taddhitārtha-*. By the rule *ahnasṭakhoḥ*, the *ṭi* (the final vowel and following consonant) is elided.
However, the suffix *kha* is not applied to a *samāhāra-dvigu* (collective *dvigu*), because once the suffix *ac* is added [to form *rātri*], the word *ahan* no longer exists [within the compound].

Regarding the term *dvaiyahnika*: because of the restriction "only after [the word] *ahan* ending in *ṭha* or *kha*," there is no elision of the *ṭi* (the *a* of *ahan*), but rather elision of the *al* (the entire suffix), or the substitution of *ahan*. Then, by the rule "not after *ya* or *va*," the diphthong *ai* (*aic*) is applied. Now, one might object that in the case of *dvyahīna*, once the *dvigu* compound is formed according to the rule "for the sake of a secondary derivative (*taddhita*),"...
By the rule *rātryahaḥsaṃvatsarācca*, the suffix *ṭac* is applied— overriding [the previous rule] due to its subsequent position— and by the rule *rājāhaḥsakhibhyaḥ*,
the substitution *ahn* for *ahan* occurs in accordance with *ahno'hna etebhyaḥ*.
Although the word retains the designation *ahan* by virtue of the *sthānivadbhāva* (treatment as the original) of that substitute, the suffix *ṭac* itself does not possess that designation.

If the suffix *ṭac* were applied by the rule "after *rātri*, *ahan*, and *sakhi*" (*ṭhrātryahaḥsakhibhyaḥ*), and then the substitution of *ahan* for *ahar* were applied by the rule "for *ahar* after these [words]" (*ahno'hna etebhyaḥ*),

then— even though the word would still be called *ahan* by virtue of the *sthānivadbhāva* (the substitute being treated like the original)— the suffix *kha* prescribed by the rule "after *rātri*, *ahan*, and *saṃvatsara*" (*rātryahaḥsaṃvatsarācca*) would not apply, because that [substitution] does not exist in a word ending in *ṭac*. Furthermore, even if the suffix *kha* were applied...
To the objection that [the form] should be *dvyahnīna*, he says: "Because the rule for suffixes added at the end of a compound (*samāsāntavidhi*) is not universal, there is no *ṭac*.

The sense is that since the *ṭac* is absent, there is no substitution of *ahna* [for *ahan*], because that substitution is prescribed only when a compound-final suffix (*samāsānta*) follows. This principle—that "the rule for suffixes added at the end of a compound is not universal"—is stated in the sixth chapter [of Pāṇini’s grammar].

This is clear from the commentary on the sūtra *dvitribhyāṃ pāddanmūrdhasu bahuvrīhau* in the second pāda. Now, he provides an example for a word ending in *saṃvatsara* with the suffix *kha*: *dvisaṃvatsarīṇa*.

(1728) *saṅkhyāyāḥ saṃvatsara-saṅkhyasya ca* | Pāṇini 7.3.15. When the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied, the initial *vṛddhi* would have occurred; however, regarding the rule *saṅkhyāyāḥ saṃvatsara*, this sūtra is situated within the section on initial *vṛddhi* under the governing heading *ṭh-utarapadasya*. [The compound consists of] *saṃvatsara* and a numeral (*saṅkhyā*).
The genitive case [is used] after a collective *dvandva* compound. Regarding the rule "after a numeral, [the suffix *ṭi* is added] to the final member":

this means that the suffix is added to a final member consisting of a word for a year (*saṃvatsara*) that follows a numeral. Now, one might object that the mention of "year" (*saṃvatsara*) here is redundant, since a year is defined by a measure of twelve months.
Since the rule would already be established by "ṭhparimāṇāntasyāsaṃjñāśāṇayoḥ" (Pāṇini 5.1.28), he says: "only [the word] 'parimāṇāntasya' [is intended].
(1729) "varṣālluk ca" (Pāṇini 5.1.88).

"From *varṣa*, there is also elision (*luk*); and optionally, there is elision. This is a supplement to the rule "after [the suffixes] *kha* and *ṭhañ*. The form *dvivarṣīm* is the form when the suffix *kha* is applied.

The form *dvivarṣa* is the form when there is elision (*luk*) of both *kha* and *ṭhañ*. (Pāṇini 7.3.16: "In place of *varṣa*, [there is substitution of *vatsara*], except when it refers to the future."

When the suffix *ṭhañ* is applied, an initial *vṛddhi* would have occurred; however, this rule [Pāṇini 7.3.16] belongs to the section concerning initial *vṛddhi* under the governing heading (*adhikāra*) "of the second member" (*uttarapadasya*). He explains it by completing the ellipsis: "there shall be *vṛddhi* of the second member. This applies to that which will not occur in the future (*abhaviṣyati*).

The phrase "beginning with -ñya" means when that [suffix] follows. This refers to when a taddhita suffix—excluding the one denoting the future tense—is applied to the five meanings beginning with *nirvṛta*, specifically to the four meanings other than that;
that is to say, when such a suffix follows. For example, *dvivārṣikaḥ* ("lasting two years") and *ṭhvyādhiḥ* ("a disease").

The remainder [of the rule applies]. Since the permanent elision (*nityaluk*) will be stated later for the suffix *cit*, one might object: "If this is so, how is there vowel strengthening (*vṛddhi*) of the second member in the case of *dvivārṣikaḥ*—meaning 'one who has been commissioned or hired for two years' to perform work—given that the action is yet to come (*bhaviṣyatvasya*)?"

Anticipating the objection that [the prohibition] would apply because of common understanding, he says: "The prohibition 'it shall not be' does not apply to those [cases] involving a request (*adhyeṣṭa*) or maintenance (*bhṛta*).

Why is this? To this he replies: "For in those cases, it is understood through the power of the word that [the action] occurred in the past. By means of the *kta* suffix in the words for requesting and maintaining, their state as having already come into being (*bhūtatvam*) is understood through the very power of the linguistic expression.
And by means of the *taddhita* suffix, those two are understood as being the objects (*karmībhūta*) of such solicitation (*adhyeṣaṇa*) and maintenance (*bharaṇa*).

However, the connection between these two—characterized by such solicitation and maintenance—and the future performance of the ritual action is understood from the phrase "he will perform the ritual action" (*karma kariṣyati*); thus, that [future action] is not the meaning of the *taddhita* suffix. And so it is.

The meaning is that even in that case, since there is an absence of a secondary derivative (*taddhita*) suffix denoting future time, the vowel lengthening (*vṛddhi*) of the final member (*uttarapada*) would indeed occur. For example, in *dvivārṣiko manuṣyaḥ* ("a two-year-old human"), however, the rule to be stated later— *citavati nityam*— "always [when it denotes] one who possesses a collection"— [prevents this].
