"maithunaṃ nidhuvanaṃ ratam"—thus says Amara. Regarding "bhṛjjanam": because the suffix *kyun* is marked with *k*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule "grahijyā-". By the rule of *jaś*-ness, *s* becomes *d*. By the rule of *ścutva*, *d* becomes *j*.

(240) *kṛpṛvṛjimandinidhāñaḥ kyuḥ* | 240 | *kṛpṛvṛji*: *kṛ* in the sense of scattering; *pṛ* in the sense of protecting and filling; *vṛj* in the sense of avoiding; *mad* in the senses of praising, delighting, intoxication, sleeping, beauty, and motion.

The root *dhā* preceded by *ni* means "to hold" and "to nourish"; the meaning here is that the suffix *kyu* is added to these. Regarding *kiraṇa*: there is the substitution of *i* (itvam), the substitution of *r* for the preceding vowel (*raparatvam*), and the substitution of *ṇ* (ṇatvam). Regarding *pūraṇa*: there is the substitution of *u* according to the rule *udoṣṭhyapūrvasya*. Regarding *nidhanam*: there is the elision of the vowel *ā* according to the rule *āto lopa iṭi ca*. [Thus] *nidhanam*.
"Kulanāśa" [is used] in the sense of "destruction of a family," according to Amara.
(241) *Dhṛṣerdhiṣ ca saṃjñāyām* | 241 | Regarding *dhṛṣerdhiṣ ca saṃjñāyām*: from the root *ñi dhṛṣā* in the sense of "boldness," the suffix *kyu* is applied, and *dhiṣ* is substituted for *dhṛṣ*.

The root *dhā* is replaced by *dhiṣ* [to form the noun *dhiṣaṇa*]. Thus, *dhiṣaṇa*. According to Amarasimha: "Gīṣpati, Dhiṣaṇa, and Guru [are names for Bṛhaspati]. Regarding *dhiṣaṇā*: according to Amarasimha, "Buddhi, manīṣā, and dhiṣaṇā [are synonyms for intellect].
(242) In the sense of the present tense, the suffixes *pṛṣat*, *bṛhat*, *mahat*, and *jagat* are added, and they function like words ending in the present participial suffix *śatṛ*. 242.

The meaning is that the suffix *ati* is added after the roots *pṛṣu* (to sprinkle), *bṛh* (to increase), *maha* (to honor), and *gamlṛ* (to go) when they are in the present tense. Regarding the phrase "and like the *śatṛ* [suffix]": the intention is that because of its being marked with the *u*-sign (*ugit*), the augment *num* is applied. Having raised the objection that the *guṇa* substitution of the light penultimate vowel (*laghūpadhaguṇa*) might apply when the suffix *ati* is added, he says:

Regarding "guṇābhāva" (the absence of *guṇa*): the word "is prescribed as an irregularity" (*nipātyate*) is to be supplied. He says "pṛṣanti" in order to demonstrate the result of the extended application (*atideśa*) of the status of having the suffix *śatṛ*. From the root *gam*, with the suffix *atipratyaya* and the substitution of *jagad*, the form *jagat* arises. But when there is *śatṛ* for the present tense (*laṭ*), as in *mahatī* and so on, [the suffix] *śap* applies by the rule "ācchīnadyoḥ."
Thus, the *num* augment would apply. However, in the case of the *ati* suffix, because it is an *ardhadhātuka*, the *śap* affix does not occur.
(Pāṇini 7.3.243) *saṃścattṛpaddvehat*. [The roots] *ciñ* (to accumulate), *tṛp* (to satisfy/delight), and *han* (to kill/to go)—these.

The meaning is that words ending in *atipratyaya* are treated as irregular (*nipātana*). Now, one might object: "Since this could have been included in the previous rule itself, reading it separately is redundant. To this he says: "The separate mention [is for a specific purpose].
For instance, in the case of *saṃścat*, there is the elision of the vowel *i*; and in the case of *vehat*, there is the substitution of *e* for *it*.
The meaning is: of the vowel *i* which is connected with the word *vi*.
(244) *Chandasy asānac śujṛbhyām* | 244 | [The rule] *chandasya* means: after the roots *śu* (to go) and *jṛṣ* (to decay/age), the suffix *asānac* occurs; this is the meaning.

(245) *ṛñji-vṛdhi-mandi-sahibhyaḥ kit* | The meaning is that the suffix *asānac* shall be added after the roots *ṛji* (to go), *vṛdhu* (to grow), *madī* (to rejoice), and *ṣaha* (to endure), and it shall be marked with the *k*-sign (*kit*).

(246) *arter guṇaḥ śuṭ ca* | 246 | "The root *ṛ* undergoes guṇa; *śuṭ* is the augment. This means that from the root *ṛ* in the sense of "going," the suffix *asānac* is applied, the root undergoes guṇa, and the augment *śuṭ* is added to the suffix.

(247) *samyānac stuvaḥ* | 247 | The suffix *ānac* is applied after the root *stu* (to praise) when preceded by the prefix *sam*. This means that when the prefix *sam* is present, the suffix *ānac* is added to the root *ṣṭuañ* (in the sense of praising). There is *guṇa* substitution and the replacement of *u* with *av*.

(248) *yudhibudhidṛśaḥ kicca* || 248 || [The meaning is: after the roots *yudh* "to fight," *budh* "to awaken/understand," and *dṛś* "to see," the suffix *ānac* is added, and it is *kit*. Thus, *yudhānaḥ*.
(249) *hurcheḥ sano luk cchalopaśca* | [Pāṇini 3.1.53] After the root *hurcch*, following the suffix *san*, there is the suffix *ānac*;
there is the elision (*luk*) of *san*, and the elision (*lopa*) of *ch*. Thus, *juhurāṇa*. This is based on the assumption of *san* by means of the characteristic of the suffix (*pratyayalakṣaṇa*).

Regarding the doubling (*dvitvam*): there is no prohibition by the rule *ṭhna lumatā*, because that rule means that when a suffix is elided (*luptapratyaye*), an operation [prescribed] for that which is designated as an *aṅga* (stem) on account of that suffix does not take place. However, the doubling is not prescribed for that which is designated as an *aṅga* on account of the suffix *san*; rather, it is prescribed for the whole ending in that [suffix].

(250) *śviter daś ca* | [Pāṇini 7.4.34] From the root *śvit* in the sense of "color," after it has taken the suffix *saN*, there is elision (*luk*) of *saN*, and the letter *t* is replaced by *d*. Thus, *śiśvidānaḥ*. As before, there is reduplication. *Śiśvidānaḥ* refers to one who performs meritorious deeds.
"Capala and cikura are synonyms," according to Amara. Regarding the reading "śiśvidāna akṛṣṇakarma" found in some places, its meaning is exactly the same.

(251) [Pāṇini 3.2.136] The suffixes *tṛn* and *tṛc* are applied after the roots *śaṃs*, *kṣad*, and others, when forming a proper name (*saṃjñā*), and they are not marked with the indicatory letter *i* (i.e., they do not take the augment *iṭ*). 251.

The suffixes *tṛn* and *tṛc* are applied after the roots *śaṃs* and *kṣad*. *Śaṃs* means "to praise," and *kṣad* is a root mentioned in the *sūtra* (the *dhātupāṭha*). From these two, *tṛn* and *tṛc* are respectively added; the meaning is that both of these suffixes are *aniṭ* (lacking the augment *iṭ*). Thus, *śaṃstā* is formed with *tṛn*, and *śaṃstarau* is formed with *aptṛn*;
in the rule *aptṛn*, the mention of *naptr* and others serves as a restrictive rule (*niyamārtham*).
"If there is lengthening of the penultimate vowel (*au*) for words ending in *tṛn* or *tṛc* derived from roots such as *sthā*, then it occurs only for *naptr* and others.
Therefore, here [the term] is used according to Amara: "The *prājitṛ*, *yantṛ*, *sūta*, *kṣattṛ*, and *sārathi* [are synonyms].
(252) "In many other cases as well" (Pāṇini 3.1.85).

(253) *naptṛ*, *neṣṭṛ*, *tvaṣṭṛ*, *hotṛ*, *potṛ*, *bhrātṛ*, *mātṛ*, *pitṛ*, *duhitṛ*. || 253 || These [nine] words ending in *tṛn* and *tṛc* suffixes are irregularly formed (*nipātyante*). Regarding the derivation of the word *naptṛ*, he says: "By means of this, they do not fall" (*na pataṃty anena iti*). With the negative particle (*nañ*) as an upapada, from the root *patlṛ*...
In *gātavit* and *asmṛtṛni*, the original form (*prakṛti*) is retained after the negative particle *nañ*, and the elision of the vowel *a* is prescribed as a nipātana.
Regarding *neṣṭā*, he says: "from *nī*"—the suffix is applied to the root *ṇīñ* in the sense of "leading.
Regarding *tvaṣṭā*, he says: "for *tviṣi*, the change of *i* to *a*"—the suffix is applied to the root *tviṣ* in the sense of "shining."
The meaning is that the letter *i* becomes the letter *a*. Regarding "hotā": the suffix is applied to the root *hu*, meaning "to give" or "to eat";
the sense is that there is *guṇa* (vocalization). Regarding "pātā": the suffix is applied to the root *pūñ*, meaning "to purify.
Regarding "bhrātā," he says: [it comes] from *bhrāj*; the suffix is applied to the root *bhrājṛ*, meaning "to shine."

(254) *suñyaserṛn* |254|. [The rule] *sāvaserṛn*: when *asu* in the sense of "throwing" (*kṣepaṇe*) has *sa-* as its upapada, the suffix *ṛn* is applied; this is the meaning. [The form] *svasā*: there is the substitution of *yaṇ*. [The long vowel] by the rule *aptṛn*.
(255) *yateḥ vṛddhiśca* | [Pāṇini 3.1.140] Regarding the rule *yateḥ vṛddhiśca*: from the root *yat* in the sense of "exertion" (*prayatna*), the suffix *ṛn* is applied and there is also *vṛddhi*.
He explains the meaning of the form *yātā* with the words "bhāryāstu" ("wives, however"). This is a glossary (*kośa*).

(256) *nañi ca nandeḥ* | 256 | [The suffix] *ṛn* is applied after the root *nand* when the negative particle *nañ* is the upapada. From the root *ṭu nadi* in the sense of "prosperity," [the suffix *ṛn* is added] when *nañ* is the upapada, as in *na nandati*. The phrase "even though service has been performed" is the remainder [of the commentary]. By this very rule, the *vṛddhi* substitution also occurs when the suffix *ṛn* follows.

Because it does not recur from the previous sūtra. He states another opinion with the word "iha" (here). He provides the authority for this with the verse: "But the husband’s sister is called *nanāndṛ*.
(257) [The suffix] *ṛ* is added after the root *div*. 257.

The term *divṛḥ*: the meaning is that the suffix *ṛ* occurs after the root *div*, which belongs to the class beginning with "playing" (*krīḍādi*). Although *ṛ* was already established [by other rules], this specific rule for *ṛ* is for the purpose of avoiding the *nitsvara* accent. Amara states: "The husband's brother-in-law is called *devṛ* or *devara*."
(258) *nayateḥ ḍicca* | [Pāṇini 5.4.77] The meaning is: from the root *ṇīñ* (in the sense of "leading" or "carrying"), the suffix *ṛt* is applied, and that suffix is also *ḍit*.
The *ḍit* designation serves the purpose of causing the elision (*lopa*) of the final vowel and its following consonant (*ṭi*). Thus, "the five classes of men (*pañcajanāḥ*)" are males (*pumāṃsaḥ*).
"Puruṣāḥ, pūruṣāḥ, naraḥ"—thus says Amara.
(259) *savye sthaś chandasi* | 259.
*savye sthaś chandasi*. [The root] *ṣṭhā* means "to stop" or "to stand"; from this root, with the word *savya* as an upapada...

The suffix is *ṛ*, and its meaning is that it is marked with the *ḍi*-indicator. Regarding the form *savyeṣṭha*, he states "in the rule *ambāmba* etc. to account for the substitution of *ṣ*. [In this case] there is no elision (*aluk*) due to the rule *tatpuruṣe kṛti*. According to Amara: "The driver is called *niyantṛ*, *prājitṛ*, *yantṛ*, *sūta*, *kṣattṛ*, and *sārathi*; and [the two standing at] the left and right are *savyeṣṭha* and *dakṣiṇastha* respectively."

(260) *artisṛdhṛdhamyaśyavitṛbhyo'niḥ* || After the roots *ṛ* (to go), *sṛ* (to go), *dhṛ* (to hold), the root *dham* (a Vedic/sautra root), *am* (to go), *aś* (to eat), *av* (to protect), and *tṛ* (to swim or cross), the suffix *ani* is applied.
This is the meaning. Regarding "araṇi": according to Amarasimha, "araṇi" refers to the two pieces of wood used for kindling by friction (*nirmanthadāruṇi*).

(261) *āṅ śuṣeḥ sinaś chandasi* | 261 | *āṅ śuṣeḥ*: after the prefix *āṅ*, from the root *śuṣ* (meaning "to dry"), following the desiderative suffix (*sannanta*), the suffix *ani* is applied in the Vedic language (*chandas*).

This is the meaning. Regarding the term *āśuśukṣaṇi*: *śuśukṣa* is a desiderative form. Amara states: "He who has red horses, whose friend is Vāyu, who possesses flames—he is *āśuśukṣaṇi*. (262) [The suffix *ini* is applied] after the root *kṛṣ*, and the initial *k* is replaced by *c*. 262.

The suffix *ani* is added after the root *kṛṣ*, and the letter *c* replaces the initial *k*. The meaning is that the suffix *ani* is applied to the root *kṛṣ* (meaning "to scratch" or "to plow"), and the *k* is changed to *c*. Thus, the form *carṣaṇi* is derived; here, the *guṇa* substitution occurs according to the rule "pugantalaghūpadhasya ca. (263) After the root *ad*, the augment *muṭ* is also inserted. 263.

And *ademuṭ* [is formed]. The meaning is that from the root *ada* (in the sense of "eating"), the suffix *ani* is applied, and the augment *muṭ* is added to the suffix. (264) And also from *vṛt*. 264.

And from *vṛt*: the meaning is that the suffix *ani* is added to the root *vṛt* (meaning "to turn" or "to proceed"). Amara states: "A path is called *saraṇi*, *paddhati*, *padyā*, *vartanī*, and *ekapadī*. In the word *vartinī*, the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ* is applied according to the rule *kṛdikārād...*. (265) And from *kṣip*, with *kit*. 265.

*kṣipeḥ kicca* (The suffix *ani* is added after the root *kṣip*, and it is also *kit*). The meaning is that the suffix *ani* is added to the root *kṣip* (in the sense of "impelling"), and it is *kit*. Because it is *kit*, there is no *guṇa* strengthening. [Thus we get] *kṣipaṇiḥ*.
(266) *arci-śuci-hu-sṛpi-cādi-chardibhya isiḥ* (The suffix *isi* is added after the roots *arc*, *śuc*, *hu*, *sṛp*, *cādi*, and *chard*. 266.

*Arci-śuci*: [The suffix *isi* is applied] after the roots *arca* (in the sense of worship), *śuc* (in the sense of grief), *hu* (in the sense of giving and eating), *sṛplṛ* (in the sense of moving), and *cchad* (in the sense of covering, with the causative suffix *ṇic*), as well as *ccharda* (in the sense of vomiting). This is the meaning. Regarding *arcis*: this word ends in a nasal (*sānta*). As Amara states: "The word *arcis* is neuter when it means a flame or luster."
The sense is that [the word] *arca* is derived from the root *arc* with the suffix *ṇic*, and then by applying the suffix *ip* according to the rule *aca ir*, it becomes *arci*; thus it is correct.

Regarding *cchardi*, he states that the suffix *is* is applied after the root *chad* with the suffix *ṇic*, and that the penultimate vowel is shortened, as per the rule *isman*. The analysis of *cchardyatisāra* is: "one who has vomiting (*cchardi*), diarrhea (*atisāra*), and colic (*śūla*)."

(267) *bṛṃhernalopaśca* | [Pāṇini 3.3.105] The meaning is: after the root *bṛh* (in the sense of "growth"), there is the suffix *isi*, and there is also the elision (*lopa*) of the letter *n*. Thus, *barhis*. The form is derived through the substitution of the *guṇa* vowel for the penultimate (*upadhā*).

(268) *dyauter isin ādeś ca jaḥ* | [268] From the root *dyaut*, with the suffix *isin*, there is the substitution of *j* for the initial [radical]. The meaning is that from the root *dyaut* in the sense of "shining," the suffix *isin* is applied, and the letter *d* at the beginning is replaced by the letter *j*.

(269) *vasau ruceḥ saṃjñāyām* | When the word *vasu* is the subordinate term (*upapada*), the suffix *sin* is applied to the root *ruc* (meaning "to shine") in the sense of a proper name (*saṃjñā*). This means that when *vasu* is present as the subordinate term, the suffix *sin* occurs after the root *ruc* in the sense of "shining," provided it denotes a name.
*Vasurociḥ*. (270) *bhuvaḥ kit*.
(270) *bhuvaḥ kit*. From the root *bhū* in the sense of "being," the suffix *isin* is applied, and it is *kit*.
The meaning is "it becomes. Due to the *kit* designation, there is no *guṇa* substitution.
(271) *saho dhaśca*. From the root *ṣaha* (to endure), the suffix *isin* is applied; [there is also] the change of the final [consonant] to *dha*.
The meaning is that there is the letter *dhakāra*. (272) *pibateḥ thuk*:
[The rule] "thuk after the root *pibati*. The meaning is: from the root *pā* (to drink), with the suffix *si*, there is the augment *thuk* added to the root.
The form is *pārthi*.
(273) *janerusiḥ* | 273. *janerusiḥ*: the meaning is that the suffix *usi* is applied to the root *jan*, which signifies "coming into being" (*prādurbhāve*).

(274) *manerdhaśchandasī* | Regarding *manerdhaśchandasī*: the root *manu* means "to perceive"; from this, the suffix *usi* is applied, and the meaning is that the letter *dh* is substituted for the final letter of the root.

(275) *arti-pṛ-ṝ-vapi-yaji-tani-dhani-tapi-bhyo niṣ*. From the roots *ṛ* (to go), *pṛ* (to protect and to fill), *ḍu vap* (to sow seeds), *yaja* (to worship the gods, etc.), *tanu* (to expand), *dhana* (wealth), and *tapa* (to heat/suffer): from these [the suffix *niṣ* is applied].
The meaning is that the suffix *usi* should be applied, and it is *nit*. The status of being *nit* is for the sake of the accent (*svara*).
(276) *eter ṇicca*: from the root *iṇ* (in the sense of "going"), the suffix *usi* is applied, and it is *ṇit*. This means that [the suffix] becomes *ṇit*.
There is *vṛddhi* [substitution] because of the suffix *ṇit*. Thus, *āyuḥ*. (277) *cakṣeḥ śicca*:
from the root *cakṣiṅ*, meaning "to speak clearly," the suffix *usi* is applied, and it is also [treated as] *śit*.

The meaning is that it becomes *śit*. He states the result of its being *śit*: "by virtue of being a *sārvadhātuka* [affix]. It is called *cakṣus* because one perceives form and so forth by means of it.
(278) *Muheḥ kicca* [Pāṇini 3.2.82]. 278.

The suffix *usi* is added to the root *muh*, and it is *kit*. The meaning is that *muh* signifies "bewilderment" (*vaicitye*), and because the suffix is *kit*, there is no *guṇa* substitution. According to Amara, *muhuḥ* means "again and again" (*punaḥ punaḥ*) or "constantly" (*śaśvat*).
(279) The suffix is applied diversely in other cases as well. 279.

(280) *kṛgṛśṛvṛñcatibhyaḥ ṣvarac* || 280 || The meaning is that the suffix *ṣvarac* occurs after the roots *kṛ* (to scatter), *gṛ* (to swallow), *śṛ* (to injure), *vṛñ* (to choose), and *cat* (to beg). The presence of the indicatory letter *ṣ* is for the purpose of applying the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*.

(281) *nau sadeḥ* | 281 | The meaning is that the suffix *svarac* is applied after the root *sadlṛ*, meaning "to settle, to go, or to perish," when preceded by the prefix *ni*. Demonstrating the result of the marker *ṣ* [indicating the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*], he gives the example: *niṣadvarī*.
"Rātriḥ"—
thus ends the second section (pāda) of the Uṇādi-sūtras.
Now begins the third section (pāda).
(282) *cchitvara*, *cchatvara*, *dhīvara*, *pīvaramīvara*, *cīvara*, *tīvara*, *nīvara*, *gahvara*, *kaṭvara*, *saṃyadvara*.
Now begins the third quarter: *cchitvara*, *cchatvara*, *dhīvara*. These end with the suffix *ṣvarac*.

The meaning is that [the forms] are derived through irregular derivation (*nipātana*). He states the irregular derivation itself: "the letter *t* in these two. The root *cchid* means "to split," and *cchad* means "to cover"; from these two, the suffix *ṣvarac* is applied.
By virtue of its connection with that suffix, the substitution of the letter *t* for the final of the root is irregularly prescribed, as is the absence of *guṇa* strengthening. This is the meaning.

According to the *Medinīkośa*: "The word *ṭhcchitvara* [is used] in the sense of cutting (*chedana*), as well as for a rogue (*dhūrta*) and an enemy (*vairin*), in the three genders. Regarding *dhīvara*:
it is correctly formed from the root *ḍu dhāñ* in the sense of "to injure" (*hiṃsā*) by adding the suffix *ṣvarac*. Regarding *cīvaram*:

the meaning is that it is derived from the root *ciñ* in the sense of "accumulation" (*caya*), with the suffix *śnu* as a verbal affix (*vikaraṇa*), and the lengthening of the vowel is prescribed (*nipātyate*) by the addition of the suffix *ṣvarac*.

Regarding *tīvara*: from the root *tāyṛ*, meaning "to honor" or "to observe," the suffix *svarac* is applied; by the rule "the elision of *v* and *y* [occurs]," there is elision of *y*, and the substitution of *ī* is prescribed as a grammatical anomaly (*nipātana*). Alternatively, it is a form derived from the root *tīv* with the same suffix, where by the rule "elision of *v* and *y*," there is elision of *v*. Regarding *nīvara*: from the root *ṇīñ*, meaning "to lead."
From this [root], the form is *svaraci*. Regarding the word *gahvarā*, he says: "from *gāhati*.
The meaning is that it is derived from the root *gāhṛ* in the sense of "agitating" (*viloḍane*). Amara states: "A *gahvara* is a *gaṇḍaśaila*" (a large boulder).
Because of the suffix *ṣit*, the form *gahvarī* is obtained with the feminine suffix *ṅīṣ*. Amara states: "The vast earth is *gahvarī*."
Regarding *kaṭavara*: the suffix is applied to the root *kaṭ* in the sense of "raining" and so forth. Regarding the term *saṃyadvāra*, he says:
"the letter *da* is substituted for [the final of] the root *yam*. (Pāṇini 3.2.172) *iṇ-siñ-jidīRuṣyavibhyo nak*. 283.

The meaning is that the suffix *nak* is applied after these roots: *iṇ* (to go), *ṣiñ* (to bind), *ji* (to conquer), *dīṅ* (to decay), *uṣa* (to burn), and *ava* (to protect). Because the suffix is marked with *k*, there is no *guṇa* substitution. Thus, we have *ina*. According to Amara: "Ina is the sun, the lord, and the king; [also] the possessor of fortune, the treasury of light, the one garlanded with rays, and the lord of the lotuses."
Regarding *jina*: according to Amarasimha, "The conqueror of Māra and the conqueror of the world is a *jina*. Regarding *dīna*:
according to Amarasimha, "One who is destitute, poorly off, wretched, poor, or fallen into misfortune is a *dīna*.
Regarding *ūna*: this is a form derived from the root *av-dhā*. Because the suffix *na* is marked with the *k*-diacritic (*kit*), the substitution *ūṭh* applies by the rule *jvaratvara*.
