Thus he says: "the suffix *ghañ* is used in the sense of the instrument (*karaṇa*). Regarding "citrīkaraṇam" (making variegated): [it refers to those things] by which [objects] are scattered, that is, made variegated (*citrīkriyante*).
The sense is that "by means of this, cloth and so forth [are produced]. "Like a bull" (*gauriva*) is a half-verse from the *Bhāṣya*.

In the word *nīśāra*, there is lengthening according to the rule *upasargasya ghañi*. He establishes the word *śāra* in the sense of "die" (*akṣe*) with the words "pradakṣiṇa... and so on. This is because of the usage of the author of the *Vārttika*, as stated in the second section of the fifth book (*pañcamasya dvitīye*).
This is established in the *Sūtrabhāṣya* [under the rule] "ṭhanupadasarvānnāyānaya" (Pāṇini 5.4.28).

(19) *upasarge ruvaḥ* (Pāṇini 3.3.22). The word "ghañ" is understood as the remainder. The meaning is that the suffix *ghañ* is applied to the root *rudh* when a prefix (*upasarga*) is present as an attendant word (*upapada*).
An exception: (20) *sami yudruvaḥ* |3|3|23|. Regarding *sami yudruvaḥ*:
when the prefix *sam-* is present as an upapada, [the suffix] *ghañ* is applied after the roots *yu*, *dru*, and *du*. This is the meaning.
An exception to *ac* and *ap*.

(21) *śriṇībhuvo’nupasarge* | Pāṇini 3.3.24. The meaning is that when there is no prefix (*upasarga*), the suffix *ghañ* is applied after the roots *śri*, *nī*, and *bhū*. This is an exception to [the application of] *ac* and *ap*.
"By way of frequentative application (*bāhulakāt*)" means by virtue of the inclusion of the term "frequently" (*bahulam*) in the rule *kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam* [Pāṇini 3.3.113].

(22) *vau kṣuśruvaḥ* [Pāṇini 3.3.25]: "In the presence of the prefix *vi*, after the roots *kṣu* and *śru*, [the suffix *ghañ* is applied]. This means that when the prefix *vi* is present as an attendant word (*upapada*), the suffix *ghañ* is applied to the roots *kṣu* and *śru*.
Exception: (23) *ava-udorniyaḥ* | Pāṇini 3.3.26.
The meaning is that the suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *nī* when *ava* and *ut* are the accompanying words (*upapada*).
This is the refutation of the objection. The explanation of the term *unnaya* is "utprekṣā" (poetic fancy).
(24) *Pre drustusruvaḥ* | Pāṇini 3.3.27.
Regarding *pre drustusruvaḥ*: when the prefix *pra-* is used as an upapada, the suffix *ghañ* is applied after the roots *dru*, *stu*, and *sru*. This is the meaning.
An exception to *apa*.
(25) *nirabhyo pūlvoḥ* | Pāṇini 3.3.28. [The meaning is: when *nir* and *abhi* are the governing prepositions (*upapada*), the suffix *ghañ* is applied. This is an exception to [the rule for] *apa*.

(26) *unnyor graḥ* |3|3|29|. The meaning is that the suffix *ghañ* is applied when *ut* and *ni* are used as accompanying words (*upapada*). This is an exception (*apavāda*) to [the previous rule regarding] *ap*.
(27) *kṛḍ dhānye* |3|3|30|. [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *kṛ*] when the sense is "grain" (*dhānya*).
*kṛ* is used in the sense of "grain. *kṛ* here has its fifth case ending elided; thus he says: "from this root *kṛ*.

(28) *yajñe sami stuvaḥ* |3|3|31|. Regarding *yajñe*: because it is a governing term (*prakṛtva*), the word *yajñe* does not undergo [elision]; that is, there is no separation [of the suffix] from *yajñe*.
The meaning is that [the desired form] is established simply by the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the word "beginning with" (*ādi*) from the preceding sūtra.

The meaning is that the suffix *ghañ* is applied to the root *stṛ* when the word *pra* is used as an upapada (governing word). Regarding the term *prastāra*, the ritualists (*yājñikāḥ*) define it as a particular arrangement of bricks.
(29) *prathane vāvaśabde* |3|3|33|. The analysis is: *prathane*, *vā*, *aśabde*. Thus he says: "from [the root] preceded by *vi-*, etc. (30) *cchandonāmni ca* |8|3|94|.
And in the case of the word *cchanda*: after the root *stṛ* preceded by the prefix *vi*, the suffix *ghañ* is applied.

The meaning is that this forms the name for *cchandas*, which consists of a specific arrangement of syllables. This statement is made because the previous rule [Pāṇini 3.3.120] does not apply here, as it pertains to the domain of verbal action (*kriyā*). [The term] *karmadhāraya* refers to the fact that it is both a *viṣṭara* and [that].

The intention is that the analysis of the compound is "paṅktiśca" (and the word *paṅkti*). Now, one might ask: since there is a prohibition by the rule "sātpadādyoḥ" and because the substitute [for the root] lacks the letter *s*, how can there be the substitution of *ṣ* here? To this, he says: "in the name of a Vedic meter (*cchandonāmni*). The subsequent sūtra is: "vṛkṣāsanayor viṣṭaraḥ" (the word *viṣṭara* [is used] for a tree and a seat).
The meaning is that the word *viṣṭara* is irregularly formed (*nipātyate*) when it denotes a name well-known in the Vedas.
(31) *Udi grahaḥ* | Pāṇini 3.3.35. Regarding *udi grahaḥ*: the meaning is that the suffix *ghañ* is applied to the root *grah* when the word *ut* is used as an upapada.
This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *ap*, which will be prescribed [later] by the rule "ṭh-grahi-vṛdṛ-niści-gamaś-ca.
(32) *sami muṣṭau* | 3|3|36|. When *sam* is the upapada, the suffix *ghañ* is applied to the root *grah* when the meaning of the verbal root refers to a fist (*muṣṭi*).

The meaning is "in the case of *gamya*. "The grasping of the wrestler" means a firm grip of the fist. (33) *parinyornīṇodyūtābhreṣayoḥ* |3|3|37|. [The rule applies] after *pari* and *ni*; [the roots] *nī* and *i* [are used] in the sense of gambling (*dyūta*) and non-deviation (*abhreṣa*). That is to say, *nī* in the context of gambling, and *i* in the context of non-deviation.

And the meaning is "from that which exists. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to [the rule for] vowels (*ac*). *Śārān* means dice. The principle here is this: it means proceeding without error. This is an exception to [the rule for] *aj*. *Paryāya* means having reached the proper occasion. (34) *Hastādāne cerasteye* [3.3.40]: [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *ci* when the sense is taking by the hand, provided it is not stealing.]

Regarding *hastādāna* (taking with the hand): when *hastādāna* is intended, the suffix *ghañ* is applied to the root *ci*, but not in the sense of theft (*steya*). Now, having raised the objection that there would be over-extension (*ativyāpti*) in a case such as "he climbs merely to the top of a tree and gathers flowers," he says: "proximity" (*pratyāsatti*). Of the object to be taken...
The meaning is that the substance, such as a flower,

is situated in a position reachable by the hand of a person standing on the ground. Regarding the phrase "by stealing a heap of flowers," the word "he makes" (*karoti*) is to be understood as the ellipsis.

(35) *nivāsacitiśarīropasamādhāneṣvādeśca kaḥ* |3|3|41|. The words *nivāsa*, *cit*, *śarīra*, and *upasamādhāna* [are governed by this rule], and the suffixes *ā* and *ka* [are applied]. The words *kartari* ("in the sense of the agent") and *bhāve* ("in the sense of the action") continue to apply from the previous rules. Others say that *kāśī* means *nikāya* ("an accumulation"). It is derived with the suffix *ghañ* in the sense of location (*adhikaraṇe*), as in "liberation is accumulated here"—thus, *kāśī*.

The meaning is "the dwelling place of one who has attained liberation. Regarding the statement [in the rule] *ṭhcajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ*, since that rule applies only to *ca* and *ja* when they are not separated [by other consonants], the substitution of *ka* is explicitly stated here. As for *ākāyam*:
it is derived from the root *ci* with the suffix *ghañ* in the passive sense (*karmaṇi*), meaning "that which is accumulated. As for *śarīre*: this is intended as an indication of an example.
Regarding the word *samūhe*: this indicates an example for the application of the suffix *ghañ*. [The form] *nicīyate* means "it is piled up" (*rāśīkriyate*);

here, the suffix *ghañ* is used in the sense of the action (*bhāve*). Now, one might object: why not simply state that "after the root *ci*, when preceded by *ni*, the suffix *ka* is applied in the senses of dwelling, piling up (*citi*), body, and piling up (*upasamādhāna*)"? [In that case], the inclusion of the letter *ca* [in the rule]...

Because the meaning [of the letter] *ka* is obtained, he says: "it should be stated that *caḥ* [is used] for *ka*. [The example] is *punaḥpunaḥ*, *rāśi*. Here, after the elision by the rule *ṭhro ri*, there is lengthening by the rule *ḍhralope*. (36) *saṅghe cā'nautarādharye* 3.3.42.

Regarding the rule *saṅghe ca*: this is a supplement to the sūtra *ceḥ ghañ*. The meaning is that the suffix *ghañ* occurs when a "group" (*saṅgha*) is to be expressed, but not when "vertical succession" (*autarādharya*) is intended. "Vertical succession" (*autarādharya*) refers to the state of being higher and lower (*uttarādharayoḥ bhāvaḥ*).
A "group" (*saṅgha*) is a collection of living beings. In this matter, the commentary itself is the authority.
(37) *karmavyatihāre ṇac striyām* |3|3|43|. Regarding *karmavyatihāre*: *karmavyatihāraḥ* means the exchange of actions (*kriyāvinimayaḥ*), that is, mutual performance.

The meaning is that when this [mutual action] is intended, the suffix *ṇac* shall be added to a verbal root if femininity is to be expressed. In this context, [the suffix applies] where there is no agent (*akartari*).
It should be understood that the word "kārake" (in the sense of an agent) does not carry over [from the previous rule], according to the explanation.

*Vyāvakrośī* means one who reviles one another. *Vyāvahāsī* means one who laughs with one another. In both cases, the secondary suffix *añ*—which is applied in the feminine after a word ending in *ṇac*—is used in its own sense (*svārthika*).
The suffix *ṅīp* is applied by the rule *ṭhṭhīḍḍhea*.
(38) The suffix *inuṇ* is used in the sense of *abhividhi* [inclusion]. 3.3.44. Regarding *abhividhi*: it is a connection in its entirety; when that is to be understood, [the suffix is applied].

The meaning is that [the suffix] *inuṇ* occurs in the sense of "sound. By the rule *ṭhaṇ-inuṇ-aḥ*, a *taddhita* suffix *aṇ* is added after a stem ending in *inuṇ* in its own sense (*svārthika*). Regarding "vṛddhi of the first vowel":
the remainder of the rule is *taddhiteṣvacāmādeḥ*. When *sāṃrāvin-a* is thus established...
Fearing the elision of the *ṭi* sound by the rule "ṭhnastaddhite," he recalls the preservation of the original form (*prakṛtibhāva*) with the statement:

"inaṇyanapatye" [Pāṇini 6.4.164]. The phrase "by its very nature" means that gender is dependent upon worldly usage. (39) "The suffix *ghañ* is used after the roots *ava* and *ni* when expressing abuse. [Pāṇini 3.3.45]

"Grāh is used after *ākrośa* and *avanya*. Regarding "after these two," the remainder is "when they are upapadas. This is an exception to the suffix *ap*, which will be prescribed by the rule "grahavṛdṛniścigamaśca. The explanation of the term *avagraha* is "the cutting off of what follows. [This applies to] a compound word such as *purohita*.

The meaning is that *avagraha* refers to reciting [the text] by dividing it, as in "puraḥ-hitam" and so forth. Here, the suffix *ghañ* does not apply because of the prohibition [of its application] after the root *ava-gam*. The explanation of "nigraha" is "the restraint of a thief."

(40) *pre lipsāyām* |3|3|46|. When the prefix *pra-* is used as an upapada, the suffix *ghañ* is applied to the root *grah* in the sense of "desire" (*lipsā*). This is an exception to [the rule for] the suffix *ap* prescribed by the rule *grahavṛdṛniścigamaśca*. Example: *pātrapragrāheṇa carati* ("he goes about with a collection of bowls").
"Bhikṣu" is understood here as "for the sake of obtaining alms. "Elsewhere" means when there is no desire for gain. (41) *parau yajñe* |3|3|47|.

Regarding *parau yajñe*: the meaning is that when the prefix *pari-* is used as an upapada with the root *grah*, the suffix *ghañ* occurs provided that the word is employed in the context of a sacrifice (*yajña*). This is an exception (*apavāda*) to [the rule] "grahavṛdṛ... [which prescribes the suffix *ap*]. An example is *parigraha*. The first enclosure (*parigrāha*) of the sacrificial altar (*vedi*) has been described by means of mantras beginning with "O Vasus, you... (*vasavastvā*); in comparison to that, this is the second.
This is the meaning. Regarding the word *sphyena*: the *sphya* is a specific wooden vessel shaped like a sword.
By means of it, the act of marking all around to appropriate the site for the altar (*vedi*) is called *parigrāha*; this is the meaning.
(42) [The rule] *nau vṛ dhānye* (Pāṇini 3.3.48).

The meaning is that *ghañ* is applied after the root *vṛdh* when *ni* is the preceding prefix; this is an exception to [the rule] *grahavṛdṛ*. Thus we have *nīvārāḥ*. The lengthening [of the vowel] occurs by the rule *upasargasya ghañyamanuṣye*.
*Nivarā kanyā* means "a girl who is to be chosen most excellently. [In this case too,] *ap* is applied by the rule *grahavṛdṛ*. But surely...

Regarding the form *ṭh-pravarā* in the word *kanyā*, how is the suffix *ap* applied? For there is the possibility of the suffix *ktin* in the feminine; indeed, the rule of "optionality when forms are dissimilar" (*vā-sarūpa-vidhi*) does not apply here, because it has been stated that "the suffixes *tha*, *ac*, *ap*, *jha*, *ab*, and *ap* [supersede] *stri*, *khal*, and *naḥ* [respectively], and *stri* [supersedes] *khal* and *naḥ* by way of prohibition. To this, he says: "even in the scope of *ktin*. In that regard:

He cites the usage of the elders as an authority: "as in *pravarā senā* (an excellent army) and *pravarā gauḥ* (an excellent cow). Now, one might object that since the rule states "words ending in *ghañ*, *ac*, and *ap* are masculine," the feminine gender is difficult to establish for a word ending in *ap*; to this he replies: "And thus. This means: on account of the aforementioned usage by the elders. The underlying sense is that gender is dependent upon common worldly usage (*loka-āśrayatvāl liṅgasya*).
(43) *udi śrayati-yauti-pū-druvaḥ* |3|3|49|. The meaning is that the suffix *ghañ* is applied after the roots *śri*, *yu*, *pū*, and *dru* when the word *ud* is used as an upapada.
This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the application of the suffixes *ac* and *ap*.

(44) *vibhāṣā''ṅ-rup-luvoḥ* | Pāṇini 3.3.50. The genitive case (*ṣaṣṭhī*) is used in the sense of the ablative (*pañcamyarthe*). The meaning is that when the prefix *āṅ* is present as an upapada, the suffix *ghañ* is optionally applied after the roots *ru* and *plu*. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the rule for the suffix *ap*.

(45) *ave graho varṣapratibandhe* |3|3|51|. Regarding *ave grahaḥ*: when *ava* is used as an upapada, the suffix *ghañ* may optionally be applied to the root *grah*, provided the meaning is "obstructing rain. In the alternative case, by the rule *grahavṛdṛ*, the suffix *ap* is applied. [The word *devasya* means "of Parjanya" (the rain-god).]

The genitive case is used in the sense of the agent. Thus he says: "having the gods as the agents. Regarding the term *avagraha*, it means the reading of two words that form a compound by separating them. (46) *pre vaṇijām* | Pāṇini 3.3.52.

[The suffix *aṇ*] is used after words meaning "merchants. This is an exception (*apavāda*) to [the rule] *ṭh-grah-vṛ-dṛ*. "Tulāsūtra" means, according to the explanation, the cord of a scale. "Tulā" refers to a balance.
(47) And [the suffix *aṇ* is used] after a word meaning "rope" [to form a name]. 3.3.53.
"And in the sense of 'ray' (*raśmi*). This means that the suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *grah* when the word *upapada* is present, even when "ray" is to be expressed.
The word *ca* ("and") serves to include what has been previously stated.
(48) *vṛṇoteḥ ācchādane* 3.3.54. [The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *vṛ* in the sense of covering.]

The root *vṛ* means "to cover. When the prefix *pra-* is used as an upapada, the suffix *ghañ* may optionally be applied to the root *vṛdh* in the sense of "covering. In the alternative case, the suffix *ap* is applied by the rule *grahavṛdṛ*. Thus we have *prāvāraḥ*, which means "a garment" (*paṭa*). The lengthening of the vowel occurs by the rule *upasargasya ghañi*.

(49) *parau bhuvo 'vajñāne* [Pāṇini 3.3.55]. Regarding *parau bhuvo 'vajñāne*: the meaning is that when the word *pari* is used as a subordinate element (*upapada*), the suffix *ghañ* is applied to the root *bhū* when it functions in the sense of contempt (*avahelana*).

The meaning of *er ac* is that the suffix *ac* occurs after a verbal root ending in an *i*-vowel (*ivarṇa*), in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) or a factor other than the agent (*akartṛ-kāraka*).
This is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *ghañ*. [The mention of] "for the sake of *bhaya* and so forth" means for the establishment of words such as *bhaya*.
The meaning is that there is an extension (*upasaṅkhyāna*) of the suffix *ac* after roots such as *bhī*.
Now, one might object that since the rule *theraj* alone would suffice, the mention of *bhaya* is redundant; to this he replies:

"In order to exclude the suffix *kta* and others. By the word "others" (*ādi*), the inclusion of *lyuṭ* and so forth is intended. Otherwise, because [the suffix *kta*] is subsequent [in the order of rules], it would prevail.

The suffixes *kta* and others should occur. However, the rule regarding dissimilar suffixes (*vāsarūpavidhi*) does not apply here, because there is no status as an exception (*apavāda*); this is the intended meaning.
Regarding the word *varṣam*: here, the suffix *ac*, preceded by *a*, is prescribed, superseding the suffixes *kta*, *lyuṭ*, and so forth, which would otherwise apply to the neuter gender.

(51) *ṛdorap* | Pāṇini 3.3.57. *ṛdorap*: The genitive case here has the sense of the locative. *ṛt* and *u*: in this compound, the masculine gender is used by Vedic convention (*sautra*). The suffix *ap* occurs after verbal roots ending in *ṛ* or *u*, in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*) or a factor other than the agent (*akartari kārake*).
This is the meaning. It is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *ghañ*.
(52) *grahavṛdṛniścigamaśca* |3|3|58|. *grahavṛdṛ*: *graha*, *vṛ*, *dṛ*, *niści*, *gama*—this is a copulative compound (*dvandva*). [The suffix] *ṭhaP* shall be applied.

The remainder [of the rule]. Regarding "after *dha* and *ci*": this is an exception (*apavāda*) to the suffix *ghañ* following the root *ci* preceded by the prefix *ni*; however, the distinction is that for other roots, it is an exception to *ghañ*. Regarding "after *vaś* and *raṇ*" (*vaśiraṇyoḥ*): this is a Vārttika. It is the suffix *ap*, which is an exception to *ghañ*. Regarding *vaś*: from the root *vaś* (meaning "to desire"), the suffix *ap* is applied in the sense of a state (*bhāve*). The meaning is "desire" (*icchā*). Although *vaś*...

The sense is that although *dhātu* is a Vedic (archaic) term, it is nevertheless used in common worldly usage based on such applications as "ṭhvaṣṭi bhāguriḥ. Regarding the word *raṇa*: it is called *raṇa* because they "resound" (*raṇanti*) or make noise therein;
thus it means battle. The rule "the suffix *ka* is prescribed in the sense of *ghañ*" is a Vārttika.
The remainder of the *vārttika*, "for the roots √sthā, √snā, √pā, √vyadh, √han, and √yudh," is recited in the *Bhāṣya*. Regarding *prastha*:

it is called *prastha* because grains (*dhānyāni*) stand firm (*pratiṣṭhante*) in it; there is elision of the vowel *ā* by the rule "āto lopa iṭi ca. Regarding *prasna*: it is called *prasna* because they bathe (*prasnānti*) in it. Regarding *prapibanti asyām*: [it is called *prapā*] because they drink from it.

"Āvidham" means that in which they pierce (āvidhyanti). There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) according to the rule *grahijyāvayivyadhi*. Having treated this as already established, he says: "vighna.

It is called "vighna" because in it minds are struck down (*vihanti*). There is elision of the penultimate vowel (*upadhālopa*) according to the rule *gamahana*, and [the substitution of] *ha* [for *gha*].
In the word *han*, there is the substitution of *k* for *h*. One may also cite *āyudha* as an example, derived from the sense "that by which one fights.
Regarding the phrase "in the section on reduplication": this means "in the section [governed by] *ekāco dve prathamasya*" (Pāṇini 6.1.1), which prescribes reduplication.
Regarding the question "for *kṛñ* and others when followed by the suffix *ka*": when the suffix *ka* follows, the first syllable of the monosyllabic roots such as *kṛñ* is reduplicated.
The meaning is "it exists. Regarding *cakra*: because the rule for *sthā* and *snā* is illustrative (*upalakṣaṇatva*), the suffix *ka* is applied after the root *kṛ*.

The analysis (*vigraha*) is: "that by which the slaughter of enemies is performed. Due to the *kit* designation, there is no *guṇa* substitution. There is doubling (*dvitva*). The operations pertaining to the reduplicated syllable (*abhyāsa*) follow. Regarding *ciklidam*: [the suffix] *ka*, doubling, and so forth. Regarding *caṅkrama*: [the suffix] *ghañ*.
As before.
(53) *upasarge 'daḥ* | Pāṇini 3.3.59. The analysis of the sūtra is *upasarge adaḥ*. The remainder [of the rule] is *ap syāt*. When an upasarga is present as an upapada...
The meaning is that *ap* shall be the suffix after a root that does not end in a verbal stem (*dhātu*). This is an exception (*apavāda*) to *ghan*.
(54) *Ghañapośca* | 2.4.38. From the rule *ghañapośca*, [the word] *adaḥ* is supplied from the rule *ado jagdhir lyapti kiti*, and [the word] *ghaslṛ* is supplied from the rule *luṅsanorghaslṛ*.

The term *ghaslṛ* also continues [from the previous rule]. Thus he says: "of *ad*" (*ader*). Furthermore, he says: "also when the suffix *ap* follows" (*api ca*); the meaning is: "when the suffix *ap* follows. *Vighasa* refers to food remaining after guests have been served. *Ghāsa*: Amara states, "tender grass is *śaṣpa*; *ghāsa* is fodder."
(55) *nau ṇa ca* | Pāṇini 3.3.60.

*nau ṇa ca*: The word *ṇa* here has its nominative case ending elided. Regarding *nighasa*: by the rule *ṭhghañapośca*, there is the substitution of *ghaslṛ* [for the root *ad*] when followed by the suffixes *ṭha*, *ghañ*, or *ap*.

(56) *vyadhajaporanupasarge* |3|3|61|. The genitive case (*vyadhajapoḥ*) is used in the sense of the ablative. The remainder of the rule is that the suffix *ṭhaP* should be applied. The meaning is: the suffix *ap* is added after the roots *vyadh* and *jap*, but not when a prefix (*upasarga*) precedes them. An example is *upajāpaḥ*, meaning "the divulging of counsel."
The meaning is "slander" (*paiśunya*).
(57) *svanahasor vā* | Pāṇini 3.3.62. Regarding *svanahasor vā*: the genitive case is used in the sense of the ablative; the word *ṭhañ* is understood as the remainder. [The roots] *svan* and *has*.
The meaning is "with these two" [roots] preceded by *a*.

(58) *yamaḥ samupaniviṣu ca* |3|3|63|. [The rule states: *yamaḥ samupa-*; *sam*, *upa*, *ni*, and *vi* form a *dvandva* compound. By the word *ca* ("and"), it is understood that the prefix *anupasarga* ("without a prefix") is also included.
It is thus collected [in the rule]. He says this: "And when there is no prefix (*anupasarga*) in these cases.
(59) *nau gadanadapaṭhasvanaḥ* | Pāṇini 3.3.64. *nau gadanada*: *gada*, *nada*, *paṭha*, *svana*—this is a *dvandva* compound. *abvi*... [refers to the rule *abve*].
This is a supplement to the rule. (60) *kvaṇo vīṇāyāṃ ca* |3|3|65|.

[The word] *kvaṇaḥ* [is used] when [the word] *vīṇā* is present; and also when *nau* is present—that is, when *nau* is the governing word (*upapada*), and when it is other than that [i.e., when there is another prefix].

And "in the absence [of a prefix]" means "other than when the object is a lute. Now, one might object: since the meaning "also after a prefix" is obtained by the rule *kvaṇaśca* (Pāṇini 3.3.65), which states that the suffix *ap* follows *kvaṇ* after a prefix, the formation of *vīṇākvaṇaḥ* is already established even without the mention of "lute"; therefore, the inclusion of "lute" is redundant. To this, he says: "The mention of 'lute' is for the sake of including prefixes. This means it is for the sake of including [the word] with a prefix.

(61) *nityaṃ paṇaḥ parimāṇe* |3|3|66|. "Always *paṇaḥ*" [is the rule]; "the suffix *ṭhañ*" is the understood remainder. From the root *paṇ* [meaning] "to deal in trade," the suffix *ap* shall always occur when a specific measure (*parimāṇa*) is to be understood. By the inclusion of the word "always" (*nityam*), the optionality [of the suffix] is excluded.

*Nivṛtam* means "for the purpose of trade"; that is to say, for the purpose of selling. [The word *paṇya*] is derived from the root √*paṇ* with the suffix *ap* in the sense of the object (*karman*), meaning "that which is sold" or "bound for sale," namely a mere handful. The analysis of the compound is *mūlakānāṃ paṇaḥ* ("the sale-price of radishes").
(62) *mada-anupasarge* (Pāṇini 3.3.67).
*mada* when there is no prefix (*anupasarga*). This means that when a prefix is not present as an upapada, the suffix *ap* is applied to the root *mad*.
(63) *pramada-saṃmadau harṣe* [Pāṇini 3.3.68]. *pramada* and *saṃmada*: these two are irregularly formed (*nipātita*) with the suffix *ap* when joy (*harṣa*) is to be understood.

The meaning is as follows: "the intoxication of maidens" (*kanyānāṃ pramadaḥ*) and "the exhilaration of cuckoos" (*kokilānāṃ saṃmadaḥ*) are the examples. Although [the form] would have been established by the rule *samormado harṣe* ("*mada* with *pra* and *sam* means joy"), this specific grammatical derivation (*nipātana*) is for the purpose of establishing the conventional usage (*rūḍhi*). (64) *samudorajaḥ paśuṣu* | Pāṇini 3.3.69.
The suffix *añ* is applied after the roots *sam* and *ud* when used with the object *aja* [in the sense of "born"]. The analysis is *sam-udaḥ ajaḥ*;
that is to say, when these two, *sam* and *ut*, are the governing prepositions (*upapada*).
(65) The suffix *ghañ* is applied after the root *glah* when the object is *akṣa*. 3.3.70.

Regarding the phrase "akṣeṣu glahaḥ" (a stake in dice): since the word *akṣa* is used as an upapada [in the sense of "in dice"], the use of the plural form *akṣeṣu* would otherwise be unjustified; therefore, he says, "by the word *akṣa*. He explains, "it is indicated," because gambling is generally accomplished by means of dice—this is the intended meaning. "Therein" means "in gambling."

Regarding the term *paṇarūpeṇa*: the substance to be given by the defeated party to the winner in a game of chance is called *paṇa*. The word *glaha* is derived from the root *grah* (in the sense of "taking" or "accepting") with the suffix *ap*, following the rule *grahavṛdṛniścigamaśca*; the form *glaha* is thus a conventional derivative (*nipātana*) signifying that which is to be taken as the stake in that activity. This is the meaning.

However, in the case of the root *gṛhū* "to seize," the form *glaha* is read [in the Dhātupāṭha] as "glaha ca. There, the suffix *ap* is prescribed for the root *glah*, superseding the suffix *dhañ*. Thus we have *akṣasya glahaḥ* ("the stake of the die"). The meaning is: that which is to be taken as a wager in a game of dice. Amarasimha states: "In the context of dice, a stake (*paṇa*) is called a *glaha*. Here, it is in the form of a gambling stake.
Intending to show that the word *devana* (gambling) is the object of the action, and not [the act] of gambling itself, he provides the example:

*vyātyukṣīm*. This is from the *Māghakāvya*. Because of the rule *divastadarthasya*, the instrumental case is treated as the accusative, hence the second case ending. *Abhisaraṇaglahām*: *abhisaraṇaṃ*... [is] the stake (*glaha*).

Going for the purpose of secret sexual intercourse—that very act; *glaha* is that which is to be taken as a stake (*paṇa*), and she who possesses such [a stake] is so described; *vyātyukṣīm*—the root *ukṣ* means "to sprinkle"—*vyātyukṣī* is the mutual sprinkling of water. That [is the meaning]. By that [means], it is said: "In the sense of reciprocal action, the suffix *ṇac* is used in the feminine."
From the word *vyatyukṣa*, the secondary suffix *añ* is applied in the sense of the base itself (*svārthe*) by the rule *ṭhacah striyām añ*;

there is vṛddhi of the first vowel; and the feminine suffix *ṅīp* is applied by the rule *ṭiḍḍhāṇañ*. This refers to one who has engaged in the activity after making a formal agreement (*samayabandha*) with a man who won at play, stipulating that his pursuit of her (*abhisaraṇam*) shall be the wager (*paṇa*).

This means they were playing by splashing each other with water. Here, although in this water-game there is no stake consisting of a rendezvous (*abhisaraṇa*), the suffix *ap* still occurs after the root *glah* (to stake), because in the rule the word *akṣa* is intended to signify gambling in general.

The intention is that if only the game of dice were intended here, the root *glah* would not be used. [The question] "What about in the case of dice? means "What about in the case of gambling? [The phrase] "the grasping of a foot" means for the purpose of salutation and so forth. Here, from the root *grah*, the suffix *ap* is applied by the rule *grahavṛdṛ*, but there is no substitution of *l*. However, in the case of *glah*, when the suffix *ghañ* is applied, [there is the substitution of *l*].
[The suffix *ghañ* is applied] after the root *glah* with the sense of "foot" (*pāda*).

(66) [The suffix *ghañ* is applied] after the root *sṛ* with the sense of "procreation" (*prajana*). Regarding "procreation": it means the first conception of a fetus. The prefix *pra-* has the sense of "first. It is born for the first time.
Thus, the suffix *ghañ* is applied in the sense of the abstract action (*bhāve*). The intention is that there is no *vṛddhi* substitution for the penultimate vowel by the rule "ṭhjanivadhyośca.

The result is that the suffix *ap* is added after the root *sṛdh*, which has the meaning of "procreation" (*prajana*). [In the word *prasūti*], the suffix *ghañ* is applied in the sense of the abstract action (*bhāve*) because it is first produced (*prathamaṃ jāyate*).
The intention is that there is no *vṛddhi* substitution for the penultimate vowel by the rule "ṭhjanivadhyośca."

The conclusion is that [the suffix] ap is added to the root *sṛdh* in the sense of *prajana*. How so? The objection is that since the meaning "approaching" (*upasaraṇa*) or "flowing forth" (*prasaraṇa*) is not perceived in *prajana*, the augment *vṛddhi* of the penultimate vowel would occur when the suffix *ghañ* is applied. He provides the resolution: "in the sense of a locus" (*adhikaraṇe*). [That is, it means] "that in which one approaches."

The meaning is that the suffix *gha* is applied by the rule "In the sense of the locus (*adhikaraṇa*-kāraka), in the sense of time, in the masculine, when it is a name, and generally in the sense of 'tendency' (*prāyeṇa*)," for [the word] "it spreads in this.
(67) "There is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the root *hve* when preceded by *ni*, *abhi*, *upa*, and *vi*. (Pāṇini 3.3.72).

"Also *hvā* [is used] when there is *saṃprasāraṇa*. When these four prefixes—*ni*, *abhi*, *upa*, and *vi*—are present as upapadas, the root *hve* (to call) takes the suffix *ap* and undergoes *saṃprasāraṇa*. This is an exception to the suffix *ghañ*. Thus, *nihavaḥ* (calling down). [In this case,] *ap* is applied;
there is *saṃprasāraṇa* of the vowel [of the root], which becomes *u*; this then undergoes the *pūrvarūpa* sandhi, followed by the *guṇa* and *avādeśa* substitutions. Thus, *prahvāyaḥ*."
In the case of the suffix *ghañ*, there is the substitution of *vṛddhi* and *āya*.

*Āiṅ* [is used] when battle is expressed. *Āiṅ* is the *ap*-suffix added to the root *hve* (to call) when it follows the prefix *āṅ*, and there is also vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) when battle is to be expressed.
This is the meaning. (69) *nipānam āhāvaḥ* | Pāṇini 3.3.74.
*nipānam āhāvaḥ*: the word *āhāva* is prescribed as a substitute for *nipāna* when the latter is the meaning to be expressed. This is the sense.
He states the result [of the rule]: "of that preceded by *ā*" (70). *hanaśca vadhaḥ* | 3|3|76|.
[The sūtra reads: *hanaśca vadhaḥ*. The particle *ca* is displaced [from its position]. Thus he says: "and there is the substitute *vadha*. It is udātta on the final syllable.

Thus [it is said]. The intention is that in the Sūtra, the word *vadha* is uttered with an udātta accent on the final syllable. Although the formation is established even by the rule "the suffix *ka* is prescribed in the sense of *ghañ* for the root *vadh* when used independently," this [statement] is nevertheless made in order to specify the condition "when not preceded by a prefix" (*anupasargāt*). In reality, the root *vadh* is independent.

"It does not exist at all," according to the *Śabdenduśekhara*. Regarding the phrase "by the slaying of the Dasyu": this mantra from the *Ṛgveda* is cited here for the purpose of demonstrating the accentuation. Regarding the form *ghāta*: by the rule *hanasta'ciṇṇaloḥ*, there is the substitution of *t* for the root-final *n*; and by the rule *cajoḥ ku ghiṇṇyatoḥ*, there is the substitution of *k* (the *kutva*).

(71) *mūrtau ghanaḥ* |3|3|77|. [The suffix] *ghana* is used in the sense of a solid form (*mūrti*). For example, *abhraghanaḥ*. This means "the hardness of the cloud," because the word *bhāve* ("in the sense of a state") is understood as a governing term (*anuvṛtti*).
[Question: How so? [Answer: Because it is impossible for the hardness of rock salt (*saindhava*) to be construed with the act of bringing (*ānayana*). This is the intended meaning.
He explains with the words "by the word *dharma*.

(72) *antarghana* when the location is expressed [is used] with *antar* as the governing preposition (*upapada*). 3.3.78: *antarghana* when the location is expressed. When a specific location is to be expressed, [the suffix *ghañ* is applied] with *antar* as the governing preposition.

The meaning is that there is the substitution of *ghana* for *han*, and the absence of *ṇatva* due to nipātana [by the rule] "pūrvapadāt saṃjñāyām". (73) *praghaṇaḥ* and *praghāṇaḥ* [denote] a portion of a house. Pāṇini 3.3.79.

"In a portion of the house": by the term "a portion of the house," a specific type of portion of the house is intended, as established by the commentary. Thus he says: "a portion of the door," and so forth. The two *prakoṣṭhas* are long, square-shaped chambers; they are called *alindas* and are suitable for entry.

(74) *uddhano 'tyādhānam* |3|3|80|. The meaning is that when *atyādhāna* (placing upon) is the sense, the word *uddhana* is an irregularly formed (*nipātita*) term derived from the root *han* preceded by the prefix *ud*, with the substitution of *gh* for *h*. Thus, *uddhana* is established.

(75) *apaghana* means a limb (*aṅga*). [Pāṇini 3.3.81] The meaning is that when "limb" is to be expressed, the suffix *ap* is applied after the root *han* preceded by the prefix *apa*; and since the *h* is changed to *gh*, the form *apaghana* is thus established as an irregularity (*nipātana*). It refers to the hand and the foot. Regarding this, the commentary itself is the authority.
"Refuge" (*śaraṇam*). Regarding the term "instrument" (*karaṇe*): the sense is that it is derived from the instrumental case (*karaṇa-vyutpatti*), meaning "that by which something is struck.
(76) *Karaṇe 'yovidruṣu* | Pāṇini 3.3.82. "In the sense of instrument, after the words *ayas*, *vi*, and *dru*. *Drughaṇaḥ*: because it is not a technical name (*asaṃjñātvāt*).
The intention is that there is no substitution of *ṇ* [for *n*] by the rule "ṭh-pūrvapadāt-saṃjñāyām" (Pāṇini 8.4.3). Regarding the view that it is a proper name (*saṃjñā*), he says:
"drughaṇaḥ.
(77) "In the sense of 'stump,' [the suffix] *ka* [is applied]. (Pāṇini 3.3.83).

Regarding *stambe ka*: the word *ka* has its nominative case ending elided (*luptaprathamākam*). Regarding *ap ca pakṣe*: the sense is that because the substitution of *ghan* is understood as being connected specifically with *ap*, [the rule applies]. In *stambaghna*, when the suffix *kap* is present, there is the elision of the penultimate vowel by the rule *gamahana-*. In *stambaghāta*, when the suffix *ghañ* is present, there is the change to a guttural (*kutvam*) by the rule *cajoḥ ku-*.

(78) *parau ghaḥ* | Pāṇini 3.3.84. Regarding *parau ghaḥ*: the sūtra *karaṇe hanaḥ* and *abīti ca* are understood to carry over. Therefore, he says: "after *pari*, [the suffix *ghañ* is applied] to the root *han*."
(79) *pareśca ghāṅkayoḥ* | 8|2|22|.

Regarding *pareśca ghāṅkayoḥ*: the phrase *rephasya lo vā* [is understood]; the portion *ro laḥ* is carried over from *kṛpo ro laḥ*, and the word *vibhāṣā* is carried over from *aci vibhāṣā*. This is the intended meaning.

One might object: "According to the maxim *'In the case of an artificial and a non-artificial [term], the operation applies to the artificial one,' here only the forms *tarap* and *tamap*—which bear the technical designation *gha*—should be understood, and not the word *gha* itself; furthermore, under the rule *'A word's own form [is its meaning],' there is an exclusion (*paryudāsa*) for technical designations (*saṃjñā*). To this, he says: "In this context... (*iha*).
(80) *upaghna* [is used] in the sense of a support (*āśraya*). 3.3.85. The meaning is that when the sense of "support" is to be understood, *upaghna* is prescribed as an irregular form (*nipātana*).
He states the result: "from the prefix *upa*" (*upapūrvāt*). "It is indicated" (*lakṣyate*)—this is the sense, based on the explanatory commentary (*vyākhyāna*).

(81) *saṅghoddhau gaṇapraśaṃsayoḥ* |3|3|86|. Regarding *saṅgha* and *uddha*: the application follows the respective order. The meaning is that *saṅgha* is substituted for [the root] when referring to a group (*gaṇa*), and *uddha* is substituted as an irregular form (*nipātana*) when expressing praise (*praśaṃsā*). This occurs when *sam* and *ut* are the accompanying words (*upapada*).
This means that the suffix *han*, the elision of the *ṭi* portion, and the substitution of *gh* are treated as irregularities (*nipātana*).
Regarding the term *saṃhananam*: its meaning is "conjunction" (*melanam*), due to the influence of the prefix (*upasarga*). Regarding the phrase "of those whose meaning is motion":
the intention is based on the maxim that "all roots whose meaning is motion have the sense of cognition."

(82) *nigho nimitam* |3|3|87|. The meaning is that if the word *nimita* is to be expressed, it is prescribed as the irregular form *nigha*. Here too, the elision of the *ṭi*-portion and the substitution of *gh* for *m* are prescribed as irregularities. He explains the word *nimita*:

"Samantāt," and so forth. The sense is that the indeclinable *niḥ* has the meaning "on all sides" (*samantāt*), because indeclinables have multiple meanings. Regarding "nirviśeṣam": here the indeclinable *ni-* means "without distinction," and the root *han-* means "to know"—this is the intended sense. Regarding "sama-": the two, *āroha* (height) and *pariṇāha* (circumference), are equal; that is, their proportions of height and thickness are identical.
The analysis [of the compound] is *yeṣām iti*.
(83) *ḍvitaḥ kriḥ* | Pāṇini 3.3.88. Regarding *ḍvitaḥ kriḥ*: that which has *ḍu* as its *it* is called *ḍvit*; from such a root, the suffix *kri* shall occur—this is the meaning.

The letter *ka* [in the rule] means "only in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāva*). The point is that only the term *bhāve* continues to apply from the previous rule, and not the phrase *ṭhakartari ca kārake* as well. Regarding the expression "by its own nature": in forms such as *paktramam*, which ends in the suffix *ktri* and signifies "that which has been brought about by cooking" and so forth, [the suffix applies] only in the sense of "cooking" and the like.

The sense is that [the suffix] is seen in usage in the world. *Karmeṇi nityam* (Pāṇini 4.4.20). This is the sūtra in the fourth quarter of the fourth chapter. The analysis of the rule is *map nityam*. The sense is that the word *nirvṛte* is carried over from the previous rule, "nirvṛte 'kṣadyūtādibhyaḥ" (Pāṇini 5.1.97), because it occurs within the section on secondary derivatives (*taddhita*).

Although this has already been explained, it is explained again here for the sake of recollection. Now, one might object that the inclusion of the term *nitya* (always) here is redundant. Nor should it be said that its purpose is to exclude the *mahāvibhāṣā* rule "after a [stem] capable [of forming a compound], two [suffixes] may optionally follow the first"; for in this context, the term *nirvṛta* (formed/completed) continues to apply from the previous rule. And thus:

If one intends to express a completed action (*nirvṛta-artha*), then because the *map* suffix is obligatory after a word ending in the *kṛt* suffix *tr*, even when the periphrastic construction such as "it is cooked" (*paktram asti*) is set aside by forms like *paktra*, it would follow— just as in the case of "cooking exists" (*pākaḥ asti*)— that expressions such as "the cooker exists" (*paktriḥ asti*) or "the cooker will exist" (*paktriḥ bhaviṣyati*) would also result; and that is undesirable.

Since it is desired that a word ending in the suffix *ktri* always have the suffix *map* added to it even when the sense of "accomplished" (*nirvṛta*) is not intended to be expressed, he says: "because of the mention of 'always' (*nitya*).

For the mention of "always" is not for the purpose of excluding the *mahāvibhāṣā* (the general optionality). [As stated in the rule: "After words such as *akṣadyūta*, [the suffix *map* is used] when the sense is 'accomplished'."

Since the rule would have been established by the single sūtra *ktreḥ tu maṭ* alone, the fact that a separate yoga (*pṛthagyoga*) is formulated proves the cessation of the *mahāvibhāṣā*. Thus, by the force of the inclusion of the word "nityam" (always), another yoga is understood as "nityam" [itself]. Consequently, the word "nivṛte" is removed. And so it is.

It is understood that when used in connection with the sense of "being accomplished" (*nirvṛta*), a word ending in the *ktri* suffix must always end in the *map* suffix as well. And thus, it is understood that a word ending in the *ktri* suffix is never employed alone without the *map* suffix; this is clear in the Bhāṣya. This is why [it says] "for this very reason."

Since the suffix *ktri* cannot occur without the suffix *map*, there is no analysis using its own constituent words (*svapadavigraha*) such as "prepared by cooking" (*pāktryā nirvṛtam*); rather, the meaning is that the analysis is not composed of its own words, namely "produced by means of cooking" (*pākena nirvṛtam*). Regarding the form *uptrimam*: because of the *kit* designation [of the root], the rule *vacisvapi-* [applies].
The meaning is that there is *saṃprasāraṇa* (vocalization).
(84) *ṭvito 'thuc* | Pāṇini 3.3.89. *ṭvito 'thuc*: the analysis is *athuc*. The analysis of the compound is *ṭu* is that which has *it* (the marker *ṭu*). [The example is] *śvayathuḥ* (swelling).
The form *ṭhṭua* is derived from the rule *o śvigativṛddhyoḥ*.

(85) Regarding the rule *yajayācayatavicchapraccharakṣo naṅ* [Pāṇini 3.3.90]: after the roots *yaji*, *yāci*, *yati*, *vicchi*, *pracchi*, and *rakṣi*, the suffix *naṅ* is applied. The phrase "when not denoting the agent" (*akartari ca kārake*) and "in the sense of the abstract state" (*bhāve*) are understood to carry over [from previous rules].

Regarding "yācñā": the *ś* of the root *yacch* becomes *ñ* by the rule for *ścutva*. Regarding "viśna": the suffix *naṅ* is added to the root *vicch*; the *cch* is replaced by *ś* by the rule *ṭhcchÂavo'ri*. Similarly, from the root *pracch*, the form is *praśna* with the suffix *naṅ*. Anticipating the objection that there might be vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) by the rule *grahijyā*, he says: "and in the case of *praśna*. [The opponent asks: But if there is no vocalization, how is the status of being a *ṅit* [justified]?
To show that [the objection] is futile, he says: "But this...
(86). *Svapo nan* | Pāṇini 3.3.91. *Svapo nan*. The letter *n* is for the sake of the *nit*-accent.

(87) *upasarge ghoḥ kiḥ* | Pāṇini 3.3.92. When a prefix (*upasarga*) is present, the verbal root *ghu* takes the suffix *ki*. This applies in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) or a non-agentive factor (*akartari kārake*). The fact that it is a *kit* suffix serves the purpose of causing the elision of the long vowel *ā*. Thus, *pradhi* is a form derived from the root *dhā*. It means "that which is placed near" (*upādhīyate*).
The meaning is that one's own inherent property is attributed to another.
(88) *karmaṇy adhikaraṇe ca* | 3|3|93|. Here, "object" (*karman*) is the subordinate word (*upapada*), and "locus" (*adhikaraṇa*) is the meaning, according to the explanation.
Thus he says: "When [the action] is the subordinate element (*upapada*) in relation to the verbal root," and so forth.
(89) *Striyāṃ ktin* |3|3|94|. The suffix *ktin* occurs when feminine gender is intended. This applies prior to the rule *kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam* (Pāṇini 3.3.113).

The term *striyām* (in the feminine) is the governing heading (*adhikāra*). "In the feminine gender" means: in the sense of an action (*bhāva*) qualified by femininity, and in the sense of a factor of action (*kāraka*) other than the agent (*akartari*). This suffix *ktin* is applied after any verbal root (*dhātu*). It is an exception (*apavāda*) to *ghañ*; that is to say, it is an exception to the *ghañ* suffix which will be taught by the rule *halaśca*. And thus, in the case of [an action] qualified by femininity—

Just as with the suffix *ktin* in the case of abstract action (*bhāva*) and so forth, the suffix *ghañ* is understood to denote abstract action and so forth qualified by masculinity. The rule for optional application of dissimilar suffixes (*vāsarūpavidhi*) does not apply here, because of the statement "not in the feminine" (*astriyām*). [Objection:
In that case, why is there no [application of *ghañ*] after words ending in *ik*, *ṛk*, or *ūk* when denoting feminine-qualified action and so forth?

The suffixes *ṭhac* (as in *sthairya*) and *ṭhuran* (as in *sthaulya*) would apply even when the suffix *ktin* is expected, because they are prescribed as specific exceptions (*viśeṣavihita*). Furthermore, since there is no rule for "non-identity of form" (*asarūpavidhi*) regarding feminine nouns, he says:
"But *ajapau*... These two, however, find their scope of application in the sense of abstract state (*bhāva*) and so forth, characterized by masculinity.
The meaning is as follows: regarding "sphāti," there is the elision of *y* by the rule "lopo vyorvali. There is no insertion of *iṭ* by the rule "titutratathasisusarakaseṣu.

Regarding the phrase "due to negligence": the meaning is that the substitution of *sphī* for the root *sphāy* occurs only in the case of the *niṣṭhā* (past participle) suffix, according to the rule "sphāyaḥ sphī niṣṭhāyām. He provides a resolution in some way: "from a form ending in *kta*"; that is, when the suffix *kta* is applied to the root *sphāy*.

The word *sphīta* [is used] in the sense of expansion (*sphībhāve*). *Sphīti* is either the description of that which has expanded or the action [of expanding]. By the rule "he causes that to be done" or "he describes that," the causative suffix (*ṇic*) is applied; then there is the elision of the vowel *a* (*allopaḥ*). Then, by the rule "the suffix *i* after *ac*," the suffix *i* is added in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāve*). The intention is that it may somehow be explained as "one who desires expansion" (*sphītikāma*).

*Śru*, *yaj*, *iṣ*, and *stu* [take the suffix] *kṛtya* in the sense of the instrument (*karaṇa*). This is a Vārttika. The meaning is that the suffix *ktin* is applied after these four roots in the feminine when denoting the instrument. Since the suffixes *ra* (by P. 3.3.57) and *ap* (by P. 3.3.58) would otherwise apply to the roots *śru* and *stu*, and since the suffix *ghañ* (by P. 3.3.121) would apply to *yaj* and *iṣ*, this rule is stated as an exception. [It applies] in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāva*).

Since [the designation of *karana*] would otherwise apply everywhere to any *kāraka* other than the agent (*kartṛ*), the specific mention of the instrument (*karaṇa*) is made. Regarding the word "desire" (*iṣṭi*): there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*) of the root *yaj* according to Pāṇini 6.1.15 (*vacisvapiyajādīnāṃ kiti*). There is the substitution of *ṣ* by the rule beginning with *braśca* (Pāṇini 8.2.36). Regarding the phrase "after those ending in *ṛ* and *lvādi*": this means after roots ending in the vowel *ṛ* and after those belonging to the *lvādi* group. By that [word "tena"].

The meaning is "by means of a word ending in the suffix *niṣṭhā*. Regarding "not [the substitution of] *n*": the intention is that the substitution of *n* (as prescribed by the rule *radābhyāṃ niṣṭhātaḥ*) would otherwise apply because it is the original form (*prakṛti*). Regarding *kīrṇi*: from the root *kṛ*, with the suffix *ktin*, there is the substitution of *ī* for *ṝ*, followed by *rapara* (substitution of *r*), and then the lengthening by the rule *hali ca*. Then there is the substitution of *n* for the *t*, and subsequently the substitution of *ṇ*. In the same way, from the root *gad*— [End of excerpt]

*Gīrṇiḥ*. He provides examples for roots beginning with *lū*, such as *lūniḥ* and so forth. Now, he establishes the shortening of the penultimate vowel (*upadhā-hrasva*) in the word *prahlanni* by stating "in the sense of *hlāda*. This refers to the rule for the shortening of the penultimate vowel in the case of the root *hlād* when followed by the *niṣṭhā* suffixes.

The intention is that by means of a *yogavibhāga* (splitting of a rule), there is sometimes shortening even when the suffix is not *niṣṭhā*. However, this is not seen in the *Bhāṣya*. Now, [the author] reminds us of the substitution of *u* for the vowel *a* in *ktin* after the roots *car* and *phal*, stating "ti ca.
This subsequent sūtra, "caraphaloścaṭa" and "utparasyātaḥ," applies when a suffix beginning with *t* follows.

It has been explained in the section on *yaṅluk* that when a suffix follows, the letter *u* replaces the vowel *a* of the roots *car* and *phal*. Thus, *cūrtiḥ*: from *car* with the suffix *ktin*, the *a* becomes *u*, and by the rule *hali ca*, there is lengthening.
*Phultiriti*: this form arises from *phal* with the suffix *ktin* after the *a* has become *u*; because it does not end in the letter *r*, [the rule *hali ca* does not apply].

The word *dīrghaḥ* [is used]. In both cases, by the rule *titutratatha-sisusarakaseṣu ca*, the augment *iṭ* is prohibited. [The suffix] *kvip* is applied after roots such as *sampad*. [Regarding] the Vārttika: the remainder [of the rule] is "in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) and when not denoting an agent (*akartari*), provided it is feminine. Now, one might object:

since there is no application of the rule for non-identical suffixes (*vā'sarūpa-vidhi*) due to the prohibition "not in the feminine" (*astriyām*), how can this [suffix] *kvip* [be applied] in place of *ktin*?
To the question, "How is it that there is the attainment [of the result] despite the obstruction? he says: "The suffix *ktin* is also desired.
They say that this is established by the inclusion of the term *bahulam* (variously) in the rule *kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam*; however, this is not seen in the Bhāṣya.

(90) *sthāgāpāco bhāve* ||3|3|95|| The meaning is that *ktin* should be applied after the roots *sthā*, *gā*, and *pā*. However, *kvip* is not carried over because it is not marked with the *svarita* accent. Regarding *aṅ*: this refers to [the suffix] to be mentioned later in the rule *sthādibhyaḥ* and *ātaścopasarge*; but for the root *pac*, [the suffix is *a*].

The meaning is that this is an exception (*apavāda*) to the *aṅ* suffix prescribed by the rule "after roots beginning with *ṣṭhiv*, *bhram*, etc. [Pāṇini 3.3.49]. Regarding the forms *prasthitiḥ* and so on: the substitution of *i* for the vowel is applied by the rule "for the vowels of *dyati*, *syati*, *māti*, and *sthā*" [Pāṇini 6.1.45], and the substitution of *ī* is applied by the rule "for the vowels of *ghu*, *mā*, *sthā*, *gā*, and *pā*" [Pāṇini 6.4.66]. As for the question "How?", [it is answered]: by the suffix *ktin* in the rule "for *sthā* and *gā*" [Pāṇini 3.3.94], and by the rule "also after a root ending in long *ā* when preceded by a prefix" [Pāṇini 3.3.106].
The meaning is that [the rule] will be superseded by the *aṅ* suffix which is about to be mentioned. He provides the solution with the words "In the case of a fixed rule," and so forth.

Regarding *ūti* and *yūti*: the meaning is that these are irregularly formed (*nipātita*) feminine nouns ending in the suffix *ktin*. Regarding *ūṭh*: the meaning is [the substitution of] *ū* for the vowels *a* and *v*. Now, one might object: since this is already established by the rule "the suffix *ktil* occurs in the feminine," [why the need for this?]
To the question, "For what purpose is this inclusion of *ūti*? he says: "For the sake of accent" (*svarārtham*). To the question, "What is the accent?

he says: "The acute" (*udātta iti*). The mention of "acute" from the previous rule—"In a mantra, [the words] *vṛṣa*, *iṣa*, *pacamana*, *vidabhū*, *vīra*, and *ūti* are acute"—is carried over here, having been modified into the singular number.

This is the meaning. And thus, the acute accent (*udātta*) for the suffix *ktin* is obtained. Otherwise, by the rule "the first syllable of a root is always acute" (*ñnityādir nityam*), the acute accent would belong to the base (*prakṛti*). This is the meaning. "Of these two" means of the roots *yudh* and *jugh*. "Of *syati*" means from the root *ṣo* in the sense of "concluding an action."

The meaning is that the form is *sāti* with the suffix *ktin*. [In this context,] by the rule "ādeca upadeśe 'śiti," there is the substitution of *ā* for the final vowel. Regarding this, having raised the objection that the substitution of *it* (as prescribed by the rule "dyatisyatimāsthāmiti kitī") might apply, he says: "here there is an absence of *it*.
Alternatively, he says "or from the root *san*" to indicate that *sāti* is an irregularly formed word (*nipātana*) derived from the root *san*. Or [it is derived] from *san*.

The meaning is that once the substitution of *ā* for *i* has been applied by the rule "ṭhjanasana," the form *sātī* is established through this specific grammatical exception (*nipātana*). Here, since the substitution of *i* (by the rule "dyatisyatī") is not applicable, its absence is not what is being prescribed as an exception; thus, there is brevity (*lāghava*), which is the intended sense.
Now, one might ask: since the form *sātī* is already established for the feminine of the root *san* by adding the suffix *ktin*, for what purpose is it mentioned here?

Regarding the statement "sāti is a nipātana," he says: "for the sake of the accent. This means that because the term *udātta* (acute) is understood from the preceding rule *mantre vṛṣa-* and is carried over here, the acute accent of the suffix *ktin* is established; otherwise, the acute accent would belong to the base (*prakṛti*). Regarding *hanter*: [this refers to] the substitution of *na* for the *n* of *han* when followed by *ktin*.
The form *hetu* arises from the substitution of *it* by irregular derivation (*nipātana*) and the application of *ād-guṇa*. Regarding *hinoteḥ*:

the meaning is that although there is a prohibition by the rule *kṅiti ca*, the form is established through irregular derivation (*nipātana*) after applying *guṇa* to the root *hi* with the suffix *ktin*. Regarding *kīrti*: [this is derived] from the root *kṛt* in the sense of "proclaiming" (*saṃśabdana*).

From a root ending in the causative suffix *ṇic* used in its own sense (*svārthika*), the suffix *ktin* is applied by way of exception to the suffix *yuc* [prescribed by Pāṇini 3.3.107] according to the rule "ṭhṇyāsaśrantho yuj"; furthermore, that [suffix *ktin*] is acute-accented (*udātta*).
(91) The suffix *kyap* is applied after the roots *vaj* and *yaj* in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*). (Pāṇini 3.3.98).

Regarding *vajrayajoḥ*: the genitive case (*ṣaṣṭhī*) is used in the sense of the ablative (*pañcamyarthe*). It applies specifically in the feminine (*striyām*). *Vrajyā*: from the root *vraj* (meaning "to go") with the suffix *kyap*. *Vṛjyā*:

if the reading is *vṛjayajoḥ*, then it is derived from *vṛjī* (meaning "to avoid" or "to exclude") with the suffix *kyap*. *Ijyā*: [derived from *yaj*] with *saṃprasāraṇa* (vowel substitution) according to the rule *vacisvapi-*.

(92) *saṃjñāyāṃ samaja-niṣada-nipata-mana-vida-ṣuñ-śīṅ-bhṛñ-iṇaḥ* |3|3|99|. Regarding the term *saṃjñāyām*: from the compound formed by the collective grouping (*samāhāra-dvandva*) of these nine roots—*samaja*, *niṣada*, *nipata*, *mana*, *vida*, *ṣuñ*, *śīṅ*, *bhṛñ*, and *iṇ*—the fifth case ending [is applied].

Since the rule *ṭhājervyaghañapoḥ* would have applied [to the form *samajyā*], he says: *ajeḥ kyapi*. "They gather" (*samajanti*) means they become a multitude (*saṅghībhavanti*). "Assembly" (*samajyā*): the suffix *kyap* is added to the root *aj* preceded by the prefix *sam*. Amara states: "A *samajyā*, however, is a court (*sabhā*) or a social gathering (*goṣṭhī*). "Sitting down" (*niṣadyā*): the suffix *kyap* is added to the root *sad* preceded by the prefix *ni*.

The substitution of *ṣ* [for *s*] is by the rule "ṣadiraprate. Amara states: "āpaṇa, however, means a shop (niṣadyā). Regarding "nipatya": the suffix *kyap* is added to the root *pat* preceded by the prefix *ni*. Regarding "picchilā": the meaning is that the ground is uneven (having depressions and elevations). Regarding "galā": Amara states: "the nape of the neck (manyā) is the vessel behind the head. Regarding "vidyā":...

The meaning is "the Vedas, the Śāstras, and so forth. Regarding *sutyā*: it refers to the Soma sacrifice (*somejyā*); [it is derived from] the root *ṣuñ* with the suffix *kyap* and the augment *tuk*. Regarding *āśibikā*: the lexicon (*kośa*) for this should be sought. (93) *kṛñaḥ śa ca* | Pāṇini 3.3.100.

Regarding the rule *kṛñaḥ śa ca*: because of the word "ca" (and), *kyap* is also understood; the phrase "*ṭhśe*" has its nominative case elided. Thus, the implied meaning is that after the root *kṛ*, there shall be the suffix *śa* as well as *kyap*. This being the case, the form *kṛtiḥ* would not be possible through the suffix *ktin*, because there is no application of the rule for dissimilar suffixes (*vā'sarūpa*) when a feminine suffix is involved. To this, he says: "There is a division of the yoga (*yogavibhāga*) after *kṛñaḥ*."

In this context, considering the word *kyap* to be carried over [from the previous rule], he says: "The suffix *kyap* shall occur. Regarding the term *kṛtya*: there is the augment *tuk* after the root *kṛ* when *kyap* follows. The phrase *śa ca* constitutes the second section [of this rule]. The intention is that the suffix *ktin* is mentioned with the particle *ca* ("and"), because *kyap* is already established by the preceding section alone. Regarding the form *kriyā*: the suffix *śa* is applied to the root *kṛ*, according to the rule *riṅ śayagliṅkṣu*.

Thus, because [the suffix] *riṅ* is long and is a *sārvadhātuka*, there is no *guṇa* due to its being marked with *ṅ*; the intention is that it becomes *iyaṅ*. (94) *icchā* | 3|3|101|. [The suffix] *śa* is used in the sense of the abstract state (*bhāve*), but not in the sense of an agent other than the subject (*akartari kārake*).

This is the meaning; the intention is that [the suffix] is applied by virtue of the power of the *nipātana* (irregular formation). And "the absence of *ya*"—the intention is that otherwise, because it would be a *sārvadhātuka* suffix due to its being marked with *ś*, the suffix *yak* would apply. "Paricaryā"—here, from the root *car* preceded by *pari*, the suffix *śa* is applied for the abstract sense (*bhāve*), as well as *yak*. "Parisaryā."

From the root *sṛ* preceded by *pari*, there is the suffix *śa* and also *yak*. Here, because the suffix *śap* is marked with *śit*, it is treated as a *sārvadhātuka*; consequently, one might suspect that the prohibition of *guṇa* applies due to its being *ṅit*. Anticipating this, he says: "In this case, even *guṇa* [occurs]. The word "is irregularly formed" (*nipātyate*) is to be supplied as the remainder. Furthermore, the rule of *halādiśeṣa* (the retention of the first consonant) does not apply here, because...

They say [this is so] because it has as its object the duality of the sixth [case]. However, from the root *yaṅ* (the intensive), the suffix *a*—which will be mentioned later as "after [a root ending in] *yaṅ*, the suffix *a*"—is applied. In that case, it should be understood that after the elision of the *at* (of the suffix) and the elision of the *yal* (of the *yaṅ*), the form is *aṭāṭā*.
Regarding the rule "or *a* for *jāgarti*," the remainder [of the sūtra] is "it should be stated [that this applies] in the sense of an abstract action (*bhāva*)."
He provides an example with the suffix *ap*: *jāgarā*. The *guṇa* substitution is conditioned by the *ārddhadhātuka* nature [of the suffix].

He provides an example with the suffix *śa*: *jāgaryā*. Because it has the marker *ś*, it is a *sārvadhātuka* suffix, and thus there is *yak*; furthermore, there is *guṇa* by the rule "there is *guṇa* for *jāgr* except before *vi*, *ciṇ*, and *ṅt*" (*jāgro'viciṇṇalṅtsu*).

(95) *a-pratyayāt* |3|3|102|. *a-pratyayāt*: the word *ṭha* has its nominative case ending elided. It applies to the sense of abstract action (*bhāva*) and to a factor other than the agent (*akartṛ-kāraka*).

(96) *gurośca halaḥ* |3|3|103|. The word *dhātoḥ* (of a root), which is understood from the previous rule, is qualified by *hal* (consonant). This is a *tadantavidhi* (a rule concerning that which ends with it). Since it is impossible for a root ending in a consonant to possess the quality of being "heavy" (*guru*), the term "possessing a heavy [vowel]" (*gurumān*) is indicated. Thus he says: *gurumataḥ*.

Thus [it is stated]: "In the sense of a state (bhāva) and when not denoting the agent (akartari) among the kārakas. Regarding the term *niṣṭhāyām*: the meaning is that the suffix *ap* occurs after a root ending in a consonant (*halanta*) that is heavy (*gurumata*) and which takes the augment *iṭ* (*seṭ*) when followed by a *niṣṭhā* suffix. Regarding the word *āpti*: because the root *āp* does not take the augment *iṭ* when followed by a *niṣṭhā* suffix, this suffix *ap* does not apply here.

But the sense is that it occurs only in the feminine (*ktin*). Regarding the word *dīptīḥ*, having raised the doubt concerning the augment *iṭ*, he says: *titutreti*. [The meaning is: in the rule *titutratathasisu* (Pāṇini 7.2.9), it should be stated that "the prohibition applies to *agrah* and others. [Thus we have] *nigṛhītiḥ*; if *iṭ* were present, there would be lengthening by the rule *graho'liṭi* (Pāṇini 6.1.16).
In the rule *ṭhgrahijyē*, there is vocalization (*saṃprasāraṇa*). The words *nigṛhītiḥ*, *upasnihitiḥ*, *nikucitiḥ*, and *nipaṭhitiriti*—beginning with *grah*—are established in the Bhāṣya.
(97) [The suffix] *aṅ* is applied after roots ending in *ṣit* and those beginning with *bhid*. (Pāṇini 3.3.104).

From the roots *ṣid* and those beginning with *bhid*, the suffix *aṅ* is applied; this applies to the abstract state (*bhāva*) and to a factor other than the agent (*akartari kārake*). Regarding *jarā*: by setting aside the prohibition of *guṇa* that would otherwise be required by the marker *ṅ*, the *guṇa* substitution is applied according to the rule *ṛdṛśo’ṅi*. Regarding *vidāraṇa*: this is also a *vārtika*. *Vidāraṇa* means splitting upwards.
Regarding that same meaning, "bhidā" ends in the suffix *aṅ*; this is the sense. [The statement] "cchidā means splitting (*dvaidhīkaraṇa*)": this too is a Vārttika.

The meaning is that the form ending in *aṅ*, namely "cchidā," applies only to the state of being split (*dvaidhībhāva*), whether it occurs horizontally or not. The explanation of "cchiti" is: "cchiti means a hole (*cchidra*)."
*bhid* in the sense of splitting; *chid* in the sense of dividing into two; *vid* in the sense of knowing; *kṣip* in the sense of impelling;

*guh* in the sense of concealing; *ḍudhāñ* in the sense of supporting and nourishing; *mithṛ* and *methṛ* in the senses of harming and sprinkling; *ṛ* in the sense of going; *hṛñ* in the sense of taking away; *kṣi* in the sense of destruction, and *kṣi* in the senses of dwelling and going.

The roots *tṛ* (in the sense of floating and crossing), *dhṛ* (in the sense of holding), *likh* (in the sense of arranging letters), *cud* (in the sense of impelling), *pīḍ* (in the sense of plunging), *vap* (with the prefix *ṭu-*, in the sense of sowing seeds), *kṛ* (in the sense of scattering), *vas* (in the sense of dwelling), *mṛj* (in the sense of purification), and *kṛp* (in the sense of compassion) belong to the *bhidādi* group. [The root] *guh*.

Regarding the rule *giryoṣadhyoriti*: this is a Vārtika. Regarding the form *gūḍhiḥ*: when the suffix *ktin* is applied, there is the substitution of *ḍha* for *ha*, *dha* for *da*, *ṣṭu* for *ṣṭa*, the elision of *ḍha*, and the lengthening of the vowel. [The examples are] *ārā*, *hārā*, *kārā*, *tārā*, *dhārā*. Regarding the word *atra*:
from the roots *ṛ*, *hṛ*, *kṛ*, *tṛ*, and *dhṛ*, by the rule *ṛdṛśo’ṅ guṇī*, the suffix *aṅ* is applied and the *guṇa* substitution occurs.

The meaning is that there is lengthening of the vowel due to the *upadhā* (penultimate). Regarding the statement "ārā means a knife," this is a *vārttika*. The meaning is that *śastrī* refers to a goad (*pratoda*), and it is precisely in that sense that the form *ārā* ending in the suffix *aṅ* is used. Now, one might object: since the root is *ṛ*, the form *ṛtiḥ* derived from the suffix *ktin* would be appropriate, not *ārtiḥ*; to this he says: "after the root *ṛ* with the prefix *ā-*, [the suffix *ktin* becomes feminine]."

The meaning is that from the root *ṛ* preceded by the prefix *ā*, when the suffix *ktin* is added, there is a single substitution (*ekādeśa*) by the rule "vṛddhi [occurs] after a prefix before a root beginning with *ṛ*. *Rekhā* and *lekhā*: this is a *gaṇasūtra*. Regarding *guṇa*: the *aṅ* suffix is applied to the root *likh*, and there is *guṇa* [substitution];
the meaning is that the letter *l* becomes *r*. *Cūḍā*: this is a *gaṇasūtra*. *Dhārā* and *prapāt*: [these are also *gaṇasūtras*].
The Vārttika: It should be understood that [the suffix] applies when there is the falling of a liquid substance.
(98) *cinti-pūji-kathi-kuṃbha-carcaś-ca* | Pāṇini 3.1.105. *cinti-pūji*: these belong to the *curādigaṇa*. Since the rule *ṭhṇyāsasrantho yuj* would have applied to them, [the following is stated].
This is the rule for *aṅ*. Thus it says: "It is an exception (*apavāda*) to *yuc*. In words such as *cintā*, there is the substitution of *aṅ* and the elision of the *iṇ* suffix.
The letter *ca* (in the sūtra) serves to include what has not been explicitly mentioned; therefore, there is also the inclusion of *tolayati*. As it says: "And *atula* etc. (*cātuletiṭ*).

(99) *ātaścopasarge* |3|3|106|. [The word] *aṅ* shall be [the suffix]. That is to say, when a prefix (*upasarga*) is present as an attendant word (*upapada*), the suffix *aṅ* shall be applied after a verbal root ending in long *ā*, in the sense of an abstract state (*bhāva*) or a factor other than the agent (*akartṛ-kāraka*). For example: *pradā*.

From the root *dā* preceded by *pra*, the suffix *aṅ* is applied; then, by the rule "the elision of *ā*" (*āto lopaḥ*), the long *ā* is dropped, resulting in *pradā*. Similarly, *upadā*. Now, one might object: how can the suffix *aṅ* be applied after the roots *dhā* preceded by the indeclinables *śrat* and *antar*, given that these two lack the status of prepositions (*upasarga*)?
To this, he says: "The words *śrat* and *antar* are treated like prepositions."

The meaning is that, according to the Vārttikas—"the status of *pra* as an *upasarga* must be stated for the application of the suffix *aṅ*" and "the status of *antaḥ* as an *upasarga* must be stated for the application of the suffixes *aṅ*, *ki*, and *ṇatva* (nasalization)"—there is a derivative (*vṛtti*) consisting of the *kṛt*-suffix *aṅ* from roots ending in long vowels preceded by those [two] *upasargas*. The term "derivative" (*vṛtti*) also implies the rule for *ṇatva* (nasalization); thus, forms such as *antarddhā*, *antarddhiḥ*, and *antarṇayati* are included. This is the general direction.

(100) *ṇyāsaśrantho yuc* |3|3|107|. The meaning is that the suffix *yuc* occurs after roots ending in *ṇi*, as well as after *ās* and *śranth*, in the sense of feminine action (*bhāva*) and so forth. Regarding "of the vowel *a*": this means of the *a* prescribed by [Pāṇini 3.3.104] *ṭha pratyayāt*. [The examples are] *ghaṭṭi* and *vandī*.

The rule for *yuc* applies because the root ends in a non-causative (*aṇ*) form. Regarding "vedanā": the suffix *yuc* is applied to the root *vid* meaning "to obtain," as established by the commentary;

however, for the root *vid* meaning "to know" (*vida jñāne*), the form is *vitti*. Furthermore, from the *cur*-class root *vid* meaning "to feel, to know, or to dwell" (*vida vedanājñānanivāseṣu*), the suffix *yuc* is applied according to the rule *ṇyāsaśrantho yuc*, resulting in *vedanā* as well. Regarding "of the root *iṣ* meaning 'to desire'": [the suffix *san* is applied].
The word "should be stated" (*vaktavya*) is the ellipsis. Regarding "anveṣaṇā": it means searching (*mārgaṇā*). However, when [the root] *iṣ* means desire, the form is *anviṣṭi*.
Regarding "after *pari*": the meaning is that *yuj* is added after the root *iṣ* preceded by *pari*. Thus, *parīṣṭi*; the *ṣ* is substituted [for the *s*] by the rule *vraśca-*.

(101) *rogākhyāyāṃ ṇvul bahulam* || 3.3.108 || In the case of naming a disease, the suffix *ṇvul* is used diversely. [The rule applies] specifically when the word is feminine. *Pracchardikā* is explained as *vamir* (vomiting); the meaning is "the act of vomiting. *Pravāhikā* is explained as *grahaṇī* (dysentery).
A specific type of diarrhea. The explanation of *vacarcikā* is "pāmā" (scabies).
Regarding "not in some cases," the remainder is "by the suffix *ṇvuL*"; the intention is that this is due to the mention of the term *bahulam* (variously). [Regarding *ardati*:
this is a demonstration of the verbal root for the word *arti*, namely *arda hiṃsāyām* (to injure). "Headache" (*śiro'rti*). "The head..."

The meaning is "affliction" (*pīḍā*). [This is derived from] the root *ṛd* with the suffix *ktin*; by the rule *titutra*, the augment *iṭ* is not applied. Regarding the phrase "when the meaning of the root is to be indicated": this means that when the meaning of the root is to be expressed, the suffix *ṇvul* is frequently added to the root in its own sense. It occurs only in the feminine gender. Examples are *āsikā* and *śāyikā*, which mean "sitting" (*āsana*) and "lying down" (*śayana*), respectively.

Regarding the rule *ik-stip-au*: the meaning is that when the actual form of a verbal root (*dhātu-svarūpa*) is to be designated, the suffixes *ik* and *tip* should be stated. The result is that the actual form of the root itself is what is to be expressed. Thus, *paciḥ* and *pacatiḥ* mean "the verbal root *pac*. Because it possesses the quality of being *śit*, it is treated as a *sārvadhātuka* suffix, and consequently, the *ch* [of *pac*] is replaced by *c*.

Even though [the root *su*] expresses the absence of an agent (*akartṛka*), the verbal suffixes (*vikaraṇa*) such as *śap* and so on still apply, because of the specific grammatical instruction (*nirdeśa*) in the rule "after a prefix, [the suffix *śap* is applied] to *sanoti* and *suvati*" (Pāṇini 7.3.78). The claim of the ancients that this is due to the force of the marker *ś* (*śitva-sāmarthyāt*) is incorrect; for if it were so, the substitutes *piba-* and others would apply in cases such as *pibati* and *gāyati*, and the substitution of *āt* (for *a*) would be precluded.

Since the purpose of [the rule] *śit* has been fulfilled, enough [of this discussion]. Here, [the word] *striyām* ("in the feminine") is not connected [to the rule], according to the commentary (*vyākhyāna*). Regarding the statement "after a phoneme (*varṇa*), [the suffix] *kāra* [is added]," this is a *vārttika*. Regarding the phrase "only in the case of a mention (*nirdeśa*)," when a mention of phonemes such as *a*, *i*, *u*, etc., is to be made, [the forms] *a*, *i*, *u* [are used] because they are imitations (*anukaraṇa*) of those phonemes.

The meaning is that the suffix *kāra* should be applied in its own sense (*svārthe*) after nominal stems (*prātipadika*) such as these. Regarding the term "akāra": it means the vowel *a*. Here, although the suffix *kāra* is not prescribed after a verbal root (*dhātu*), it receives the technical designation *kṛt* by virtue of the governing rule (*adhikāra*). Consequently, since it follows a nominal stem, the case-endings (*sup*) are produced. As for the letter *ka*...

The designation "net" (indicating the absence of *iṭ*) applies because there is no purpose [for its presence]; since it is not an *ārdhadhātuka* suffix, the elision of the long *ā* (as in *āto lopaḥ*) does not apply in cases such as *ṭhākāra*. Precisely because it is not an *ārdhadhātuka*, there is no *iṭ*. Due to the continued application of the term "variously" (*bahulagrahaṇa*), in some instances it does not apply—as in *ṭhasya cvau* and so forth. [The mention of] the letter *k* [is for the sake of indicating the *kit* designation].

The meaning is "the letter *ka*. In this context, the vowel *a* is for the purpose of pronunciation (*uccāraṇārtha*). This is because of the commentary on the sūtra "udāttasvaritayoḥ... (Pāṇini 1.2.31), which states: "Furthermore, the pronunciation of a consonant does not occur without a vowel. In some cases, the suffix *kāra* is applied even to a cluster [of sounds], as in "evakāra" and so forth.

This is because of the rule-indication in the sūtra "ṭhvaṣaṭkāra" and because of the Bhāṣya statement, "all occurrences of the letter 'ca' are rejected. Regarding "rādipha," the word "should be stated" (vācya) is the ellipsis. By the rule of optional non-homogeneity (vā'sarūpa-vidhi), the suffix *kāra* is also [permissible]. Here, this is accepted on the basis of the continued application (anuvṛtti) of the term "in the feminine" (striyām).

Because there is no prohibition [of the suffix] in the case of non-feminine genders. "From a word having the sense of possession (*matvartha*)," means that the suffix *cha* should be stated as occurring in its own meaning (without changing the base) after a word expressing possession. Now, one might ask: how is the elision of the vowel *a* in the rule "ṭhyasyeti ca" [Pāṇini 6.4.148] applied here, given that this is not a *taddhita* suffix and because it is not a *bha*-stem? To this, he says:

"Due to the mention of *bahula*, there is the elision of the vowel *a*. Regarding "possessive suffix" (*matvarthīya*): that suffix whose meaning is that of the possessive suffix *mat* is "possessive"; that very thing is a "possessive suffix" (*matvarthīya*). However, in the rule *tasau matvarthe*, [the elision does not occur] because of the inclusion of the term *bahula*. In the rule *śaiṣikān matvarthīyāt*, the suffix *cha* is applied in the sense of "originating from" (*bhava*) because [the base] belongs to the *gahādi* group.
Regarding the rule *bodhī-ṇ-añ-ādibhyaḥ*: the word "should be stated" (*vācya*) is the ellipsis. This applies only in the feminine gender.
[In the case of *ājir*, having raised the doubt regarding the substitution of *vī* for *aj*, he says: "in various ways" (*bahulam*). Regarding the rule *iñ-vā-padibhyaḥ*:

the word "should be stated" (*vācya*) is the ellipsis. This applies only in the feminine gender. Now, one might object: since this is already established by the continued application (*anuvṛtti*) of the suffix *iñ* alone...
The inclusion of the term *iñ* is purposeless; therefore, he says: "There is a difference in accent.
The meaning is that a specific accentuation—namely, the rule "that which begins with *ñ* or *ṇ* is always acute" (*ñnityādir nityam*)—is the result of prescribing *iñ*.

Regarding "from *kṛṣi* and so forth," the word "it should be stated" (*vācya*) is to be supplied as the remainder [of the sūtra]. As for "agriculture" (*kṛṣi*), because it is marked with the *k*-sign (*kitva*), there is no [acute accent on the first syllable].

The class of roots beginning with *laghu* has a light penultimate vowel. Regarding the word *giri*: [it is derived] from the root *gṛ* with the suffix *ik*. Because the suffix is marked with *k*, there is no *guṇa* substitution. By the rule *ṛta iddhātoḥ*, the *ṛ* is changed to *it*, and by the rule regarding *rapara*, the *r* is substituted for the *ṛ*. (102) *saṃjñāyām* 3.3.109.

Regarding "saṃjñāyām" (in the sense of a name): "varaṇa" refers to a specific type of tree, well-known among ritualists from such passages as "vāraṇyāny ahomārthāni" (the *vāraṇa* trees are not for the purpose of oblations). [The explanation of "abhyūṣa" is] "pūrikā" (a fried cake); its further explanation is "a specific kind of *apūpa*" (a baked cake).
Thus [it is said]: "When fried in ghee, combined with asafoetida and black pepper, smeared with ghee, mixed with water, and rolled upon a board;
or else fried in ghee or oil—that is considered a *pūrikā*," according to its definition in the *Bhojanakautūhala*.

(103) *vibhāṣākhyānaparipraśnayoriñ ca* |3|3|110|. [The suffix] *iñ* is optionally applied after [a word denoting] a question (*paripraśna*) or a narration (*ākhyāna*), provided it refers to a woman. [The compound is analyzed as follows: first there is the questioning (*paripraśna*), and subsequently there is the telling of what was said, which is the narration (*ākhyāna*). Because the word *ākhyāna* has fewer syllables, it is placed first in the compound.
He says this: "In the case of *paripraśna*. Since the form would be established by the rule of *vāsarūpa*, he states that the mention of *vibhāṣā* (optionality) is redundant;

therefore, he says: "Because of the statement of *vibhāṣā*. Due to the non-application of the *vāsarūpa* rule in the feminine, if the mention of *vibhāṣā* were absent, only the suffixes *iñ* and *ṇvul* would occur, and not [the others].

The meaning is "another suffix. He provides an example for the inquiry [regarding] *paripraśna*: "kāṃ tvam" (what have you done?). The grammatical connection (*anvaya*) is: "kāṃ tvaṃ kārim akārṣīḥ" (what action have you performed?). This is the form derived with the suffix *iñ*. In the same way, the connection of "kāṃ tvam" and "kārṣīḥ" should be understood in cases such as "kārikām" and so forth. The form "kārikām" is derived with the suffix *ṇvul*.
